proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing threat models, defensive architecture patterns, runtime sandboxing, sensitive data management, and privacy-preserving agent workflows.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group is a cross-cutting technical initiative within the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) focused on identifying, mitigating, and formalizing defensive practices for autonomous and semi-autonomous AI systems.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e080ea2d4af5-49d9592e] The group acts as an intersecting security and privacy review layer across other AAIF initiatives—including [Identity and Trust](identity-and-trust.md) and [Agentic Commerce](agentic-commerce.md)—delivering pre-competitive threat models, guardrail specifications, auditability standards, and reference implementations.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d]

# Architecture / Specification

## Charter Themes and Technical Focus Areas

The working group concentrates on technical security patterns and privacy controls tailored to multi-turn, tool-using, and distributed agent environments:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e080ea2d4af5-49d9592e][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d]

- **Sensitive Data and Secrets Management**: Defining handling standards that differentiate traditional runtime credentials (API keys, environment variables) from confidential enterprise context and proprietary data loaded into memory or prompt context.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d]
- **Privacy-Preserving Workflows**: Investigating cryptographic and architectural safeguards—including Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs), zero-knowledge verification mechanisms, and encrypted vector databases—that allow agents to compute over protected information without leaking plaintext state.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d]
- **Protected Data and PII Obfuscation**: Classifying regulated data categories (such as HIPAA-governed health records) and formulating redaction and obfuscation patterns across tool calls and context windows.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d]
- **Rogue Agent Blast Radius and Derailment**: Measuring and bounding attack surfaces, establishing containment patterns for compromised or derailed agents, and formulating controls for non-malicious operational failures.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d]
- **Commerce and Payment Guardrails**: Narrowing commerce-related efforts strictly to financial security boundaries, including fund-draining prevention, account credential leak mitigation, and delegated payment scope limits.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d]
- **Shared Security Taxonomy**: Developing an internal catalog of security and privacy definitions to align working group terminology before contributing upstream to the foundation-wide [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](taxonomy-and-landscape.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d]

## Governance and Cross-Group Boundaries

To prevent duplicative efforts across the AAIF ecosystem, the group enforces specific operational boundaries:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d]

- **Responsible AI and Ethics**: Ethical philosophy, bias analysis, and subjective value judgments are explicitly deferred to the [Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Working Group](governance-risk-and-regulatory.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d]
- **Reliability and Hallucinations**: Model performance benchmarking and truthfulness metrics fall under the [Accuracy and Reliability Working Group](accuracy-and-reliability.md), while the Security and Privacy Working Group retains jurisdiction over non-malicious derailment, prompt injections, and adversarial manipulation.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d]
- **External Coordination**: Aligning agenda and output with external open-source security efforts, such as the OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e080ea2d4af5-49d9592e][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d]

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-02-17**: Working group orientation convened by Linux Foundation AI leadership. Brainstormed core problem areas including capability-based authorization, memory security, red teaming, and blast radius mitigation, while opening chair nominations via LFX voting.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e080ea2d4af5-49d9592e]
- **2026-03-03**: Alex Frazer confirmed as elected Chair. The group established bi-weekly meeting schedules, confirmed charter milestones (mission/scope finalization, deliverable mapping, and Governing Board charter submission), and resolved scope demarcations with the Governance and Reliability working groups.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d]

proposed_concept.title: Governance, Risk and Regulatory Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group bridging global AI policy developments, regulatory compliance, and risk frameworks into actionable architectural guidance for autonomous agents.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Governance, Risk and Regulatory Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) technical body dedicated to mapping global artificial intelligence regulations, legal risk postures, and compliance mandates to technical patterns and system architectures for autonomous agents[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a20272325759-501fd75f]. The working group operates under pre-competitive collaboration principles governed by the Linux Foundation and the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md)[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a20272325759-501fd75f].

The group focuses on analyzing existing regulatory regimes—such as the European Union AI Act, eIDAS 2, GDPR, and emerging frameworks in jurisdictions like Singapore—to assess risk boundaries, liability distribution, and human oversight mechanisms in agentic software deployments[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a20272325759-501fd75f][^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77].

# Architecture / Specification

## Three-Step Working Model

The working group structures its primary technical outputs across a three-step progression model[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77][^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d7a6875f36a3-5c7bc654]:

1. **Landscape Analysis**: Systematic review and cataloging of existing regulatory standards, compliance frameworks, industry best practices, and production use cases across regulated sectors (such as GDPR, PII handling, and identity verification)[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77].
2. **Gap Analysis**: Detailed evaluation identifying where existing governance frameworks and risk management protocols fail to address risks specific to agentic AI, including autonomous tool invocation, non-deterministic action loops, and multi-agent delegation[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77].
3. **Distilled Guidance and Principles**: Synthesis of actionable architectural principles, risk-assessment protocols, and implementation baselines for enterprise organizations adopting autonomous agents[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77].

## Deliverable Backlog

The current deliverables backlog includes:
- Formal problem set definitions for governance and regulatory compliance in agentic systems[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77].
- Cross-regulatory landscape mapping matrix[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77].
- Agentic risk assessment protocols governing agent-human oversight interactions and probabilistic risk models[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a20272325759-501fd75f].
- A working group charter submitted to the Technical Committee for lifecycle advancement under the [Working Group Lifecycle Policy](../policies/working-group-lifecycle-policy.md)[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a20272325759-501fd75f].

## Operating Cadence and Documentation Protocol

The group conducts biweekly working meetings recorded via LFX Zoom[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77]. Meeting records are published in the group's repository following a canonical structure governed by an agent instruction workflow (`AGENTS.md`) and template (`TEMPLATE.md`)[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-6fa126354b0b-2d7e8a4a][^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-eb9c68e792e7-c6422732]. Notes are named in `YYYY-MM-DD.md` format, indexing resources (AI summaries, transcripts, and recordings), discussed topics, decisions, deliverables, and assigned action item tables[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-eb9c68e792e7-c6422732].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-02-19**: Working group kickoff meeting convened to establish Linux Foundation governance expectations, antitrust compliance, charter drafting logistics, and chair nomination procedures[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a20272325759-501fd75f].
- **2026-03-05**: Second meeting led by co-chairs Ryan and Junjie; formal adoption of the three-step working model (landscape analysis, gap analysis, and distilled guidance) and establishment of the deliverable backlog[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77][^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d7a6875f36a3-5c7bc654].

proposed_concept.title: Technical Committee
proposed_concept.description: Governing technical body of the Agentic AI Foundation overseeing technical vision, project lifecycles, working group charters, and architectural alignment.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Technical Committee (TC) is the governing technical authority of the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF), a directed fund of The Linux Foundation, responsible for technical strategy, working group oversight, and open-source project lifecycle evaluation [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941]. Operating under its formal charter adopted on March 3, 2026, the TC assists the AAIF Governing Board (GB) by vetting technical proposals, coordinating cross-project collaboration, and enforcing the Foundation's project lifecycle rules [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].

# Architecture / Specification

## Purpose and Mandate

The TC fulfills three primary charter duties on behalf of the Governing Board [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941]:

1. Reviewing new technical project proposals submitted to the Foundation [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].
2. Recommending technical projects that fit the scope and mission of the AAIF to the Governing Board [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].
3. Applying and maintaining the [Project Lifecycle Policy](../policies/project-lifecycle-policy.md) across all AAIF Technical Projects [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].

Additionally, the TC is tasked with establishing, managing, and archiving AAIF Working Groups, defining overall technical priorities, recommending resource allocations to the GB, and electing its leadership annually [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].

## Composition

Each Platinum Member of the AAIF is entitled to appoint one representative (a TC Representative) to serve as a voting member of the Technical Committee [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941]. The TC elects a TC Chair and may elect a Co-Chair to preside over proceedings until resignation or replacement [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].

## Governance and Decision Mechanics

The TC functions as a consensus-seeking body governed by specific procedural mechanisms [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941]:

- **Voting Basis:** When formal votes are required, decisions operate on a one-vote-per-voting-member basis [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].
- **Quorum:** Actionable voting requires at least fifty percent (50%) of active voting members present [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941]. Meetings without quorum may discuss matters but cannot hold binding votes [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].
- **Lazy Consensus:** The TC utilizes a silence-as-agreement model where proposals are automatically adopted if no formal objection is recorded by a voting member within 72 hours [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941]. If an objection is lodged, decision by electronic vote requires an absolute majority of all TC voting members [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].
- **Escalation:** In the event an impasse cannot be resolved internally, any TC voting member may refer the matter to the Governing Board [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].
- **Charter Amendments:** Amending the TC Charter requires a two-thirds supermajority approval of the TC followed by Governing Board ratification [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-03-03:** Formal Technical Committee Charter adopted under The Linux Foundation [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group (SP-WG) is an AAIF technical body focused on establishing security and privacy as a shared discipline across the agentic AI ecosystem [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35]. Guided by its adopted mission statement, the group produces open threat models, a shared taxonomy, and reusable security architecture patterns that providers, consumers, and peer working groups can adopt to implement shared responsibility for trustworthy agentic systems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35].

# Architecture / Specification

## Mission and Leadership

The working group formally adopted its mission statement on March 31, 2026 [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35]:

> "The Security and Privacy Working Group advances the Agentic AI Foundation's mission by establishing security and privacy as a shared discipline across the Agentic AI ecosystem. Producing open threat models, a shared taxonomy, and design patterns that providers, consumers, and peer working groups can adopt to share responsibility for trustworthy agentic AI." [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35]

The group is co-chaired by Alex Frazer and Junjie Bu (Google) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-822dcec9cbfd-b1d860ec].

## Scope and Inter-Group Boundaries

The SP-WG focuses on technical controls, attack surface analysis, and privacy engineering, establishing explicit operational boundaries with peer working groups [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-822dcec9cbfd-b1d860ec] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35]:

- **Security Architecture & Design Patterns:** Encompasses defensive patterns, agent sandboxing, prompt injection mitigations, and execution boundaries for agent skills and tools [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35].
- **Identity and Trust Boundary:** Rather than developing identity protocols, SP-WG provides security requirements to the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md), maintaining focus on logging, execution bounding, and runtime auditing [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-822dcec9cbfd-b1d860ec] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35].
- **Privacy Engineering:** Centers on technical mitigations—such as data minimization, memory isolation, and sensitive data handling—rather than direct legal interpretations of GDPR or HIPAA, collaborating with the [Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Working Group](../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md) on regulatory compliance alignment [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35].
- **Commerce Security:** Interfaces with the [Agentic Commerce Working Group](../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md) through dedicated liaison members to align financial transaction guardrails and payment isolation [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35].
- **Observability and Forensics:** Coordinates with the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) on behavioral anomaly detection, telemetry protection, and runtime incident playbooks [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-822dcec9cbfd-b1d860ec].

## Deliverables Roadmap

The working group tracks five core deliverable streams [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-822dcec9cbfd-b1d860ec]:

1. **Living Taxonomy:** Standardized definitions and classifications for agentic security concepts [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-822dcec9cbfd-b1d860ec].
2. **Agentic AI Threat Modeling Framework:** Methodologies and attack surface mapping targeting prompt injection, tool abuse, and subagent privilege escalation [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-822dcec9cbfd-b1d860ec] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35].
3. **Security and Privacy Design Patterns:** Concrete architectural blueprints for safe agent execution [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-822dcec9cbfd-b1d860ec].
4. **Security Best Practices Guide:** Actionable deployment guidance reflecting the [Agentic AI Security Best Practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-822dcec9cbfd-b1d860ec].
5. **Cross-Workgroup Security & Privacy Checklist:** Review criteria enabling peer WGs to assess deliverables for privacy leaks and security risks [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-822dcec9cbfd-b1d860ec].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-03-17:** Junjie Bu appointed co-chair; five deliverable tracks and inter-group coordination models introduced [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-822dcec9cbfd-b1d860ec].
- **2026-03-31:** Formal adoption of Mission Statement Option G; skills incorporated into security architecture scope; privacy engineering distinction established [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35].

proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing vendor-neutral agent telemetry standards, cross-boundary tracing frameworks, and behavioral observability conventions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability & Traceability Working Group (OT-WG) is an AAIF technical body convened to build a shared understanding of AI agent observability across practitioners, enterprise vendors, and external standards bodies [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88]. Led by Primary Contact and Chair Pavan Sudheendra, the group functions as an ecosystem coordination forum designed to address trace fragmentation, close the gap between single LLM call tracing and complex multi-turn session behavior, and establish auditability for production agent deployments [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88].

# Architecture / Specification

## Mandate and Positioning

The OT-WG is explicitly structured as an alignment forum rather than a competing specification body [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88]. Rather than fracturing the ecosystem with incompatible schemas, the group coordinates AAIF efforts with adjacent external standards initiatives—including the [OpenTelemetry](../resources/opentelemetry.md) GenAI Special Interest Group (SIG), OWASP AOS, and W3C Trace Context [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88]. The group targets specification development only when concrete gap analyses confirm an unmet ecosystem need, with the primary objective of upstreaming specifications where possible [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88].

## Guiding Principles

The working group operates under six core principles defined in its charter [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88]:

- **Coordinate First, Specify Only When Necessary:** Prioritize aligning with and contributing to existing standards before creating new ones [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88].
- **Interoperability Over Innovation:** Favor composing with established trace and context mechanisms over bespoke standards [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88].
- **Observable by Default:** Ensure agent systems provide foundational observability natively rather than as an external add-on [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88].
- **Move at Ecosystem Speed:** Emphasize incremental releases and rapid iteration to match evolving agent runtimes [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88].
- **Adoption Is Key:** Focus on practical, implementable specifications that solve real practitioner problems [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88].
- **Vendor and Framework Neutrality:** Prevent bias toward specific commercial platforms or framework implementations [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88].

## Core Focus Areas

The group's founding technical track centers on the [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md), bridging the visibility gap between low-level model inference and multi-turn, multi-agent workflows [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88]. Activities encompass tool boundary tracing, content lineage, fidelity tracking across modalities, and multi-agent interaction auditing [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-04-13:** Working Group charter draft updated under chair leadership of Pavan Sudheendra, formalizing the founding Agent Behavior Trace Model focus area and coordination mandate [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical working group chartered to establish threat models, privacy engineering standards, defensive reference architectures, and security design patterns across autonomous AI agent runtimes and workflows.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151] The working group develops cross-cutting security evaluation criteria, cataloged implementation patterns, and advisory review mechanisms across the AAIF ecosystem.

# Scope and Deliverables
The working group operates under a charter approved by member vote, targeting five initial deliverables across a three-to-six month horizon:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151]

1. **Taxonomy**: A living reference catalog defining shared security and privacy terminology for contribution into broader AAIF taxonomy initiatives.
2. **Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design**: A research deliverable assessing coverage across OWASP and NIST models while addressing agent-specific risk contexts such as shared memory stores, dynamic neural network weights, and complex identity delegation boundaries.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151] (See [Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis](../resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md)).
3. **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: A builder-oriented catalog defining reusable patterns for human-in-the-loop oversight, hook extensibility, logical and semantic constraint enforcement, and privacy-preserving execution.
4. **Agentic Security Best Practices Guide**: Practical operational guidance spanning secrets management, containment, and secure tool invocation for builders implementing agentic workflows.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151] (See [Agentic AI Security Best Practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md)).
5. **Cross-Working Group Review Checklist**: An evaluation checklist assisting other AAIF working groups in identifying security and privacy ramifications early in their deliverable lifecycles.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151]

In addition to baseline deliverables, the group monitors relevant external developments including Model Context Protocol (MCP) Interceptor hook standards, browser-like agent trust verification in MCP Apps, and upstream Linux Foundation security efforts.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151]

# Lifecycle History
On 2026-04-14, the working group unanimously approved its operational scope, charter, and initial five deliverables by formal member vote ahead of scheduled presentation to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151]

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Landscape
proposed_concept.description: Interactive ecosystem map and open-source catalog categorizing agentic AI frameworks, protocols, and runtimes under AAIF governance.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The AAIF Agentic AI Landscape provides an interactive visualization and categorized directory of the broader agentic AI ecosystem, tracking prominent open-source software, open standards, member organizations, and foundation projects.[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1] Curated under the auspices of the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md), the catalog establishes a vendor-neutral index of functional capabilities, tooling runtimes, and protocol implementations across agentic computing.

The catalog is publicly hosted at `landscape.aaif.io` and rendered using the Cloud Native Computing Foundation's `cncf/landscape2` compilation engine.[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1]

# Architecture / Specification

### Data Sources and Build Pipeline

The landscape repository maintains canonical metadata definitions, organization affiliations, and visual assets required by the `landscape2` generator:[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1]
- **`landscape.yml`**: The primary data file organizing entries into hierarchical categories and subcategories in alphabetical order.
- **`hosted_logos`**: Repository storage containing vector brand marks formatted as SVG files.
- **Crunchbase Integration**: Corporate entities and trademark owners are mapped to Crunchbase organizations to ingest funding, organization type, and operational metadata under Linux Foundation data access terms.
- **Automated Publishing**: The live landscape site is generated on a daily schedule, reflecting merged pull request changes within 24 hours.

### Inclusion and Governance Criteria

To ensure quality and maintain an objective open ecosystem overview, admissions into the landscape must satisfy strict repository acceptance policies:[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1]
1. **Open-Source Threshold**: Entries must be open-source projects possessing at least 1,000 GitHub stars and clearly matching an established category taxonomy.
2. **Category Exclusivity**: A project is assigned to a single best-fitting category. Organizations are limited to one entry representing their major or primary offering, with rare exceptions granted only for large multi-product organizations.
3. **Exclusion of Closed Software**: Closed-source commercial products, hosted services, proprietary standards, and proprietary commercial distributions of open-source projects are strictly excluded. Closed-source products implementing open-source protocols or specifications are also ineligible.
4. **Asset Standards**: Logos must be provided in SVG format with English typography, transparent or white backgrounds (no reversed color variants), and stacked orientations when multiple geometry options exist.

# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group (SP WG) is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body dedicated to defining defensive security architectures, privacy-preserving runtime boundaries, and threat modeling frameworks for autonomous AI agents. The working group operates under the oversight of the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) to provide practical guidance, architectural reference patterns, and community-driven taxonomies across agent execution environments.

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its technical initiatives across several key workstreams:
- **Taxonomy and Threat Modeling**: Drafting standardized agent security terminology and threat classifications, serving as a foundational contribution to cross-working group harmonization efforts [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].
- **Protocol Security and Middleware**: Evaluating security and privacy boundaries in emerging integration protocols, including Model Context Protocol (MCP) Interceptor hooks for data redaction and the security implications of MCP Apps introducing user interfaces across execution boundaries [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].
- **Defensive Best Practices and Sandboxing**: Developing architectural recommendations for runtime isolation, credential management, and guardrail integration within multi-agent workflows.

# Lifecycle History
The working group's initial charter was submitted to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) in April 2026 [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5]. During the formal voting review, four affirmative votes were recorded while procedural delays and quorum constraints prevented immediate formal ratification; with zero substantive objections filed, the group proceeded with operational deliverables [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].

In April 2026, the working group coordinated with foundation leadership to establish taxonomy as the initial cross-working group collaboration project, contributing the SP WG draft taxonomy as the baseline [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5]. Concurrently, the group restructured its operating cadence into focused checkpoint meetings complemented by asynchronous workstream self-organization to accommodate global participant distribution and the appointment of foundation CTO Manik [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].

proposed_concept.title: Technical Committee
proposed_concept.description: Governing technical body of the Agentic AI Foundation overseeing technical vision, project lifecycle transitions, and working group charters.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Technical Committee (TC) is the governing technical steering body of the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF), responsible for setting the technical vision, establishing operational policies, reviewing project proposals, and chartering technical working groups. Operating under Linux Foundation guidelines, the committee provides cross-project architectural alignment, reviews community submissions, and serves as the formal approval board for foundation initiatives.

# Architecture / Specification
The Technical Committee exercises governance over foundation activities through structured procedural workflows:
- **Working Group Charter Approval**: Acts as the governing board requiring formal review and voting approval for new working group charters, such as the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), ensuring clear scope, deliverables, and alignment across technical areas [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].
- **Proposal Intake and Review**: Maintains standardized submission channels for incoming working group proposals, tracking member organization affiliations and membership tiers while conducting scheduled review cycles [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-87b3376703c5-cfe1353c] [^evt-working-group-proposals-pr-1].
- **Cross-Group Harmonization**: Coordinates common deliverables among active groups, initiating shared foundations such as cross-working group taxonomy synchronization [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].

# Lifecycle History
In early 2026, the Technical Committee initiated formal governance operations across project and working group tracks [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-87b3376703c5-cfe1353c]. A leadership transition occurred in April 2026 when Matt concluded his tenure as AAIF Chief Technology Officer and Manik assumed the role, steering the foundation's technical roadmap across global time zones [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].

In late April 2026, the committee began receiving working group formation submissions through an issue-template workflow assigned to Christina Harter, with formal review cycles designated to open on June 1, 2026 [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-87b3376703c5-cfe1353c] [^evt-working-group-proposals-pr-1]. Concurrently, the committee evaluated inaugural working group charters, navigating volunteer quorum schedules to progress foundational bodies into active standing [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].

proposed_concept.title: Identity and Trust Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing vendor-neutral architectures, delegation chains, authority models, and attestation mechanisms for cross-organizational AI agent trust.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Identity and Trust Working Group (I&T WG) is a technical working group within the Agentic AI Foundation tasked with identifying and promoting vendor-neutral, interoperable standards and architectural viewpoints for AI agent identity, attestation, authentication, delegation, and authorization [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c]. Led by primary contact and chair Grant Miller, the group enables autonomous agents to establish verifiable provenance, represent organizational and human delegation, communicate policy constraints, and traverse multi-tenant trust boundaries securely and auditably [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group's charter delineates six core technical areas within scope [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c]:

- **Agent Identity, Authentication, and Provenance:** Formats and mechanisms for agent identification, cryptographic authentication, and origin attribution reflecting runtime software, host platform, and operating entity.
- **Delegation and Authority Chains:** Standards for expressing agency when acting on behalf of humans, organizations, teams, or automated processes, including depth and lifetime constraints on delegated authority.
- **Authorization and Consent Models:** Fine-grained, short-lived authorization and consent schemas conveying explicit permissions, human approval gates, and governance policies.
- **Trust Evaluation and Cross-Organizational Trust:** Verification mechanisms for evaluating agent identity and authorization assertions received from external, third-party, or federated domains.
- **Agent Discovery and Trust-Relevant Metadata:** Interoperable registries, descriptions, and discovery metadata supporting observability and traceability.
- **Enterprise and Consumer Contexts:** Harmonizing deployment models across enterprise workflows and consumer-facing agent interactions.

### Scope Boundaries and External Coordination
The group explicitly operates with clear governance boundaries [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c]:
- **Standards Development Bodies:** The working group does not ratify formal standards on behalf of external standards development organizations (SDOs), acting instead as an advisory, recommendation, and upstream contribution forum.
- **Execution Security:** Broad runtime isolation, hardened sandbox boundaries, and general security controls fall under [Security & Privacy](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md).
- **Public Policy and Normative AI Ethics:** The group does not define broad ethical frameworks or regulatory policy positions except where directly required for identity, consent, and accountability representations.
- **Production Infrastructure:** The group develops reference implementations and testing guidance rather than operating production identity services or certification authorities.

# Lifecycle History
The Identity and Trust Working Group operates under standard AAIF governance under oversight of the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md), developing baseline charters and collaborating with [Attestation & Evidence](../working-groups/attestation-and-evidence.md) on cryptographic proof formats [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c].

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing vendor-neutral agent telemetry standards, cross-boundary trace correlation, and coordination across OpenTelemetry and OWASP initiatives.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability & Traceability Working Group (OT-WG) is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body convened to align practitioners, enterprise vendors, and standards organizations around common agent telemetry, debugging, and behavioral accountability models [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d]. Chaired by Pavan Sudheendra and ratified by the foundation in May 2026, the working group serves primarily as a cross-ecosystem coordination forum rather than a duplicative standards body, focusing on bridging the gap between single-turn LLM call tracing and complex multi-turn, multi-modal agent workflows [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group functions under six core guiding principles [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d]:
- **Coordinate first, specify only when necessary:** Prioritize aligning with and contributing upstream to established initiatives such as the [OpenTelemetry](../resources/opentelemetry.md) GenAI SIG, OWASP AOS, and W3C Trace Context before creating new specifications.
- **Interoperability over innovation:** Extend existing distributed tracing and telemetry formats rather than fragmenting the ecosystem with proprietary conventions.
- **Observable by default:** Advocate for intrinsic observability built into agent runtimes and orchestration frameworks out of the box.
- **Move at the speed of the ecosystem:** Deliver incremental, practical guidance matched to rapid industry iteration.
- **Adoption as success:** Value real-world implementation across production frameworks over theoretical completeness.
- **Vendor and framework neutrality:** Ensure specifications do not advantage proprietary platforms.

### Focus Areas and Mandate
The working group establishes a modular focus group operating model anchored by its founding technical initiative [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d]:
- **[Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md):** Developing a unified telemetry schema and correlation context capturing multi-turn tool invocations, goal decomposition, and reasoning state transitions across disparate execution boundaries.
- **Cross-Boundary Telemetry:** Resolving context propagation challenges between agents, Model Context Protocol servers, and CLI tooling.
- **Lineage and Multi-Modal Tracing:** Investigating trace conventions for content transformations, grounding fidelity, and artifact provenance across multi-modal pipelines.

# Lifecycle History
Formally established and ratified under the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) in May 2026, the working group coordinates AAIF member contributions with external cloud-native and cybersecurity observability standards [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d].

proposed_concept.description: Operating procedure and governance requirements for open-source projects submitting proposals for AAIF hosting, evaluation, and lifecycle progression.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Project Proposal Process defines the formal intake procedure, submission criteria, and evaluation workflow for open-source software projects seeking entry into the Agentic AI Foundation [^evt-project-proposals-pr-23]. Maintained under the oversight of the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md), the process establishes structured intake templates in the `aaif/project-proposals` repository to evaluate applicant readiness against foundation governance and intellectual property standards [^evt-project-proposals-pr-23].

# Architecture / Specification
Project proposals must provide verified information regarding project scope, architecture, licensing, and maintainer commitment. In alignment with the [Project Lifecycle Policy](../policies/project-lifecycle-policy.md), submission criteria distinguish mandatory prerequisites from optional readiness indicators [^evt-project-proposals-pr-23]:

### Intake Requirements
- **Core Proposal Metadata:** Submission details including project name, summary, target lifecycle stage (such as Sandbox or Growth), open-source license conformance (e.g., Apache 2.0), and maintainer contact information.
- **Technical Scope and Relevance:** Alignment with AAIF agentic interoperability goals and foundational capabilities.
- **Optional Readiness Fields:** To prevent blocking early-stage sandbox applicants, items such as a formal published roadmap and an OpenSSF Best Practices badge are explicitly designated as optional in both the submission form and lifecycle policy evaluations [^evt-project-proposals-pr-23].

# Lifecycle History
The proposal workflow was updated to reconcile intake form validation with the governing lifecycle policy, converting roadmap and OpenSSF badge inputs from mandatory blockers to optional fields [^evt-project-proposals-pr-23].

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing open threat models, security architecture, containment patterns, and privacy engineering controls for agentic AI systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security & Privacy Working Group (SPAA) establishes security and privacy as a shared, pre-competitive discipline across the Agentic AI Foundation ecosystem.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899] It produces vendor-neutral threat models, taxonomies, and architectural design patterns addressing failure modes and risks unique to autonomous agents, including prompt injection, confused deputy behaviors, authorization boundary violations, tool invocation vulnerabilities, and persistent agent memory exposure.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899]

The working group operates under the technical governance of the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) and acts as an intersecting security layer supporting peer working groups such as [Identity and Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) and [Taxonomy and Landscape](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899]

# Architecture / Specification
## Scope and Boundaries
The working group focuses strictly on technical security controls and architectural patterns for autonomous agents:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899]
- **In Scope:** Threat modeling and attack analysis, security architecture and design patterns, agent control and containment mechanisms, data protection and privacy engineering, and cross-working-group security reviews.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899]
- **Out of Scope:** Value judgments, ethics, and bias questions (deferred to governance bodies); regulatory compliance interpretations (monitoring technical mandates without offering legal prescriptions); and commercial certification programs for agentic systems.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899]

## Governance and Operations
- **Leadership:** Chaired by Alex Frazer with Co-Chair Junjie Bu.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1] Working group chairs serve 12-month terms with a maximum limit of two consecutive terms.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1]
- **Decision-Making:** Operates primarily by consensus, falling back to a simple-majority vote requiring a 51% quorum if consensus fails, with unresolved escalations directed to the Technical Committee.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1]
- **Cadence and Collaboration:** Conducts biweekly open meetings recorded on LFX, coordinating through GitHub issues, pull requests, and mailing lists.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1]
- **Deliverables:** Core planned outputs include the Agentic Security Taxonomy v0, Cross-WG Security Review Checklist, Threat Modeling Gap Analysis, Design Patterns Catalog, and Best Practices Guide.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1]
- **Intellectual Property:** Source code is released under Apache-2.0 or MIT licenses, and documentation under CC-BY-4.0 or CC-BY-SA 4.0 under Developer Certificate of Origin (DCO) sign-offs.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1]

# Lifecycle History
The Security & Privacy Working Group charter was drafted and finalized under PR#1, establishing the working group's scope, operational model, and deliverables approved on May 13, 2026.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899]

proposed_concept.title: Blog Content Intake and Editorial Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Editorial standards, submission workflows, contributor eligibility rules, and neutrality constraints governing technical publications on aaif.io.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Foundation Blog Guidelines establish the intake process, review workflow, and editorial quality standards for publications appearing on the official aaif.io website.[^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c] The blog acts as an educational and technical publishing platform highlighting hosted open-source projects, architectural patterns, technical guides, and community developments across the agentic AI ecosystem.[^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c]

Publishing is managed end-to-end by the Linux Foundation team, requiring all submissions to be routed through the foundation's official submission form with a standard two-week review lead time.[^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c] Contributors can also leverage the [`skills/aaif-blog-guidelines`](../skills/aaif-blog-guidelines.md) agent skill to automate drafting, quality checks, and submission packaging.[^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c] [^evt-foundation-pr-2]

# Architecture / Specification
## Contributor Eligibility and Scope
Content submissions are accepted from several contributor classes subject to clear editorial boundaries:[^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c]
- **Member Companies:** Content must remain strictly vendor-neutral, educational, and aligned with AAIF's mission; posts may include at most one or two closing sentences with a single external link (such as a company repository or open role).[^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c]
- **Project Maintainers and Contributors:** Updates, roadmaps, and deep-dives regarding AAIF-hosted technologies such as MCP, goose, and AGENTS.md.[^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c]
- **Working Groups and Technical Committee:** Official announcements and technical reports produced by AAIF working groups or the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md).[^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c]
- **Community Contributors:** Tutorials and ecosystem experiences, limited to a maximum quota of two published posts per month per contributor.[^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c]
- **Program Participants:** Recaps, findings, and reflections stemming from AAIF hackathons and events.[^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c]

## Editorial Invariants
Submissions must adhere to strict requirements prior to intake:[^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c]
- **Readiness and Approval:** Submissions must be final, ready for publication, and pre-approved by the contributor's corporate or project stakeholders.[^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c]
- **Originality and Timeliness:** Posts must be original (not published elsewhere) and reflect activities or releases from the preceding two months.[^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c]
- **Neutrality and Non-Disparagement:** No promotional, sponsored, or comparative superiority claims benefiting one member over another; content must not criticize or discourage adoption of any open-source project.[^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c]
- **Format and Length:** Structured narrative format, typically 600–1,500 words, accompanied by titles, author bios, headshots, and social amplification copy.[^evt-public-agents-file-2aebb9feb4df-f97f79ed]

# Lifecycle History
The intake and editorial policy was published in `policies-guidelines/blog-guidelines.md` and later updated via PR#2 to integrate distribution instructions for the `aaif-blog-guidelines` agent skill via `npx skills add aaif/public-agents --skill aaif-blog-guidelines --global`.[^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c] [^evt-foundation-pr-2]

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Blog Guidelines Skill
proposed_concept.description: Modular agent skill assisting contributors in drafting, reviewing, neutralizing, and packaging blog submissions for aaif.io.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The `aaif-blog-guidelines` skill is a standardized agent skill packaged within the `aaif/public-agents` repository that guides AI agents through drafting, reviewing, neutralizing, and packaging blog content for the Agentic AI Foundation blog on aaif.io.[^evt-public-agents-file-2aebb9feb4df-f97f79ed] Authored by Angie Jones, the skill enforces the foundation's official [Blog Content Intake and Editorial Guidelines](../guidelines/blog-guidelines.md).[^evt-public-agents-file-2aebb9feb4df-f97f79ed]

It can be installed globally into compliant agent harnesses using the command `npx skills add aaif/public-agents --skill aaif-blog-guidelines --global`.[^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c]

# Architecture / Specification
## Procedural Workflow
The skill directs agents through a seven-stage assistance pipeline:[^evt-public-agents-file-2aebb9feb4df-f97f79ed]
1. **Clarify the story:** Identify core audience, AAIF relevance, timeliness, practical value, and target publishing window.[^evt-public-agents-file-2aebb9feb4df-f97f79ed]
2. **Check eligibility:** Confirm contributor category, stakeholder approval path, and original unpublished status.[^evt-public-agents-file-2aebb9feb4df-f97f79ed]
3. **Shape the post:** Structure content into an engaging narrative rather than a marketing press release or product brief.[^evt-public-agents-file-2aebb9feb4df-f97f79ed]
4. **Enforce neutrality:** Strip promotional jargon, vendor-centric framing, comparative superiority claims, and member favoritism.[^evt-public-agents-file-2aebb9feb4df-f97f79ed]
5. **Strengthen utility:** Enrich draft with implementation details, architecture diagrams, concrete examples, and ecosystem context.[^evt-public-agents-file-2aebb9feb4df-f97f79ed]
6. **Prepare submission package:** Assemble title, author names, bios, headshot/logo assets, social amplification copy, hashtags, and target release date.[^evt-public-agents-file-2aebb9feb4df-f97f79ed]
7. **Set expectations:** Communicate that publication is contingent on review and requires approximately a two-week lead time.[^evt-public-agents-file-2aebb9feb4df-f97f79ed]

## Submission Package Checklist
The skill ensures every submission bundle contains verified artifacts before routing to the official intake form: complete draft (recommended 600–1,500 words), vendor neutrality verification, stakeholder approvals, and social amplification text.[^evt-public-agents-file-2aebb9feb4df-f97f79ed]

# Lifecycle History
Version 1.0 of the skill was authored by Angie Jones in `aaif/public-agents` to provide an automated operational counterpart to the foundation's editorial policy.[^evt-public-agents-file-2aebb9feb4df-f97f79ed] The installation command was subsequently referenced directly inside the primary AAIF repository guideline documentation.[^evt-foundation-pr-2]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Foundation Code of Conduct defines community standards, expected professional behaviors, and enforcement mechanisms across all foundation communication channels, working groups, technical repositories, and affiliated events.[^evt-foundation-pr-1]

All contributors, maintainers, and community delegates are required to adhere to these standards to maintain an inclusive, collaborative, and harassment-free environment.[^evt-foundation-pr-1]

# Architecture / Specification
## Standards and Enforcement
The policy defines unacceptable harassment and discriminatory behaviors across physical and digital spaces managed under the Linux Foundation umbrella. Violations are reported to foundation leadership and evaluated through standardized Linux Foundation community enforcement processes.[^evt-foundation-pr-1]

## Repository Compliance
The policy is anchored across AAIF repositories under the standard community health file path `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md` to support automated health detection by source code platforms and CI tooling.[^evt-foundation-pr-1]

# Lifecycle History
In PR#1 of `aaif/foundation`, the repository filename was standardized from `Code_of_Conduct.md` to `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md` to enable automated recognition by GitHub's community standards and repository health checklist.[^evt-foundation-pr-1]

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing open threat models, security architecture, containment patterns, and cross-group review checklists.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body tasked with establishing open threat models, security architecture benchmarks, containment patterns, and baseline security controls across autonomous agent lifecycles[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab]. The group develops reference threat assessments, coordinates security and privacy review standards across other foundation working groups, and collaborates with adjacent ecosystem standards bodies to foster coherent industry adoption[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].

# Architecture / Specification

## Active Workstreams and Deliverables
The working group organizes its technical outputs into sequenced deliverables managed across dedicated async coordination channels[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab]:
- **Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design**: The foundational near-term deliverable assessing existing frameworks to identify coverage gaps for agentic architectures[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab]. See also [../resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md](../resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md).
- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: A technical implementation catalog detailing concrete architectural patterns (such as execution hooks, checkpointing, and human-in-the-loop gates) alongside documented anti-patterns[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].
- **Agentic Security Best Practices Guide**: Advisory guidance paired with the design patterns catalog providing higher-level implementation principles and operational recommendations[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab]. See also [../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md).
- **Cross-Working Group Security and Privacy Review Checklist**: A portable checklist designed to be socialized across all foundation working groups to embed baseline security review into work products early in their lifecycle[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].
- **Taxonomy Contributions**: Formerly an internal workstream, unified agentic taxonomy was elevated to a cross-foundation initiative led under [../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md); the working group acts as a core contributor bringing its security and privacy domain definitions[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].

## Protocol Interoperability and Ecosystem Outreach
The working group actively investigates hook semantics and containment interfaces across distributed agent protocols:
- **Hook Standardization**: Coordinating with protocol efforts such as MCP Interceptors and the Model Context Protocol Access Control System (MCP ACS) initiative on generalized hook mechanisms and standardized protocol error signaling[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].
- **Industry Standards Outreach**: Engaging external security initiatives, including Vanta's Agent Security and Risk Management (AARM) standard and CISA publications, to align recommendations before engaging downstream model providers[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].

# Lifecycle History
Formal charter balloting for the working group migrated from GitHub to the Linux Foundation LFX platform in May 2026[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab]. Workstream operations follow a co-lead structure with decentralized task cadences feeding into regular all-hands status updates[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].

# Overview
The Identity and Trust Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body establishing vendor-neutral architectures, cryptographic delegation chains, authority models, and verification infrastructure for autonomous AI systems[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-1]. The group defines standards for machine identity attestation, credential delegation, and verifiable audit trails across multi-agent environments[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-1].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group's charter defines its operational scope around several core trust surfaces[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-1]:
- **Agent Identity & Attestation**: Cryptographic identification mechanisms and runtime attestation models confirming agent provenance and executable integrity.
- **Delegation and Authority**: Protocol primitives governing scoped, revocable task and credential delegation between human principals, supervisory agents, and autonomous subagents.
- **Interoperable Trust Fabrics**: Cross-platform verification standards enabling independent runtime boundaries to validate identity claims without proprietary vendor lock-in.

# Lifecycle History
The formal charter for the Identity and Trust Working Group was initialized and approved via pull request merge, establishing its foundational scope, governance rules, and deliverable targets[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-1].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Commerce Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing vendor-neutral capability models, protocol evaluations, and transaction standards for agentic commerce.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Commerce Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body establishing vendor-neutral capability models, protocol evaluations, and transaction standards for agent-executed transactions[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-1]. The group focuses on defining secure, interoperable architectures for product discovery, checkout negotiation, and delegated payment handling[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-1].

# Architecture / Specification
The group's operational charter defines the following primary domains of inquiry[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-1]:
- **Transaction Protocols**: Architectural requirements for deterministic agentic checkout and settlement workflows. See also [../taxonomy/agentic-checkout.md](../taxonomy/agentic-checkout.md).
- **Payment Delegation**: Authorization frameworks establishing human-in-the-loop controls and cryptographic proofs for automated purchasing decisions. See also [../taxonomy/delegated-payment.md](../taxonomy/delegated-payment.md).
- **Merchant and Agent Interfaces**: Standardized protocols connecting commercial inventory APIs, user agent preferences, and payment gateways.

# Lifecycle History
The initial draft charter establishing the working group's scope and governance was merged into the repository via PR #1[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-1].

# Overview
The Accuracy and Reliability Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical working group defining evaluation benchmarks, failure taxonomies, and testing methodologies for autonomous agents[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-1]. The group focuses on quantifying task completion fidelity, context drift, and non-deterministic regression across production agent deployments[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-1].

# Architecture / Specification
The group's charter establishes workstreams focused on the operational dependability of agent workflows[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-1]:
- **Evaluation Benchmarks**: Standardized test suites measuring agent decision-making accuracy under ambiguous or multi-step execution constraints. See also [../resources/accuracy-and-reliability-survey.md](../resources/accuracy-and-reliability-survey.md).
- **Failure Taxonomies**: Rigorous categorization of failure modes, including hallucinations, tool execution faults, and cascading subagent desynchronization.
- **Reliability Metrics**: Observable health signals and empirical scoring frameworks for validating agentic system stability in continuous integration and production environments.

# Lifecycle History
The working group's charter was formally initialized into the repository via pull request merge[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-1].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Ecosystem Architecture Map is an interactive, CNCF Landscape 2-powered market map and catalog categorizing agentic AI frameworks, protocols, runtimes, security guardrails, and open-source tooling across the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-50664ea2b31a-0cc09007]. Maintained across `aaif/ws-taxonomy-landscape` and `aaif/aaif-landscape` in collaboration with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md), the map provides structured navigation across agent runtimes, observability platforms, commerce rails, and regulatory standards.

The map categorizes ecosystem entries into distinct project tiers and groups, providing interactive filtering between member projects, foundation deliverables, and external open-source initiatives[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-50664ea2b31a-0cc09007][^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-14].

# Architecture / Specification

## Configuration and Deployment
The landscape is generated using the CNCF Landscape 2 engine (`cncf/landscape2`), configured through centralized settings[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-50664ea2b31a-0cc09007]:
- **Production Hosts**: Hosted dynamically at `https://aaif.landscape2.io` as well as deployed as a Next.js static export on GitHub Pages at `https://aaif.github.io/ws-taxonomy-landscape/landscape/`[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-50664ea2b31a-0cc09007][^evt-aaif-landscape-file-16e486445ce2-29580b00].
- **Palette**: Slate-based UI theme utilizing Slate 900 (`#0f172a`) as primary, Blue 500 (`#3b82f6`) as secondary, and Slate 800 (`#1e293b`) for navigation surfaces[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-50664ea2b31a-0cc09007].
- **Display Modes**: Supports grid card view and logos with embedded project descriptions[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-50664ea2b31a-0cc09007].

## Project Tiers and Watchlists
The map groups projects and foundation participants according to standardized tiers[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-50664ea2b31a-0cc09007][^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-14]:
- **Graduated** (`#00f5d4`): Mature open-source projects meeting high adoption and governance standards[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-50664ea2b31a-0cc09007].
- **Incubating** (`#9b5de5`): Developing projects establishing community governance and security audits[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-50664ea2b31a-0cc09007].
- **Member** (`#00b4d8`): Projects contributed or maintained by AAIF member organizations[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-50664ea2b31a-0cc09007][^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-14].
- **External** (`#f15bb5`): Ecosystem projects outside direct foundation governance[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-50664ea2b31a-0cc09007].
- **Agentic AI Project Watchlist**: A curated section tracking top agentic AI open-source projects, decoupled from foundation membership and synchronized with the LFX Insights Agentic AI Momentum Dashboard[^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-14].

## CI/CD Validation and Previews
Pull requests modifying `landscape.yml`, `settings.yml`, or `hosted_logos/*` trigger automated GitHub Actions workflows:
- **Validation**: Enforces structural schema conformance via `cncf/landscape2-validate-action@v2` targeting both data definitions and settings configuration[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-a5c0f08bc43f-3b9f2340].
- **Pull Request Preview**: Automatically comments on opened pull requests with an experimental preview link using `overlay-data`, `overlay-settings`, and `overlay-logos` query parameters against `https://aaif.landscape2.io`[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-16e486445ce2-29580b00].

# References
- [AAIF Landscape Repository](https://github.com/aaif/aaif-landscape)[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-a5c0f08bc43f-3b9f2340]
- [Taxonomy Landscape Repository](https://github.com/aaif/ws-taxonomy-landscape)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-50664ea2b31a-0cc09007]

proposed_concept.title: Working Group Idea Submission Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Operational guidelines governing proposal intake requirements, member eligibility restrictions, evaluation criteria, and review processes for new AAIF working groups.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Working Group Idea Submission Guidelines define the formal requirements, proposer eligibility rules, and evaluation criteria for proposing new Technical Working Groups within the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF)[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a]. Working Groups serve as the Foundation's primary mechanism for advancing domain-specific research, formulating technical standards, and authoring actionable operational guidance across the agentic AI ecosystem[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].

Proposals are formally restricted to AAIF member organizations in good standing; submissions received from outside Foundation membership are not reviewed[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].

# Architecture / Specification

## Eligibility
Submissions are accepted exclusively from Foundation Member organizations across any membership tier[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a]. Non-member organizations or individuals must collaborate with an existing member sponsor to advance a proposal into the intake pipeline[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].

## Submission Requirements
Prospective working group charters must address eight standard proposal sections[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a]:
1. **Submitter Information**: Proposer name, organizational affiliation, role, contact email, proposed leadership availability, and organization membership tier[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].
2. **Working Group Identity**: Clear working group title and a jargon-free one-sentence executive summary understandable to generalist reviewers[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].
3. **Problem Statement & Purpose**: Core challenge or gap addressed, specific relevance to agentic AI, and alignment with AAIF strategic priorities[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].
4. **Proposed Scope & Deliverables**: Boundaries of technical work and intended artifacts, such as technical reports, whitepapers, specifications, benchmarks, datasets, or policy guidance[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].
5. **Timeline & Structure**: Target delivery schedule, meeting cadence, and charter duration, with working groups typically operating on a 12–24 month charter cycle[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].
6. **Membership & Expertise**: Profile of required subject matter expertise and documented expressions of interest from collaborating individuals and member organizations[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].
7. **Impact & Urgency**: Assessment of ecosystem consequences, timeliness, and industry need[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].
8. **Resource Considerations**: Tooling, infrastructure, meeting administration, and repository hosting requirements[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].

## Review and Lifecycle Transition
Submitted proposals undergo structured evaluation against strategic alignment, feasibility, member support, and non-duplication with active working groups[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a]. Approved working group proposals transition into the lifecycle governance model governed by the [Working Group Lifecycle Policy](../policies/working-group-lifecycle-policy.md) and [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md).

# References
- [AAIF Working Group Proposals Repository](https://github.com/aaif/working-group-proposals)[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a]

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Commerce Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group cataloging and harmonizing open specifications, interoperability patterns, and delegated authority models across agentic commerce lifecycles.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic Commerce Working Group (AC WG) is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body chartered to catalog, align, and harmonize open specifications, frameworks, and terminology for commerce workflows conducted by AI agents on behalf of individuals, enterprises, and software services.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be] Rather than authoring competing commerce protocol standards, the working group maintains protocol neutrality, synthesizes common interfaces across existing market proposals, and delivers architectural guidance and recommendations to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md).[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be]

Approved on May 15, 2026, the working group is co-chaired by Ilya Grigorik and Rahul Bansal, operating through the `aaif/wg-agentic-commerce` repository.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be]

# Architecture / Specification

### Scoping Boundaries

The working group focuses strictly on interfaces, signals, and interoperability patterns between agentic orchestration layers and external commercial infrastructure, explicitly excluding the internal mechanics of underlying payment rails, fraud engines, and identity backends.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be]

- **In Scope**:
  - Discovery and negotiation interfaces between agents and merchants concerning inventory, terms, and fulfillment.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be]
  - Cart composition, validation, and handoff models supporting [agentic checkout](../taxonomy/agentic-checkout.md).[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be]
  - Identity, authority scoping, and consent signaling in active collaboration with the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md).[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be]
  - [Delegated payment](../taxonomy/delegated-payment.md) interfaces spanning wallets and payment networks (cards, real-time rails, and distributed ledgers) for intent, authorization, and settlement signals.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be]
  - Risk-posture signaling exchanged with external fraud detection platforms.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be]
  - Autonomy boundaries, human escalation triggers, and post-purchase claim/chargeback signaling interfaces.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be]
- **Out of Scope**:
  - Operational settlement mechanics, payment rail clearing, and proprietary merchant marketplace implementations.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be]
  - Fraud detection or mitigation algorithm design.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be]
  - Consumer UI, Point of Sale (PoS) terminal hardware, and foundational responsible AI societal policies.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be]

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-05-15**: Working group charter formally approved by foundation leadership with Ilya Grigorik and Rahul Bansal designated as chairs.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be]

proposed_concept.title: Project Lifecycle Policy
proposed_concept.description: Governance policy defining intake submission criteria, annual review processes, and stage progression across Growth, Impact, and Emeritus project tiers.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Foundation Project Lifecycle Policy sets forth the formal governance framework through which open-source technical projects are proposed, evaluated, admitted, and advanced across maturity stages within the foundation.[^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171] Effective March 18, 2026, the policy applies uniformly to pre-existing open-source initiatives seeking entry and newly created projects originating inside the AAIF.[^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171]

Progression across lifecycle stages is overseen by the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) through standardized review workflows and an annual review process that benchmarks adoption, governance maturity, and alignment with foundation objectives.[^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171]

# Architecture / Specification

### Proposal Submission Requirements

Proposals enter through the centralized `aaif/project-proposals` repository following the [Project Proposal Process](../policies/project-proposal-process.md).[^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171] Submissions mandate documentation of:
- Project identity, mission alignment, origin history, and concrete adoption use cases.[^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171]
- Identification of a Technical Committee sponsor, where available, to provide governance mentorship.[^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171]
- Release under an OSI-approved permissive open-source license, public repository hosting, and automated validation/release pipelines.[^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171]
- Formal contribution workflows, public issue tracking, documented third-party dependencies, and dependency licenses.[^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171]
- Core maintainer identities, leadership decision-making procedures, documented governance practices (`GOVERNANCE.md`), official communication channels, financial sponsorships, and requested foundation infrastructure support.[^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171]

### Lifecycle Stages

The policy categorizes project progression across distinct tiers:[^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171]
1. **Growth Stage**: Maturing projects establishing multi-organizational contribution, stable release mechanics, and growing production adoption.[^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171]
2. **Impact Stage**: Established, mission-critical foundation projects exhibiting widespread production deployment, diverse maintainer governance, and high operational reliability.[^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171]
3. **Emeritus Stage**: Projects that are no longer actively maintained, have reached end-of-life status, or show minimal maintenance activity, preserved in archival status.[^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171][^evt-project-proposals-pr-30]

### Annual Review Process

Project status, community health, and stage progression requests undergo evaluation through an Annual Review Process conducted by the Technical Committee to ensure continuous alignment with foundation standards.[^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171]

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-03-18**: Project Lifecycle Policy becomes formally effective across AAIF repositories.[^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171]
- **2026-05**: Editorial cleanup of duplicate phrasing and template syntax merged in PR #30.[^evt-project-proposals-pr-30]
