proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing open threat models, security architecture, containment patterns, and vulnerability review checklists.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body chartered to establish open threat modeling frameworks, actionable security controls, defense-in-depth runtime architectures, and cross-cutting security evaluation checklists for autonomous agents.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9] Led by Alex Frazer, the group coordinates security baselines across foundation initiatives and aligns runtime safety expectations with external risk standards.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9]

Following formal charter approval in May 2026, the working group restructured volunteer staffing into self-selecting workstream squads and established collaborative ties with cross-cutting taxonomy efforts.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9]

# Architecture / Specification

### Active Deliverables and Workstreams

The working group organizes its technical output into five primary tracks:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9]

1. **Agentic Security Best Practices Guide**: High-interest workstream detailing actionable security controls and execution boundaries documented in [Agentic AI Security Best Practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9]
2. **Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design**: Structured threat modeling framework assessing gaps across OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, and NIST AI RMF, detailed in [Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis](../resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9]
3. **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Architectural catalog standardizing security boundaries, sandbox isolation, and runtime verification patterns.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9]
4. **Cross-Working Group Security and Privacy Review Checklist**: Reusable audit instrument applied across other AAIF working group proposals and runtime reference architectures.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9]
5. **Taxonomy and Landscape Coordination**: Security and privacy mapping into the unified foundation taxonomy in partnership with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md), co-chaired by Junjie Bu.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9]

### Operational Governance

Workstream leadership utilizes a decentralized model where contributors within dedicated channels self-select leads and co-leads tasked with facilitating discussions, coordinating status updates, and delegating draft authoring.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9] Target deliverable deadlines were adjusted back by approximately one month in late May 2026 to account for initial charter approval timelines.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9]

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-05-26**: Formal working group charter approval confirmed; Junjie Bu appointed co-chair of cross-WG Taxonomy workstream and chair of Landscape workstream; deliverable timelines extended by one month.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9]

proposed_concept.title: Project Proposal Process
proposed_concept.description: Operating procedure, review lifecycle, voting thresholds, and issue triage labels for open-source projects applying to join the Agentic AI Foundation.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Project Proposal Process defines the official intake path, review lifecycle, and voting requirements for open-source software projects seeking foundation-hosted status within the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) [^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6]. Managed under the oversight of the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md), the process guides candidate projects through formal submission, technical presentations, classification into either Growth or Impact stages under the [Project Lifecycle Policy](../policies/project-lifecycle-policy.md), and final Governing Board approval [^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].

# Architecture / Specification

## Application Submission and Triage
Applicants prepare their proposal in accordance with published submission guidance and lifecycle criteria before opening a proposal issue [^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6][^evt-project-proposals-pr-35]:
1. Review the Foundation's [Project Lifecycle Policy](../policies/project-lifecycle-policy.md) to confirm eligibility.
2. Review the public guidance documenting submission expectations and benefits [^evt-project-proposals-pr-35].
3. File a standardized issue via the Foundation's proposal template (`project-proposal.yml`) in the `aaif/project-proposals` repository [^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].
4. Submissions enter the triage queue on the Foundation's public Project Proposals tracking board [^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].

## Review Lifecycle and Classification
Once triaged, projects undergo a structured review track [^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6]:
- **Presentation Preparation**: Maintainers collaborate with AAIF staff to draft a technical review presentation [^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].
- **Technical Committee Review**: The project presents during a scheduled Technical Committee meeting, where technical scope, community health, and architectural alignment are assessed [^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].
- **Classification**: The Technical Committee classifies qualifying projects into either the **Growth** or **Impact** maturity tier [^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].

## Voting Thresholds and Approval
- **Technical Committee Approval**: Acceptance requires an absolute majority vote (>50%) across all voting members of the Technical Committee [^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].
- **Governing Board Referral**: Upon receiving majority TC approval, the proposal is referred to the AAIF Governing Board for final administrative approval [^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].

## Status Labels
The project tracking board classifies proposal lifecycle states using standardized issue labels [^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6]:
- `New`: The application has entered the backlog and awaits formal triage.
- `Waiting on Comment`: Additional technical clarification or operational details have been requested from maintainers.
- `Approved`: The application has satisfied all requirements and is accepted into the foundation-hosted structure.
- `Declined`: The proposal was reviewed and rejected, with feedback recorded in issue comments.
- `Too Early`: The project is not yet sufficiently mature; reviewers supply specific milestones required before reapplication.

## Reapplication Rules and Membership Decoupling
- **Reapplication Waiting Period**: Projects that are declined or marked too early may reapply as soon as three months after the vote, provided tangible progress has addressed previous TC feedback [^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].
- **Membership Decoupling**: Project hosting is open to the global open-source community. Submitting organizations are not required to hold corporate membership in the AAIF, and acceptance into the Foundation does not confer corporate membership status (such as Silver, Gold, or Platinum) or a seat on the Governing Board [^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Landscape
proposed_concept.description: Interactive market map and catalog categorizing agent runtimes, protocols, security guardrails, telemetry, commerce, governance, and evaluation harnesses across AAIF working groups.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Landscape is an open ecosystem directory and interactive market map maintained by the [Taxonomy & Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) to structure, classify, and track open-source and commercial technologies across the autonomous AI agent domain [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8]. The landscape maps projects directly to technical domains governed by AAIF working groups, providing clear taxonomy boundaries and distinguishing foundation-hosted, member, and external technologies [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8].

# Architecture / Specification

## Category Alignment Matrix
The landscape data architecture structures agentic technologies across seven primary categories aligned with AAIF working groups [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8]:

1. **Agent Runtimes, Frameworks & Workflow Orchestration**: Autonomous agent frameworks (e.g., AutoGen, CrewAI, OpenHands, ADK) and cyclical orchestration runtimes (e.g., LangChain, LlamaIndex, LangGraph, Diagrid Dapr), aligned with the [Workflows & Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) and [Accuracy & Reliability Working Group](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md) [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8].
2. **Protocols & Discovery Registries**: Interoperability standards, communication layers, and capability directories, aligned with the [Identity & Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8].
3. **Security Guardrails & Firewalls**: Runtime boundary enforcement, prompt shields, containment sandboxes, and policy gateways, aligned with the [Security & Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8].
4. **Observability & Tracing Telemetry**: Cross-boundary execution tracing, context propagation, and runtime inspection platforms, aligned with the [Observability & Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8].
5. **Agentic Commerce & Wallets**: Agent-driven checkout protocols, delegated transaction authorization, and cryptographic wallets, aligned with the [Agentic Commerce Working Group](../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md) [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8].
6. **Global Governance & Regulatory Regimes**: Compliance tools, policy audit matrices, and legal-risk containment frameworks, aligned with the [Governance, Risk & Regulatory Working Group](../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md) [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8].
7. **Agent Evaluation & Benchmarking Harnesses**: Deterministic eval suites, failure benchmarks, and harness runners, aligned with the [Accuracy & Reliability Working Group](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md) [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8].

## Entry Metadata Schema
Each item listed in `landscape.yml` adheres to a uniform YAML schema capturing project identity and community affiliation [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8]:
- `name`: Human-readable title of the project or framework.
- `logo`: Vector or raster image asset filename.
- `homepage_url`: Canonical public URL for documentation and website.
- `repo_url`: Source code repository URL.
- `description`: Single-paragraph summary of capabilities and purpose.
- `project`: Affiliation designation classifying the entry as `member` or `external` [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8].

proposed_concept.title: Working Group Reporting Template
proposed_concept.description: Standardized monthly reporting template, pull request workflow, review timelines, and required metadata for AAIF working groups reporting to the Technical Committee.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Working Group Reporting Template defines the standard file format, submission cadence, and review workflow through which AAIF working groups and cross-cutting workstreams report monthly status asynchronously to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md)[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-9677055e316b-93d6f75a][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-9677055e316b-9ddc8f32].

# Architecture / Specification

## Submission and Review Workflow

Working group reports follow a structured submission lifecycle[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e]:
1. **Path convention**: The template file (`reporting/TEMPLATE.md`) is copied to `reporting/YYYY-MM-report.md` (e.g., `reporting/2026-06-report.md`).
2. **Pull request format**: A pull request is submitted to the working group repository with the title `[Report] <WG name> – <Month YYYY>`.
3. **Reviewers**: The Technical Committee (or designated TC GitHub team) is assigned as reviewers.
4. **Deadlines**: Reports are due by the last business day of the reporting month.
5. **Review window**: The TC review window closes 7 calendar days after submission.
6. **Merging**: The report PR is merged once the TC signs off or the 7-day review window elapses, whichever comes first.

## Required Metadata and Sections

Each report includes mandatory front-matter metadata and six content sections[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-9677055e316b-93d6f75a]:
- **Header Metadata**: Working Group name, reporting period (`Month YYYY`), Chair(s) with organizational affiliation, and date submitted (`YYYY-MM-DD`).
- **Summary**: Two to three concise sentences capturing the month at a glance.
- **Progress Against Objectives**: Deliverables shipped and objectives advanced during the cycle.
- **Blockers and Risks**: Current impediment notices for TC awareness, or explicitly marked `None this month`.
- **Decisions Needed from the TC**: Specific actionable decisions requested for TC response, or `None`.
- **Next Month's Focus**: Top 2–3 priorities planned for the upcoming cycle.
- **Metrics / Links**: References to merged pull requests, tracked issues, releases, meeting notes, or project dashboards.

# Lifecycle History

Adopted across foundation repositories in June 2026, replacing synchronous verbal reporting with asynchronous, publicly auditable GitHub pull request reviews[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-9677055e316b-93d6f75a][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-9677055e316b-9ddc8f32].

mutations.rationale: Document standardized monthly reporting cadence, pull request review window, and adoption across multiple AAIF working groups based on merged templates.

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Working Group Reporting Template standardizes monthly asynchronous status reporting from Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) working groups to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md)[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-9677055e316b-2e851e23]. It establishes a uniform pull request workflow, standard review timelines, and concise section formatting designed for rapid asynchronous review[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-9677055e316b-dc950981].

# Architecture / Specification
Working groups instantiate the reporting template under `reporting/YYYY-MM-report.md` within their repositories and open a pull request titled `[Report] <WG name> – <Month YYYY>`[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-9677055e316b-2e851e23].

## Submission and Review Timeline
- **Submission Deadline**: Reports are due by the final business day of the reporting month[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-9677055e316b-188b9d10].
- **Reviewers**: The Technical Committee (or designated TC GitHub team) must be assigned as pull request reviewers[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-9677055e316b-9220099f].
- **Review Window**: The TC review window closes seven calendar days following submission[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-9677055e316b-2e851e23].
- **Merge Condition**: Reports are merged upon explicit TC sign-off or when the seven-day review window closes, whichever occurs first[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-9677055e316b-dc950981].

## Report Structure
Reports must contain the following standardized sections:
1. **Header Metadata**: Working group name, reporting period, chair names with organizational affiliations, and date submitted[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-9677055e316b-2e851e23].
2. **Summary**: Two to three sentences summarizing the month at a glance[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-9677055e316b-188b9d10].
3. **Progress Against Objectives**: Concrete milestones shipped or advanced, mapped back to charter objectives[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-9677055e316b-9220099f].
4. **Blockers and Risks**: Operational or technical impediments requiring TC awareness[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-9677055e316b-dc950981].
5. **Decisions Needed from the TC**: Explicit, actionable requests requiring formal TC determination[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-9677055e316b-2e851e23].
6. **Next Month's Focus**: Top two to three working group priorities for the upcoming cycle[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-9677055e316b-188b9d10].
7. **Metrics / Links**: Relevant pull requests, issues, releases, dashboards, or meeting notes[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-9677055e316b-9220099f].

# Lifecycle History
The reporting template has been authoritatively adopted across multiple AAIF working groups, including [WG Identity & Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md)[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-9677055e316b-2e851e23], [WG Agentic Commerce](../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md)[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-9677055e316b-dc950981], [WG Accuracy & Reliability](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md)[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-9677055e316b-188b9d10], and [WG Workflows & Process Integration](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-9677055e316b-9220099f].

# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body establishing open threat taxonomies, runtime defense patterns, execution boundaries, and privacy safeguards for autonomous agents[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a54ff182c7e8-57e8a423]. Its scope covers threat modeling, design patterns such as human-in-the-loop controls, and security practices across agent lifecycles[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-6].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its technical work and deliverables across structured repository directories governed by dedicated agent instructions[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a54ff182c7e8-57e8a423].

## Repository Structure and Governance
- `charter/`: Contains working group governance documents, with the charter maintained in `charter/DRAFT.md` until formally approved by working group consensus[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a54ff182c7e8-57e8a423].
- `deliverables/`: Houses published deliverables and threat taxonomies, including active draft taxonomies and design patterns[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a54ff182c7e8-57e8a423][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-6].
- `meeting-notes/`: Records working group meeting agendas, attendance, and decision summaries[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a54ff182c7e8-57e8a423].
- **Subdirectory Instructions**: Folders such as `deliverables/` and `meeting-notes/` maintain folder-level `AGENTS.md` instruction files defining localized workflow and naming rules[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a54ff182c7e8-57e8a423].

## Style and Operational Conventions
- **Syntax**: Markdown documents adhere to CommonMark with ATX-style headers (`#`, `##`) and ISO dates (`YYYY-MM-DD`)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a54ff182c7e8-57e8a423].
- **Tone and Voice**: Operational guidelines prohibit contrastive phrasing, horizontal-rule line breaks, and partial sentence clauses, mandating a neutral, professional, and direct voice[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a54ff182c7e8-57e8a423].
- **Participation**: While working group meetings require member organization affiliation, external contributors propose technical bridges through public issues and pull requests, such as mappings to the OWASP Agentic Systems Incidents (ASI) catalog and static analysis practices[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-6].

# References
- Security and Privacy Working Group agent repository instructions[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a54ff182c7e8-57e8a423].
- Non-member contribution offer and threat taxonomy gap analysis[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-6].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group (SP WG) establishes open threat modeling frameworks, security design patterns, and runtime containment guidelines for autonomous agentic AI deployments [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-6a261a55][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-9c4ed1d4]. It analyzes threat boundaries specific to agentic workflows—such as multi-agent persuasion, tool invocation misuse, delegated authority leakage, and prompt supply-chain integrity—and curates reusable architectural mitigations [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-6a261a55][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-9c4ed1d4].

The working group feeds its analytical findings into concrete reference designs such as [Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis](../resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md), [Agentic AI Security Best Practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md), and related architectural patterns.

# Architecture / Specification

### Workstreams and Leadership

The working group organizes its technical agenda across targeted workstreams:

1. **Threat Modeling**: Evaluates established frameworks (such as CSA MAESTRO, OWASP, and NIST AI RMF) to identify gaps unique to agentic architectures, including tool manifest verification and delegated authorization boundaries [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-6a261a55]. Led by Alon Mazor (Ocean Security) and Fernando Lucktemberg (SAP) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-6a261a55].
2. **Design Patterns Catalog**: Curates reusable patterns structured around problem, context, solution, trade-offs, and anti-patterns [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-9c4ed1d4]. Key topic areas include hooks and checkpointing, human-in-the-loop patterns, privacy-preserving execution (such as TEEs and zero-knowledge proofs), blast radius containment, secure memory retention, and agent containment intervention mechanisms (such as [kill switches](../patterns/kill-switch.md), permission downgrades, and rollback controls) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-9c4ed1d4]. Led by Dan Kommatas (Circle) and Sagar Dashora (JPMorgan Chase) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-9c4ed1d4].
3. **Taxonomy and Landscape Delegation**: Formerly an internal workstream, taxonomy efforts have transitioned into the cross-WG [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](taxonomy-and-landscape.md) chaired by Junjie Bu [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-84f82d5fdbae-3ec725c7]. Security and Privacy is represented by official delegates Jay White (Microsoft) and Katherine Druckman (JetBrains) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-84f82d5fdbae-3ec725c7].

### Deliverable Lifecycle and Governance

The working group enforces strict deliverable lifecycle states [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-7a84413abf98-945bcd5d]:

- **Draft**: Work in progress prefixed with `DRAFT-` in file naming [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-7a84413abf98-945bcd5d].
- **Final**: Deliverables that have achieved formal approval recorded in the **Decisions** section of an authoritative meeting notes document (`YYYY-MM-DD.md`) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-7a84413abf98-945bcd5d]. Files drop the `DRAFT-` prefix upon final approval [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-7a84413abf98-945bcd5d].
- **Moved**: Workstreams or deliverables transitioned to foundation-wide or external repositories (such as `Taxonomy of Terms and Definitions` moving to `aaif/ws-taxonomy-landscape`) retain a redirect stub preserving existing links and documenting ongoing WG involvement [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-7a84413abf98-945bcd5d][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a9e41c531556-8d5cff93].

Meeting administration requires canonical notes files capturing AI summaries, transcripts, topics discussed, formal decisions, deliverables, and assigned action item owners [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-eb9c68e792e7-3538ca31].

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group defining threat models, reusable security patterns, runtime containment controls, and cross-group review checklists across the AAIF.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group (SP WG) defines threat models, reusable design patterns, runtime containment controls, and security assessment checklists across the Agentic AI Foundation ecosystem. It operates as an intersecting architectural layer across AAIF initiatives, reviewing deliverables from peer technical working groups and producing actionable builder guidance.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b0dad759cb11-f74bdc54]

# Architecture / Specification

## Formalized Workstreams

The working group organizes its technical outputs into five dedicated workstreams, each structured under repository-level ownership with designated leads and contributor rosters:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]

1. **Threat Modeling** (`threat-modeling/`): Conducts gap analyses of established AI risk frameworks (OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, CSA MAESTRO, and NIST AI RMF) against agentic-specific threat surfaces such as memory poisoning, multi-agent persuasion, excessive agency, and delegated authorization failures.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9] Co-led by Alon Mazor and Fernando Lucktemberg.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]
2. **Design Patterns Catalog** (`design-patterns/`): Authors reusable security and privacy patterns documented under standard problem, context, solution, and trade-offs formats.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5] Co-led by Dan Kommatas and Sagar Dashora.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]
3. **Best Practices Guide** (`best-practices/`): Provides operational guidance for agent system builders, spanning secrets management, secure tool invocation, guardrails, and post-incident forensics.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-f8906e55] Co-led by Fernando Lucktemberg and Matthew Khouzam.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-f8906e55]
4. **Cross-WG Review Checklist** (`review-checklist/`): Operates a lightweight security and privacy review process evaluating external working group specifications.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b0dad759cb11-f74bdc54] Led by Govindaraj Palanisamy.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b0dad759cb11-f74bdc54]
5. **Taxonomy and Landscape** (`taxonomy/`): Elevated original WG definitions into the foundation-wide [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86] Represented by appointed delegates Jay White and Katherine Druckman.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86]

## Governance and Operations

- **System of Record**: The working group uses public GitHub repositories as its authoritative system of record for maturing and finalized deliverables, maintaining strict contributor attribution and change tracking.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]
- **Technical Committee Interface**: Progress updates are reported monthly to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) using a standardized report template, triggering a seven-day review and question acknowledgment window.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]
- **Cross-Group Liaison**: The working group coordinates review checkpoints with the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md), [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), and [Agentic Commerce Working Group](../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b0dad759cb11-f74bdc54]

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-05-12**: Elevated original working group taxonomy work to cross-foundation initiative.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86]
- **2026-06-09**: Appointed formal delegates to the cross-WG Taxonomy workstream.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86]
- **2026-06-23**: Public repository transition announced, formal workstream directory structure committed, and monthly TC update workflow adopted.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide
proposed_concept.description: Practical implementation guidance and external framework mappings for builders of secure autonomous agent systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide provides practical, actionable architectural guidance for engineers designing and deploying agentic systems.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-f8906e55] Maintained by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), the guide complements granular pattern specifications by addressing high-level design choices ("if you want to do X, here is what you should do") and curating external industry benchmarks rather than re-deriving existing standards.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-f8906e55]

# Architecture / Specification

## Scope and Core Topic Areas

The guide spans six primary operational domains:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-f8906e55]

1. **Secrets Management**: Safe resolution, ephemeral provisioning, and credential isolation preventing tool-level leakage or subagent exposure.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-f8906e55]
2. **Secure Tool Invocation**: Enforcing deterministic policy engines, schema validation, and parameter sanitization between agent execution plans and tool interfaces.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-f8906e55][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]
3. **Guardrails**: Architecting verifiable, non-AI-modifiable boundary controls and hard constraints to mitigate prompt injection and unauthorized privilege escalation.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-f8906e55][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]
4. **Evaluation Frameworks**: Standardized testing suites assessing model resilience against prompt injection, jailbreaking, and goal hijacking.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-f8906e55]
5. **Post-Incident Forensics**: Preserving tamper-evident traces and interaction histories for root-cause analysis after behavioral or security failures.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-f8906e55]
6. **Curated Reference Frameworks**: Explicit integration mappings pointing builders toward verified external standards (e.g., OWASP, NIST AI RMF, MITRE ATLAS).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-f8906e55]

## Workstream Leadership

The guide is developed within the Security and Privacy Working Group under co-leads Fernando Lucktemberg (SAP) and Matthew Khouzam (Ericsson).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-f8906e55]

# Overview

The Cross-WG Security and Privacy Review Checklist defines a lightweight, repeatable evaluation process for reviewing AAIF technical deliverables through an adversarial security and privacy lens.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b0dad759cb11-f74bdc54] Maintained by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), this review mechanism operationalizes the working group's mandate as an intersecting architectural verification layer across the foundation.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b0dad759cb11-f74bdc54]

# Architecture / Specification

## Priority Review Targets

The checklist establishes baseline security review criteria targeted at early deliverable domains:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b0dad759cb11-f74bdc54]

- **[Identity and Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md)**: Reviewing cryptographic agent identity formats, delegation chains, authority attenuation, and revocation mechanisms.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b0dad759cb11-f74bdc54]
- **[Observability and Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md)**: Evaluating behavioral anomaly detection patterns, audit log immutability, telemetry sanitization, and PII redaction across spans.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b0dad759cb11-f74bdc54]
- **[Agentic Commerce](../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md)**: Inspecting transaction guardrails to prevent fund draining, account credential leakage, unconstrained checkout execution, and out-of-scope payment agent delegation.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b0dad759cb11-f74bdc54]
- **Cross-Foundation Deliverables**: General evaluation of newly emerging runtime, pattern, and framework proposals prior to graduation.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b0dad759cb11-f74bdc54]

## Ownership and Cadence

The review checklist workstream is led by Govindaraj Palanisamy (Global Payments) with active participation from industry security contributors across financial services, cloud infrastructure, and enterprise software.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b0dad759cb11-f74bdc54][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing vendor-neutral agent telemetry standards, cross-boundary trace correlation, and observable execution plane models.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability and Traceability Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body chartered to define open specifications, semantic conventions, and reference architectures for capturing multi-agent execution telemetry across heterogeneous infrastructure.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4]

Its technical agenda includes modeling agent execution boundaries, defining structured trace correlation across protocols like Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Agent-to-Agent (A2A), and formulating the [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-12]

# Architecture / Specification

### Operational Workstreams and Focus Groups

The working group organizes technical evaluation and landscape surveys across four specialized focus groups:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4]

1. **LLM Primitives**: Investigates foundation model invocation telemetry, prompt/response metadata, token utilization, and runtime auditing formats.
2. **Agent State and Context**: Explores runtime working memory retention, context compaction, state transitions, and memory graph persistence.
3. **Orchestration and Coordination**: Analyzes multi-agent topologies, fan-out/join synchronization, subagent delegation, and task scheduling.
4. **Agentic Reasoning**: Evaluates plan generation, intermediate chain-of-thought representations, reflection loops, and internal verification checks.

### Taxonomy and Conceptual Planes

The working group maintains an observability taxonomy mapping core concepts across four observable planes:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-10]
- **Orchestration Plane**: Workflow sequencing, subtask routing, and boundary lifecycle events.
- **Execution Plane**: Direct tool calls, operating system subprocesses, and environment mutations.
- **Protocol Plane**: Transport-level message interchange across MCP, A2A, and REST/gRPC gateways.
- **Reasoning and Context Plane**: Intent synthesis, context assembly, and prompt-context exhaustion boundaries.

These planes map directly to the dimensions of the [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md) while maintaining strict alignment guardrails with [OpenTelemetry](../resources/opentelemetry.md) semantic conventions.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-10]

# Lifecycle History

In June 2026, the working group published its GitHub repository for open tracking, scheduled bi-weekly community presentations, and initiated formal planning for its 12-month Agent Behavior Trace Model recommendation.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4] Workstream milestones include crosswalk coordination with the central [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](taxonomy-and-landscape.md) and evaluating potential synergies with the [Agentic Resource Discovery](../standards/agentic-resource-discovery.md) specification.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-10]

mutations.rationale: Document the taxonomy plane crosswalk, three-dimensional trace model mapping, and formal standard recommendation decision framework.

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Standardized telemetry context and correlation framework capturing causal relationships, execution structure, reasoning, and operational outcomes across agent workflows.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open telemetry framework proposed within the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) to record the operational, cognitive, and communicative behaviors of autonomous agents across distributed systems.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-10]

Unlike traditional distributed tracing systems focused solely on network call graphs and latency spans, the model captures causal relationships between model planning, contextual inputs, external tool invocations, and environmental outcomes.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-10][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-12]

# Architecture / Specification

### Trace Model Dimensions

The specification structures agent telemetry along three primary analytical dimensions:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-10]

1. **Execution Structure**: Traces the hierarchical and temporal arrangement of workflow primitives, agent-to-agent delegations, tool calls, and fan-out orchestrations.
2. **Reasoning and Planning**: Records intent formulation, intermediate deliberation steps, hypothesis scoring, and dynamic plan alterations prior to action execution.
3. **Outcomes and Effects**: Captures environmental state changes, user-facing output payloads, external system mutations, and error or convergence classifications.

### Taxonomy Crosswalk and OpenTelemetry Alignment

The trace model maps against the working group's four conceptual observability planes:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-10]
- **Orchestration Plane** correlates with *Execution Structure*.
- **Protocol Plane** and **Execution Plane** provide concrete transport and tool spans feeding both *Execution Structure* and *Outcomes and Effects*.
- **Reasoning/Context Plane** maps to *Reasoning and Planning*.

To prevent ecosystem fragmentation, the model adheres to strict [OpenTelemetry](../resources/opentelemetry.md) alignment guardrails, ensuring that standard attributes (such as OTel `gen_ai` semantic conventions) are extended rather than duplicated or replaced.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-10]

# Lifecycle History

The working group's charter establishes a 12-month evaluation framework to determine the long-term path for the Agent Behavior Trace Model.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-12] Grounded in landscape surveys and gap analyses, the decision process evaluates three prospective paths: adopting an existing industry standard, extending an ongoing upstream specification (such as OpenTelemetry), or producing a net-new AAIF specification only if structural gaps demonstrate its necessity.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-12]

proposed_concept.description: Open-source traffic mediation and policy enforcement proxy managing MCP and A2A communications as an AAIF member project.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

`agentgateway` is an open-source traffic mediation proxy and policy enforcement layer designed to govern Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Agent-to-Agent (A2A) communications between autonomous clients, tools, and remote agents.[^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-17]

It sits at the boundary between orchestration engines and downstream services, providing centralized authentication, granular tool authorization, rate limiting, and structured audit telemetry.[^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-17]

# Architecture / Specification

The proxy mediates communication across multiple protocol surfaces:
- **MCP Routing and Policy**: Filters and routes tool invocations, enforcing schema validation and parameter redaction prior to tool execution.
- **A2A Coordination**: Secures direct agent-to-agent exchanges and delegation chains.
- **Observability Ingestion**: Emits structured telemetry records compatible with cross-boundary trace models and standardized gateways.

# Lifecycle History

`agentgateway` was accepted into the Agentic AI Foundation landscape as an active member project to support reference gateway implementations for agent protocols.[^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-17]

proposed_concept.title: Accuracy and Reliability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing benchmarks, failure taxonomies, recovery specifications, and architectural patterns for dependable agent execution.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Accuracy and Reliability Working Group (ARWG) is a technical initiative within the Agentic AI Foundation chartered to formulate benchmarks, failure classification schemas, and engineering practices for non-deterministic AI agent deployments [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44]. Chaired by Jordan Augé (Cisco) and formally approved in May 2026, the working group targets the visibility and quality gaps inherent in complex agent workflows by standardizing proactive reliability controls, detection mechanisms, and remediation blueprints [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44].

# Architecture / Specification

### Strategic Objectives and Guiding Principles

The ARWG operates according to four strategic imperatives [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44]:
- **Shared Understanding:** Establish shared vocabularies and failure taxonomies across autonomous multi-agent lifecycles.
- **Measurement and Detection:** Supply reference measurement methodologies to quantify output reliability, drift, and functional degradation.
- **Correction Patterns:** Formalize corrective pathways spanning autonomous retry routines, architectural resilience, and mandatory human interventions.
- **Design Guidance:** Formulate reference architectures embedding accuracy controls as first-class constraints.

These objectives are guided by four foundational tenets: reliability and accuracy by design, evidence-grounded prescriptions, strict vendor and runtime neutrality, and transparency as a prerequisite for verification [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44].

### Technical Scope

The working group bounds its responsibilities across three in-scope pillars [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44]:
1. **Evaluation Frameworks:** Metrics, failure mode definitions, and quality thresholds for validating agent reasoning and decision consistency.
2. **Reliable Architecture Patterns:** Proactive structural invariants, including authoritative grounding and verification loops, complementing patterns like [../patterns/bounded-convergence-loop.md](../patterns/bounded-convergence-loop.md).
3. **Recovery and Corrective Actions:** Formal interfaces for rollback, safe-state restoration, automated compensation, and human handoff gates.

Explicitly out of scope are foundation model pre-training, fine-tuning, prompt engineering, commercial guardrail product development, and domain-specific regulatory policy. Additionally, log and trace emission formats are explicitly delegated to [../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), with ARWG restricting its domain to defining the required observable semantic signals [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44].

### Operational Dependencies and Assumptions

The working group relies on four external runtime assumptions [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44]:
- **Operational Predictability:** Agent runtimes implement standardized execution hooks for trajectory tracking and state recovery.
- **Immutable Identity:** Systems provide verifiable, immutable identification across agent instances and deployment versions.
- **Reproducible Versioning:** Model weights, system instructions, and tool schemas remain frozen and version-pinned during evaluation cycles.
- **Authoritative Trust Anchors:** Critical execution domains maintain external systems of record against which agent actions can be decisively reconciled.

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-05-15:** Working group charter formally approved under the Technical Committee [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44].
- **2026-06-30:** Charter revisions finalized, standardizing deliverable milestones to canonical deliverables D1 through D6 alongside internal deliverable I1 [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-6].

proposed_concept.title: Accuracy and Reliability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing failure taxonomies, evaluation benchmarks, and recovery specifications across enterprise agent deployments.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Accuracy and Reliability Working Group (ARWG) is an AAIF technical body tasked with standardizing terminology, failure taxonomies, enterprise requirement baselines, and evaluation protocols for autonomous agents.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1] Approved under full charter on May 15, 2026, the group operates across theoretical vocabulary structuring and applied production gap analysis to deliver rigorous reliability benchmarks.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1]

# Architecture / Specification

## Leadership and Meeting Cadence
The working group is co-chaired by Jordan Augé (Cisco) and Casper Nielsen (Diagrid).[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1] Operational work follows a biweekly alternating rhythm:
- Main plenary syncs held every two weeks.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1]
- Dedicated deliverable working sessions alternating with plenary meetings to advance deliverable authoring without spinning off siloed focus groups.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1]

## Core Deliverables
The working group executes across three primary deliverable tracks:
- **D1 (ARWG Taxonomy):** Architectural framing of terminology covering evaluation subjects, output quality, reliability dimensions, observability, attribution, grounding, symptoms, root causes, evaluation ecosystems, and correction mechanisms.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1]
- **D2 (Enterprise Gap Analysis):** Applied evidence report led by Sanjeev Suresh focusing on B2B enterprise personas (product managers, operations/deployment engineers, evaluators, and data scientists) to document production requirements, benchmark limitations, and tooling interoperability gaps.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1]
- **D6 (Evaluation Protocol):** Forthcoming testing and validation protocol whose scope is informed directly by the gaps and production needs synthesized in D2.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1]

## Cross-Working-Group Collaboration
ARWG coordinates directly with peer AAIF groups via designated liaisons:
- Contributes terminology to the unified gathering initiatives led by [Taxonomy and Landscape](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md).[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1]
- Maintains active liaison tracks with [Observability and Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md).[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1]

# Lifecycle History
Following charter approval on May 15, 2026, the working group entered full execution mode in June 2026, advancing D1 through an initial 41-term census and ratifying the table of contents for D2.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1]

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream
proposed_concept.description: Cross-cutting AAIF initiative establishing unified agentic terminology, landscape mapping, and delegate-driven triage across working groups.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream is a cross-cutting AAIF initiative established to build a shared terminology standard and an authoritative agentic ecosystem directory.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1] By establishing delegate-driven review workflows and common vocabulary schemas across AAIF working groups, the workstream eliminates siloed terminology and redundant domain research.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1]

# Architecture / Specification

## Schema Architecture and Landscape Integration
The workstream separates terminology definition and ecosystem visualization across modern, decoupled infrastructure:
- **CNCF Metadata Standard:** The vocabulary uses a CNCF-style metadata schema defining terms through concise summaries alongside comprehensive scope notes and disambiguation criteria.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1]
- **Ecosystem Directory:** The landscape visualization integrates with existing AAIF landscape infrastructure while maintaining a dedicated repository and pipeline for taxonomy definitions.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1]
- **International Standards Alignment:** Term definitions actively cross-reference and align with international standards bodies, including ISO and NIST, requiring explicit justification for domain deviations.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a51b00ec455f-a054be90]

## Delegate Review Workflow
Terminology triage follows an asynchronous, pull-request-driven process enforced through cross-working-group representation:[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1]
- **Working Group Delegates:** Each AAIF working group—including [Accuracy and Reliability](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md), [Security and Privacy](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), and [Workflows and Process Integration](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md)—nominates active delegates and domain editors.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-f5653280f5fa-c283d985][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-4885f35209fd-df51791c]
- **Offline Triage and Whiteboard Collection:** Raw term proposals are first aggregated across unified cross-WG spreadsheets and whiteboard documents to surface overlaps, conflicting boundaries, and universal terms before formal pull requests are authored.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a51b00ec455f-a054be90][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-4885f35209fd-df51791c]
- **Editorial Policies:** Term contributions must adhere to a standardized definitions style guide and an AI usage policy mandating human editorial oversight.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a51b00ec455f-a054be90]

# Lifecycle History
The workstream initiated kickoff sessions in June 2026, establishing a decoupled web architecture and PR-based workflow.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1] In mid-June 2026, the charter achieved cross-WG consensus across six constituent working groups, resetting initial legacy definitions in favor of formal delegate-reviewed pull requests and collaborative spreadsheet triage.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-f5653280f5fa-c283d985][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a51b00ec455f-a054be90][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-4885f35209fd-df51791c]

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy and Landscape Meeting Notes Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Standardized structure, section requirements, and metadata conventions for authoring Taxonomy and Landscape workstream meeting notes.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy and Landscape Meeting Notes Guidelines define the standardized template and document structure for recording weekly syncs of the Taxonomy and Landscape workstream.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-32390fa5133a-785f207f] Maintained in the workstream repository, the format guarantees consistent tracking of automated meeting summaries, topics, consensus decisions, deliverables, and assigned action items.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-32390fa5133a-785f207f]

# Architecture / Specification

## Canonical Markdown Template
Meeting note documents must adhere to the standardized markdown structure:[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-32390fa5133a-785f207f]

```markdown
# Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream

## Meeting — YYYY-MM-DD

## Resources

- [AI Summary](link)

## Topics Discussed

- Topic 1
- Topic 2

## Decisions

- Decision 1

## Deliverables

- Deliverable 1

## Action Items

| Owner | Action | Due |
|-------|--------|-----|
| Name  | Task   | Date |
```

## Section Requirements
- **Meeting Header:** Level-1 title identifying the workstream followed by a Level-2 header specifying the date in ISO format (`YYYY-MM-DD`).[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-32390fa5133a-785f207f]
- **Resources:** Direct link to recording or AI summary platforms (such as Zoom LFX).[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-32390fa5133a-785f207f]
- **Topics Discussed:** Bulleted narrative tracking discussion items, debate points, and presentations.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-32390fa5133a-785f207f]
- **Decisions:** Explicit record of consensus decisions, procedural resets, and policy agreements.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-32390fa5133a-785f207f]
- **Deliverables:** Status updates or milestone completions for workstream artifacts.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-32390fa5133a-785f207f]
- **Action Items:** Structured Markdown table capturing the owner, specific action, and due date.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-32390fa5133a-785f207f]

# Lifecycle History
The standardized `TEMPLATES.md` specification was ratified in June 2026 to govern all synchronous meeting records published to the workstream repository.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-32390fa5133a-785f207f]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream (WS Taxonomy & Landscape) is a cross-cutting AAIF initiative chartered to establish unified terminology, standardized metadata models, and ecosystem landscape mapping across all foundation working groups[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0]. Co-chaired by Junjie Bu (Google) and Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1], the workstream prevents fragmented vocabularies and eliminates duplicate research efforts across the agentic AI domain.

# Architecture / Specification
The workstream operates across two primary technical surfaces:

- **Taxonomy Schema**: Terminology definitions and relational hierarchies are encoded using a lightweight SKOS Lite metadata schema[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0]. Terms undergo global peer review via tracking sheets before being merged into the master schema[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1].
- **Ecosystem Landscape**: The agentic AI landscape map follows a CNCF-style category and item configuration structure hosted on a public web portal with automated CI/CD publishing pipelines[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1].

Operational intake relies on an asynchronous, PR-driven review workflow supported by designated domain editors and appointed delegates from each technical working group[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0]. Monthly operational reports are submitted to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) on the final business day of each reporting period, followed by a seven-day review window[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-33d3ff4f1e08-3ee3542b].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-05-21**: Kickoff meeting reviewed the initial charter, demonstrated the decoupled web portal architecture, and adopted the SKOS Lite schema and CNCF landscape model[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0].
- **2026-06-30**: Formally approved workstream charter, onboarded two formal delegates across all working groups except the [Agentic Commerce Working Group](../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md), and began cross-WG review of the initial batch of 10-20 core terms per domain[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Alignment Working Group (WG Government, Risk & Regulatory Alignment) serves as the primary AAIF body evaluating international public policy, compliance requirements, and risk management standards affecting autonomous agentic systems[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a17a580f85c2-e56de454]. Chaired by Ryan Hagemann (IBM) and Deborah Eng (JPMorgan Chase), the group translates regulatory mandates into technical controls and architectural specifications.

# Architecture / Specification
The working group conducts comparative and gap analyses across major AI governance frameworks, standards bodies, and legislative statutes to identify required controls for agentic deployments. Core areas of investigation include:

- Harmonization of regulatory baselines against external standards (including NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001, and the EU AI Act).
- Mapping of policy expectations to tangible operational safeguards such as hard-constraint gates, hardware authorization, and tamper-evident audit trails.
- Cross-collaboration with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) and the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) to ensure consistent legal and risk terminology.

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-06-30**: Completed initial three-month landscape assessment mapping existing agentic AI policy frameworks, regulatory guidance documents, and standards; initiated follow-on sprint to establish comparative baselines for formal gap analysis[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a17a580f85c2-e56de454].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group (WG Observability & Traceability) establishes vendor-neutral telemetry standards, execution lineage specifications, and audit mechanisms for autonomous AI workflows[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2]. Co-chaired by Pavan Sudheendra (Cisco) and Matthew Lee (Datadog), the group standardizes trace schemas across LLM inferences, protocol boundaries, and distributed agent swarms.

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its deliverables into specialized focus groups targeting key architectural seams[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2]:

- **LLM Primitives and Protocol Observability**: Standardizing telemetry and context propagation across model calls, MCP server interfaces, and tool invocations. (Merged from separate primitives and protocol groups in July 2026 to organize around unified problem surfaces)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a].
- **Multi-Agentic Observability**: Coordinating orchestration, handoffs, and distributed execution graph tracking across autonomous subagents[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2].
- **Agentic State, Context, and Reasoning**: Capturing memory mutation, reasoning chains, and prompt assembly transitions[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2].

The group collaborates with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) on domain terms and evaluates decentralized discovery frameworks like [Agentic Resource Discovery](../standards/agentic-resource-discovery.md) for telemetry integration[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-06-29**: Finalized initial six-month charter milestones, launched five specialized focus groups, and published initial use case and gap analysis drafts[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2].
- **2026-07-09**: Agreed to merge LLM Primitives and Protocol Observability focus groups to address deliverable overlap, reviewed the Agentic Resource Discovery specification, and planned architectural trace model tracks[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Resource Discovery Specification
proposed_concept.description: Decentralized discovery, verification, and admission specification enabling agents to find, trust, and verify AI resources via catalogs and dynamic registries.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Resource Discovery (ARD) specification defines a decentralized architecture for discovering, evaluating, and verifying AI tools, capabilities, and agent resources across administrative boundaries[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a]. Jointly announced by a multi-vendor consortium of 11 organizations, ARD standardizes how autonomous agents locate trusted endpoints while enforcing provenance and identity guarantees.

# Architecture / Specification
The ARD specification is structured around two core functional components[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a]:

- **Catalog (Static Indexing)**: Declarative, machine-readable manifests enabling offline search, capability indexing, and structural schema inspection.
- **Registry (Dynamic REST API)**: Active control plane exposing RESTful endpoints for runtime admission, health validation, and dynamic capability lookup.

### Trust and Identification Model
ARD integrates with decentralized identity and security frameworks to establish cryptographically verifiable discovery:

- **Identity Federation**: Leverages SPIFFE (Secure Production Identity Framework for Everyone) and ANS (Agent Name Service) standards to authenticate agents and resource providers[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a].
- **Trust Manifests**: Encodes cryptographic attestation and authorization requirements within discovery metadata, enabling consuming agents to verify endpoint integrity prior to execution.
- **Natural Language Search**: Implements semantic and natural language discovery layers that resolve plain-language agent requests to verified interface contracts[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-07-09**: Presented to the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) by Junjie Bu following joint industry announcement; initiated cross-group reviews on identity standards, ANS integration, and telemetry trace correlation[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body co-chaired by Alexander Frazer (Runlayer) and Junjie Bu (Google)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d]. The group transitions agentic security from ad-hoc mitigations to systematic threat modeling, actionable architectural patterns, and cross-cutting reviews across the AAIF ecosystem[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group structures its activities across five core workstreams[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d]:

1. **Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design**: Co-led by Alon Mazor and Fernando Lucktemberg, evaluating external security frameworks including OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, CSA MAESTRO, and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework across agent operational boundaries[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].
2. **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide**: Co-led by Fernando Lucktemberg and Matthew Khouzam, providing practical implementer guidance and operational guardrails for autonomous systems[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].
3. **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Co-led by Dan Kommatas and Sagar Dashora, defining reusable architectural patterns addressing agent isolation, verification, and runtime containment[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].
4. **Cross-Working Group Security and Privacy Review Checklist**: Led by Govindaraj Palanisamy, establishing lightweight security review checklists and consultation workflows across other AAIF working groups[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].
5. **Taxonomy and Landscape Liaison**: Coordinated with the cross-cutting `../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md` initiative, with Jay White and Katherine Druckman serving as delegates[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].

# Lifecycle History
In June 2026, the working group transitioned from formation into execution, publishing workstream charters and initial drafts for the threat modeling gap analysis and security best practices guide[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d]. The group escalated external alignment requests to the `../governance/technical-committee.md` regarding collaboration postures with external bodies including OWASP, AARM, MCP ACS, and FINOS AI initiatives[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].

# References
- Working group reporting guidelines: `../guidelines/working-group-reporting-template.md`
- Review checklist: `../guidelines/cross-wg-security-review-checklist.md`
- Security guidelines: `../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md`

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream is a cross-cutting AAIF initiative led by Junjie Bu that coordinates standardized agentic definitions, concept boundaries, and ecosystem categorizations across all foundation working groups[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-1ee494c46a19-56a82d6e][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d]. The workstream operates through designated delegates from each domain working group to curate terminology and maintain parity across technical specifications[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-1ee494c46a19-56a82d6e][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-d7a6875f36a3-d28591c2].

# Architecture / Specification
The workstream coordinates terminology through an asynchronous spreadsheet intake and pull request review pipeline[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-1ee494c46a19-56a82d6e][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-d7a6875f36a3-d28591c2]:

- **Intake and Delegate Model**: Each AAIF working group designates delegates (such as Jay White and Katherine Druckman for `../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md`) who submit 10 to 20 core domain terms for inclusion into an initial v1.0 foundation vocabulary release[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-1ee494c46a19-56a82d6e].
- **Curation and Consensus Workflow**: The consolidated working inventory encompasses approximately 250 terms. Terms are classified using consensus tracking columns ("LGTM", "cull", or "debate") and conditional highlighting to triage candidate definitions[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-1ee494c46a19-56a82d6e]. Universal terms spanning multiple working groups are prioritized at the root of the hierarchy[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-1ee494c46a19-56a82d6e].
- **Contentious Term Resolution**: Terms subject to cross-group debate or ambiguity (such as "identity" or the boundary between "bot" and "agent") are debated during weekly sync meetings and surfaced in cross-WG discussion channels prior to consensus decisions[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-1ee494c46a19-56a82d6e][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].

# Lifecycle History
Following its kickoff on May 21, 2026, the workstream formalized its charter and pull request-driven workflow throughout June 2026[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-d7a6875f36a3-d28591c2]. In July 2026, the initiative entered its active execution phase, extending weekly meetings to one hour and initiating structured culling and promotion rounds across all submitted working group glossaries to finalize v1.0 milestones[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-1ee494c46a19-56a82d6e].

# References
- Meeting procedures: `../guidelines/taxonomy-landscape-meeting-notes.md`
- Contribution skill: `../skills/taxonomy-contributions.md`
- Technical Committee: `../governance/technical-committee.md`

proposed_concept.title: Working Group Monthly Reporting Guidelines and Template
proposed_concept.description: Standardized cadence, structure, review timeline, and pull request workflow for AAIF working groups reporting monthly to the Technical Committee.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Working Group Monthly Reporting Guidelines define the mandatory format, submission cadence, and review workflow for progress reports delivered by AAIF working groups to the `../governance/technical-committee.md`[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-33d3ff4f1e08-f33f7a28]. These updates maintain asynchronous transparency across working group activities, track deliverable velocity against charter milestones, and surface explicit governance requests requiring Technical Committee review[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-33d3ff4f1e08-f33f7a28][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d].

# Architecture / Specification

## Cadence and Review Lifecycles
Monthly reports follow strict scheduling invariants[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-33d3ff4f1e08-f33f7a28]:
- **Submission Deadline**: Due by the last business day of each reporting calendar month under the naming convention `reporting/YYYY-MM-report.md`[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-33d3ff4f1e08-f33f7a28].
- **Review Window**: The Technical Committee review window closes seven calendar days following submission[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-33d3ff4f1e08-f33f7a28].
- **Merge Criteria**: The pull request is merged once the Technical Committee liaison signs off or when the seven-day review window elapses without objection, whichever occurs sooner[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-33d3ff4f1e08-f33f7a28][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].

## Document Structure
Each report implements the canonical template structure[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9677055e316b-27369ef5]:
1. **Header Metadata**: Working Group name, reporting period (`Month YYYY`), Chair(s) and affiliations, and submission date (`YYYY-MM-DD`)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9677055e316b-27369ef5].
2. **Summary**: High-level two-to-three sentence narrative summarizing overall monthly progress[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-33d3ff4f1e08-f33f7a28][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9677055e316b-27369ef5].
3. **Progress Against Objectives**: Concise bullet points tying delivered or progressed work directly back to charter deliverables[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-33d3ff4f1e08-f33f7a28].
4. **Ecosystem Highlights**: External engagement updates with complementary standards organizations (e.g. OWASP, AARM, MCP ACS)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-33d3ff4f1e08-f33f7a28][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9677055e316b-27369ef5].
5. **Blockers and Risks**: Operational, scheduling, or technical risks affecting workstream pacing[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-33d3ff4f1e08-f33f7a28].
6. **Decisions Needed from the TC**: Unambiguous, actionable governance questions or mandate requests requiring formal Technical Committee decision[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-33d3ff4f1e08-f33f7a28][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9677055e316b-27369ef5].
7. **Next Month's Focus**: Top two to three forward-looking priorities[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-33d3ff4f1e08-f33f7a28].
8. **Metrics / Links**: Progress against charter Key Performance Indicators across Adoption, Quality, Community, and Timeliness, followed by supporting URLs to pull requests and meeting records[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-33d3ff4f1e08-f33f7a28][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d].

## Authoring and Evidence Constraints
Authors and automated agents preparing reports must observe strict sourcing rules[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-33d3ff4f1e08-f33f7a28]:
- Every claim must be grounded in repository git history, deliverables indexes, or authoritative meeting minutes[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-33d3ff4f1e08-f33f7a28].
- Uncommitted deliverables may only be described as "drafted" or "in progress"[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-33d3ff4f1e08-f33f7a28].
- Sections lacking activity must retain headings with explicit "None." or "None this month." placeholders rather than being omitted[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-33d3ff4f1e08-f33f7a28].
- Reports are linked in reverse-chronological order within the working group's `reporting/README.md` index table[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-33d3ff4f1e08-f33f7a28].

# References
- Governance policy: `../policies/working-group-lifecycle-policy.md`
- Technical Committee: `../governance/technical-committee.md`
- Report synthesis skill: `../skills/aaif-wg-monthly-report.md`

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream
proposed_concept.description: Cross-cutting AAIF initiative maintaining a SKOS-Lite agentic glossary and interactive CNCF-style ecosystem landscape through federated working group delegates.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream is a cross-cutting Agentic AI Foundation initiative tasked with curating a unified glossary of agentic AI terminology and an authoritative global ecosystem architecture map.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b] Approved as a foundational cross-working group body in June 2026, the workstream prevents siloed domain definitions and eliminates redundant ecosystem surveys across vertical technical working groups.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b] [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-b33563055168-8ff39019]

# Architecture / Specification
## Scope and Governance
The workstream operates on a federated curation model rather than authoring isolated domain-specific standards from scratch.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b]
- **Federated Delegates**: Each AAIF technical working group nominates two Domain Editors who represent their domain, review terminology pull requests, and arbitrate naming conflicts.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b]
- **Horizontal versus Vertical Guardrails**: The workstream maintains horizontal terminology consolidation and global landscape curation, while vertical domain specifications, regulatory whitepapers, and core protocol designs remain under their respective technical working groups.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b]

## Artifacts and Publishing Architecture
The workstream maintains two core deliverables deployed to public web properties through GitHub Actions automation:[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b] [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-0f132b096200-171c31ea]
1. **Shared Taxonomy Explorer**: A standardized vocabulary repository utilizing a SKOS-Lite metadata model (`prefLabel`, `altLabel`, `broaderTerm`, `scopeNote`, `relatedTerms`, `contrastsWith`) serialized in data files like `taxonomy-data.js`.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b]
2. **Ecosystem Landscape Map**: An interactive CNCF-style ecosystem map (`landscape.yml`) whose categorization buckets evolve through delegate consensus.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b]

Web distributions are assembled and deployed to GitHub Pages via `.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml`.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-0f132b096200-171c31ea]

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-06-21**: Charter officially approved with Junjie Bu (Google) as Chair and Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg) as Co-Chair.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b]
- **Cadence**: Weekly on Mondays at 8:30 AM PT (30 minutes).[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b]

# Overview
The Accuracy & Reliability Working Group establishes standards, benchmarks, and engineering practices required for AI agents to operate accurately and reliably under real-world enterprise conditions.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-b33563055168-8ff39019] Operating under the technical direction of the Technical Committee, the group investigates agent failure modes, evaluation criteria, and reliability patterns across open agent ecosystems.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-b33563055168-8ff39019]

# Architecture / Specification
## Leadership and Governance
- **Chair**: Jordan Augé (Cisco)[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-b33563055168-8ff39019]
- **Co-Chair**: Casper Nielsen (Diagrid)[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-b33563055168-8ff39019]
- **Current Term**: March 1, 2026 – January 31, 2027, appointed by Platinum and Gold members of the working group.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-b33563055168-8ff39019]
- **Neutrality**: Contributors participate as individuals rather than employer representatives under Linux Foundation antitrust compliance.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-b33563055168-8ff39019]

## Operations and Meetings
- **Meeting Schedule**: Biweekly on Tuesdays at 9:00 AM PT via LFX Zoom.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-b33563055168-8ff39019]
- **Communications**: Public mailing list `wg-accuracy-reliability@lists.aaif.io` and the `#wg-accuracy-and-reliability` Discord channel.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-b33563055168-8ff39019]

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-03-01**: Current chair term commenced for Jordan Augé and Casper Nielsen.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-b33563055168-8ff39019]
