# Overview
The Security & Privacy Working Group establishes threat models, security best practice guides, and runtime defense patterns across the Agentic AI Foundation ecosystem.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-7] The group assesses vulnerabilities unique to autonomous systems—such as prompt injection, unauthorized tool execution, and memory poisoning—and coordinates cross-cutting security reviews with other working groups.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-7]

# Architecture / Specification
## Workstreams and Operational Focus
In mid-2026, the working group transitioned from formation into execution across five active workstreams:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-7]
- **Threat Modeling Gap Analysis**: Authoring comparative assessments of established frameworks against agentic vulnerabilities.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-7]
- **Security Best Practices Guide**: Drafting actionable configuration and runtime guidance for agent developers.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-7]
- **Taxonomy Alignment**: Delegated baseline security definitions to the cross-working group [Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream](taxonomy-and-landscape.md) to maintain foundation-wide terminology consistency.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-7]
- **External Collaboration**: Submitted policy and scope decision requests to the Technical Committee concerning engagement posture with external initiatives including OWASP, AARM, and MCP ACS.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-7]

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-06**: Published first monthly Technical Committee report recording the activation of five workstreams with dedicated leads and initial draft deliverables.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-7]

# Overview
The Observability & Traceability Working Group defines open standards and telemetry propagation models for monitoring agentic AI systems across runtime boundaries.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c6471d290754-349d30a5] The group collaborates with upstream foundations and standards bodies, including OpenTelemetry and IETF working groups, to ensure interoperable execution tracing and forensic auditability.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c6471d290754-349d30a5]

# Architecture / Specification
## Focus Groups and Operational Structure
The working group organizes technical contributions through specialized focus groups:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c6471d290754-349d30a5]
- **Protocols and Primitives Merger**: Merged the protocols focus group into the primitives focus group in July 2026 to streamline meeting cadence and unify architectural terminology.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c6471d290754-349d30a5]
- **Multi-Agent Observability**: Investigating multi-agent delegation semantics, trace context propagation, and agent-to-agent network layer telemetry.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c6471d290754-349d30a5]
- **Taxonomy Harmonization**: Actively reviewing foundation-wide universal taxonomy terms in coordination with the [Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream](taxonomy-and-landscape.md).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c6471d290754-349d30a5]
- **External Standards Engagement**: Tracking peer-to-peer agent network measurement with libp2p, IETF agent protocol initiatives, OpenID specifications, and planned reference contributions back to OpenTelemetry.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c6471d290754-349d30a5]

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-07-22**: Consolidated protocols and primitives focus groups and reviewed external contributor policy guidance pending Governing Council review.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c6471d290754-349d30a5]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Governance, Risk and Regulatory Alignment Working Group (WG Governance, Risk & Regulatory) serves as the primary bridge between international artificial intelligence policy developments and technical implementations across agentic AI systems within the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF)[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-b33563055168-432cf673]. Operating under the oversight of the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md), the group analyzes emerging legal, risk, and compliance frameworks to inform architectural guidance, assurance baselines, and cross-working group security and operational policies.

# Leadership and Operations
The working group's leadership was appointed by Platinum and Gold foundation members for an initial term spanning March 1, 2026 through January 31, 2027[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-b33563055168-432cf673]:
- **Chair:** Ryan Hagemann (IBM)[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-b33563055168-432cf673]
- **Co-Chair:** Deborah Eng (JP Morgan Chase)[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-b33563055168-432cf673]

Working group sessions convene bi-weekly on Thursdays at 10:00 AM Pacific Time via Linux Foundation (LFX) Zoom infrastructure, maintaining public running agendas, minutes, and recorded archives on LFX[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-b33563055168-432cf673]. Public coordination is conducted through the working group mailing list (`wg-governance-risk-regulatory@lists.aaif.io`) and designated AAIF Discord discussion channels[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-b33563055168-432cf673].

# Governance and Collaboration
All working group participants operate under standard Linux Foundation antitrust compliance policies and the AAIF individual neutrality covenant, contributing as individual technical experts rather than corporate representatives[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-b33563055168-432cf673]. The group liaises with peer domain bodies, including [Security and Privacy](security-and-privacy.md), [Identity and Trust](identity-and-trust.md), and the cross-cutting [Taxonomy and Landscape](taxonomy-and-landscape.md) workstream, ensuring consistent regulatory interpretations across foundation outputs.

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Commerce Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group cataloging and harmonizing open specifications, interoperability patterns, and terminology for AI agent commerce workflows.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Commerce Working Group advances the Agentic AI Foundation's mission by cataloging, aligning, and harmonizing open specifications, frameworks, and terminology for commerce workflows conducted by autonomous agents on behalf of consumers, merchants, and enterprise platforms[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-b33563055168-41e54563]. The working group formulates interoperability guidance and reference architectures spanning intent discovery, multi-party negotiation, [agentic checkout](../taxonomy/agentic-checkout.md), [delegated payment](../taxonomy/delegated-payment.md) orchestration, and post-purchase lifecycles, maintaining strict protocol neutrality without publishing competing proprietary commerce specifications[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-b33563055168-41e54563].

# Leadership and Operations
Working group chairs were appointed by Platinum and Gold AAIF members for a term spanning March 1, 2026 to January 31, 2027[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-b33563055168-41e54563]:
- **Chair:** Ilya Grigorik (Shopify)[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-b33563055168-41e54563]
- **Co-Chair:** Rahul Bansal (OpenAI)[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-b33563055168-41e54563]

The group meets biweekly on Wednesdays at 9:00 AM Pacific Time via LFX Zoom, maintaining running minutes and archived session recordings on LFX[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-b33563055168-41e54563]. Public communication and community reviews take place through the working group mailing list (`wg-agentic-commerce@lists.aaif.io`) and the AAIF Discord server[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-b33563055168-41e54563].

# Scope and Cross-Group Harmonization
The working group identifies common ground across emerging commercial protocols and reports recommendations directly to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md)[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-b33563055168-41e54563]. Core work areas intersect with [Identity and Trust](identity-and-trust.md) for delegated authority and credential presentation, [Security and Privacy](security-and-privacy.md) for transaction integrity, and [Taxonomy and Landscape](taxonomy-and-landscape.md) for shared commerce definitions[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-b33563055168-41e54563].

proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing shared workflow execution models, common terminology, and interoperability patterns for cross-framework agent orchestration.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Workflows and Process Integration Working Group (W&PI) establishes a shared workflow execution model and common terminology for agentic AI systems, extending open specifications and publishing vendor-neutral interoperability patterns across frameworks, tools, and runtime environments[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56]. Formally approved on May 13, 2026 and reporting to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md), W&PI defines canonical [workflow primitives](../taxonomy/workflow-primitives.md) (tasks, tool calls, branching, retries, and sub-agent handoffs) to prevent enterprise vendor lock-in and enable stateful replayability across heterogeneous agent architectures[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56].

# Leadership and Organization
The working group operates under designated leadership established in its charter[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56]:
- **Chair:** Yaron Schneider (Diagrid)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56]
- **Co-Chair:** Adam Seligman (Workato)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56]

# Scope and Technical Focus
The working group's charter delineates three core technical domains[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56]:
1. **Agent Workflow Models and Semantics:** Standardizing execution representations, step ordering, parallelism, conditional logic, and handoff semantics between agents and sub-agents to bridge deterministic workflow engines with autonomous non-deterministic models[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56].
2. **Long-Running and Stateful Agent Execution:** Formulating durability patterns for multi-hour or multi-day runs, state persistence, partial resumption, idempotency, failure recovery, and workflow-level systems of record distinct from runtime telemetry handled by [Observability and Traceability](observability-and-traceability.md)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56].
3. **Tool Invocation and External System Coordination:** Defining standard coordination patterns governing agent interactions with external enterprise APIs, command-line interfaces, services, and human reviewers[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56].

# Overview
The Accuracy and Reliability Working Group (ARWG) investigates failure modes, reproducibility barriers, and empirical verification methodologies across autonomous agentic systems[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-fa4050a9f626-df96ac2e]. Operating under the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md), the group produces standardized failure taxonomies, enterprise-grade evaluation criteria, and recovery guidelines to measure outcome correctness, multi-run consistency, perturbation robustness, and operational reliability in production deployments[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-fa4050a9f626-df96ac2e].

# Leadership and Workstream Progress
The working group is led by designated co-chairs[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-fa4050a9f626-df96ac2e]:
- **Co-Chair:** Jordan Augé (Cisco)[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-fa4050a9f626-df96ac2e]
- **Co-Chair:** Casper Nielsen (Diagrid)[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-fa4050a9f626-df96ac2e]

The working group coordinates two primary workstreams alongside cross-foundation liaison efforts[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-fa4050a9f626-df96ac2e]:
- **D1 (Terminology and Methodology Support):** Structures terminology batches grounded in technical literature and contributes prioritized term definitions to the shared [Taxonomy and Landscape](taxonomy-and-landscape.md) spreadsheet across accuracy dimensions[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-fa4050a9f626-df96ac2e].
- **D2 (Enterprise Gap Analysis):** Investigates practitioner-focused requirements, operational pain points, and reuse barriers that hinder enterprise adoption of academic benchmarks, supported by dedicated survey initiatives[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-fa4050a9f626-df96ac2e].
- **Liaison Initiatives (I1):** Establishes formal cross-working group communication channels, including initial liaison touchpoints with [Observability and Traceability](observability-and-traceability.md)[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-fa4050a9f626-df96ac2e].

proposed_concept.title: Identity and Trust Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing vendor-neutral architectures, delegation chains, authority models, and verifiable action records for autonomous agents.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Identity and Trust Working Group (WG Identity & Trust) establishes vendor-neutral architectures, delegation chains, and verifiable identity systems for autonomous agents across organizational and platform boundaries. The working group operates across three primary sub-groups focusing on taxonomy, reference architecture, and critical use cases [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758].

# Architecture / Specification

WG Identity & Trust coordinates architectural foundations across several core components:

- **Sub-Working Groups:**
  - **Taxonomy:** Defining shared vocabulary including Agent, [Action Record](../taxonomy/action-record.md), Audit Log, Consent Receipt, and Human-in-the-Loop boundaries [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758].
  - **Reference Architecture:** Standardizing components across Discovery Metadata, Identifier, Identity, Authorization, Revocability, Evidence, Verification, and Reputation [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758]. Key invariants enforce that subagents cannot hold permissions exceeding their delegating agent, which cannot exceed the initiating user's scope.
  - **Critical Use Cases:** Developing operational patterns across Internal, B2B, and B2C environments governing naming, deployment, dynamic per-request authorization, and principal-attested revocation [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758].
- **External Framework Evaluations:** Assessing industry models such as NVIDIA's Secure Agent Workspace (SAW) reference design (covering four-layer identity, delegation records, OpenShell policy enforcement, and ODIS) and the OpenID Foundation whitepaper *Identity Management for Agentic AI* [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758].
- **Authorization Profiling:** Proposed profiling of OAuth 2.0 as the normative cross-platform baseline for token format, delegation chains, and scope expressions, while keeping internal policy enforcement within backend systems out of scope [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-07 / 2026-08:** Advanced candidate definitions for Action Records and Consent Receipts; drafted reference architecture components table; evaluated NVIDIA SAW; proposed OAuth 2.0 authorization baseline to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Commerce Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group cataloging and harmonizing open specifications, capability maps, and payment interoperability models across agent-driven commercial transactions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic Commerce Working Group (WG Agentic Commerce) develops open specifications, capability maps, and interoperability patterns enabling autonomous AI agents to negotiate, orchestrate, and finalize multi-party commercial transactions [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393].

# Architecture / Specification

The group focuses on standardizing protocol-neutral interfaces across discovery, delegated authority, checkout, payment, fraud signaling, and post-purchase lifecycles [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393]:

- **Capability Map:** The foundational deliverable defining standardized touchpoints across commercial agent workflows [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393].
- **Payment Handler Model:** Structures payment capabilities around three reusable primitives:
  - `handler`: Execution mechanism mediating interactions between agent platforms, payment providers, and checkout systems [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393].
  - `instrument`: Standardized representation of payment methods or wallets attached during checkout [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393].
  - `credential`: Authentication artifacts and tokens authorizing transactions within sensitive data boundaries [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393].
- **Protocol Comparative Analysis:** Evaluates payment handler models across the Agent Client Protocol (ACP), Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP), and Machine Payments Protocol (MPP), assessing MPP's challenge-credential-receipt pattern for delegated tokenization [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393].
- **Trust & Identity Separation:** Isolating agent identity and risk profiles from shopper identity and risk profiles to support fraud signaling across merchants, agent platforms, and risk engines [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-05:** Charter formally approved; delivered technical comparative analysis of ACP, UCP, and MPP payment handler structures; initiated Agentic Commerce Capability Map [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393].

proposed_concept.title: Action Record
proposed_concept.description: Tamper-evident, content-private, and independently verifiable record proving what an agent executed, distinct from operator telemetry and authorization grants.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

An **Action Record** is a tamper-evident, content-private, independently verifiable record proving that an agent executed a specific, consequential action [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758]. Distinct from operational telemetry, audit logs, and identity/authorization tokens, an action record serves as legal and technical evidence for external counterparties, auditors, or adjudicators [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758].

# Architecture / Specification

Within the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) taxonomy, action records maintain distinct functional boundaries [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758]:

- **Boundary with Observability/Tracing:** Observability telemetry answers *"what is my agent doing?"* for internal operators during development, debugging, and performance monitoring. In contrast, an Action Record answers *"what did this agent verifiably do?"* for counterparties, compliance auditors, or courts [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758].
- **Boundary with Authorization:** Identity tokens and authorization assertions attest to permissions granted *prior* to execution; Action Records attest to what took place *during or after* execution, binding the agent identity, intent, and delegation proof to the resulting artifact [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758].
- **Selective Disclosure:** Action records support content privacy, allowing selective redaction or zero-knowledge revelation of sensitive parameters without invalidating third-party cryptographic verification [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-07:** Formalized as a distinct concept within the Identity & Trust WG Taxonomy sub-group [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Commerce Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing vendor-neutral capability maps, protocol gap analyses, and reference architectures across discovery, checkout, payment, and post-purchase lifecycles.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Commerce Working Group is a technical initiative within the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) providing a protocol-neutral forum to map, evaluate, and harmonize specifications across the end-to-end autonomous commerce lifecycle[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-baf22ae9aa4b-28feda26][^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a439311d16f4-f0496332]. Co-chaired by Ilya Grigorik (Shopify) and Rahul Bansal (OpenAI), the group addresses protocol fragmentation and merchant integration burden across consumers, agents, merchants, wallets, payment providers, and financial networks[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-baf22ae9aa4b-28feda26][^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760].

Rather than authoring a competing commerce protocol, the working group maintains a protocol-neutral remit focusing on commerce-facing external interfaces, stateful negotiations, and delegation boundaries rather than underlying platform internals[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760].

# Architecture / Specification

## Lifecycle Model
The group structures its capability mapping and gap analysis across four key stages of the commerce journey[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a439311d16f4-f0496332][^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760]:
1. **Product Discovery**: Separating asynchronous product feeds from live merchant/marketplace retrieval, while addressing source discovery, catalog normalization, data freshness, and trust[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760].
2. **Checkout and Negotiation**: Analyzing stateful, merchant-authoritative negotiations across specifications including the Agentic Commerce Protocol (ACP) and Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP), detailing transport bindings, protocol extensibility, and human handoff mechanisms[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760].
3. **Payment**: Evaluating payment-handler models, instrument credentials, dynamic eligibility, delegated authority mandates (such as AP2), and tokenized or micropayment exchanges (such as MPP and x402)[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760][^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-fa4050a9f626-c7520564].
4. **Post-Purchase**: Mapping order observation, event tracking, and adjustment ledgers against state-changing actions such as cancellations, returns, refunds, and dispute arbitration[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-fa4050a9f626-c7520564].

## Fraud and Trust Signal Propagation
The group investigates trust preservation across agent, platform, merchant, payment provider, and risk system boundaries[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a17a580f85c2-056b6afe]. It distinguishes between agent identity and risk, shopper identity and risk, and evidence binding the two to a specific delegation and transaction, aiming to establish portable baselines of bounded facts or attestations without triggering indiscriminate data sharing[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a17a580f85c2-056b6afe].

## Core Deliverables
The working group centers its work on four primary deliverables[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760][^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-fa4050a9f626-c7520564]:
- **Agentic Commerce Capability Map**: Structured matrix defining roles, capabilities, signal visibility, and handoffs across existing and emerging commerce protocols.
- **Protocol Gap Analysis**: Identification of capability gaps, integration burdens, and missing handoffs between commerce lifecycle phases.
- **Implementation Best Practices**: Guidance for secure agent-to-merchant integration, delegation verification, and consent preservation.
- **Reference Architecture**: Architectural blueprints illustrating multi-turn commerce workflows spanning discovery, wallets, and settlement.

## Cross-Working Group Coordination
Commerce workflows depend on work from adjacent AAIF technical bodies[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760][^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a17a580f85c2-056b6afe]:
- [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) for identity proofing, delegation chains, and authority binding.
- [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) for boundary controls and risk mitigation.
- [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) for cross-boundary audit logging and dispute provenance.

# Lifecycle History
The working group launched in February 2026 with an initial problem inventory[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-baf22ae9aa4b-28feda26]. In March 2026, it adopted a problem-first lifecycle method[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a439311d16f4-f0496332]. # Overview
The Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group (WS Taxonomy & Landscape) is a cross-cutting initiative within the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) tasked with arbitrating a canonical agentic terminology taxonomy and maintaining an interactive ecosystem landscape portal[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103]. Co-chaired by Junjie Bu (Google) and Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg), the group provides semantic governance across all AAIF working groups by reconciling term definitions and maintaining unified conceptual boundaries[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103].

# Architecture / Specification

## Term Arbitration Pipeline
The workstream operates a structured review workflow to arbitrate terms submitted across foundational domains[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103]:
- **Admitted First, Defined Second**: Terms undergo scope admission review before final definition drafting, decoupling structural taxonomic inclusion from contested semantic tuning[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103].
- **Sequential Domain Review**: Arbitration proceeds through universal terms into domain-specific clusters, including Identity & Trust, Workflows & Process Integration, and Governance, Risk & Regulatory Alignment[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103].
- **Contested Term Backlog**: Highly debated terms with divergent working group positions (such as the definition of `Agent`) are isolated in a tracked debate backlog for dedicated arbitration prior to v1.0 release[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103].
- **Portal Publication**: Approved terms are merged via version-controlled pull requests directly into the public Taxonomy and Landscape portal[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103].

## Operational Policies
External contributions against the landscape and taxonomy are synchronized directly through weekly working group review sessions to ensure consistent evaluation criteria across submissions[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103].

# Lifecycle History
In July 2026, the workstream shifted from collecting raw terms to active arbitration across its 128-term backlog, admitting its first 13 standardized terms via pull request #33 and deploying them to the public portal[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103].

proposed_concept.description: Standardized architecture decision record template capturing context, rationale, consequences, and alternatives for workflow reference architectures.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Reference Architecture Decision Template provides the standardized Architecture Decision Record (ADR) format used by the [Workflows & Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) to record significant structural choices, trade-offs, and governance invariants across AAIF reference architectures.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-3a311f3edf5a-27d0e407]

By formalizing how decisions are proposed, debated, and adopted, the template ensures that design rationale remains auditable and that follow-on consequences and rejected alternatives are preserved alongside reference implementations.

# Architecture / Specification

Decision documents conforming to this template must implement the following sequential sections:[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-3a311f3edf5a-27d0e407]

1. **Decision Title**: Markdown heading identifying the decision scope.
2. **Date**: Timestamp of proposal or resolution.
3. **Status**: Lifecycle status, restricted to `Proposed`, `accepted`, `rejected`, or `superseded`, accompanied by decision issue or pull request links.
4. **Context**: Articulation of the conditions prompting the decision, detailing prior architectural state, ambiguities, or technical constraints requiring resolution.
5. **Decision**: Explicit, unambiguous declaration of the chosen pattern or architectural contract.
6. **Rationale**: Technical and operational justification supporting the choice.
7. **Consequences**: Downstream impacts resulting from adoption, covering implementation requirements, necessary follow-on tasks, and documented trade-offs.
8. **Alternatives considered**: Viable alternative architectures and explicit reasoning for why they were rejected.
9. **Follow-up**: Actionable next steps, tracking issues, or evaluation milestones.

# References

- Template definition: [workstreams/reference-architectures/decisions/TEMPLATE.md](https://github.com/aaif/wg-workflows-and-process-integration/blob/3b4d645499620b10b313297e7f365148fa6d0ee1/workstreams/reference-architectures/decisions/TEMPLATE.md)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-3a311f3edf5a-27d0e407]

# Overview

The Observability & Traceability Working Group develops vendor-neutral telemetry specifications, distributed tracing standards, and audit frameworks that capture causal relationships across autonomous agent lifecycles, protocol boundaries, and multi-agent coordination topologies.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7]

Chaired by Pavan Sudheendra (Cisco) and Matthew Lee (Datadog), the group coordinates semantic conventions, execution trace models, and hardware/networking integrations with external standards bodies including the OpenTelemetry project, LibP2P, and the IETF.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763]

# Architecture / Specification

## Focus Group Structure

In July 2026, the working group restructured its initial five focus groups into three consolidated tracks to streamline review bandwidth and eliminate overlapping scopes:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7]

1. **LLM Primitives & Protocol Observability** (Lead: Zayne Turner): Merged track handling protocol boundaries, [cross-boundary observability models](../resources/cross-boundary-observability-model.md), [Agentic Resource Discovery](../standards/agentic-resource-discovery.md) (ARD) telemetry for pre-execution trust decisions, and modeling skills as first-class citizens in execution traces.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7]
2. **Multi-Agentic Observability - Orchestration & Coordination** (Lead: Ty Smith): Focuses on multi-agent communication, modular observability maps, and context intelligence graph runtimes.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763]
3. **Agentic State & Context** (Lead: Govindaraj Palanisamy): Merged track combining reasoning traces and persistent memory state observability, covering landscape and gap analyses.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7]

## Core Initiatives

- **Agent Behavior Trace Model**: Standardized recommendation led by Matthew Lee advancing through community review to formalize execution state and causal graphs.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763]
- **Taxonomy Alignment**: Joint harmonization with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) to reconcile telemetry and trace concepts with universal agent vocabulary.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7]
- **Composable Trust Blueprint & P2P Telemetry**: Joint collaboration with LibP2P exploring peer-to-peer GossipSub observability, Verifiable Telemetry Objects (VTO), and Agent Action Capsules (AAC) serialized via CBOR42.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763]

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-07-31**: Monthly report submitted to the Technical Committee detailing focus group consolidation from five to three active tracks.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7]
- **2026-08-05**: Working group session demonstrating LibP2P P2P observability stack, initiation of Composable Trust Blueprint integration with VTO and AAC, and community scheduling for the Agent Behavior Trace Model recommendation.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763]

# Overview
The Workflows and Process Integration Working Group (WG) is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body establishing shared workflow models, common terminology, interoperability guidelines, and design patterns that enable agent workflows to operate across diverse frameworks, tools, and execution environments[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b33563055168-a6ab4b87].

The working group collaborates across foundation initiatives to harmonize workflow abstractions and reference architectures with cross-cutting efforts such as the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b33563055168-a6ab4b87].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide
proposed_concept.description: Implementation guidelines, threat mitigation controls, and decision frameworks for securing agentic AI systems across secrets, tools, guardrails, evals, and forensics.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide provides practical implementation guidance, failure pattern analyses, and decision frameworks for builders securing autonomous agent systems[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9]. Developed under the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), the guide articulates both the rationale and concrete controls required to protect agent execution loops against compromise[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9].

The guide addresses five primary security domains while explicitly decoupling identity federation and delegated authorization mechanisms, which remain governed by the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9].

# Architecture / Specification

## Core Domains
The guide structures technical controls across five foundational domains[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9]:
1. **Secrets Management:** Securing credential resolution, least-privilege token injection, and runtime isolation for agent-accessible API keys and persistent data stores[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9].
2. **Secure Tool Invocation:** Mitigating risks across the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and external tool supply chains, preventing prompt injection cascades and unauthorized command execution[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9].
3. **Guardrails:** Implementing model-level and runtime constraint layers that bound autonomous actions and enforce organizational safety policies[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9].
4. **Evaluation Frameworks:** Standardizing pre-deployment benchmark suites and red-teaming harnesses to assess behavioral vulnerabilities and adversarial robustness[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9].
5. **Post-Incident Forensics:** Structuring telemetry collection, execution provenance, and audit trails to enable forensic reconstruction after security breaches[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9].

## Structural Blueprint
Each domain in the guide applies a standardized three-part layout[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9]:
- **Failure Patterns:** Detailed analysis of real-world exploitation mechanisms and architectural design flaws.
- **Controls:** Prescriptive, verifiable safeguards and mitigation practices.
- **Decision Frameworks:** Pragmatic decision trees enabling engineering teams to select appropriate trade-offs between autonomy, latency, and defensive depth.

The specification also provides a curated reference table evaluating tooling maturity and deployment costs, backed by an authoritative source ledger[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9].

## Boundary Clarifications
Identity architectures, delegated authorization protocols, and credential formats (including SPIFFE/SVID and RFC 8693 token exchange) are intentionally designated as out of scope for this deliverable to avoid fragmentation with the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9].

# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group (SPAA) is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body tasked with establishing threat models, security baseline controls, runtime protection patterns, and evaluation checklists across agentic architectures [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed]. The working group is co-chaired by Alexander Frazer (Runlayer) and Junjie Bu (Google) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed].

# Operational Procedures

## Governance and Pull Request Acceptance

The working group operates under a charter approved by the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md). Deliverables and repository pull requests may be reviewed and merged directly by working group maintainers without waiting for individual Technical Committee approvals, provided the work falls within the approved charter [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5]. The Technical Committee reviews ongoing progress and raises governance queries through standardized monthly reports [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-c9b4ccd3][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].

## Transparency Policy

The group enforces a default-open policy across all collaboration surfaces. Discord channels, GitHub repositories, and regular working group meetings—including retrospective recordings and transcripts—are public [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].

# Architecture / Specification

## Active Workstreams and Deliverables

The working group organizes its technical production into five primary workstreams [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed]:

1. **Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design**: Led by Fernando Lucktemberg and Alon Mazor, evaluating agentic risks across MITRE ATLAS, OWASP, CSA MAESTRO, and NIST AI RMF, while mapping STRIDE and PASTA methodologies [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5]. Tracked under [resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis](../resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md).
2. **Security Best Practices Guide**: Led by Fernando Lucktemberg and Matthew Khouzam, articulating baseline operational controls and coordinating human-to-user-agent (HUA) and identity boundaries with the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5]. Tracked under [guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md).
3. **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Led by Dan Kommatas and Sagar Dashora, defining structured design pattern specifications for secure agent deployment [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].
4. **Cross-Working Group Security and Privacy Review Checklist**: Led by Govindaraj Palanisamy, establishing a review rubric to assess potential security and data exposure risks across sibling AAIF working group specifications [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5]. Tracked under [guidelines/cross-wg-security-review-checklist](../guidelines/cross-wg-security-review-checklist.md).
5. **Taxonomy and Landscape Alignment**: Represented by delegates Jay White and Katherine Druckman to ensure consistency with the unified cross-working group agentic terminology registry curated by the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].

## External Standards Liaisons

The working group maintains informal liaisons with ETSI TC SAI, OWASP (including the State of Agentic AI Security initiative), Model Context Protocol (MCP) security specifications, and the FINOS AI governance framework while formal collaboration agreements remain under Technical Committee review [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-10].

# Overview

The Observability and Traceability Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body chartered to define telemetry standards, cross-boundary trace contexts, and observability reference architectures across agent runtimes, tool boundaries, and communication protocols [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff]. The group coordinates operational standards to ensure execution records, causal trees, and evaluation traces remain discoverable and interoperable.

# Operational Procedures

## Repository Working Methods

The working group designates GitHub as its single source of truth for durable tracking [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff]:

- **Issues** track work items, decisions, external standards coordination, and follow-ups [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff].
- **Pull Requests** govern all durable repository modifications and deliverable publications [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff].
- **External Documents**: Collaborative drafting occurs in shared documents during exploratory phases, but finalized deliverables must migrate to version-controlled repository Markdown for status tracking and review windows [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff].

## Work Item Tracking Schema

Every deliverable and workstream task is tracked via a standardized GitHub issue template containing explicit fields [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b44b5d93b435-bb190e50]:

- **Outcome**: The concrete artifact, decision, or coordination result produced.
- **Workstream**: Categorization (e.g., WG deliverable, focus-group task, cross-WG coordination, external standards).
- **Owner**: Named driver or marked as `needs owner`.
- **Status**: Discrete state from the standardized vocabulary.
- **Next Step**: Explicit next action item.
- **Review or Decision Needed**: Feedback scope, approvals, or review deadlines.
- **Acceptance Criteria**: Verifiable closure conditions.

## Status Lifecycle Vocabulary

Work tracking issues adopt six standardized statuses [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b44b5d93b435-bb190e50][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff]:

- `needs owner`: Valid task lacking an assigned driver.
- `scoping`: Establishing boundaries, input parameters, and expected outcome.
- `in progress`: Active drafting, research, or cross-group coordination.
- `ready for review`: Material is complete and awaiting review or feedback.
- `blocked`: Execution depends on an explicit decision, dependency, or upstream input.
- `done`: Deliverable landed, closed intentionally, or superseded.

## Operating Cadence

The working group synchronizes repository state with its meeting schedule [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff]:

- **Pre-Meeting**: Reviewing open issues and pull requests to flag blocked tasks and structure agenda topics.
- **In-Meeting**: Logging decisions and assigned action items directly into meeting minutes with links to corresponding issues.
- **Post-Meeting**: Updating issue owners, statuses, and next steps to provide transparent visibility for asynchronous contributors.
- **Reporting**: Pulling directly from active issues and merged pull requests to author monthly reports for the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) under [guidelines/working-group-reporting-template](../guidelines/working-group-reporting-template.md).

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical working group tasked with establishing security and privacy as a shared discipline across the agentic AI ecosystem [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-3c263a95]. The working group develops open threat models, risk mitigation frameworks, architectural security patterns, and domain terminology that AI providers, platform builders, and peer AAIF working groups can adopt to secure agentic workflows [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-3c263a95].

The group is chaired by Alex Frazer (Runlayer) and co-chaired by Junjie Bu (Google), whose terms run from March 1, 2026 through January 31, 2027 following appointment by Platinum and Gold members [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-3c263a95].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its technical production across dedicated workstreams and collaborative repositories [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-3c263a95][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-18be1974]:

- **Threat Modeling & Gap Analysis**: Evaluates current security frameworks (OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, CSA MAESTRO, NIST AI RMF) against agentic failure modes and publishes comparative threat models [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-18be1974][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-8].
- **Security Best Practices**: Develops operational implementation baselines and threat mitigation guidelines for agentic deployments [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-18be1974].
- **Design Patterns**: Curates vendor-neutral security and privacy architectures, including hardware-isolated execution boundaries such as the [Attested Isolated Runtime](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-18be1974].
- **Taxonomy & Terminology**: Coordinates with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](taxonomy-and-landscape.md) to harmonize security, privacy, guardrail, and boundary definitions [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-18be1974].

The working group maintains its primary code and deliverable artifacts under `charter/`, `deliverables/`, and `meeting-notes/`, conducting open reviews via GitHub pull requests without blocking on [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) approval for workstream deliverables [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-3c263a95][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-18be1974].

# Lifecycle History
The working group initiated orientation in February 2026 and confirmed its mission and deliverable scope in March and April 2026 [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-18be1974]. The Technical Committee officially approved its charter in May 2026 [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-18be1974]. In June 2026, working group repositories were made public, establishing GitHub as the formal system of record alongside biweekly public meetings [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-3c263a95][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-18be1974].

proposed_concept.title: Attested Isolated Runtime
proposed_concept.description: Architectural security pattern isolating policy evaluation and evidence signing inside hardware-attested environments while leaving agent execution outside the trust boundary.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Attested Isolated Runtime is an architectural security pattern designed for agentic deployments where the host infrastructure operator is situated inside the threat model [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11]. The pattern isolates policy evaluation and evidence signing within a hardware-enforced Trusted Execution Environment (TEE), gating data release and sensitive actions on an independent verifier's appraisal while purposefully leaving the agent execution itself outside the trust boundary [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11].

By maintaining the agent outside the isolated boundary, the pattern prevents attacker-manipulated prompt or context flows from expanding the trusted computing base (TCB) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11].

# Architecture / Specification
The pattern specifies four mandatory architectural elements, each paired with a distinct failure mode if omitted [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11]:

1. **External Agent Boundary**: The policy decision point (PDP) is isolated within the hardware boundary, leaving the agent runtime outside to avoid exposing the TCB to untrusted model inputs [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11].
2. **Internal Key Generation**: Cryptographic signing keys are generated strictly inside the hardware-isolated boundary and bound to tamper-evident action evidence [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11].
3. **Measurement-Sealed Policy**: Operational policy bundles and system configurations are sealed to initial platform measurements and unsealed solely upon successful appraisal [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11].
4. **Independent Verifier Appraisal**: An external verifier appraises per-unit-of-work attestation evidence before releasing sensitive data or authorization tokens [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11].

### Implementation and Neutrality
The pattern maintains vendor neutrality by supporting diverse hardware attestation environments—including AMD SEV-SNP, Intel TDX, ARM CCA, NVIDIA GPU confidential computing, and TPM 2.0—alongside an explicit software-only fallback mode for testing and non-TEE environments [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11]. Standards alignment includes RFC 9334 (RATS architecture), RFC 9711, RFC 8747, IETF SCITT, and SLSA [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11].

# Lifecycle History
Authored by Opaque Systems, the initial draft of the Attested Isolated Runtime pattern was introduced to the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) in July/August 2026 under PR#11 to establish reference architectures for privacy-preserving execution [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-18be1974].

proposed_concept.title: Project Lifecycle Policy
proposed_concept.description: AAIF governance policy defining mandatory project proposal intake requirements, Sandbox, Growth, Impact, and Emeritus progression stages, and annual review processes.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Project Lifecycle Policy is an official governance policy of the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF), effective March 18, 2026, governing how open technical projects formally enter, progress through, and conclude within the foundation [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0]. Managed under the oversight of the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md), the policy establishes standard entry requirements, stage-specific operational expectations, and an annual review process to align projects with foundation resources and community needs [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].

# Architecture / Specification
The lifecycle framework establishes the intake workflow, maturity tiers, and evaluation processes across three functional components [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0]:

### Project Proposal Requirements
Proposals for both new and existing open-source projects must be submitted through the foundation's project proposals repository and contain comprehensive intake metadata [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0]:
- Project name, description, origin, and mission alignment with the AAIF [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].
- Adoption evidence, use cases, and relationships or integrations with existing foundation projects [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].
- Technical Committee sponsor identification, if designated [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].
- OSI-approved permissive open-source license, public repository, and public issue tracker [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].
- Automated public-facing CI/CD release mechanics, specification contribution workflows, and external dependency manifests [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].
- Documented governance structure (`GOVERNANCE.md`), leadership team decision processes, communication channels, and infrastructure requests [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].

### Progression Stages
Projects transition through formal lifecycle stages based on adoption, governance maturity, and community footprint [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0]:
- **Sandbox**: Entry point for early-stage or incubating projects undergoing initial foundation alignment and community onboarding [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].
- **Growth**: Intermediate stage for maturing projects demonstrating active contributor growth, production adoption, and stable releases [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].
- **Impact**: Highest maturity tier for flagship projects providing critical ecosystem infrastructure with broad multi-organizational governance [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].
- **Emeritus**: Terminal stage for completed, inactive, or superseded projects transitioning into archived maintenance [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].

### Annual Review Process
The Technical Committee conducts structured annual reviews across all hosted projects to assess health, adherence to foundation policies, and readiness for stage progression or reclassification [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].

# Lifecycle History
Adopted with an effective date of March 18, 2026, the policy standardizes foundation-wide onboarding and graduation tracks across all software repositories and specifications [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].

proposed_concept.title: Issue Analysis Skill
proposed_concept.description: Modular agent skill standardizing first-pass GitHub issue triage, codebase grounding, prompt injection defenses, and precedent review.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Issue Analysis skill (`issue-analysis`) equips an automated agent to generate structured first-pass assessments of filed GitHub issues for repository maintainers[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690]. Designed for the [Submission Analyser](../resources/submission-analyser.md) system, the skill classifies issue reports, evaluates operational and security severity, formulates verifiable root-cause hypotheses, and provides actionable recommendations grounded in checked-out code and repository review precedents[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690].

# Architecture / Specification
The skill operates across four primary operational phases, governed by strict sandbox and security boundaries[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690]:

1. **Untrusted Evidence Ingestion and Injection Defense**:
   - Issue text is ingested inside a nonce-delimited data block, treating all content strictly as untrusted data rather than operational instructions[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690].
   - If an issue attempts prompt injection or directive hijacking (such as commanding the agent to ignore rules, invoke external tools, dump credentials, or execute obfuscated commands), the agent flags `injectionSuspected: true` and documents the attack mechanics in `injectionNotes` while continuing technical analysis on remaining merits[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690].
   - Reporter association metadata (`OWNER`, `MEMBER`, `CONTRIBUTOR`, `NONE`) is evaluated solely to gauge technical familiarity, never as authorization to execute embedded directives[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690].

2. **Codebase Grounding**:
   - The agent inspects the local checked-out repository using read-only filesystem calls[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690].
   - Repository modifications, network egress, and build commands are strictly prohibited during analysis[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690].
   - Hypotheses must reference concrete file paths and module identifiers (such as `src/http/client.ts` or `src/config/loader.ts`) rather than abstract component names[^evt-submission-analyser-file-4754a1b8e47b-9ed9890b][^evt-submission-analyser-file-6d47851ad176-ba0f0f22].

3. **Precedent Consultation**:
   - The agent consults curated historical reviews in `references/`, evaluating frontmatter metadata (`tags`, `issue-type`, `severity`, `issue-number`)[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690].
   - The agent selects overlapping reviews and explicitly links influential precedents under `relatedPastIssues`, articulating specific shared root causes or severity rationales[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690].
   - Synthetic reference examples marked with `example: true` illustrate structural expectations (e.g., credential disclosure bypasses[^evt-submission-analyser-file-4754a1b8e47b-9ed9890b] or feature request hot-reloading[^evt-submission-analyser-file-6d47851ad176-ba0f0f22]) and are excluded from historical citation[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690].

4. **Structured Report Template**:
   Analyses follow a standardized template containing the following sections[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef]:
   - **Summary**: A single-paragraph synopsis restating the report in maintainer terms[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef].
   - **Classification**: Standardized classification covering `Type` (`bug`, `feature-request`, `documentation`, `question`, `security`, `ambiguous`), `Severity` (`critical`, `high`, `medium`, `low`, `informational`), `Reproducibility` (`reproducible`, `not-reproducible`, `insufficient-information`, `not-applicable`), and an explicit `Severity rationale`[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef].
   - **Affected components**: Concrete file paths and module identifiers[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef].
   - **Root-cause hypotheses**: Explanatory mechanisms alongside verification and refutation criteria[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef].
   - **Suggested actions**: Ordered diagnostics, files to inspect, and maintainer follow-ups[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef].
   - **Open questions**: Missing contextual or environmental questions for the reporter[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef].
   - **Related past reviews**: Explicit references to historical review documents that informed the evaluation[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef].

# Lifecycle History
Authored and merged within the `aaif/submission-analyser` repository under Apache-2.0 to provide automated triage support for AAIF project maintainers[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Submission Analyser is an automated, headless triage agent running within GitHub Actions that evaluates newly submitted repository issues[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690]. Leveraging the [Issue Analysis Skill](../skills/issue-analysis.md), the system ingests filed issues, grounds claims against checked-out source code, detects adversarial prompt injections, and generates structured triage syntheses for project maintainers[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690].

# Architecture / Specification
The Submission Analyser integrates defensive runtime isolation with an extensive adversarial test fixture suite:
- **Execution Boundaries**: The agent operates as a read-only analysis process within continuous integration, disallowing repository mutations, build execution, or unauthorized network calls[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690].
- **Untrusted Input Noncing**: Inbound issue bodies are wrapped within nonce-delimited blocks to ensure that external markdown content cannot break parsing boundaries or masquerade as operational commands[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690].
- **Adversarial Injection Evaluation**: The agent's defense mechanisms are evaluated against automated test fixtures designed to stress prompt boundaries, including:
  - *Mass Mention Hijacking*: Attempts to force the agent to reproduce notification pings such as `@everyone`, `@here`, or specific channel/user IDs to cause notification spam[^evt-submission-analyser-file-04ecd65ab81f-33714e60].
  - *Obfuscated Directives*: Payloads encoding instruction overrides in Base64 strings, ROT13 ciphers, or Cyrillic homoglyphs designed to evade static keyword filters[^evt-submission-analyser-file-0f27825af60d-1d3aca33].
- **Triage Output Generation**: Upon evaluating an issue, the analyser populates an analysis template documenting classification, concrete components, and root causes, while logging injection attempts via dedicated `injectionSuspected` telemetry[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690][^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef].

# Lifecycle History
Maintained by the AAIF as part of the `aaif/submission-analyser` repository, implementing automated triage and prompt injection security regression testing for project workflows[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Submission Analyser is a headless triage agent executing in GitHub Actions that inspects issue submissions against codebase guidelines while validating processing pipelines against adversarial prompt injection test suites.

# Architecture / Specification

The analyser's test suite establishes regression fixtures across multiple prompt injection vectors:
- Direct instruction overrides attempting system prompt extraction and behavioral replacement[^evt-submission-analyser-file-297ef7f1b871-f950e3d6].
- Synthetic tool calls and function invocation tags attempting unauthorized command execution and data exfiltration[^evt-submission-analyser-file-2e092a0c54ea-4363d97f].
- Hidden HTML comments embedding privileged directives to suppress injection alerts and manipulate severity classifications[^evt-submission-analyser-file-305b7ba8fb0c-d60ec9fe].
- Obfuscated Unicode bidirectional markers paired with persona-adoption and role-play evasion framing[^evt-submission-analyser-file-7385a2d6a676-148647ca].
- External link dereferencing instructions directing the agent to retrieve secondary adversarial payloads[^evt-submission-analyser-file-7cf6ee468c96-f0fe2bdd].
- Nested collapsed markup, platform mentions, and simulated approval text crafted to bypass sanitation filters[^evt-submission-analyser-file-a072a88a60fa-f5eaa4ea].

These automated fixtures validate triage safety boundaries defined in [Agentic AI Security Best Practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md) and support standardized [Issue Analysis](../skills/issue-analysis.md) workflows.

proposed_concept.title: Goose Reference Architecture
proposed_concept.description: Reference architecture for Goose, an open-source general-purpose AI agent runtime with built-in telemetry, security scanning, MCP, and ACP extensibility.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Goose is an open-source, general-purpose AI agent runtime that executes multi-turn tool workflows driven by large language models, providing integrated telemetry collection, security filtering, and permission management.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ebe69a7a8f5d-31c4429c] It operates as a local service binding desktop or terminal interfaces to language model providers and local extension processes using the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and [Agent Client Protocol](../standards/agent-client-protocol.md).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ebe69a7a8f5d-31c4429c]

# Architecture / Specification
The Goose architecture operates at the system runtime layer and is partitioned across user interfaces, a centralized daemon server, and an extensible agent core.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ebe69a7a8f5d-31c4429c]

## Interface Layer
Goose supports multiple client surfaces interacting with the underlying daemon:
- **CLI (`goose-cli`)**: Terminal interface communicating over REST and Server-Sent Events (SSE).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ebe69a7a8f5d-31c4429c]
- **Desktop Application**: Electron-based interface connecting to the daemon over local REST and SSE endpoints.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ebe69a7a8f5d-31c4429c]
- **ACP Clients**: Direct editor integrations (such as JetBrains and Zed) connecting via the [Agent Client Protocol](../standards/agent-client-protocol.md) over standard input/output (stdio).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ebe69a7a8f5d-31c4429c]

## Server Daemon (`goosed`)
The core service is implemented in Rust using an Axum HTTP router, exposing endpoints for session management (`/session`), reply streaming (`/reply`), event broadcasting (`/session_events`), configuration, recipes, scheduling, telemetry, and MCP proxies.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ebe69a7a8f5d-31c4429c] State persistence relies on an embedded SQLite database managed through `sqlx`.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ebe69a7a8f5d-31c4429c]

## Agent Core and Execution Loop
The agent core coordinates:
- **Provider Manager**: Interfaces with over 15 language model providers using API keys or OAuth credentials.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ebe69a7a8f5d-31c4429c]
- **Permission Inspector**: Evaluates tool calls against configured user authorization policies.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ebe69a7a8f5d-31c4429c]
- **Security Manager**: Combines regex pattern filtering with machine learning scanners to detect prompt injection and dangerous invocations prior to tool execution.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ebe69a7a8f5d-31c4429c]
- **Execution Loop**: Handles iterative request cycles, subagent delegation, context compaction, and MCP extension invocation over stdio or SSE transports.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ebe69a7a8f5d-31c4429c]

## Observability and Telemetry
Goose emits native distributed tracing and telemetry:
- **OpenTelemetry Export**: Emits hierarchical spans (`agent_reply`, `provider_chat`, and `tool_execution`) over OTLP HTTP/protobuf to an [OpenTelemetry](../resources/opentelemetry.md) collector.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ebe69a7a8f5d-31c4429c]
- **Langfuse Integration**: Direct integration with [Langfuse](../resources/langfuse.md) captures generation traces, token metrics, and multi-turn execution graphs.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ebe69a7a8f5d-31c4429c]

# References
- AAIF Working Group Observability and Traceability repository: https://github.com/aaif/wg-observability-and-traceability
- Goose source repository: https://github.com/aaif-goose/goose

proposed_concept.title: Linux Device Driver Tracing Reference Architecture
proposed_concept.description: Kernel-level device driver observability architecture combining structured logging, dynamic debug, tracepoints, and bus-level tracers.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Linux device driver tracing encompasses the subsystem instrumentation and observability mechanisms exposed by the Linux kernel for device driver development, diagnostics, and production runtime troubleshooting.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-633832607329-9b56d321] Positioned between generic kernel tracing infrastructures (such as [Ftrace](../resources/ftrace.md), [Linux perf](../resources/linux-perf.md), and [LTTng](../resources/lttng-kernel.md)) and hardware-specific diagnostic tooling, driver tracing establishes visibility into device initialization, control bus exchanges, interrupt handling, and hardware state transitions.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-633832607329-9b56d321]

# Architecture / Specification
The driver tracing architecture spans five distinct instrumentation layers within the Linux kernel (version 4.19+ and 6.x).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-633832607329-9b56d321]

## Instrumentation Mechanisms
- **Structured Device Logging**: Kernel macros (`dev_dbg`, `dev_info`, `dev_warn`, `dev_err`) prefix messages with device, bus, and driver identifiers to provide context-aware dmesg and journald logs.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-633832607329-9b56d321]
- **Dynamic Debug (`dyndbg`)**: Configured via `CONFIG_DYNAMIC_DEBUG=y`, this mechanism allows selective runtime enabling of debug call sites per module, file, function, or line number via `/sys/kernel/debug/dynamic_debug/control` with near-zero overhead when disabled.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-633832607329-9b56d321]
- **Custom Driver Tracepoints (`TRACE_EVENT`)**: Static kernel tracepoints defined within driver headers export structured binary event records into `tracefs` without string formatting overhead, enabling consumption by tools such as `trace-cmd` and [perf](../resources/linux-perf.md).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-633832607329-9b56d321]
- **Bus and Subsystem Monitors**: Specialized monitoring interfaces (e.g., `usbmon` for USB protocol exchanges, `blktrace` for block I/O requests) capture bus-specific packet streams for offline or live inspection.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-633832607329-9b56d321]
- **Diagnostic File Systems and Crash Dumps**: `debugfs` endpoints expose internal driver state variables and hardware counters, while `devcoredump` captures ephemeral crash states when device hardware fails.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-633832607329-9b56d321]

## Runtime Interfaces and Prerequisites
Instrumentation requires kernel configuration options `CONFIG_DYNAMIC_DEBUG=y`, `CONFIG_DEBUG_FS=y`, and `CONFIG_TRACEPOINTS=y`, with `debugfs` mounted at `/sys/kernel/debug` and `tracefs` mounted at `/sys/kernel/tracing`.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-633832607329-9b56d321]

# References
- AAIF Working Group Observability and Traceability repository: https://github.com/aaif/wg-observability-and-traceability

proposed_concept.description: Headless triage agent executing in GitHub Actions that analyses repository issues and validates resilience against prompt injection attacks.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Submission Analyser is a headless triage agent deployed within GitHub Actions workflows to evaluate repository issue submissions, extract operational metadata, and assess incoming content against adversarial prompt injection attempts.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-c385a440d3d1-196a4a61] It integrates explicit automated test suites evaluating adversarial input vectors designed to manipulate automated agent reasoning.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-e761e6213598-a8166ad6]

# Architecture / Specification
The submission analyser incorporates automated testing fixtures located in `tests/fixtures/injections/` to validate runtime resilience against multi-vector prompt injection strategies:[^evt-submission-analyser-file-c385a440d3d1-196a4a61]

## Injection Test Categories
- **Environment Exfiltration**: Fixtures that simulate requests to leak sensitive runtime secrets (such as GitHub tokens, API keys, or service account credentials) into public issue summaries, external communication webhooks, or obfuscated component fields.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-c385a440d3d1-196a4a61]
- **Fake Authority and Priority Overrides**: Fixtures attempting to bypass egress controls and inspection banners by spoofing system prompts, maintainer identities, or platform safety teams.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-fdb9d913d85d-8ad69d31]
- **Delimiter Forging**: Attacks employing forged XML/markdown delimiter tags (such as fake system prompts and closing tags) to trick the model into interpreting untrusted issue text as privileged system directives.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-f4ad28ba849d-48065e61]
- **Authority and Urgency Simulation**: Attacks impersonating governance or security entities (such as Linux Foundation security teams) using coercive policy threats to force configuration disclosure and exfiltration.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-e761e6213598-a8166ad6]

## Operational Safeguards
The analyser implements boundary protections separating untrusted issue bodies from privileged execution contexts, preventing credential leakage and ensuring suspected injections are flagged prior to downstream workflow triggers.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-fdb9d913d85d-8ad69d31]

# References
- AAIF Submission Analyser repository: https://github.com/aaif/submission-analyser

proposed_concept.title: Submission Analyser
proposed_concept.description: Headless triage agent executing in GitHub Actions that analyses repository issues and publishes assessments to Google Drive and Discord under strict privilege boundaries.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Submission Analyser (`submission-analyser`) is an open-source headless triage agent runtime designed to inspect GitHub issues filed in external repositories, conduct codebase grounding via the Flue agent harness, and publish analytical summaries to isolated channels (Google Docs and Discord) without holding repository write permissions [^evt-submission-analyser-file-6ae19f00f4c0-5634c5c6]. It operates across a hardened cross-repository trust boundary, enforcing privilege separation against adversarial public issue inputs [^evt-submission-analyser-file-9fd5455b8db0-50f35660].

The agent addresses the core security challenge where untrusted user input from public GitHub issues is read by an LLM with shell access to a repository checkout [^evt-submission-analyser-file-6ae19f00f4c0-5634c5c6]. To neutralize prompt injection and workflow hijacking risks, the system completely disallows repository write tokens, disallowing any write-back into target or tooling repositories [^evt-submission-analyser-file-cbe7142ed7e3-716e943f].

# Architecture / Specification

### Cross-Repository Dispatch Boundary

The analyser executes from a centralized tooling repository and evaluates issues submitted in separate target repositories [^evt-submission-analyser-file-6ae19f00f4c0-5634c5c6]. Execution is triggered via `workflow_dispatch` over the GitHub REST API rather than `repository_dispatch` [^evt-submission-analyser-file-9fd5455b8db0-50f35660]:
- **Target Dispatch Token**: Target repositories hold an `ANALYST_DISPATCH_TOKEN` with fine-grained `Actions: write` scope restricted strictly to the analyst repository. This grants permission to queue an analysis run without granting `Contents: write`, preventing target repository maintainers or compromised tokens from pushing code or mutating analyst workflow definitions [^evt-submission-analyser-file-9fd5455b8db0-50f35660].
- **Trigger Filtering**: Workflows initiate either on issue `opened` or when maintainers apply a `needs-analysis` label, filtering out bot-submitted issues to preserve runner and model inference budgets [^evt-submission-analyser-file-9fd5455b8db0-50f35660].
- **Input Sanitization**: Dispatched inputs (`issue_number` as digits, `target_repo` as `owner/repo`) are strictly asserted prior to command execution [^evt-submission-analyser-file-cbe7142ed7e3-716e943f].

### Token Isolation and Egress Paths

The GitHub Actions workflow (`issue-analyst.yml`) enforces strict credential compartmentalization [^evt-submission-analyser-file-cbe7142ed7e3-716e943f]:
- **Permissions**: Configured strictly with `contents: read` and `copilot-requests: write`. No `issues: write` or pull request write capabilities are provisioned [^evt-submission-analyser-file-cbe7142ed7e3-716e943f].
- **Model Entitlement**: Inference access relies on the ambient `GITHUB_TOKEN` requesting GitHub Copilot model endpoints under `copilot-requests: write`, obviating the need to store third-party model vendor API keys [^evt-submission-analyser-file-973b5680342c-d651657e].
- **Publishing Egress**: Analytical outputs bypass git storage, publishing directly to Google Drive via a dedicated `GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON` and emitting notifications via `DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL` [^evt-submission-analyser-file-973b5680342c-d651657e].

### Supply Chain Hardening and Offline CI

All external GitHub Actions steps are pinned to immutable 40-character commit SHAs with trailing version documentation to mitigate mutable tag supply chain attacks [^evt-submission-analyser-file-b803fcb7f17e-c4652926]. The offline CI pipeline (`ci.yml`) runs entirely without secrets (`permissions: contents: read`), executing validation through `FLUE_FAUX=1 flue run ... --json` against in-memory mock providers to enforce schema conformance and skill validation prior to deployment [^evt-submission-analyser-file-b803fcb7f17e-c4652926].

# References

- Skill execution logic: [../skills/issue-analysis.md](../skills/issue-analysis.md)
- Architectural governance split: [../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md)
