proposed_concept.title: Issue Analysis
proposed_concept.description: Modular agent skill standardizing first-pass GitHub issue triage, codebase grounding, and precedent retrieval across structured reference analyses.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Issue Analysis skill (`issue-analysis`) is a modular agent skill executed within the [../resources/submission-analyser.md](../resources/submission-analyser.md) runtime to perform automated first-pass triage and deep technical assessment of GitHub issues [^evt-submission-analyser-file-562ca4e251fc-8c9734e5]. It grounds agent reasoning in project-specific historical precedents using an indexed reference corpus of past analyses [^evt-submission-analyser-file-562ca4e251fc-8c9734e5].

During execution, the skill balances broad issue interpretation against project conventions by loading relevant historical precedents into model context and preventing prompt injection vulnerabilities from unvetted issue text [^evt-submission-analyser-file-562ca4e251fc-8c9734e5].

# Architecture / Specification

### Reference Corpus and Precedent Matching

The skill incorporates an extensible reference directory (`src/skills/issue-analysis/references/`) containing validated hand-written historical assessments [^evt-submission-analyser-file-562ca4e251fc-8c9734e5]:
- **Metadata Inspection**: The skill reads the YAML frontmatter of every file in the reference corpus without loading full bodies immediately [^evt-submission-analyser-file-562ca4e251fc-8c9734e5]. Frontmatter attributes include `issue-number`, `date`, `issue-type`, `severity`, `tags`, and `components` [^evt-submission-analyser-file-562ca4e251fc-8c9734e5].
- **Relevance Retrieval**: The agent matches reporter keywords against `tags` and `components`, selecting the 3–5 most relevant documents to read in full into working context [^evt-submission-analyser-file-562ca4e251fc-8c9734e5].
- **Synthetic vs. Real Baselines**: Synthetic examples (`example: true`) provide structural formatting baselines for unit testing and CI but are explicitly excluded from being cited as legal or operational precedent during actual triage [^evt-submission-analyser-file-562ca4e251fc-8c9734e5].

### Frontmatter Validation and Build Integration

Skill metadata and frontmatter constraints are strictly enforced at load time [^evt-submission-analyser-file-b803fcb7f17e-c4652926]:
- In Flue 2.0, skill loading via `flue run` serves as the primary validation gate, rejecting malformed frontmatter and exiting with code 1 before any model inference or tool dispatch occurs [^evt-submission-analyser-file-b803fcb7f17e-c4652926].
- Offline verification harnesses test skill mounting and execution paths with zero secrets using mock in-memory providers [^evt-submission-analyser-file-b803fcb7f17e-c4652926].

### Data Sanitization and Committing Rules

Because corpus entries are loaded into LLM prompts and quoted in published Google Docs and Discord alerts, contributors must audit candidate reference files prior to committing [^evt-submission-analyser-file-562ca4e251fc-8c9734e5]. The guidelines strictly prohibit committing customer names, internal infrastructure hostnames, credentials, unreleased roadmap commitments, or details under active security embargos [^evt-submission-analyser-file-562ca4e251fc-8c9734e5].

# References

- Harness and runtime environment: [../resources/submission-analyser.md](../resources/submission-analyser.md)
- Packaging specification: [../standards/agent-skills.md](../standards/agent-skills.md)

proposed_concept.title: Submission Analyser
proposed_concept.description: Headless triage agent executing in GitHub Actions that analyses repository issues and publishes assessments using GitHub Copilot model credentials.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Submission Analyser is a headless triage agent deployed in GitHub Actions workflows to parse and assess incoming repository issues against codebase documentation.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-4a20043f76a6-7597f83c] The runtime executes via Flue and restricts model inference strictly to GitHub Copilot endpoints to prevent accidental data disclosure to unauthorized third-party model vendors.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-4a20043f76a6-7597f83c]

# Architecture / Specification

## Model Specifier Validation
Model endpoints are configured using the format `<provider-id>/<model-id>`, where version numbers strictly use dots instead of dashes (for example, `github-copilot/claude-opus-4.7` and `github-copilot/gpt-5.4`).[^evt-submission-analyser-file-4a20043f76a6-7597f83c] Runtime initialization strictly validates that specifiers consist of two non-empty segments and enforces that `provider-id` is `github-copilot`, preventing repository variable overrides from silently invoking unapproved alternative providers.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-4a20043f76a6-7597f83c]

## Copilot Credential and Token Exchange
Direct requests bearing standard Personal Access Tokens (PATs) or Actions server-to-server tokens are rejected by Copilot inference backends with HTTP 400 errors.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-4a20043f76a6-7597f83c] Valid model access requires exchanging an authenticated GitHub token at `https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token` for a short-lived Copilot bearer token.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-4a20043f76a6-7597f83c] In GitHub Actions, the workflow's built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN` is granted `copilot-requests: write` permissions, entitling Copilot requests billed to the repository organization without granting broader repository write access.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-31e1ac583aa4-9cc8bb73][^evt-submission-analyser-file-4a20043f76a6-7597f83c]

## Entitlement Probing Workflow
A manual diagnostic workflow (`probe-copilot.yml`) allows maintainers to validate Copilot entitlement and host connectivity without invoking model inference or incurring usage charges.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-31e1ac583aa4-9cc8bb73] The probe executes read-only listing requests and strips credential strings from logs to ensure sensitive bearer tokens are not leaked into issue reports.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-31e1ac583aa4-9cc8bb73]

# References
- Model specification and Copilot credential exchange in `docs/models.md`.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-4a20043f76a6-7597f83c]
- Automated Copilot entitlement check workflow in `.github/workflows/probe-copilot.yml`.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-31e1ac583aa4-9cc8bb73]

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing vendor-neutral agent telemetry standards, cross-boundary trace correlation, and full-stack observability layers.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body developing vendor-neutral specifications, semantic conventions, and reference architectures for AI agent telemetry.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512] The group focuses on end-to-end full-stack observability, bridging gaps between application-layer tracing and lower-level execution environments.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512]

# Architecture / Specification

## Five-Layer Observability Stack
The working group evaluates agent observability through a five-layer architectural model covering hardware accelerators, CPU and operating system layers, network infrastructure, runtime execution frameworks, and application-level agent interactions.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512] The working group notes that existing frameworks like OpenTelemetry primarily target application-level behavior (Layer 5), leaving lower-level hardware, network dynamics, and multi-turn session replay unaddressed in current tooling.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512]

## Focus Groups and Core Workstreams
Technical initiatives are structured across several collaborative tracks:
- **Protocols and Primitives**: Standardizing observability across agent communication boundaries, remote procedure calls, and infrastructure contracts.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512]
- **State, Context, and Reasoning**: Designing telemetry capturing agent memory, reasoning trees, dynamic rule-based verification, and cryptographic audit artifacts such as Merkle link graphs.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512]
- **Agent Behavior Trace Model**: Addressing semantic gaps in agent frameworks, specifically around session identification, causality, and execution replay.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512]
- **Observability Taxonomy**: Defining and reviewing core observability terms across foundation working groups.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512]

# References
- Observability and Traceability Working Group meeting minutes, August 19, 2026.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512]

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Project Proposal Process
proposed_concept.description: Operating procedure establishing the intake, review, voting, and onboarding workflow for open-source projects joining the Agentic AI Foundation.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The AAIF Project Proposal Process is the standardized operational procedure implementing the [AAIF Project Lifecycle Policy](../policies/project-lifecycle-policy.md) for proposing, reviewing, approving, and onboarding open-source projects into the Agentic AI Foundation[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a]. It establishes six sequential steps, one parallel legal track, and an optional on-demand presentation window, designed primarily for asynchronous, offline execution across a distributed Technical Committee[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].

# Architecture / Specification

## Governance Roles and Responsibilities

The operating procedure defines specific obligations across foundation roles[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a]:

- **Project Submitter**: Files the project proposal, addresses Technical Committee inquiries on GitHub during Step 2, conducts on-demand presentations if requested, completes contributor agreements, and executes technical onboarding.
- **CTO**: Owns Step 1 intake triage, screens proposals for completeness and charter alignment, conducts smoke tests assisted by the intake agent, and compiles TC briefs. Approves Q&A extensions and invokes the on-demand TC supporter mechanism when engagement thresholds are missed.
- **Intake Agent**: Automated triage agent executing two advisory functions on new proposals: a public technical compliance assessment posted to the GitHub issue, and a private advisory evaluation sent to TC members.
- **TC Chairs**: Review proposals during initial intake and appoint an on-demand TC supporter if the Step 2 engagement bar is not met.
- **TC Supporter (On-Demand)**: A Technical Committee member designated only when broad committee engagement fails to meet the required bar, responsible for championing the proposal through an extended Q&A window.
- **Technical Committee**: Exercises collective oversight during the Step 2 Q&A window, requests presentations if needed, and casts formal admission votes in Step 3.
- **Governing Board**: Evaluates foundation resource implications and organizational readiness, casting the final admission vote in Step 4.
- **LF PMO, Legal, and IT**: PMO tracks ticket state and schedules; LF Legal coordinates contribution agreements, charters, and trademark transfers in Step 5; LF IT assumes repository infrastructure and access management in Step 6.

## Sequential Lifecycle Steps

1. **Step 1 - Initial Intake (Offline)**: The CTO screens submissions with automated assistance from the intake agent, gathering TC chair input and issuing an advisory compliance check[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].
2. **Step 2 - TC Q&A Window (Offline)**: An asynchronous review window on GitHub requiring a minimum engagement bar across multiple TC members rather than relying on a single pre-assigned champion[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].
   - *Optional Presentation (Live)*: Scheduled on demand if requested by a TC member.
   - *On-Demand Supporter*: Invoked by TC chairs if the engagement bar is not reached; if no supporter volunteers, the proposal is rejected.
3. **Parallel Step - Contributor Paperwork (Offline)**: Submitter completes contributor and licensing agreements concurrently with technical review.
4. **Step 3 - TC Vote (Offline)**: Technical Committee conducts a formal admission and stage assignment vote via LFX Vote[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].
5. **Step 4 - GB Approval (Offline)**: Governing Board votes on foundation admission and resource allocation via LFX Vote[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].
6. **Step 5 - Legal Formation (Offline)**: LF Legal and AAIF staff execute contribution agreements, technical charters, and trademark transfers via DocuSign[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].
7. **Step 6 - Technical Onboarding (Offline)**: Submitter and LF IT transfer repository ownership, CI/CD pipelines, and domain assets[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].

# Lifecycle History

- **v0.3 (2026-08-28)**: Formalized six-step workflow with offline-default execution, replaced single-champion requirement with committee-wide engagement bar, introduced automated intake agent role, and structured on-demand supporter fallback[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Observability Use Cases
proposed_concept.description: Comprehensive catalog defining multi-category agent observability use cases, cross-cutting telemetry requirements, and compliance audit frameworks.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agent Observability Use Cases catalog defines core operational, performance, diagnostic, and compliance scenarios governing telemetry collection for agentic AI systems[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-30]. Maintained by the [Observability & Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), the catalog establishes concrete evaluation criteria and telemetry requirements across agent execution boundaries, informing standards such as the [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-30].

# Architecture / Specification

## Safety and Compliance Category

The safety, governance, and regulatory compliance workstream categorizes observability requirements needed to verify agent operation against legal, policy, and organizational boundaries:

- **E1–E3 Compliance Cluster**: Telemetry capturing safety violations, prompt injection attempts, guardrail interventions, and policy drift across model invocations.
- **Use Case E4 - Tamper-Evident Evidence for Audit and Dispute Resolution**: Addresses the requirement for regulated organizations to prove to auditors, regulatory bodies, or legal courts what an autonomous agent executed[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-30]. Core technical capabilities include:
  - **Cryptographic Audit Trails**: Merkle-chained, digitally signed execution event logs ensuring non-repudiation and detection of retroactive alterations[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-30].
  - **Write-Once Storage and Timestamping**: Immutable Write Once Read Many (WORM) storage paired with RFC 3161 trusted timestamping authorities[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-30].
  - **Approval Chain & Intent Linkage**: Explicit binding between declared intent, human or automated approval tokens, and observed runtime tool executions[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-30].
  - **Evidence-Grade Ladder**: Grounding observability records in formal evidence tiers ranging from self-declared claims (E0 Declared) through externally anchored cryptographic proofs (E4 Anchored), referencing models such as WitnessOS and EU AI Act compliance ladders[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-30].

proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing vendor-neutral agent telemetry standards, cross-boundary trace models, and tamper-evident audit evidence.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability and Traceability Working Group is an AAIF technical body focused on vendor-neutral telemetry specifications, distributed tracing conventions, and tamper-evident audit records across agent runtimes, protocol gateways, and tool boundaries[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-2][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-30]. The group operates as a cross-industry coordination forum rather than an isolated standards body, aligning agent telemetry with existing distributed tracing and observability specifications[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-11].

# Architecture / Specification

## Scope and Coordination Strategy

The working group's charter defines key technical deliverables and collaboration vectors[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-2][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-11]:

- **Agent Behavior Trace Model**: Standardizing context propagation, causal graph linking, and execution state telemetry via [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md).
- **Audit and Tamper-Evidence**: Defining cryptographic logging criteria, Merkle-chain verification, and evidence-strength ladders for regulated environments via [Agent Observability Use Cases](../resources/agent-observability-use-cases.md)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-30].
- **External Standards Liaisons**: Active coordination tracking with OpenTelemetry GenAI Semantic Conventions, OWASP AI Observability Standards (AOS), W3C Trace Context, Model Context Protocol (MCP), AGNTCY, and Monocle[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-11].
- **Internal AAIF Alignment**: Regular intake tracking and bidirectional coordination with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) and related functional working groups[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-11].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-04-15**: Working group formally approved charter (`CHARTER.md`) and submitted for AAIF [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) review[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-2].
- **2026-04-21**: Formal submission to Technical Committee for review and stage confirmation[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-2].

proposed_concept.description: Production workflow repository classifying real-world agent deployments across verified multi-tiered capability tiers and standardized activity schemas.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic Use Case Inventory is a curated catalog of production agent implementations maintained by the [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-32]. It standardizes real-world enterprise deployments across distinct capability tiers, interaction boundaries, and execution models, providing concrete operational baselines for workflow architecture patterns[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-32].

# Architecture / Specification

## Structural Schema and Terminology

The inventory documents agentic workflows using structured schema conventions aligned with the core taxonomy[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-32]:

- **Activity-Based Decomposition**: Workflows decompose into distinct **activities** rather than generic procedural steps, directly aligning use-case definitions with foundational taxonomy terms and execution primitives[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-32].
- **Capability Tiers**: Workflows map against tiered autonomy and supervision levels, distinguishing single-agent deterministic task execution from multi-agent collaborative workflows.
- **Boundary Contracts**: Each workflow activity specifies input schemas, required tool access, human review checkpoints, and boundary validation criteria.

mutations.rationale: Update the Proposal/Execution Split architectural pattern with its core problem definition, tripartite separation of intent, authorization, and execution, and mandatory failure invariants.

proposed_concept.title: Proposal/Execution Split
proposed_concept.description: Architectural governance pattern separating intent generation, authorization, and workflow execution into distinct roles with independent audit records.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Proposal/Execution Split is an architectural governance pattern that enforces authorization and attribution at the protected-effect boundary when intent originates from a probabilistic AI agent[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-5b43d950]. Because a probabilistic actor cannot provide non-repudiation or deterministic policy guarantees, the pattern mandates that intent generation, authorization, and execution must belong to distinct roles, each maintaining separate audit records[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-5b43d950].

This pattern is foundational to reference architectures such as [Single-Agent Human Approval](../architectures/single-agent-human-approval.md) and [Bounded Autonomous Remediation](../architectures/bounded-autonomous-remediation.md), and coordinates directly with patterns like the [Human Approval Gate](human-approval-gate.md) and [Durable Wait](durable-wait.md)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-5b43d950].

# Architecture / Specification

The pattern establishes three distinct separations across the lifecycle of an action[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-5b43d950]:

1. **Proposer (Agent)**: Generates a proposal as immutable structured data. The agent proposes data, never an executable action, and possesses no direct invocation path to downstream systems of record.
2. **Authorization Authority**: A human principal or versioned policy engine evaluates whether that exact proposal may proceed. Authorization binds strictly to the exact proposal payload.
3. **Executor (System)**: A workflow-controlled component executes the authorized proposal upon receiving explicit approval evidence. The executor is isolated from direct agent interaction.

```text
  proposer (agent)            authorization authority       executor (system)
        │                             │                            │
        ▼                             ▼                            ▼
   proposal ─────────► gate: authorize this exact ─ yes ─► workflow-controlled
   (immutable data,         proposal?                      execution of the
    not an action)            │                            authorized proposal
                              └─ no / invalid ──► terminal or     │
                                 recovery path                    ▼
                                                                effect
  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    system of record: proposal · authority + decision evidence · effect
```

### Core Invariants

Implementations must satisfy critical invariants[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-5b43d950]:
- **Fail Closed**: In the absence, expiration, or failure of an authorization decision, the gate fails closed and prevents execution.
- **Payload Immutability**: What executes must match *exactly* what was authorized; mutations or drift invalidate authorization.
- **Separate Audit Logging**: Intent, authorization evidence, and execution effect are logged independently to preserve non-repudiation and clear attribution of authority.
- **Idempotency**: Retried workflow executions must avoid duplicate side effects.

# Lifecycle History

Documented as a core reference architecture pattern by the Workflows and Process Integration Working Group[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-5b43d950].

mutations.rationale: Update workflow taxonomy primitives with the WG-approved decision to standardize on Activity instead of Step, incorporating core foundational, control, and coordination terms.

proposed_concept.title: Workflow Primitives
proposed_concept.description: Foundational vocabulary and structural execution primitives defined by the Workflows and Process Integration Working Group, centered on Activities and Workflows.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Workflow Primitives define the core structural concepts and operational vocabulary established by the Workflows and Process Integration Working Group to model agentic workflows, execution lifecycles, and system coordination[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f]. Central to this taxonomy is the replacement of terms like "step" or "task" with **Activity**, preventing circular definitions and establishing clear boundaries between individual tasks and structured multi-activity execution[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-31].

# Architecture / Specification

The primitives are structured across several conceptual layers[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f]:

### Foundational Concepts
- **Activity**: A single, bounded task with defined inputs and outputs that can be tracked to completion[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f][^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-31].
- **Workflow**: The primary unit of structured, multi-activity work with a defined goal and outcome. A workflow is composed of one or more activities, their relationships, and the execution logic required to achieve that outcome[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f].
- **Workflow Execution**: A runtime instance of a workflow definition, maintaining its own execution state and lifecycle independently of other concurrent instances[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f].
- **Workflow State**: The data representing the condition of a workflow execution at a specific point in time, including progress tracking and continuation requirements[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f].
- **Workflow Context**: The shared information available to workflow participants during execution, informing decisions across activities and workflow boundaries[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f].

### Execution & Control
- **Control Flow**: The logic that determines activity ordering, conditions, branching, iteration, parallelism, and synchronization[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f].
- **Trigger**: An event, signal, schedule, condition, or request initiating or advancing a workflow execution[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f].
- **Durability**: The property of preserving workflow execution state across interruptions and infrastructure failures without loss of progress[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f].
- **Determinism**: The property ensuring a workflow produces identical execution behavior given identical inputs, state, and history[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f].

### Coordination Models
- **Orchestration**: Centralized coordination directing activity dispatch and evaluation.
- **Choreography**: Decentralized coordination where activities interact via direct peer signaling without a central controller.
- **Composition**: Combining existing workflows and activities into higher-order operational units.

# Lifecycle History

The Workflows and Process Integration Working Group adopted "Activity" to replace "Workflow Step / Workflow Task" in PR #31, standardizing independent task definitions before workflow composition[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-31].

proposed_concept.title: Project Lifecycle Policy
proposed_concept.description: AAIF governance policy defining mandatory project proposal intake requirements, Sandbox, Growth, and Impact progression stages.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Project Lifecycle Policy governs the intake, graduation, and governance stages of open-source software, standards, and specification projects hosted within the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF)[^evt-technical-committee-pr-9]. Overseen by the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md), it establishes explicit operational criteria, contributor diversity expectations, and maturity benchmarks for projects progressing from entry-level incubation through graduation[^evt-technical-committee-pr-9].

# Architecture / Specification

The project lifecycle is organized into tiered progression stages[^evt-technical-committee-pr-9]:

- **Sandbox Stage**: Entry-level stage facilitating rapid experimentation, initial community formation, and open development under AAIF intellectual property policies.
- **Growth Stage**: Intermediate stage for projects demonstrating sustained adoption, active multi-organizational contribution, structured release cadences, and robust governance models.
- **Impact Stage**: Mature stage for production-grade flagship technologies that demonstrate wide industry deployment, security audit compliance, and strict vendor neutrality.

The Technical Committee streamlined the lifecycle by tightening Growth stage criteria and removing redundant proposal and acceptance phrasing while formally establishing the Sandbox stage[^evt-technical-committee-pr-9].

# Lifecycle History

Updated via Technical Committee PR #9 to formalize the Sandbox tier, tighten Growth stage criteria, and eliminate redundant proposal intake language[^evt-technical-committee-pr-9].

proposed_concept.title: Accuracy and Reliability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing failure taxonomies, evaluation benchmarks, and recovery specifications for agentic systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Accuracy and Reliability Working Group (ARWG) is an AAIF technical working group dedicated to defining failure taxonomies, evaluation benchmarks, and recovery specifications for agentic systems[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-922f59c26329-135870e7]. Co-chaired by Jordan Auge (Cisco) and Casper Nielsen (Diagrid), the group investigates failure modes such as hallucination, non-determinism, and context exhaustion, and develops standardized metrics to appraise autonomous reasoning and recovery[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-922f59c26329-135870e7].

# Architecture / Specification

The working group executes against multiple core deliverables[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-922f59c26329-135870e7]:

- **D1 (Terminology and Taxonomy)**: Developing foundational accuracy and failure terminology batches for contribution to the shared [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](taxonomy-and-landscape.md). Under review in PR #8.
- **D2 (Gap Analysis and Survey Support)**: Conducting empirical gap analyses backed by the [Accuracy and Reliability Survey](../resources/accuracy-and-reliability-survey.md) (under review in PR #9). The survey targets practitioners with firsthand agent-system deployment experience across pain points and operational experimentation.
- **Phase 2 Deliverables & Cross-WG Coordination**: Engaging sibling working groups and progressing internal deliverables to establish cross-foundation reliability baselines.

# Lifecycle History

In August 2026, the working group consolidated review feedback across PR #8 (D1 terminology) and PR #9 (D2 survey specification), seeking Technical Committee support for broad survey outreach across practitioner communities[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-922f59c26329-135870e7].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic Commerce Working Group is an AAIF technical body developing vendor-neutral capability maps, protocol gap analyses, and reference architectures for autonomous agent-driven transactions, discovery, and post-purchase operations[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-6]. Its work spans [Agentic Checkout](../taxonomy/agentic-checkout.md), [Delegated Payment](../taxonomy/delegated-payment.md), and interoperability across protocols such as UCP, ACP, AP2, and x402[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-6].

# Architecture / Specification

The working group's scope is organized around core deliverables[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-6]:

- **Deliverable 1 (Agentic Commerce Capability Map)**: A comprehensive capability matrix spanning discovery, checkout, payment, and post-purchase workflows. Proposed additions (P1–P7) cover eligibility inquiries, remedy negotiation, consent evidence, state-change execution signals, dispute initiation, and adjustment ledgers.
- **Machine-Readable Evidence Contracts**: Structuring auditability via an 8-field bounded verdict envelope (`verdict`, `verifier`, `verifier_signature`, `evidence_refs`, `evidence_fingerprints`, `verification_basis`, `witness_scope`, `timestamp`) for tamper-evident transaction verification.
- **Deliverable 2 (Protocol Gap Analysis)**: Assessing protocol coverage and functional shortfalls across candidate commerce protocols.
- **Cross-WG Alignment**: Coordinating with [Identity and Trust](identity-and-trust.md) on delegation and consent, and [Observability and Traceability](observability-and-traceability.md) on evidence records.

# Lifecycle History

In PR #6, working group participants contributed the post-purchase section (capabilities P1–P7 and the machine-readable bounded verdict contract) to feed into the Deliverable 1 Capability Map and Deliverable 2 Gap Analysis[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-6].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group is a cross-cutting technical body of the Agentic AI Foundation responsible for arbitrating a standardized, vendor-neutral vocabulary across working groups and cataloging technologies in the interactive Agentic AI Landscape portal.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2] The group establishes foundational definitions, disambiguates adjacent conceptual boundaries, and evaluates open-source and proprietary software submissions against neutrality criteria.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2]

# Architecture / Specification
The working group governs terminology progression through unified triage spreadsheets and pull request workflows. Concepts undergo multi-round review cycles where terms are categorized as kept, culled, or held for debate prior to formal definition drafting.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2] Definition proposals explicitly capture relational mappings among paired concepts—including `Skill` versus `Tool`, `Kill switch` versus `Reversibility`, `Harness` versus `Meta-harness`, and `Delegation` versus `Handoff`.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2]

The group also manages landscape category boundaries and ingest pipelines, requiring cross-workgroup domain editor consensus to ensure vendor neutrality across operational disciplines such as Attestation & Verifiable Evidence and Agentic Vulnerability Enumeration.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2]

# Lifecycle History
In August 2026, the working group transitioned from term intake into definition formalization under co-chairs Junjie Bu (Google) and Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg).[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2] Across three syncs, 53 candidate terms were evaluated, resulting in 37 kept terms, 15 culled terms, and one held debate (`Multi-agent misdirection`).[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2] The universal definition for `Harness` merged in pull request #37, while definition pull requests for `Human in the loop`, `Meta-harness`, Identity & Trust terms, and Workflow & Process Integration terms entered formal review.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2] Representative liaison coverage was also expanded with Leonardo Galesky representing the [Agentic Commerce Working Group](../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md).[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Commerce Working Group is an AAIF technical body developing vendor-neutral capability maps, protocol gap analyses, and architectural standards for agent-driven commercial transactions.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-922f59c26329-125f7307] Chaired by Ilya Grigorik (Shopify) and Rahul Bansal (OpenAI), the group addresses both conversational and fully autonomous commerce, spanning payment execution protocols, intent verification, and post-transaction dispute resolution.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-922f59c26329-125f7307]

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes agentic transaction systems across distinct protocol layers and operational boundaries:[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-922f59c26329-125f7307]
- **Payment Rail Abstraction**: The group evaluates transport-agnostic payment execution protocols such as x402—an independent Linux Foundation project—which decouples single payment transactions into scheme, network, asset, and mechanism primitives across HTTP, MCP, and Agent-to-Agent (A2A) transports.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-922f59c26329-125f7307] Payment protocols compose as execution rails beneath application-level standards like AP2, UCP, and ACP, isolating settlement contracts from agent-level policy enforcement.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-922f59c26329-125f7307]
- **Dispute and Accountability Architecture**: In delegated purchasing where the human cardholder is absent at checkout, traditional fraud signals (such as device telemetry and clickstreams) are invalid.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-922f59c26329-125f7307] The group is specifying verifiable intent records, agent provenance metadata (platform identifiers, agent ID, model version), and structured consent surface protocols to reconstruct authority, limits, and merchant policy acceptance during chargeback and dispute workflows.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-922f59c26329-125f7307]

# Lifecycle History
In August 2026, the working group conducted dedicated technical sessions analyzing payment delivery and dispute settlement.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-922f59c26329-125f7307] The x402 evaluation expanded the working group's Capability Map to include pay-per-use autonomous micropayments for API, content, and context consumption.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-922f59c26329-125f7307] In subsequent milestones, the group scheduled deep dives on the Order Network eXchange (OnX) standard and Machine Payment Protocol (MPP).[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-922f59c26329-125f7307]

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Standardized telemetry context and correlation framework capturing causal relationships, execution spans, and session continuity across agent runtimes.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open AAIF telemetry standard and correlation framework that tracks agent intent, reasoning cycles, tool invocations, and multi-turn session progression across distributed execution boundaries.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-40] Developed within the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), the model correlates agent execution without mandating unbroken, session-long spans.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-43]

# Architecture / Specification
The specification outlines standardized telemetry schemas, context propagation protocols, and reference validation criteria:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-40][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-43]
- **Telemetry Baseline and Gap Classification**: Framework captures distinguish between runtime instrumentation defects, missing semantic attributes, unsupported engine behavior, and configuration guidance.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-40] Reference behaviors are validated across independent agent runtimes—including [Goose](../resources/goose.md) and secondary SDK implementations—to ensure standard attributes represent shared execution needs.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-40]
- **Session and Turn Correlation**: Multi-turn and multi-trace continuity links disparate conversational turns across process restarts, paused states, and caller traces using exported telemetry context rather than persistent active spans.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-43]
- **Provider API and Extensibility Profiles**: The model defines standardized test harnesses, fixtures, and mappings for LLM provider APIs covering streaming outputs, error payloads, and tool-call requests without falsely indicating external tool execution.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-46]

# Lifecycle History
Following working group sessions in August 2026, a nine-task execution plan was chartered to implement and validate reference captures across production runtimes.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-40][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-46] Key milestones include Task 2 (baseline telemetry comparison between Goose and a second agent runtime), Task 5 (cross-trace session and turn continuity verification), and Task 8 (packaging runnable provider API examples and community contributor guidelines).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-40][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-43][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-46]

proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group defining open threat models, security best practices, runtime protection architectures, and cross-WG security review checklists.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group develops baseline security profiles, threat taxonomies, runtime sandboxing requirements, and cross-cutting security evaluation checklists for agentic artificial intelligence systems across the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d].

# Architecture / Specification

The working group manages several active workstreams:
- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide**: A foundational implementation and hardening guide whose initial version focuses on runtime controls while reserving identity and delegation topics for the [Identity and Trust Working Group](identity-and-trust.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d].
- **Static Analysis Rules Deliverable**: An initiative translating textual best practices into actionable, machine-readable rule definitions compatible with static analysis tools and SDKs[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d].
- **Cross-WG Security and Privacy Review Checklist**: A review instrument and inter-group coordination process led across sibling working groups including [Observability and Traceability](observability-and-traceability.md), [Agentic Commerce](agentic-commerce.md), and [Accuracy and Reliability](accuracy-and-reliability.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d].
- **Design Patterns Catalog**: Architectural security patterns including the [kill-switch](../patterns/kill-switch.md) pattern and forthcoming memory security patterns[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d].
- **Security Taxonomy**: Contributions to the foundation taxonomy, including definitions and disambiguations for terms such as privacy-preserving execution and sensitive context handling[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d].

# Lifecycle History

On September 1, 2026, the working group decided to freeze and release its first version of the Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide as an official AAIF deliverable, initiated a code-facing static analysis deliverable, and commenced structured outreach for the cross-WG checklist review process[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Alignment Working Group analyzes global AI policy developments, regulatory compliance mandates, and enterprise risk controls, producing mapping matrices and gap analyses for open agent deployments[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-fa4050a9f626-ee69c81a].

# Architecture / Specification

The working group is chaired by Ryan Hagemann (IBM) and Deborah Eng (JPMorgan Chase)[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-fa4050a9f626-ee69c81a]. Its roadmap proceeds across three major phases:
1. **Landscape Analysis (Phase 1)**: Identifying and categorizing existing global policy instruments, statutory requirements, and administrative frameworks impacting agentic AI deployments[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-fa4050a9f626-ee69c81a].
2. **Mapping and Gap Analysis (Phase 2)**: Synthesizing policy instruments against a dozen standardized governance themes using structured prompt-assisted information extraction to locate regulatory gaps in contemporary agent implementations[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-fa4050a9f626-ee69c81a].
3. **Final Recommendations (Phase 3)**: Formal delivery of consolidated regulatory alignment guidance for Foundation projects and enterprise adopters[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-fa4050a9f626-ee69c81a].

# Lifecycle History

In July 2026, the working group concluded consensus on its baseline instrument inventory and core themes, transitioning operations from Phase 1 landscape collection into the Phase 2 mapping and gap analysis workstream[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-fa4050a9f626-ee69c81a].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability and Traceability Working Group defines open standards, trace data models, and instrumentation architectures to capture causal execution chains, state transitions, and protocol interactions across AI agents and host environments[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ec358f3e3170-5d21c611].

# Architecture / Specification

The working group organizes its technical work through specialized focus areas and liaison channels:
- **Primitives and Protocols Focus Group**: Governs application-level and below-L7 protocol observability, including kernel syscall tracing and network boundary monitoring to establish full-stack execution provenance[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ec358f3e3170-5d21c611].
- **Agent State Context and Reasoning Focus Group**: Addresses internal reasoning traces, context lifecycle events, and memory interaction tracking[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ec358f3e3170-5d21c611].
- **Agent Action Capsules**: Exploration of tamper-evident cryptographic execution records (such as MeshLLM ledger integration) that record task dispatches, observed actions, and policy compliance verification[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ec358f3e3170-5d21c611].
- **External and Cross-WG Liaisons**: Formal liaison mapping covering external standards bodies (W3C Trace Context, OpenTelemetry GenAI SIG, OWASP AOS, Agent Trace) and AAIF technical working groups via structured intake trackers[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-33].

# Lifecycle History

In September 2026, the working group expanded its Primitives and Protocols scope to include kernel- and system-level observability below L7, evaluated Agent Action Capsules for verifiable auditing, and formalized its external liaison intake registry[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ec358f3e3170-5d21c611][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-33].

proposed_concept.title: Single-Agent Workflow with Human Approval
proposed_concept.description: Reference architecture establishing an enforceable human approval gate and structural separation of proposal generation from action execution.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Single-Agent Workflow with Human Approval is an AAIF reference architecture that enforces an architectural separation between an autonomous agent generating proposed actions and an authorized human gatekeeper executing those actions[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36].

# Architecture / Specification

The architecture relies on three distinct boundaries defined by the [proposal-execution-split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md) and [human-approval-gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md) patterns:
1. **Proposal Boundary**: The primary agent consumes task context, executes analytical queries, and emits a structured proposal payload without directly accessing write-privileged mutation endpoints[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36].
2. **Approval Gate**: An out-of-band human interface presents the proposed modification, contextual diffs, and verification artifacts to an authorized operator[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36].
3. **Publication / Execution Boundary**: Once explicit approval is registered, the action is committed via dedicated operational credentials that the proposing agent cannot directly access or manipulate[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36].

## Validated Use Cases

The reference architecture has been validated across specific content lifecycle workflows mapped to the [agentic-use-case-inventory](../resources/agentic-use-case-inventory.md)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36]:
- **FAQ and Knowledge-Base Updates**: Agents draft synthesized documentation answers, which remain staged until documentation owners review and release them[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36].
- **Software Release Notes**: Agents summarize code commits and pull request metadata into changelogs, gated on product maintainer verification[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36].
- **Catalog Listing Descriptions**: Marketing and listing copy generated by subagents is reviewed by category managers prior to live storefront indexing[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36].

# Lifecycle History

Originally drafted by the [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md), this reference architecture was augmented with empirical validation records for publishing and knowledge management workflows[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36].

proposed_concept.title: Identity and Trust Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group defining vendor-neutral standards, reference architectures, and delegation frameworks for AI agent identity, attestation, and authorization.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Identity and Trust Working Group (I&T) is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body that advances vendor-neutral, interoperable viewpoints, reference architectures, and guidance for AI agent identity, attestation, authentication, delegation, authorization, and trust evaluation[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-b33563055168-5c93d5a3]. While conventional identity infrastructure targets human single sign-on and static service-to-service authentication, agentic architectures require verifiable provenance, delegated human authority chains, dynamic cross-organizational capability propagation, and auditable proof of consequential actions[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f].

# Governance and Operations
The working group operates under the Technical Committee and conducts open public meetings alternating Thursdays at 6:30 AM and 9:00 AM US Pacific Time[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-b33563055168-5c93d5a3]. Working group leadership was appointed by Platinum and Gold foundation members for a term extending from March 1, 2026 through January 31, 2027:
- **Chair:** Grant Miller (IBM)[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-b33563055168-5c93d5a3]
- **Co-Chair:** Alper Dedeoğlu (SAP SE)[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-b33563055168-5c93d5a3]

Contributors participate as individuals adhering to foundation neutrality rather than representing corporate employers[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-b33563055168-5c93d5a3].

# Breakout Workstreams
To balance technical depth with cross-functional alignment, the working group organizes ongoing initiatives across three structured breakout streams[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f]:
- **Use Cases:** Coordinated by Wei Chen, deriving operational identity, consent, and authorization requirements from real-world enterprise and consumer agent deployments[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f].
- **Reference Architecture:** Coordinated by Brian Malone, defining architectural actors, trust boundaries, token exchange mechanics, and interoperability protocols for delegated agent authority[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f].
- **Taxonomy Coordination:** Managed by liaisons Julianna Mealin and Leonardo Galesky, harmonizing core identity terminology with the cross-working-group [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f].

# Key Reference Work
The group actively surveys and evaluates relevant external standards and industry reference implementations, including:
- [Agentic Resource Discovery](../standards/agentic-resource-discovery.md) (ARD) for decentralized capability advertisement and admission[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f].
- Uber Engineering's agent identity architecture, leveraging SPIFFE/SPIRE workload attestation, actor chains, and per-hop token exchange[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f].
- NVIDIA Secure Agent Workspace layered execution and policy boundary designs[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f].
- IETF AI Agent Authentication and Authorization protocol drafts distinguishing established transport security from open agentic authorization gaps[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f].

proposed_concept.title: Agent-Tool CLI Boundary Telemetry Model
proposed_concept.description: Observability reference matrix and context propagation model analyzing direct agent subprocess invocations across the Agent-to-Tool boundary.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent-Tool CLI Boundary Telemetry Model specifies the observability contract and context propagation mechanics governing direct tool invocations where an AI agent runtime spawns a local command-line interface (CLI) subprocess without intermediary skills or protocol wrappers[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b]. This boundary bridges the semantic Agent → Tool decision relationship with the operational Agent Runtime → Local Process operating-system boundary, defining how distributed trace context, execution metadata, and causal lineage cross process creation boundaries[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b].

# Architecture / Specification

## Boundary Hierarchy
The canonical call hierarchy separates agent-level tool scheduling from process execution[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b]:
```text
upstream caller
  └── agent turn / invocation
      └── tool execution span              (Agent → Tool semantic boundary)
          └── [optional CLI caller span]
              └── local CLI execution span (Agent Runtime → Local Process boundary)
                  └── CLI sub-operations and downstream calls
```

## Telemetry Dimension Matrix
The boundary defines six canonical observability dimensions across current standards coverage and unresolved gaps[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b]:
- **Identity:** Correlates `gen_ai.tool.name` and `gen_ai.tool.call.id` with process executable path, version, and child PID; open gaps remain in binding exact executable content digests with the delegating principal[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b].
- **Context:** Carries active W3C Trace Context and Baggage via standardized environment variable carriers (`TRACEPARENT`, `TRACESTATE`); runtimes frequently filter child environments, disrupting propagation[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b].
- **Relationship:** Connects governing agent turn spans to child execution spans; late transcript parsing after process exit breaks child-visible causality, requiring pre-execution span reservation[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b].
- **Lifecycle:** Maps progression across selection, authorization, context preparation, spawn, execution, and exit or cancellation[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b].
- **Outcome:** Captures process exit codes, structured outputs, side-effect manifests, and error classifications while preventing leakage of sensitive arguments or terminal output[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b].
- **Provenance:** Tracks declared tool schemas against resolved system binaries to detect shell expansion drift and wrapper obfuscation[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b].

# Implementation and Validation
The boundary model was validated using LoongSuite Pilot (PR #316) integrating with Claude Code CLI workflows, establishing pre-execution context reservation where trace identifiers are provisioned and injected into environment carriers before process launch rather than reconstructed post-hoc from execution transcripts[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b].

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Brand Guidelines and Design System
proposed_concept.description: Visual identity rules, typography tokens, dual surface palettes, OOXML asset mappings, and contrast requirements for AAIF communications and reports.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The AAIF Brand Guidelines and Design System define the foundational visual identity, token architecture, typography standards, and rendering rules across all Agentic AI Foundation digital assets, reports, presentations, and community deliverables[^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07]. Maintained in the `community-events` repository, the source of truth is packaged as a self-extracting bundle (`design/aaif-design-system.html`) whose design tokens are compiled into CSS variables via automated verification scripts to prevent styling drift[^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].

# Architecture / Specification

## Visual Tokens and Core Rules
The AAIF visual identity enforces several counter-intuitive principles to ensure consistent, premium foundation aesthetics[^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07]:
- **Black Accent:** The primary accent is black (`--accent: var(--ink)`). Spectrum hues (`--spec-1` through `--spec-10`) serve strictly as intra-surface accents with at most one hue leading per surface; coral (`--spec-8`) is not the foundation brand color[^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].
- **Single Typeface:** Instrument Sans (OFL) is the sole typeface across display and interface copy, utilized at weights 400, 500, 600, and 700. Monospace fonts are reserved exclusively for metadata and category eyebrows[^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].
- **Heading Geometry:** Headings are styled at weight 500 with letter tracking of `-0.02em` and tight line heights (1.05–1.15), avoiding traditional bolding except for small subheadings (h5/h6) at weight 600[^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].
- **Flat Depth and Geometry:** Visual hierarchy relies on 1px hairlines, surface tinting (`--paper`, `--paper-2`, `--paper-3`), and inset strokes without drop shadows. Containers, cards, tables, and chips use square corners (`border-radius: 0`), reserving rounded pill geometry solely for active buttons and status badges[^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].
- **Dual Surfaces Without Dark Mode:** Deliverables are authored for two explicit first-class surfaces: White Editorial and Black Plate. Inversion via automated `prefers-color-scheme` dark mode is strictly prohibited[^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].
- **Ground Backgrounds:** The base page ground is `--paper`; warm off-white (`--paper-2`) is restricted to occasional horizontal section banding, and `--paper-3` is used for tinted panels[^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].

## Asset Usage and Agent Motif
Brand marks must be rendered verbatim from official vector sources (`assets/aaif-mark.svg`, `assets/aaif-mark-square.svg`, and `assets/aaif-logo-white.svg`) without redrawing or geometric alteration[^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07]. The foundation "agent motif" robot graphic is designated for empty states, loading indicators, event collateral, and section dividers; it is strictly disallowed in governance, board, regulatory, or press documents[^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].

proposed_concept.title: Workflow Execution Primitives
proposed_concept.description: Foundational vocabulary and structural execution primitives defined by the Workflows and Process Integration Working Group.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Workflow Execution Primitives define the core taxonomy terms and execution concepts standardized by the Workflows and Process Integration Working Group to model deterministic, probabilistic, and hybrid AI agent orchestrations[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-40]. The vocabulary separates design-time intent from runtime execution dynamics, establishing clear boundaries across control flow sequencing, execution lifecycle states, layer-specific determinism, and responsibility handoffs[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-40].

# Architecture / Specification

## Core Execution Terms
The working group categorizes workflow components into distinct operational layers[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-40]:
- **Determinism:** Defined as a property of a specific execution layer—such as Workflow Execution, Control Flow, or an individual Activity—rather than an all-or-nothing property of an entire workflow[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-40]. This decoupling allows a workflow to enforce strictly deterministic control flow and governance policies while orchestrating non-deterministic, probabilistic model activities[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-40].
- **Control Flow:** The logical specification determining execution order, branching conditions, iterations, and concurrency joins[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-40]. The definition remains neutral regarding whether sequencing logic is fixed at design time or evaluated dynamically by an autonomous agent runtime[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-40].
- **Workflow Execution:** An instantiated runtime invocation possessing a continuous lifecycle identity extending from initiation through completion[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-40]. Dynamic replanning, step retries, and compensation transitions occur within the lifecycle of a single workflow execution without breaking runtime identity[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-40].
- **Handoff:** The transfer of operational responsibility, state context, and execution authority between distinct actors or agent sub-processes[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-40]. The concept bridges workflow orchestration (transfer of responsibility) and observability trace modeling (the observable boundary where delegation occurs)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-40].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Use Case Inventory is an empirical catalog maintained by the Workflows and Process Integration Working Group that maps production agent implementations against structural execution dimensions and architectural patterns [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39]. It grounds agentic industry deployments in concrete engineering documentation, evaluating coordination modes, multi-agent necessity, and execution structure against strict classification criteria [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39].

# Architecture / Specification
The inventory systematically tracks agent deployments across dimensions specified in `../resources/agentic-use-case-classification.md` [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-48]. Each entry requires verifiable source documentation to qualify pattern classifications rather than marketing assertions [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39]:

- **Lead Research & Enrichment**: Verified as a sequential pipeline following documented waterfall provider enrichment workflows [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39].
- **On-Call Incident Summary**: Classified under `../patterns/parallel-fan-out-and-join.md` as inherently multi-agent with dynamic AI planning, driven by context partitioning requirements during incident triage [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39].
- **Contract Review & Red-Lining**: Classified under AI-coordinated planning workflows [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39].

The inventory enforces rigorous gating against premature classification; rows lacking deterministic convergence verification or explicit sequential ordering remain explicitly marked as unspecified until verified documentation is provided [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39].

# Lifecycle History
Maintained by the Workflows and Process Integration Working Group [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39]. Link auditing and citation validation efforts systematically resolved 404 targets and aligned internal schema references directly with `schema-agentic-use-cases.md` [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-48].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Standardized telemetry context and correlation framework capturing causal relationships, execution spans, and identity attributes across distributed agent systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open telemetry context and correlation framework that captures causal execution lineage, agent state transitions, and identity across heterogeneous agentic systems [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-50]. Developed by the Observability and Traceability Working Group in collaboration with Security & Privacy and Identity & Trust, the model establishes vendor-neutral semantic conventions and propagation mechanisms for distributed agent interactions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-50].

# Architecture / Specification
The specification defines standard OpenTelemetry span attributes, context propagation rules, and boundary redaction requirements [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-50]:

- **Identity Semantic Conventions**: Spans capture standardized identity attributes including `agent.id`, `agent.role`, `agent.invocation_id`, `agent.principal.type`, and `agent.delegation_depth` [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-50].
- **Context and Baggage Propagation**: Employs the W3C Baggage and Trace Context specifications to ensure agent identity and execution lineage survive asynchronous, non-HTTP boundaries such as job queues, event streams, tool execution sandboxes, and streaming model completions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-50].
- **Cardinality & Sampling Management**: Enforces strict cardinality controls on high-frequency tool invocations to avoid unsustainable APM storage overhead [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-50].
- **Telemetry Sanitization & Boundary Isolation**: Explicitly forbids recording sensitive credential materials—such as raw tokens, private keys, message signatures, or raw user-identifiable payloads—within distributed tracing spans, restricting cryptographic validation material to dedicated audit stores [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-50].
- **Causal Lineage**: Preserves deterministic trace graphs across multi-tier topologies moving from initial user requests to orchestrator agents, subagents, and downstream external tools [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-50].

# Lifecycle History
The framework originated within the `../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md` working group under active scoping to evaluate agent identity integration (such as aauth.dev and OpenID COAZ-MCP bindings) into core observability pipelines [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-50].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Identity and Trust Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body responsible for defining vendor-neutral standards, delegation frameworks, and cryptographic primitives for autonomous agent identity and verification [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-c743b929b22e-3767aad0]. The working group establishes trust baselines across multi-agent systems, coordinating with observability and security groups on delegation, authentication, and token exchange [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-c743b929b22e-3767aad0].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group manages operational and technical roadmaps covering:

- **Agent Identity Primitives**: Defining core schemas, principal types, and delegation token structures for agent-to-agent and human-to-agent interactions [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-8].
- **Shared Test Environments**: Evaluating shared, bounded testbeds (such as Vector) to deploy, validate, and measure agent identity primitives under realistic operational conditions [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-8].
- **Cross-WG Collaboration**: Partnering with `../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md` to ensure identity claims and delegation depths can be propagated safely through telemetry pipelines without leaking sensitive credentials [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-c743b929b22e-3767aad0].

# Lifecycle History
The working group maintains an active presentation queue and topic backlog in `AGENDA.md` to coordinate technical evaluations, design reviews, and RFC proposals alongside its running meeting records [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-c743b929b22e-3767aad0]. Contributor onboarding procedures and structured presentation scheduling ensure standardized reviews of emerging protocols and test environments [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-7] [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-8].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Standardized telemetry context and correlation framework capturing causal relationships, execution spans, and OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic crosswalks.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agent Behavior Trace Model is a standardized telemetry context and correlation framework developed by the Observability and Traceability Working Group [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-41]. It provides consistent causality tracking, identity relationships, and OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions across asynchronous, multi-turn, and human-in-the-loop agent workflows [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-41].

# Architecture / Specification

The trace model is organized around a nine-task execution plan addressing cross-system correlation, trace identity mapping, and upstream contributions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-41][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-47]:

- **Shared Relationship Contract**: Formalizes mappings across conversation/session scopes, turns, subagent invocations, proposed actions, and observations [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-41]. It supports disconnected trace identifiers across discrete turns within a single conversation (e.g., preserving caller context while supporting standalone turn traces) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-41].
- **Proposals and Approvals**: Binds proposed actions (e.g., ticket creation or external mutation) to distinct action identities, allowing approval checkpoints or denials to reference the target action even when execution spans never materialize [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-41].
- **Taxonomy and Vocabulary Alignment**: Bridges terms with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) to maintain standard naming for agents, tools, turns, and context exhaustion [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-41][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-47].
- **Upstream OpenTelemetry GenAI Contributions**: Pushes conventions upstream to OTel GenAI semantic standards, such as resolving turn-entry span identification, missing target handling, and persistent conversation context attributes [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-47].

# References

- [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md)
- [Proposal-Execution Split Pattern](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md)
- [Approval Checkpoint Pattern](../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md)

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices
proposed_concept.description: Implementation guidelines, threat mitigation controls, and workload identity architectures for securing agentic workflows across cloud and hybrid environments.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Security Best Practices guide establishes security architectures, threat mitigation strategies, and operational control boundaries for autonomous agents, multi-agent orchestrations, and integration protocols.

# Architecture / Specification

The guidelines define threat mitigations across key execution surfaces, including sandboxing, runtime privilege separation, and credential handling [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-23].

## Workload Identity and Multi-Cloud Boundaries

While baseline security configurations document single-cloud workload identity scopes (e.g., standard one-hour IAM role lifetimes bounded by specific role designs), cross-domain deployments introduce distinct identity challenges [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-23]:

- **Cross-Cloud Role Assumption**: Agents hosted in one cloud environment accessing downstream resources in another provider or on-premises environment [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-23].
- **OIDC Identity Federation**: Using OpenID Connect (OIDC) identity federation across heterogeneous IAM providers without relying on static credentials or long-lived API tokens [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-23].
- **Blast Radius and Trust Domains**: Evaluating privilege escalation risks and bounding autonomous execution when identity chains span multiple administrative trust boundaries [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-23].
- **Hybrid On-Premises Interoperability**: Establishing workload identity baselines for legacy and private infrastructure unable to support native cloud IAM federation [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-23].

Joint work between the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) and the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) coordinates recommendations for federated agent credential lifetimes and trust federation patterns [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-23].

# References

- [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md)
- [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md)
- [Inherited Security Floor Pattern](../patterns/inherited-security-floor.md)

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic Use Case Classification provides a twelve-column taxonomy separating architectural and execution properties into distinct dimensions across verified production deployments.

# Architecture / Specification

The classification categorizes agentic workflows across execution topology, autonomy degree, verification mechanisms, and coordination styles.

## Open Orchestration Dimensions: Parallel Fan-Out vs. Sequential Pipeline

A key classification ambiguity exists around defining pipeline versus fan-out execution structures in workflow inventories [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-47]:

- **Timing as Observed**: Defining `Parallel fan-out` purely by concurrent temporal execution of sub-tasks [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-47].
- **Dependency Structure**: Defining `Sequential pipeline` strictly by dependency relationships where each phase feeds input into subsequent tasks, regardless of whether sub-phases execute concurrently [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-47].
- **Agent Count**: Distinguishing workflows based on single versus multi-agent execution boundaries [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-47].

Because timing and dependency criteria are orthogonal rather than strict opposites, workflows may satisfy neither or both definitions, impacting consistency across the [Agentic Use Case Inventory](../resources/agentic-use-case-inventory.md) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-47].
