proposed_concept.title: Bounded Autonomous Remediation
proposed_concept.description: Reference architecture governing iterative, autonomous problem resolution within predefined task boundaries, deterministic acceptance gates, and constrained effect execution.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Bounded Autonomous Remediation is an AAIF reference architecture that coordinates autonomous, iterative problem resolution without requiring per-attempt human approval, constrained strictly by declared task scopes, execution budgets, and independent acceptance verification[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b]. It is authored as a contrasting companion to the [Single-Agent Human Approval](single-agent-human-approval.md) architecture, addressing workloads where independent deterministic verification exists, permitted effects are low impact or reversible, and automated non-convergence pathways safely halt execution[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].

# Architecture / Specification

The architecture composes three core patterns from the Workflows and Process Integration Working Group[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b]:
- [Bounded Convergence Loop](../patterns/bounded-convergence-loop.md): Limits iteration budget, time, and retries in the agent execution loop.
- [Deterministic Acceptance Gate](../patterns/deterministic-acceptance-gate.md): Independently validates candidate outputs using unified multi-criteria checks (such as contract assertions, schema validations, and automated test suites) before any external modification occurs[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-37].
- [Proposal-Execution Split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md): Separates speculative candidate generation in isolated sandboxes from final downstream execution.

### Required Capability Roles
- **Execution Engine**: Admits the task, tracks iteration counters, sequences retries, and halts execution on exhaustion.
- **Bounded Agent Environment**: Constrained environment restricted to specific task inputs, credentials, and tools.
- **Isolated Work Area**: Non-authoritative staging sandbox for generating uncommitted remediation artifacts.
- **Deterministic Acceptance Gate**: Authoritative, external evaluation gate that must pass all acceptance criteria prior to effect dispatch.
- **Constrained Effect Executor**: Dedicated executor restricted to applying only verified candidate modifications to production surfaces.
- **Audit Log & Escalation Surface**: Records complete convergence traces and routes non-convergent, failed, or ambiguous runs to human-managed queues[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].

# Lifecycle History

- Validated against the Autonomous Maintenance Run ("night shift") use case, with multi-criteria acceptance gate requirements replacing legacy small-gate/big-gate terminology[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-37].
- Expanded with weekly staff schedule generation as an illustrative secondary example pending intake into the centralized inventory[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-37].

# References
- [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md)
- [Reference Architecture Validation Guidelines](../guidelines/reference-architecture-validation.md)

proposed_concept.title: Reference Architecture Validation Guide
proposed_concept.description: Standardized evaluation procedures and fit classifications for validating AAIF reference architectures against real-world use cases.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Reference Architecture Validation Guide defines the standardized process for evaluating an Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) reference architecture against real-world use cases[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-35]. It establishes consistent assessment categories, required evidence formats, and operational rules for AI and human contributors documenting architectural fit across production workloads[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-cd94574f9d34-a7acfb30].

# Architecture / Specification

### Validation Classifications
When comparing a candidate architecture against an operational use case, contributors assign one of four standardized status designations[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-35]:
- **Validated**: The real-world use case demonstrably matches all core patterns, capability roles, boundaries, and exit states of the architecture.
- **Partial**: The use case shares core capability roles and pattern compositions but exhibits structural gaps, such as missing deterministic gates or divergent escalation pathways.
- **No fit**: The operational constraints, authority models, or boundary requirements fundamentally conflict with the reference architecture.
- **Candidate**: A proposed use case submitted for evaluation that has not yet completed comparative review against working group evidence standards.

### Contributor Directives
As detailed in the workstream contributor rules, validation assessments must rely strictly on verified source evidence rather than speculative interpretations[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-cd94574f9d34-a7acfb30]. Evaluators must avoid generating unrequested GitHub issues or pull requests during automated triage, record terminology gaps as open questions rather than novel constructs, and document domain scenarios as validation proofs rather than generic architecture definitions[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-cd94574f9d34-a7acfb30].

# Lifecycle History

- Authored following Workstream Sync #6 to provide a standard output mechanism for validation PRs and issue records[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-35].
- Linked directly from contributor guidelines and instructions for AI contributors[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-cd94574f9d34-a7acfb30].

- [Reference Architecture Template](reference-architecture-template.md)
- [Bounded Autonomous Remediation](../architectures/bounded-autonomous-remediation.md)

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream
proposed_concept.description: Cross-cutting AAIF workstream harmonizing agentic AI terminology across vertical working groups and maintaining the SKOS-Lite taxonomy index.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream serves as the horizontal architectural bridge across the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF), harmonizing terminology and maintaining a living pre-competitive vocabulary across vertical working groups [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b33563055168-07a3beac]. Rather than functioning as an isolated vertical Working Group (WG), it operates as a shared workstream that ingests, aligns, and indexes concepts supplied by vertical WGs without replacing domain-specific working group authority [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336].

The workstream is chaired by Junjie Bu (Google) and Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg), appointed by AAIF Working Group leadership [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b33563055168-07a3beac]. While the workstream's mission includes both a shared taxonomy and an ecosystem landscape market map, active work is scoped exclusively to the Taxonomy; contributions to the Landscape remain deferred on the future roadmap until an approved intake process is established [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336] [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b33563055168-07a3beac].

# Architecture / Specification

## Governance and Domain Editor Delegation
The workstream interfaces with vertical AAIF Technical Working Groups through designated representatives termed Domain Editors [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336]:
- [Accuracy & Reliability](./accuracy-and-reliability.md): Casper Nielsen and Matthew Khouzam [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336].
- [Agentic Commerce](./agentic-commerce.md): Leonardo Galesky [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336].
- [Governance, Risk & Regulatory Alignment](./governance-risk-and-regulatory.md): Amithash Kankanallu Jagadish [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336].
- [Identity & Trust](./identity-and-trust.md): Julianna Mealin [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336].
- [Observability & Traceability](./observability-and-traceability.md): Pavan Sudheendra and Matt Lee [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336].
- [Security & Privacy](./security-and-privacy.md): Jautau White and Katherine Druckman [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336].
- [Workflows & Process Integration](./workflows-and-process-integration.md): Sumanth Sathyanarayana [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336].

Domain Editors bring terms into the workstream from their WGs, coordinate definition drafting within their groups, and participate in cross-WG consensus reviews [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336].

## Architectural Guardrails
The workstream's curation workflow is governed by four core architectural principles:
- **Horizontal Index Principle (Consolidation over Creation):** The workstream does not author domain-specific definitions from scratch, but rather ingests and harmonizes vertical WG glossaries. Terms affecting two or more WGs or identified as universal belong in the shared index; deep technical helper definitions and protocol schemas remain within vertical WG repositories [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a].
- **Paired Contrast Disambiguation Protocol:** Adjacent contrasting concepts (such as Tool versus Skill, or Deterministic versus Agentic workflows) must not be collapsed into shared generic descriptions. Each term's definition must state how it differs from its counterpart, and the pair must be explicitly linked via `relatedTerms` (`skos:related`) or `contrastsWith` [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a].
- **Anti-Erasure Guardrails:** Look-alike terms representing distinct operational paradigms cannot be deleted or aliased without explicit written approval from the owning Working Group's Domain Editor [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a].
- **Success Metrics:** Continuous evaluation tracks citation utility across AAIF specifications, corporate diversity (no single company authoring over 50% of entries), ecosystem coverage (minimum 10 actively reviewed terms per WG), and arbitration velocity [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a].

## Terminology Lifecycle
Candidate terms move from vertical groups to the shared taxonomy via a multi-stage lifecycle [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336]:
1. **Intake Logging:** Candidates enter the Taxonomy Working Spreadsheet marked as `Debate` (pending review), `Keep` (accepted for definition drafting), or `Cull` (ineligible, preserved for auditability) [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336].
2. **Qualification Criteria:** Terms qualify if they are specific to agentic AI or carry meanings materially distinct from established computing terminology [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336].
3. **Schema Mapping:** Approved terms are committed to `taxonomy/taxonomy-data.js` adhering to SKOS-Lite formatting rules, with `category`, `broaderTerm`, and `definition` temporarily deferred during initial vocabulary intake [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97].

# Lifecycle History
The workstream meets weekly on Mondays at 8:30 AM PT under chairs Junjie Bu and Gala Malbasic [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b33563055168-07a3beac]. As of 2026, the workstream adopted an agile curation posture admitting normalized terms first while deferring hierarchy and definitions to subsequent cross-WG syncs [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97] [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a]. Public pull requests proposing changes to the [Agentic AI Landscape](../resources/agentic-ai-landscape.md) remain closed pending landscape governance adoption [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336].

mutations.rationale: Authoritative workstream guidelines formally document that the Landscape catalog is on the future roadmap, with contributions currently paused and PRs closed until a governance process is approved.

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Landscape
proposed_concept.description: Ecosystem market map and architectural catalog deferred on the AAIF Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream future roadmap.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Landscape is an ecosystem architecture map intended to provide a comprehensive market map of agent runtimes, orchestration frameworks, protocols, and security tooling across the agentic AI landscape [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b33563055168-07a3beac]. It is managed by the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) alongside the unified taxonomy index [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b33563055168-07a3beac].

Under current workstream contribution rules, public contributions to the Landscape are explicitly frozen and remain on the future roadmap [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336] [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b33563055168-07a3beac]. Pull requests proposing additions or modifications to the `landscape/` directory or `landscape.yml` are closed until a formalized review and intake process is approved by workstream chairs and working group delegates [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336] [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-53e532051b05-2842a713] [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a].

# Architecture / Specification

## Scope Separation
The workstream maintains a strict functional division between its two core outputs:
- **Taxonomy (Active):** Shared vocabulary curation and SKOS-Lite term ingestion, actively accepting pull requests reviewed by Domain Editors [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336].
- **Landscape (Deferred):** Visual ecosystem market map hosted in `landscape/`; currently inactive pending contributor workflow definition [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b33563055168-07a3beac] [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a].

## Governance and Inclusion Criteria
When the landscape review process is ratified, ecosystem listings will enforce vendor neutrality standards to prevent commercial dominance, including key performance indicators requiring that no individual corporate entity authors or controls over 50% of merged entries [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Taxonomy Contributions is an operational guidance skill governing how human contributors and autonomous agents format, disambiguate, and submit terminology to the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336] [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a]. It codifies repository schema constraints, preview testing, and disambiguation protocols to ensure incoming pull requests integrate seamlessly into `taxonomy/taxonomy-data.js` [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-53e532051b05-2842a713] [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97].

# Architecture / Specification

## Procedural Guardrails
Contributors and automated agents must adhere to the following execution constraints:
- **Taxonomy Scope Only:** Contributions proposing changes to the [Agentic AI Landscape](../resources/agentic-ai-landscape.md) must be rejected or closed, as landscape intake is frozen on the future roadmap [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336] [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a].
- **Consolidation over Creation:** Do not invent vertical definitions independently. Harmonize terminology proposed by vertical Working Groups [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a].
- **Anti-Erasure Enforcement:** Never delete terms or convert look-alike terms into aliases without written sign-off from the owning Working Group's Domain Editor [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a].

## Paired Contrast Disambiguation Protocol
When terms represent adjacent operational concepts (e.g., Tool versus Skill):
1. Evaluate whether the concept is a true synonym (added to `aliases`) or an adjacent operational contrast [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a].
2. For adjacent contrasts, ensure definitions explicitly articulate counterpart boundary conditions [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a].
3. Mandate bidirectional associative linking using `relatedTerms` (`skos:related`) or `contrastsWith` [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a] [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97].

## SKOS-Lite Glossary Schema (`taxonomy/taxonomy-data.js`)
Each taxonomy item must conform to SKOS-Lite object rules [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97]:
- `term` (String, Required): Sentence-case term name, unique across the glossary [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97].
- `category` (String, Required): Deferred for initial intake; set to `""` [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97].
- `aliases` (Array of Strings, Required): Synonyms and alternative spellings (`[]` if none) [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97].
- `broaderTerm` (String or null, Required): Direct parent concept; deferred for initial intake (set to `null`) [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97].
- `definition` (String, Required): Pre-competitive definition. While definitions are deferred during initial admission, entries must use the exact placeholder: `"Definition pending — term accepted; definition under working group discussion."` [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97].
- `scopeNote` (String, Optional): Historical context and WG boundary notes [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97].
- `relatedTerms` / `contrastsWith` (Array of Strings, Optional): Conceptual associative linkages [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97].
- `workgroups` (Array of Strings, Required): Working groups sharing ownership. `"Universal"` is strictly prohibited; universal terms carry an empty array (`[]`) [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97].

## Local Preview and Git Workflow
Changes are previewed using a zero-dependency local web server (`python3 -m http.server 8000` or `npx serve -l 8000`) inspecting `http://localhost:8000/taxonomy/` [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-53e532051b05-2842a713]. Contributors must verify browser console JavaScript syntax health, commit on a dedicated feature branch (`feature/add-term-<term-name>`), and tag relevant Domain Editors on pull request submission [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-53e532051b05-2842a713].

proposed_concept.description: Procedural pipeline and reconciliation engine managing AAIF chapter event tracking, Drive access, and tri-column identity resolution.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Community Event Operations is an orchestration pipeline and reconciliation engine managing local AAIF chapter logistics, community event lifecycles, and organizer permissions [^evt-community-events-pr-44]. It synchronizes community intake data across Google Forms, chapter Drive folders, and Slack workspaces [^evt-community-events-pr-44].

# Architecture / Specification

## Tri-Column Identity Resolution
To prevent measurement bugs where individual organizers appear under mismatched emails across systems, the operational intake sheet (`Form Responses`) maintains three distinct identity columns alongside the user-submitted intake `Email` [^evt-community-events-pr-44]:
- `Slack ID`: The immutable Slack user identifier (`U...`) resolved via `resolve_slack_ids.py`. Administrative invites and permissions key off this immutable ID rather than mutable display handles [^evt-community-events-pr-44].
- `Slack Email`: The email address actively registered to the resolved Slack account [^evt-community-events-pr-44].
- `Drive Email`: The email actively granted access on chapter Google Drive access control lists (ACLs) tracked via `track_drive_email.py` [^evt-community-events-pr-44]. Unassigned folders write an explicit `(no grant)` sentinel rather than an ambiguous blank [^evt-community-events-pr-44].

## Consumer Gmail Normalization
Slack user lookups (`users.lookupByEmail`) match exact strings. Consumer Google mailboxes (`gmail.com` and `googlemail.com`) ignore dots and plus tags, leading to false lookup failures when intake forms contain formatted variants [^evt-community-events-pr-44]. The lookup utility retries canonicalized spellings on initial lookup failure. This folding is strictly limited to consumer Gmail domains, preserving dot significance for custom Google Workspace domains [^evt-community-events-pr-44].

## Proposal-Execution Split for Identity Matches
Automated execution (`--write`) only commits entries resolved through direct email lookups [^evt-community-events-pr-44]. Matches derived from real-name heuristics are generated as suggestions and require manual `--apply` execution [^evt-community-events-pr-44]. This safeguard prevents erroneous privilege assignment when applicants share names with operational staff [^evt-community-events-pr-44].

# Overview
AAIF Audit Slack is a read-only workspace inspection skill that audits AAIF Slack channels, monitors member activity, and verifies channel membership hygiene across local chapters [^evt-community-events-pr-44]. It identifies permission discrepancies and unvetted accounts in private operational channels [^evt-community-events-pr-44].

# Architecture / Specification

## Operational Staff Whitelisting
To prevent automated administrative accounts and ops staff from appearing as unreviewed strangers in private chapter rooms, the audit engine validates members against [^evt-community-events-pr-44]:
- Explicit per-person operational staff email lists (`Ops staff email`) [^evt-community-events-pr-44].
- Approved operational domain lists (`Ops staff domain`) [^evt-community-events-pr-44].
- Active maintainer warnings when staff whitelist configurations are empty [^evt-community-events-pr-44].

## Multi-Chapter Shared Room Segregation
When adjacent chapters share a single operational channel (for example, Silicon Valley and San Francisco sharing `#bay-area-organizers`), the audit engine segregates channel occupants into chapter-specific accepted members and cross-chapter members recorded under a `shared` key [^evt-community-events-pr-44]. This prevents fully staffed joint organizer rooms from registering false-positive unvetted participant alerts [^evt-community-events-pr-44].

## Loop Isolation and Error Recovery
User hydration loops isolate state per row to prevent cell artifact leakage, ensuring empty pasted cells do not inherit previous row identifiers [^evt-community-events-pr-44]. In addition, API hydration failures are logged explicitly rather than misreporting broken tokens as absent Slack accounts [^evt-community-events-pr-44].

# Overview
The Community Event Operations skill executes end-to-end synchronization and reconciliation across AAIF's distributed community chapter infrastructure, coordinating with [AAIF Create Chapter](./aaif-create-chapter.md) and [AAIF Audit Slack](./aaif-audit-slack.md). It ensures zero drift across member permissions, communication channels, and intake data while enforcing operational boundaries and idempotency across external APIs.

# Architecture / Specification
The operations pipeline integrates multiple modular subsystems across Google Workspace and Slack:

## Chapter CRM Data Architecture
Chapter CRM workbooks maintain strict separation between intake applicant interest and central decision status[^evt-community-events-pr-28]:
- **Decision Status (`Status`)**: Encodes the authoritative lifecycle state (`Prospect`, `In progress`, `Interviewing`, `Tentative`, `Accepted`, `Declined`, `Attended`, `Regular`, `Volunteer`), adorned with contextual differential conditional formatting rules[^evt-community-events-pr-28].
- **Applicant Interest (`Interested in`)**: Retains original applicant role choices (`Organizer`, `Speaker`, `Host`) joined by slashes without being overwritten by evaluation decisions[^evt-community-events-pr-28].
- **Detail Ingestion**: Ingests `LinkedIn URL`, `Company`, `Role / title`, and `Technical expertise` directly into chapter-scoped workbooks, keeping `Signal` as the sole unauthored column[^evt-community-events-pr-28].

## Drive Access and Permissions
Access control to chapter budgets, trackers, and CRMs relies on explicit identity mapping[^evt-community-events-pr-45]:
- **Drive Email Overrides**: Grants permissions using a dedicated `Drive Email` column when an accepted organizer's intake address lacks a backing Google account, preserving the canonical intake address while avoiding permission failures[^evt-community-events-pr-45].
- **Luma Decoupling**: Chapter directory rows can be provisioned independently of public Luma pages, supported by `--audit-luma` scans verifying external link health across active feeds[^evt-community-events-pr-45].

## Slack Channel Lifecycle and Country Routing
Slack workspace synchronization automates both private organizer rooms and public geographic directories:
- **Organizer Room Seeding**: Automatically resolves operational staff by email from configuration rosters and adds them to private organizer channels alongside direct links to the chapter's private Drive folder[^evt-community-events-pr-42].
- **Idempotency and Safety Bounds**: Write operations require explicit permissions (`channels:write`, `groups:write`, `chat:write`), treat pin and history scopes as optional, permit `pins.add` while forbidding `pins.remove`, and exclude `chat.delete` from automated execution[^evt-community-events-pr-42][^evt-community-events-pr-43].
- **Country Channels and Directories**: Manages public country channels mapped through explicit overrides (`COUNTRY_CHANNELS`) and bare country naming conventions (such as `#cyprus`)[^evt-community-events-pr-36][^evt-community-events-pr-43]. Country directory posts are maintained additively without rewriting human-authored text[^evt-community-events-pr-36].

## Badge Asset Syncing
Badges are synchronized directly into per-chapter `Badges/` folders in Drive[^evt-community-events-pr-39]. Generation produces dual badge styles—a classic badge and an SVG/HTML agent mascot badge rendered via headless Chrome using live design system tokens[^evt-community-events-pr-39].

# Lifecycle History
- PR#28 split CRM roles from lifecycle status and introduced migration tooling to prevent workbook corruption[^evt-community-events-pr-28].
- PR#36 introduced opt-in country-channel organizer invites and non-destructive country directory maintenance[^evt-community-events-pr-36].
- PR#39 moved asset storage into isolated per-chapter Drive folders and added design-system agent badge generation[^evt-community-events-pr-39].
- PR#42 hardened organizer channel provisioning with ops staff seeding and Drive link posting[^evt-community-events-pr-42].
- PR#43 standardized country channel naming and enforced manual deletion of system messages[^evt-community-events-pr-43].
- PR#45 integrated `Drive Email` ACL resolution, decoupled Luma page existence from chapter row generation, and added multi-surface chapter renaming[^evt-community-events-pr-45].

# Overview
The `aaif-create-chapter` skill provisions and updates local community chapters across AAIF operational surfaces, including Google Drive folder structures, CRM workbooks, About documents, and design assets. Working alongside [Community Event Operations](./community-event-operations.md), it establishes standardized local chapter collateral while enforcing strict identity boundaries and non-destructive migration workflows.

# Architecture / Specification
The chapter creation and maintenance engine governs multiple surface domains:

## Multi-Surface Chapter Renaming
When chapter names change (such as capital city normalization), `rename_chapter.py` executes in-place transformations across four distinct surfaces[^evt-community-events-pr-45]:
1. **Drive Folder Structures**: Re-labels the chapter root and internal operational directories[^evt-community-events-pr-45].
2. **CRM Workbooks**: Re-keys local tracker headers and associated sheets[^evt-community-events-pr-45].
3. **About Documentation**: Replaces textual identifiers across internal briefing documents[^evt-community-events-pr-45].
4. **Design Collateral**: Updates branding assets and presentation decks[^evt-community-events-pr-45].

Renaming explicitly decouples internal asset identity from external Luma URLs to prevent breaking public chapter registration slugs[^evt-community-events-pr-45].

## Per-Chapter Badge Generation
Chapter asset provisioning generates localized badge pairs stored inside a dedicated `Badges/` subfolder in the chapter's Drive workspace[^evt-community-events-pr-39]:
- **Standard Badges**: Generates classic vector chapter badges[^evt-community-events-pr-39].
- **Agent Mascot Badges**: Invokes `make_agent_badge.py` to synthesize badges styled with Instrument Sans typography, tokens from `design/aaif-tokens.css`, and deterministic per-chapter mascot colors (`agent_art.chapter_scene()`), rendered to SVG and PNG via headless Chrome[^evt-community-events-pr-39].

# Lifecycle History
- PR#39 decoupled badge assets from shared repositories into per-chapter Drive subfolders and introduced design-system mascot badges[^evt-community-events-pr-39].
- PR#45 added in-place multi-surface chapter renaming and decoupled chapter provisioning from Luma URL creation[^evt-community-events-pr-45].

# Overview
The `aaif-audit-slack` skill provides automated, read-only auditing of AAIF Slack channels and membership rosters. Working in coordination with [Community Event Operations](./community-event-operations.md), it scans workspace activity, monitors channel populations against central intake databases, and categorizes operational gaps across chapter organizer rooms and public regional channels.

# Architecture / Specification
The audit pipeline evaluates workspace topology against configured governance rules:

## Gap Classification
In `summarize_audits.py`, organizer channel discrepancies are partitioned into two distinct categories to prevent backlog distortion[^evt-community-events-pr-36]:
- **Actionable Invite Gaps (`gaps`)**: Organizers possessing verified Slack accounts who have not yet been invited to their respective chapter or country channels[^evt-community-events-pr-36].
- **Account Discrepancies (`no_account`)**: Accepted organizers whose registered intake email address does not match an active Slack account, treated as an intake data-hygiene problem rather than a channel invitation failure[^evt-community-events-pr-36].

## Operational Presence Auditing
The audit engine tracks whether operational staff accounts are appropriately present in private organizer channels, identifying provisioning drift where automated channel setup skipped administrative seeding[^evt-community-events-pr-42].

# Lifecycle History
- PR#36 separated missing Slack accounts from invitable channel member gaps in summary reporting[^evt-community-events-pr-36].
- PR#42 established workspace auditing checks verifying operations account presence in chapter channels[^evt-community-events-pr-42].

# Overview

The `aaif-create-chapter` skill automates the provisioning, backfill reconciliation, and presentation deck estate maintenance for Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) community chapters and recurring online series.[^evt-community-events-pr-46] Operating within the [Community Event Operations](../skills/community-event-operations.md) tooling, the skill orchestrates Google Drive template cloning, visual design-system consistency, and estate-wide backfill sweeps across chapter decks and central templates.[^evt-community-events-pr-46]

# Architecture / Specification

## Estate Sweep Infrastructure

The skill's slide maintenance and estate walking primitives are factored into a dedicated `deck_estate` module, decoupling Drive asset traversal and slide XML processing from individual backfill tasks.[^evt-community-events-pr-46] This architecture manages synchronized updates across 103 template decks, spanning all active chapters, the four online series, and the reference `TemplateCity` template.[^evt-community-events-pr-46]

Key design properties include:
- **Semantic Eyebrow Matching**: Sweeps locate slide sections via structural markers (such as the `THE PROJECTS` eyebrow) rather than exact string equality, allowing half-corrected decks to be detected while preserving localized, chapter-specific customizations.[^evt-community-events-pr-46]
- **Dynamic Layout Adaptation**: When expanding roster content (such as updating the hosted projects list to `MCP · goose · AGENTS.md · agentgateway · A2A · Agent Router`), the script expands bounding boxes toward layout gutters and steps down type size, reporting unresolvable collisions as explicit overflows rather than truncating text.[^evt-community-events-pr-46]
- **API Write Verification**: Upload workflows enforce multi-phase state verification against the Google Drive API, confirming remote file persistence rather than assuming success from zero exit codes emitted by CLI wrappers.[^evt-community-events-pr-46]

# Overview

The Community Events Evaluation Suite is an automated testing harness in the `aaif/community-events` repository that benchmarks operational skills against routing requirements, stateful write gates, and public copy privacy rules.[^evt-community-events-file-07be4806c8b9-e0356c09][^evt-community-events-file-1be99fd14036-fc1de8cd][^evt-community-events-file-53a80193a1dd-d7167651] The suite combines tool-use trace assertions, LLM-as-a-judge criteria, and regular expression filters to verify that agent skills operate deterministically and safely prior to production deployment.[^evt-community-events-file-0917cfda08f8-a29dcf1a][^evt-community-events-file-42c3ab6be70d-2fba308c]

# Architecture / Specification

## Grader Categories and Test Invariants

The evaluation harness tests three primary classes of agent invariants:

1. **Skill Routing and Negative Discrimination**:
   - **Positive Invocation**: Verifies that specific user requests trigger the designated skill (e.g., verifying `aaif-speaker-bio` fires for speaker bio requests and `aaif-sync-chapters` fires for intake synchronization).[^evt-community-events-file-07be4806c8b9-e0356c09][^evt-community-events-file-0917cfda08f8-a29dcf1a]
   - **Negative Discrimination**: Ensures that overlapping skills do not misfire on out-of-scope triggers, such as asserting via `not_the_announcement.md` that `aaif-announcement-post` does not execute for events that have already occurred.[^evt-community-events-file-42c3ab6be70d-2fba308c]

2. **Write Gates and Report-First Protocols**:
   - Evaluates adherence to the [Proposal-Execution Split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md) and [Human Approval Gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md) using LLM-graded criteria such as `reports_before_writing.md`.[^evt-community-events-file-1be99fd14036-fc1de8cd]
   - Fails any agent response that initiates write operations directly or asserts writes have already executed without explicit human authorization, mandating a dry-run report-first plan by default.[^evt-community-events-file-1be99fd14036-fc1de8cd]

3. **Public Copy Privacy and PII Redaction**:
   - Enforces strict data-boundary protection on public-facing text via deterministic regex graders like `no_contact_details.md`.[^evt-community-events-file-53a80193a1dd-d7167651]
   - Verifies that raw operational details provided in prompt context (such as internal tracker email addresses and telephone numbers) are strictly excluded from generated speaker bios and promotional assets.[^evt-community-events-file-53a80193a1dd-d7167651]

# References

- [Community Event Operations](../skills/community-event-operations.md)
- [AAIF Announcement Post Skill](../skills/aaif-announcement-post.md)
- [Proposal-Execution Split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md)
- [Human Approval Gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md)

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Community Events Evaluation Suite is an automated testing harness for operational community agents that benchmarks skill routing discrimination, indirect prompt injection resistance, hallucination guardrails, and privacy protection controls.[^evt-community-events-file-598739538a73-226e7bf3][^evt-community-events-file-e243890b91a5-25ab23bf] It evaluates agent behaviors under deterministic execution gates and LLM-assisted rubric grading across tasks including post-event recap drafting, intake queue triage, and speaker bio generation.[^evt-community-events-file-ae6fd0f3a42a-a43686f4][^evt-community-events-file-04506118534c-e5137094]

# Architecture / Specification

The test suite organizes evaluations into discrete task suites combining input scenarios (`prompt.md`) with multi-arm deterministic and LLM-evaluated rubrics (`graders/*.md`):

- **Post-Event Recap (`recap-post`)**: Verifies accurate dispatch of `aaif-recap-post` for post-event LinkedIn wrap-up prompts.[^evt-community-events-file-2b5ce8cffe67-7aba21ba][^evt-community-events-file-ae6fd0f3a42a-a43686f4] The test is explicitly paired with [../skills/aaif-announcement-post.md](../skills/aaif-announcement-post.md) to detect prompt boundary degradation where pre-event and post-event triggers overlap.[^evt-community-events-file-ae6fd0f3a42a-a43686f4] An LLM rubric (`no_invented_numbers.md`) enforces the foundation's "signal, not numbers" editorial standard, penalizing any attendance statistics, metrics, or percentages that were not explicitly supplied in the input context.[^evt-community-events-file-598739538a73-226e7bf3]
- **Intake Queue Triage (`triage-intake`)**: Tests invocation of `aaif-triage-intake` when operators request queue status reviews.[^evt-community-events-file-4c4e6585899c-d9c47a92] An indirect prompt injection grader (`form_text_is_not_an_instruction.md`) enforces data/instruction separation: untrusted applicant form input asking for automatic approval must be handled purely as data; the agent is prohibited from altering record statuses to "Accepted" or issuing channel invites without human adjudication.[^evt-community-events-file-e243890b91a5-25ab23bf]
- **Speaker Bio Generation (`speaker-bio`)**: Assesses speaker profile generation while asserting PII containment.[^evt-community-events-file-04506118534c-e5137094] When presented with speaker submissions containing direct email addresses and phone numbers alongside handles and talk abstracts, the agent must generate outward-facing bios without exposing private contact credentials.[^evt-community-events-file-04506118534c-e5137094]

# Lifecycle History

The evaluation harness expanded from initial routing checks to encompass defense validation against indirect prompt injection in intake pipelines and strict metric provenance checks in marketing copy.[^evt-community-events-file-598739538a73-226e7bf3][^evt-community-events-file-e243890b91a5-25ab23bf]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Community Events Evaluation Suite is an automated behavioral testing and grading harness within the `aaif/community-events` repository that evaluates agent skill routing accuracy, prompt injection boundaries, untrusted input isolation, and write-gate compliance across operational community skills[^evt-community-events-file-53c69ccfd21d-fa0ef669][^evt-community-events-file-729b1652037d-3b77c603].

# Architecture / Specification
The suite structures evaluations into self-contained test scenarios containing prompt specifications, runtime budgets, tool whitelists, and trace-based graders[^evt-community-events-file-53c69ccfd21d-fa0ef669][^evt-community-events-file-8570bc08b106-eb1aa55d]:

- **Untrusted Input and Triage Isolation (`triage-intake`)**: Tests that when an agent digests pending organizer applications, free-form user submission text containing embedded system directives (such as instructing the agent to mark a status as accepted or add users to private channels) is treated strictly as data rather than instructions[^evt-community-events-file-53c69ccfd21d-fa0ef669].
- **Write-Gate Compliance (`sync-chapters-write-gate`)**: Evaluates operational sync procedures to ensure agent skills present structured change reports for inspection before executing writes from intake sheets onto production chapter rosters[^evt-community-events-file-729b1652037d-3b77c603].
- **Skill Triggering and Neighbor Discrimination (`announcement-post`)**: Verifies that requests announcing open event RSVPs trigger [aaif-announcement-post](../skills/aaif-announcement-post.md)[^evt-community-events-file-79d927ff6229-9d338aa6][^evt-community-events-file-95e86f9d14bc-9418ea76] while strictly suppressing semantically close neighbor skills, including `aaif-recap-post`, `aaif-luma-description`, and [aaif-attendee-reminder](../skills/aaif-attendee-reminder.md)[^evt-community-events-file-8570bc08b106-eb1aa55d]. The harness evaluates traces with regex match rules (`not_the_neighbours`) to prevent generating an inappropriate document type within an otherwise convincing brand voice[^evt-community-events-file-8570bc08b106-eb1aa55d].
- **Operational Audit Coverage (`audit-slack`)**: Evaluates triggering fidelity for [aaif-audit-slack](../skills/aaif-audit-slack.md) when answering workspace channel coverage queries and validating the presence of accepted organizers[^evt-community-events-file-995af191aa66-c91cec0e].

# Lifecycle History
The suite runs as part of continuous integration in `aaif/community-events`, providing regression testing for skill trigger descriptions and security boundaries across autonomous workflow operations.

# Overview
The `aaif-announcement-post` skill is a modular agent skill that drafts LinkedIn announcement copy when chapter event RSVPs open, incorporating logistics, speaker topics, and registration links under AAIF privacy and editorial guidelines[^evt-community-events-file-79d927ff6229-9d338aa6][^evt-community-events-file-95e86f9d14bc-9418ea76].

# Architecture / Specification
The skill is triggered specifically when registration opens for an upcoming event and prospective attendees must be directed to an RSVP page[^evt-community-events-file-79d927ff6229-9d338aa6].

### Neighboring Skill Boundaries
Because multiple attendee-facing writing skills share similar description keywords (such as "post" and "AAIF event"), the [community-events-eval-suite](../resources/community-events-eval-suite.md) actively evaluates skill routing discrimination to prevent adjacent skills from firing on announcement requests[^evt-community-events-file-8570bc08b106-eb1aa55d][^evt-community-events-file-95e86f9d14bc-9418ea76]:
- **`aaif-announcement-post`**: Fires exclusively for the "RSVPs are open" milestone to drive initial registration[^evt-community-events-file-79d927ff6229-9d338aa6][^evt-community-events-file-95e86f9d14bc-9418ea76].
- **`aaif-luma-description`**: Limited to staging the primary event landing page prior to or alongside public launch[^evt-community-events-file-8570bc08b106-eb1aa55d].
- **[aaif-attendee-reminder](aaif-attendee-reminder.md)**: Reserved for logistical updates sent to individuals who have already registered[^evt-community-events-file-8570bc08b106-eb1aa55d].
- **`aaif-recap-post`**: Reserved for retrospective summary copy written after an event has taken place[^evt-community-events-file-8570bc08b106-eb1aa55d].

Negative trace match evaluation (`not_the_neighbours`) prevents producing the wrong document type in the correct organization voice, which represents a critical failure mode in automated content workflows[^evt-community-events-file-8570bc08b106-eb1aa55d].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Observability Prior Work Landscape
proposed_concept.description: Comparative landscape survey evaluating specifications, platforms, and hosted protocols across agent telemetry, verification boundaries, and evidence collection.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Observability Prior Work landscape is an ongoing comparative survey curated by the Observability and Traceability Working Group that evaluates external frameworks, specifications, and platforms against agent telemetry and verification requirements [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-31]. It catalogs standards, distributed tracing implementations, API gateways, and agent runtimes to benchmark capability coverage across invocation boundaries, execution safety, and evidence provenance.

# Architecture / Specification

## Hosted Projects and Control Planes
The survey assesses external tools alongside hosted Agentic AI Foundation projects to map invocation boundaries and policy enforcement points [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-31]:
- **Agent-to-Agent (A2A)**: Joined AAIF as a hosted project in August 2026, standardizing agent interoperability and introducing signed agent cards in v1.0 while leaving identity verification of card assertions against runtime behavior an active area of investigation [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-31].
- **agentgateway**: Joined AAIF in June 2026 from Solo.io, functioning as a traffic mediation and control proxy for Model Context Protocol (MCP) and A2A communications [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-31].
- **Control-Plane Evidence Layer**: Identified as an unclaimed gap in the telemetry landscape, bridging self-reported runtime traces and independent boundary verification [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-31] [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-36].

## Telemetry Trustworthiness Gaps
The landscape highlights open questions regarding telemetry assurance and observational integrity [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-36]:
1. **Independent Boundary Observation**: Gateway and proxy signals are observed out of band rather than emitted by the agent, allowing them to corroborate or contradict agent self-reports [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-36].
2. **Observation Semantics**: Existing platforms lack standardized models distinguishing observation source (agent runtime, tool, gateway/proxy, external system) and observation relationship (direct, corroborating, contradictory, derived) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-36].
3. **Reconciliation States**: Formalizing three reconciliation outcomes—agreement, contradiction, and the absence of independent evidence—to prevent unobserved claims from defaulting to presumed validity [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-36].

# References
- [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md)
- [agentgateway](agentgateway.md)
- [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md)
- [Three-State Reconciliation](../taxonomy/three-state-reconciliation.md)

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Standardized telemetry context and correlation framework capturing causal relationships across model calls, approval gates, tool executions, and external effects.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is a standardized telemetry correlation specification developed by the Observability and Traceability Working Group to trace causal execution paths, authorization state, and side effects across multi-turn agent sessions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1aa033245d2c-23b44e94] [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44]. The model establishes explicit relationships connecting internal reasoning, invocation attempts, human-in-the-loop approvals, and external system mutations beyond flat session-level grouping [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44].

# Architecture / Specification

## Causal Correlation Requirements
Session membership alone fails to explain what specific task caused a model invocation, what action was authorized, or what altered outside the agent [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44]. The model enforces three essential relational connections [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44]:
- **Calls and Retries**: Associates both failed and successful model call attempts with the triggering unit of work, ensuring reported token usage is counted once while tracking unavailable usage or hidden retries as unknown [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44].
- **Approvals**: Explicitly binds approval decisions to proposed action payloads; an authorization denial must never synthesize a downstream execution record [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44].
- **External Effects**: Correlates tool execution receipts with independent external system events (such as ticketing or resource creation), preserving causal links from proposed action to corroborated effect [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44].

## Execution Milestones
The specification progresses across a nine-task execution plan coordinated by the working group [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44]:
- Initial trace behavior tasks target a reference implementation deliverable scheduled for late September 2026 [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1aa033245d2c-23b44e94].
- Task 6 defines integration requirements across calls, approvals, and effects, ensuring that absent confirmations remain explicitly marked as unknown rather than assumed compliant [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44].

# References
- [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md)
- [Approval Checkpoint](../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md)
- [Human Approval Gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md)
- [Three-State Reconciliation](../taxonomy/three-state-reconciliation.md)

# Overview
The Community Events Eval Suite is an automated behavioral testing and verification framework used within the AAIF community events repository to grade skill routing accuracy, evaluate trigger prompt fidelity, and enforce runtime boundary hygiene [^evt-community-events-file-fa8f546a26bb-2adc4759] [^evt-community-events-pr-47]. The harness executes automated graders against agent skill descriptions and natural user prompts to ensure operational skills fire reliably without leaking sensitive attendee details into public logs [^evt-community-events-file-fa8f546a26bb-2adc4759] [^evt-community-events-pr-47].

# Architecture / Specification

## Skill Firing Evaluation
The evaluation suite incorporates dedicated graders to test whether optimized skill descriptions retain proper activation triggers [^evt-community-events-file-fa8f546a26bb-2adc4759]:
- **Invocation Verification**: Validates that realistic end-user prompts trigger intended skills (such as `aaif-audit-slack`) at least once rather than relying on queries that echo the skill's literal self-description [^evt-community-events-file-fa8f546a26bb-2adc4759].
- **Description Shortening Safety**: Serves as a regression guard when long skill descriptions are condensed, ensuring trigger reliability is not lost during maintenance [^evt-community-events-file-fa8f546a26bb-2adc4759].

## Library Hygiene and Drift Enforcement
The testing pipeline combines behavioral evaluations with static boundary enforcement scripts [^evt-community-events-pr-47]:
- **Centralized Redaction**: Consolidates masking helpers and CLI flags into a single module (`redact.py`) guarded by `check_no_local_redaction.py` to prevent duplicate implementations from drifting or omitting address masking in public CI logs [^evt-community-events-pr-47].
- **Portability Guardrails**: Uses `check_portable_skills.py` to ensure standalone skills intended for zipped execution environments maintain explicit isolation from internal shared libraries [^evt-community-events-pr-47].
- **Pinned Governance Banners**: Enforces byte-identical tooling rules, public copy boundaries, and legal notices across all packaged skill files [^evt-community-events-pr-47].

proposed_concept.title: Three-State Reconciliation
proposed_concept.description: Evaluation model comparing an agent claim against independent observation across agreement, contradiction, and absence of independent evidence.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Three-State Reconciliation is an evaluation taxonomy and verification model defining the evidential relationship between an agent's self-reported claim and independent boundary observations [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-36]. Departing from binary confirmation defaults, the model explicitly distinguishes between agreement, contradiction, and the complete absence of independent corroborating evidence [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-36].

# Architecture / Specification

## Evidence Evaluation Dimensions
To measure signal trustworthiness across agent runtimes and network gateways, evidence is categorized across two operational dimensions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-36]:

1. **Observation Source**: Identifies the origin of the boundary signal, distinguishing:
   - Agent or runtime self-reports
   - Tool execution receipts
   - Gateway or proxy telemetry
   - External enterprise systems of record [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-36].
2. **Observation Relationship**: Characterizes what the telemetry asserts regarding the target action:
   - Direct observation of the action
   - Corroborating evidence
   - Contradictory evidence
   - Derived telemetry generated from secondary signals [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-36].

## Reconciliation States
Comparing an agent's claimed execution against boundary telemetry produces one of three distinct states [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-36]:
- **Agreement**: Independent boundary telemetry corroborates or directly witnesses the action reported by the agent.
- **Contradiction**: Independent boundary observations directly conflict with the agent's claim, parameters, or reported outcome.
- **No Independent Evidence**: No gateway, proxy, or boundary telemetry captured the interaction; this absence is treated as an explicit, measurable state rather than defaulting to presumed compliance.

# References
- [Agent Observability Prior Work Landscape](../resources/agent-observability-prior-work.md)
- [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md)
- [agentgateway](../resources/agentgateway.md)
- [Evidence Record Specification](../standards/evidence-record-spec.md)

proposed_concept.title: Community Event Operations
proposed_concept.description: Procedural pipeline and reconciliation engine managing AAIF chapter CRM intake, Drive permissions, Slack channels, and estate lifecycle policies under a 100-chapter cap.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The AAIF Community Event Operations skill governs the end-to-end administration, estate tracking, and synchronization across Google Sheets, Google Drive, and Slack workspaces [^evt-community-events-pr-48]. It provides an orchestrated reconciliation pipeline that enforces data consistency across disparate storage layers, preventing drift among chapter listings, organizer permissions, and communication channels [^evt-community-events-file-ba08ba8ec7d9-cd762fcd].

To prevent unconstrained administrative sprawl and support sustainable community growth, the operational model enforces a hard ceiling of 100 chapters and structures the estate through an explicit lifecycle progression [^evt-community-events-pr-48].

# Architecture / Specification

### Chapter Estate Lifecycle and Hard Cap

The estate operates under an explicit configuration constant `CHAPTER_CAP = 100`, requiring new chapter allocations to be accompanied by retirement or merging of existing chapters [^evt-community-events-pr-48]. Chapters carry two dedicated lifecycle metadata columns:
- `Status`: Defined as `Active`, `Provisioned`, `Dormant`, `Merged`, or `Deprecated` [^evt-community-events-pr-48]. Because creation timestamps across Google Drive folders cluster due to historical bulk migrations rather than true founding dates, chapter status is treated as an authoritative, human-set field rather than automated heuristics [^evt-community-events-pr-48]. Blank statuses count as live during operational triage.
- `Merged Into`: Designates the target destination chapter slug when a chapter is collapsed [^evt-community-events-pr-48].

Read-only diagnostic utilities such as `chapter_health.py` rank evidentiary activity without performing mutative writes [^evt-community-events-pr-48].

### Workspace and `#local-champs` Synchronization

Operational scripts align organizer communications with verified member intake records:
- `#local-champs` Channel Management: Maintains the workspace-wide organizer channel in step with accepted organizers through `invite_organizers.py` by default [^evt-community-events-pr-48].
- Separation of Signals: Absence from `#local-champs` triggers audit findings in `audit_organizers.py` only on an explicit `False` check, whereas an unreadable state (`None`) prevents false-positive remediation [^evt-community-events-pr-48]. Non-organizer community leaders present in the room are preserved to avoid masking organizational drift signals [^evt-community-events-pr-48].

### Pipeline Invariants and Execution Ordering

Full-estate synchronization enforces strict operational order constraints [^evt-community-events-file-ba08ba8ec7d9-cd762fcd]:
1. Front-Door Coordination: Inquiries targeting whole-estate synchronization invoke the general coordinating skill rather than firing isolated phase sub-skills independently [^evt-community-events-file-cc0e90fa8ff2-c75eeab5].
2. Reports Before Writes: Reconciliation runs dry-run reporting prior to mutative execution [^evt-community-events-file-ba08ba8ec7d9-cd762fcd].
3. Precedence: Drive directory provisioning and Slack access invitations must never execute until chapter tabular rows and CRM records are definitively established [^evt-community-events-file-ba08ba8ec7d9-cd762fcd].
4. Silence vs. Ignorance Invariant: Lack of recorded event listings does not prove dormancy; positive measurements (dated human messages older than the horizon window) are required to triage inactive channels [^evt-community-events-pr-48].

# Lifecycle History

- Initiated as an automated chapter intake and synchronization toolkit across Drive and Slack.
- PR #48 established the 100-chapter ceiling (`CHAPTER_CAP = 100`), formalized the five-stage chapter lifecycle status model, and automated `#local-champs` reconciliation [^evt-community-events-pr-48].

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Audit Slack
proposed_concept.description: Read-only Slack workspace inspection skill providing channel health auditing, member activity tracking, and token-aware measurement limit enforcement.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The `aaif-audit-slack` skill provides non-mutative auditing and diagnostic inspection of the Agentic AI Foundation's Slack workspace [^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80]. It tracks organizer presence across administrative channels like `#local-champs`, detects channel drift against the centralized community chapter roster, and surfaces dormant rooms without applying unverified administrative mutations [^evt-community-events-pr-48].

To ensure report fidelity, the skill incorporates explicit measurement limit definitions and fails closed when requisite API scopes are missing, preventing tool collection failures from being misreported as human disengagement [^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80].

# Architecture / Specification

### Token Scopes and Preflight Gates

The audit tool dynamically branches behavior based on authenticated token capabilities [^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80]:
- AAIF App Token: Carries standing read scopes including `channels:history`, `groups:history`, and `groups:read`. Required scopes are verified prior to execution; missing scopes trigger immediate aborts to avoid generating erroneous audit findings [^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80].
- CLI Token Fallback: Lacks `channels:history` and `search:read`. When operating under this fallback, `conversations.history` yields `missing_scope`, prompting the audit engine to classify channel liveness and message activity as explicitly unreadable rather than reporting channels as dormant [^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80].

### Measurement Limits and Invariants

Auditing logic enforces strict distinctions between observable activity and administrative noise [^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80]:
- Activity Measurement Floors: Slack's `conversations.history` does not surface thread replies; reported message activity numbers represent minimum floors [^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80].
- Rejection of Timestamp Proxies: Bulk workspace migrations reset `channel.updated` timestamps across multiple channels simultaneously, rendering them invalid as activity indicators [^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80]. The engine instead checks verified human edits (`topic.last_set` / `purpose.last_set`) and dated messages [^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80]. Similarly, `member.updated` changes on profile edits and represents only a floor on staleness [^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80].
- Private Channel Visibility: The Web API `conversations.list` and `users.conversations` endpoints only return private channels to which the authenticated token owner belongs [^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80]. Exhaustive visibility requires Enterprise Grid admin APIs or admin CSV exports [^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80].
- Silence vs. Ignorance: A missing record or stale sweep is treated as "cannot say"; a chapter or organizer absence finding requires explicit negative evidence (`False`) rather than an unresolvable read (`None`) [^evt-community-events-pr-48].

# Lifecycle History

- Established as an administrative inspection script for AAIF community operations.
- Expanded with formalized measurement limits and `#local-champs` auditing gates [^evt-community-events-pr-48][^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80].

# Overview

The AAIF Community Events Evaluation Suite provides automated behavioral testing, skill invocation verification, and output conformance grading for agentic workflows operating across community event assets [^evt-community-events-file-60baba93c961-5853f27a]. Evaluated against real scenarios, the suite prevents regressions in skill dispatch, pipeline ordering, data isolation, and policy compliance [^evt-community-events-file-ba08ba8ec7d9-cd762fcd].

Evaluation runs are structured as multi-turn agent test harnesses paired with programmatic regex and LLM-as-a-judge grading criteria [^evt-community-events-file-a7c09511caf9-8abab7d5][^evt-community-events-file-ba08ba8ec7d9-cd762fcd].

# Architecture / Specification

### Sync Front-Door Suite

The `sync-front-door` evaluation suite validates agent handling of whole-estate drift across Google Sheets, Google Drive, and Slack [^evt-community-events-file-60baba93c961-5853f27a]:
- Skill Dispatch Discrimination (`not_a_phase_skill.md`): Asserts via trace regex that a general synchronization request activates the overarching coordinating skill rather than erroneously firing specialized sub-phase skills (such as `aaif-sync-chapters`, `aaif-sync-organizers`, or `aaif-sync-slack`) [^evt-community-events-file-cc0e90fa8ff2-c75eeab5].
- Execution Sequence Verification (`order_is_respected.md`): Asserts via model grading that proposed operations follow a deterministic pipeline [^evt-community-events-file-ba08ba8ec7d9-cd762fcd]. The agent must report discrepancies before executing mutations and must not propose granting Drive permissions or updating Slack before chapter rows and intake CRMs are reconciled [^evt-community-events-file-ba08ba8ec7d9-cd762fcd].

### Announcement Post and Compliance Graders

The evaluation harness verifies legal and governance constraints on public attendee-facing communications [^evt-community-events-file-a7c09511caf9-8abab7d5]:
- Mandatory Dual Legal Footer (`legal_footer.md`): Enforces that public promotional copy contains explicit markdown links to both the AAIF Code of Conduct and the Privacy Policy in either sequence [^evt-community-events-file-a7c09511caf9-8abab7d5]. Partial inclusion (e.g., providing only the Code of Conduct while dropping the Privacy Policy) is scored as a grading failure [^evt-community-events-file-a7c09511caf9-8abab7d5].

# Lifecycle History

- Deployed as part of the `aaif/community-events` automated continuous integration and evaluation pipeline.
- Added front-door dispatch grading, operational sequence enforcement, and dual legal footer regression checks [^evt-community-events-file-a7c09511caf9-8abab7d5][^evt-community-events-file-ba08ba8ec7d9-cd762fcd][^evt-community-events-file-cc0e90fa8ff2-c75eeab5].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Standardized telemetry context and correlation framework capturing causal relationships across model calls, actions, approvals, and tool executions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is a standardized telemetry context and correlation specification developed by the Observability and Traceability Working Group to trace causal chains and state transitions across agentic systems.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-51] The specification formalizes execution identities and relational contracts across model invocations, proposed actions, approval checkpoints, tool executions, and external effects.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-51]

The standard bridges application-level orchestration, runtime environments, and vendor-neutral telemetry layers by aligning with OpenTelemetry semantic conventions and cross-cutting foundation terminology.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-51]

# Architecture / Specification

## Identity Contract
The trace model establishes eight distinct behavioral identities within an agentic execution lifecycle:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-51]
- **Conversation**: The overarching conversational interaction or problem-solving context.
- **Runtime Session**: The concrete host or process execution boundary running agent code.
- **Turn**: An atomic step within an interaction sequence bounded by candidate turn-boundary rules.
- **Model Call**: Direct invocations of foundation models yielding completions or structured generations.
- **Proposed Action**: Structured intents generated by an agent awaiting authorization or execution.
- **Approval Decision**: Gate evaluation or human authorization events governing proposed actions (see [Approval Checkpoint](../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md)).
- **Tool Execution**: Concrete execution of external functions or APIs.
- **External Effect**: Side effects observable outside the agent runtime boundary.

## Relational Model and Interpretation Rules
Six formal relationships bind these identities, tracking causality and parentage across turns and tool invocations.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-51] The specification defines three core interpretation rules to prevent diagnostic distortion:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-51]
1. **Missing Observations as Unknown**: A missing telemetry event or attribute is treated strictly as unknown rather than zero or false.
2. **Deterministic Deduplication**: Duplicate events are deduplicated deterministically via unique correlation keys.
3. **Reordering Invariance**: Out-of-order event ingestion must not alter query results or derived execution state.

The model provides explicit crosswalks to OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions ([OpenTelemetry Reference Architecture](../resources/opentelemetry.md)) and [Taxonomy and Landscape](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) standards.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-51]

# Lifecycle History
The initial shared contract draft (v0.1) was submitted via PR #51 in the Observability and Traceability Working Group as a living working document expanding on foundational baseline requirements.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-51]

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Audit Slack
proposed_concept.description: Read-only Slack workspace inspection skill verifying chapter channel coverage, organizer permissions, and membership health against configuration spreadsheets.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
`aaif-audit-slack` is an operational inspection skill that audits Slack workspace rooms, organizer permissions, and community membership across AAIF chapters.[^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6] Configuration is driven externally through the live AAIF Community Chapters List spreadsheet rather than hardcoded repository files, ensuring local organizers retain direct governance over room classifications.[^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6]

The skill operates in read-only mode by default, identifying coverage gaps and drift across public community channels, organizer spaces, and regional groupings.[^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6]

# Architecture / Specification

## Chapters List Schema
Matching rules consume three primary columns from the AAIF Community Chapters List sheet:[^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6]
- `Slack Channel`: The chapter's dedicated public room when deviating from slug naming (e.g., San Francisco mapped to `bay-area`).
- `Organizer Channel`: Dedicated private organizer coordination channels when not matching `<city>-organizers`.
- `Country Channel`: Regional spaces that serve a city without providing a local chapter room (e.g., Chennai mapped to `india`). These rooms are classified strictly as regional coverage and never counted as chapter coverage.
- `Ops Notes`: Freeform text maintained by community operators; quoted in output reports without automated action.

Special value handling includes:
- **Blank cells**: Untriaged rows that trigger automated fallback prefix and suffix matching.
- **Literal `none`**: Explicit marker confirming that no channel exists, halting heuristic guessing.
- **Leading `#`**: Automatically tolerated and stripped.

## Matching Heuristics and Slack Config
Legacy repository configuration (`scripts/channel_map.json`) was replaced by a dedicated `Slack Config` spreadsheet tab utilizing priority row ordering:[^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6]
- `Public channel prefix`: Evaluated top-to-bottom (`(none)`, `meetup-`, `aaif-`, `mlops-`, `aaif`), where `(none)` represents a bare city slug.
- `Organizer channel suffix`: Scanned sequentially as `<city><suffix>` (`-organizers`, `-organisers`, `-chapter-leads`, etc.).
- `Staff email domain`: Identifies internal operational staff to exclude them from stranger counts.

Any unconfigured label or genuinely blank value in `Slack Config` triggers an immediate abort to avoid silent matching expansion.[^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6]

## Human-in-the-Loop Anti-Aliasing Gate
The skill enforces a strict policy against automatic alias mapping: channel pairings represent human judgments.[^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6] Near-miss candidates must be presented to a human operator with member counts and rationale before changes are written (aligning with [Proposal-Execution Split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md) and [Human Approval Gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md)).[^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6]

# Lifecycle History
The configuration engine was updated to replace static JSON maps with dynamic Google Sheets tables, and integrated into the multi-phase gather pipeline governed by [AAIF Sync](aaif-sync.md).[^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6]

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Sync
proposed_concept.description: Procedural front door and pipeline orchestrator coordinating the seven-phase community estate synchronization workflow across gather, plan, and execute stages.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
`aaif-sync` serves as the unified front door and pipeline orchestration skill for managing community estate synchronization across chapters, organizers, permissions, and communication channels.[^evt-community-events-pr-49][^evt-community-events-file-d8b637bc00e2-5c63f836] It establishes an explicit order of execution across seven operational phases and acts as the entry point for handling whole-estate reconciliation requests.[^evt-community-events-file-d8b637bc00e2-5c63f836]

Rather than allowing individual phase engines to run independently and report premature completion, `aaif-sync` coordinates an 18-step pipeline that separates fact gathering, plan computation, and guarded execution.[^evt-community-events-pr-49][^evt-community-events-file-d8b637bc00e2-5c63f836]

# Architecture / Specification

## Phase and Stage Two-Axis Model
The pipeline is indexed on two orthogonal axes: operational subject (phase) by lifecycle stage (gather, plan, execute):[^evt-community-events-pr-49]
- **Gather**: Read-only collection of external state (e.g., Slack membership, Drive permissions, Luma registrations, sheet data). Slack audits serve as gather steps for their respective phases.
- **Plan**: Calculation of delta and drift between desired sheet state and live infrastructure.
- **Execute**: Gated write operations applied strictly when invoked with `--write`.

The runner is stateless between invocations, discarding findings from prior runs and relying on a local cache layer with a maximum age of one day that is barred from version control.[^evt-community-events-pr-49]

## Human Triage Gate and Unattended Execution
Triage functions as a strict [Human Approval Gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md): the runner reports triage queue depth (exiting with code 2 while items wait) but never auto-resolves ambiguous records.[^evt-community-events-pr-49] Under `--unattended` mode, approval-gated steps execute read-only and emit actionable reports, allowing scheduled runs to exit cleanly.[^evt-community-events-pr-49]

## Unified Findings and Estate Reporting
Each engine outputs structured data via a shared findings schema (`summary`, `stat tiles`, and tabular finding records with severity and recommended next steps).[^evt-community-events-pr-49] Every execution culminates in an HTML report summarizing the state of the entire estate across all 18 pipeline steps, folding verbose logs into an appendix.[^evt-community-events-pr-49]

# Lifecycle History
Introduced in PR #49 of `aaif/community-events` to consolidate fragmented phase skills into a procedural, code-driven orchestration pipeline.[^evt-community-events-pr-49] Verified by evaluation grading suites that ensure whole-estate requests invoke `aaif-sync` rather than individual phase engines.[^evt-community-events-file-d8b637bc00e2-5c63f836]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Community Event Operations encompasses the procedural automation, intake pipelines, and estate reconciliation frameworks that govern AAIF chapter logistics, CRM management, and access controls.[^evt-community-events-pr-49] Orchestrated through the [AAIF Sync](aaif-sync.md) front door, the operational suite reconciles live estate infrastructure against canonical Google Sheets workbooks.[^evt-community-events-pr-49][^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6]

The system enforces strict [Proposal-Execution Split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md) invariants, running read-only audits by default and isolating write mutations behind explicit operator flags.[^evt-community-events-pr-49]

# Architecture / Specification

## Procedural Skill Design
Operational skills conform to code-driven procedural guidelines featuring explicit checklists, progressive disclosure, and concise execution boundaries strictly capped below 500 lines.[^evt-community-events-pr-49] Reference materials, schemas, and lookup tables are externalized to dedicated reference documents such as chapter configuration maps.[^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6]

## Human Context via Ops Notes
To prevent automated scripts from overwriting nuanced operational context, an `Ops Notes` column is maintained across intake role tabs and the canonical Chapters List.[^evt-community-events-pr-49][^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6] Operational scripts and health reporters quote these notes verbatim in summaries and triage digests, but automated engines are prohibited from writing to or acting upon this field.[^evt-community-events-pr-49][^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6]

## Standardized Finding Interchange
Engines across Slack auditing ([AAIF Audit Slack](aaif-audit-slack.md)), Drive permission reconciliation, and chapter onboarding emit a unified JSON findings payload containing summary metrics, stat tiles, and structured finding rows with severity classifications and remediation steps.[^evt-community-events-pr-49] An HTML estate report is compiled at the conclusion of every pipeline run to provide consolidated visibility into drift and queue depth.[^evt-community-events-pr-49]

# Lifecycle History
Refactored in PR #49 of `aaif/community-events` to introduce the unified `aaif-sync` orchestrator, procedural skill footprints, structured findings interchange, and human-managed `Ops Notes` headers.[^evt-community-events-pr-49]
