proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Telemetry context, turn correlation, and causality framework tracking agent execution across model calls, approval gates, and external effects via OpenTelemetry.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an OpenTelemetry-aligned standard and correlation framework developed by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) to follow an agent's work across conversation turns, runtime interruptions, and distributed system boundaries[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831]. It establishes a shared semantic contract for identifying agent work units, capturing causal relationships, and harmonizing GenAI telemetry across heterogeneous agent runtimes and monitoring backends.

# Architecture / Specification
The trace model defines identity conventions, boundary semantics, and relationship links addressing four core runtime questions[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831]:
- **Continuity:** Identifies which interaction turns belong together across session pauses, process restarts, or asynchronous resumptions without requiring consumers to query internal agent state.
- **Calls and retries:** Distinguishes underlying foundation model calls and retries serving a specific turn to prevent double-counting token usage or computational work.
- **Approvals:** Formally correlates human approval or policy decisions with candidate tool actions and tracks whether approved actions were executed.
- **Effects:** Binds tool executions to independently observable external side-effects recorded by external services.

### Execution Plan and Tasks
The working group maintains a nine-task execution plan tracking the standard's implementation and upstream contributions[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831]:
1. *Execution Plan Documentation:* Establishes baseline scope and tracking issues.
2. *Baseline Examples:* Validates shared scenarios using a support workflow (investigating delayed orders, proposing ticket creation, requesting approval, and executing via an instrumented test service) across [Goose](../resources/goose.md) and a secondary agent SDK.
3. *Shared Contract:* Defines identities, turn boundaries, and entity relationships mapped to OpenTelemetry conventions and AAIF taxonomy.
4. *Shared Test Suite:* Provides test fixtures, trace records, and validation checks runnable without a full application runtime.
5. *Session and Turn Correlation:* Demonstrates turn resumption across separate traces.
6. *Calls, Approvals, and Effects:* Validates telemetry relationships connecting provider retries, approval decisions, and external mutations.
7. *Independent Interpretation:* Confirms multiple query backends produce consistent interpretations from incomplete, delayed, or conflicting trace records.
8. *Runnable Harnesses:* Delivers multi-provider integration examples and test coverage matrices.
9. *Upstream Contribution:* Submits semantic convention proposals and GenAI guidance to the OpenTelemetry project.

### Boundary and Evidence Rules
The specification enforces clear operational boundaries[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831]:
- **Turn boundaries:** Tests one trace per turn as a candidate standalone default while preserving caller traces and defining turn-entry span structures.
- **Taxonomic alignment:** Distinguishes conversational continuity, runtime sessions, and agent trajectories, aligning terminology with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md).
- **Evidence semantics:** Treats missing telemetry as an unknown state rather than confirmation of success; observed approval records do not imply verified cryptographic attestation or runtime policy enforcement.
- **Privacy:** Mandates that raw payload and prompt content capture remains strictly opt-in.

# Lifecycle History
The execution plan and initial scope were finalized following working group reviews in August 2026, establishing Goose and an independent agent runtime as initial reference implementations alongside OpenTelemetry upstream contribution targets[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831].

proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing vendor-neutral agent telemetry standards, cross-boundary trace models, and OpenTelemetry semantic conventions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body that convenes practitioners, vendors, and standards organizations to establish vendor-neutral observability specifications, evaluation criteria, and tracing models for AI agents[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-18bf39f3]. The working group focuses on aligning existing instrumentation efforts, identifying telemetry gaps across agent reasoning and tool boundaries, and collaborating directly with external standards bodies including OpenTelemetry.

# Architecture / Specification
The working group structures its technical roadmap around several core initiatives[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-18bf39f3]:
- **[Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md):** An active nine-task execution plan standardizing session continuity, turn boundaries, provider call retries, human approvals, and external side-effects across runtimes like [Goose](../resources/goose.md)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831].
- **Landscape and Prior Work Surveys:** Ongoing analysis of existing commercial, open-source, and protocol tracing standards to avoid duplication[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-18bf39f3].
- **Use Case Inventories:** Real-world catalogs documenting cross-boundary debugging, security monitoring, and cost attribution requirements[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-18bf39f3].
- **OpenTelemetry Collaboration:** Proposing semantic convention expansions and guidance for agent reasoning steps, approval gates, and multi-turn execution.

### Governance and Operations
- **Leadership:** The working group is chaired by Pavan Sudheendra (Cisco) and co-chaired by Matthew Lee (Datadog), appointed by Platinum and Gold members for a term extending from March 1, 2026 to January 31, 2027[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-18bf39f3].
- **Cadence:** Biweekly working group meetings take place on Wednesdays at 10:00 AM PT over LFX Zoom[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-18bf39f3].
- **Operations:** GitHub issues serve as the primary source of truth for work items, task ownership, and decision logging, coordinated with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-18bf39f3][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831].

# Lifecycle History
Following formal chartering, the working group initiated the Agent Behavior Trace Model execution plan in August 2026, targeting initial multi-agent baseline implementations, test fixtures, and upstream submissions during Q3 2026[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831].

proposed_concept.title: Community Event Operations
proposed_concept.description: Procedural operations pipeline and reconciliation framework managing AAIF chapter CRM intake, Drive estate provisioning, and idempotent Google Workspace execution.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Community Event Operations encompasses the tooling, automation scripts, and verification rules that govern the Agentic AI Foundation's community estate, including chapter provisioning, slide generation, badge synchronization, and Google Workspace integrations[^evt-community-events-pr-51]. The pipeline enforces deterministic execution boundaries to prevent accidental state corruption, duplicate artifact generation, and credential leakage across automated agent tasks.

# Architecture / Specification
### Google Workspace Mutation Idempotency
Non-idempotent Google Workspace API mutations (such as `drive.files.create`, `drive.files.copy`, `appendDimension`, `insertDimension`, and `addSheet`) are strictly prohibited from utilizing automatic retries on timeouts[^evt-community-events-pr-51]. Because a timed-out request may have succeeded server-side, retrying blindly risks creating duplicate files, orphaned folders, or renamed duplicate sheet tabs that corrupt downstream discovery.
- **`aaif_events.gws.NO_RETRY`:** Centralized execution constant passed to API client wrappers to disable retries on write operations[^evt-community-events-pr-51].
- **`check_non_idempotent_retries.py`:** Automated static analysis guard detecting opt-in retry regressions across Drive and Sheets call sites[^evt-community-events-pr-51].
- **Centralized Client Wrappers:** Deprecated divergent, private `gws` wrappers across `create_chapter.py`, `create_series.py`, `slides_export.py`, `sync_badges.py`, and `install_ops_notes.py` in favor of a single shared `aaif_events.gws` module[^evt-community-events-pr-51].

### Credential Sanitization and Error Handling
- **Environment Scrubbing:** Subprocess execution scrubs environment variables, removing Slack tokens and limiting Google Workspace credentials to explicit child CLI requirements to prevent OAuth refresh tokens or client secrets from appearing in error traces[^evt-community-events-pr-51].
- **Payload Redaction:** Subprocess failure exceptions report the specific API verb and HTTP status from stderr without echoing raw request payloads or streamed tabular data from stdout[^evt-community-events-pr-51].
- **Operator Recovery:** Provisioning scripts fail with actionable human-readable abort sentences rather than raw stack traces, supporting `--resume` flags to recover orphaned resources[^evt-community-events-pr-51].

# Lifecycle History
In PR#51 (merged), the community events automation estate resolved non-idempotent retry corruption vectors across six API call sites, consolidated five drifting script wrappers into `aaif_events.gws`, and added mutation tests verifying that retry budgets and environment scrubbing cannot silently fail[^evt-community-events-pr-51].

# Overview
The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream is a cross-cutting Agentic AI Foundation body responsible for harmonizing definitions, maintaining canonical agent taxonomies, and establishing classification schemas across AAIF working groups[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-440eb159591a-01f77049]. It conducts systematic term review syncs to evaluate community submissions and reconcile terminology across workstreams.

# Architecture / Specification
The workstream coordinates vocabulary alignment across specialized working groups, including the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md), and [Attestation and Evidence Working Group](../working-groups/attestation-and-evidence.md). It operates review cycles that intake candidate terms, evaluate conceptual overlaps, and publish accepted definitions to the foundation's official terminology registry.

# Lifecycle History
The workstream tracks monthly progress and term admissions in reports submitted to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-440eb159591a-01f77049]:
- **June 2026:** Secured charter approvals, established core SKOS-aligned data schemas, and launched the initial web portal publishing pipelines[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-440eb159591a-01f77049].
- **July 2026:** Evaluated 46 terms across four group review syncs and formally admitted 13 terms in the workstream's first taxonomy pull request, bringing backlog review progress to 67 of 128 terms[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-440eb159591a-01f77049].
- **August 2026:** Reviewed 53 terms across three terminology-review syncs (retaining 37 terms) and completed a four-pull-request review cycle leading into a September approval vote[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-440eb159591a-01f77049].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is a standardized telemetry context and causality framework developed by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) to record, correlate, and inspect runtime agent behavior across model queries, tool executions, and multi-agent interactions.

# Architecture / Specification
The specification establishes correlation semantics across hierarchical spans and asynchronous turns, connecting user intent prompts, subagent delegations, tool calls, and LLM responses. Rather than treating an agent invocation as an opaque single-hop service call, the trace model structures causality graphs that capture planning iterations, retry boundaries, and context evolution.

### Execution Plan and Milestones
The working group formalised the model execution plan through a dedicated issue series (issues #39–#47) encompassing core specification and implementation milestones [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-48]:
- **Shared Relationship Contract**: Formalising causality link schemas and turn relationship semantics [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-48].
- **Reference Implementations**: Constructing two distinct agent SDK reference implementations and provider API integration examples [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-48].
- **Conformance Suite**: Establishing reusable test suites validating cross-vendor trace serialization and link preservation [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-48].
- **Upstream Alignment**: Coordinating evidence-backed contributions into upstream open telemetry ecosystems [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-48].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-08**: WG Observability & Traceability approved the execution plan of record via PR#48, organizing work across issues #40–#47 while isolating separate recommendation tracks [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-48].

proposed_concept.title: aaif-sync
proposed_concept.description: Procedural pipeline orchestrator coordinating the eighteen-step AAIF community estate reconciliation across Slack, Google Workspace, and GitHub.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
`aaif-sync` is an operational agent skill and procedural runner executing the multi-step reconciliation pipeline that synchronizes AAIF chapter directories, organizer rosters, and community estate records across Slack, Google Workspace, and GitHub repositories.

# Architecture / Specification
The orchestration script executes an 18-step sequential pipeline straight through without manual narrowing to maintain state consistency across community assets [^evt-community-events-pr-53].

### Performance and Ephemeral Run Memos
To eliminate redundant API calls across separate step processes, the runner utilizes append-only, short-lived run memos via `jsoncache.RunMemo` [^evt-community-events-pr-52]:
- **Slack Run Memo (`AAIF_SLACK_RUN_MEMO`)**: Caches resolved organizer Slack accounts from `users.lookupByEmail` and `users.info` across steps [^evt-community-events-pr-52].
- **Google Workspace Run Memo (`AAIF_GWS_RUN_MEMO`)**: Memos Sheets and Drive reads strictly during report runs [^evt-community-events-pr-52]. Write-enabled runs (`--write`) disable read memoization to ensure steps observe preceding writes (such as `luma` reading updated chapter rows written by `chapters` or `resources`) [^evt-community-events-pr-52].
- **Lifecycle & Security**: Memo files are provisioned with 0600 file permissions and are automatically purged upon run termination, crash, or interrupt [^evt-community-events-pr-52].
- **Parallelized CRM Reads**: Chapter workbook inspection in `sync_crm` runs across a six-worker thread pool, incorporating folder IDs in download paths to prevent collision between identically named locations [^evt-community-events-pr-52].

### Runtime Keep-Awake Hook
To prevent workstation sleep states from interrupting long-running report executions and invalidating Google OAuth session tokens, the runner invokes a background `caffeinate -i -w <runner_pid>` process on macOS environments, ensuring execution continuity for the full eighteen-step sequence [^evt-community-events-pr-53].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-09**: Introduced `RunMemo` caching and CRM thread pooling in PR#52, reducing report run durations from ~50 minutes to ~11–21 minutes [^evt-community-events-pr-52].
- **2026-09**: Added macOS `caffeinate` runner guard in PR#53 to enforce end-to-end execution without sleep interruption [^evt-community-events-pr-53].

proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing shared workflow execution models, reference architectures, and taxonomy primitives for enterprise process integration.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Workflows and Process Integration Working Group (WG WPI) is a technical working group within the Agentic AI Foundation focused on standardizing architectural patterns, capability boundaries, and enterprise integration semantics for agent-driven automated workflows.

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its deliverables into three operational work streams [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a17a580f85c2-46ce20ea]:
1. **Reference Architectures**: Authoring formalized reference implementations for critical multi-agent patterns, including [Bounded Autonomous Remediation](../architectures/bounded-autonomous-remediation.md), [Parallel Research and Merge](../architectures/parallel-research-and-merge.md), and [Single-Agent Human Approval](../architectures/single-agent-human-approval.md).
2. **Critical Use Cases**: Scoping, cataloging, and evaluating real-world production workflow scenarios to establish common requirements.
3. **Taxonomy & Workflow Primitives**: Defining the fundamental vocabulary and execution primitives for agent orchestration in collaboration with the cross-cutting [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a17a580f85c2-46ce20ea].

### Cross-Working-Group Harmonization
Due to concurrent definitions emerging across different AAIF working groups, WG WPI advocates for global taxonomy authority under the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) to enforce unified terminology across all technical working groups and avoid conflicting or overlapping term definitions [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a17a580f85c2-46ce20ea].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-06**: Chaired by Yaron Schneider (Diagrid) and Adam Seligman (Workato); established three work streams and initiated cross-WG alignment with Taxonomy & Landscape [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a17a580f85c2-46ce20ea].

proposed_concept.title: Job-Oriented Architecture Model
proposed_concept.description: Architectural framework structuring agent workflows around recognizable practitioner jobs rather than abstract capabilities, evaluating machine-readable Workflow Design Specifications.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Job-Oriented Architecture Model organizes agentic reference architectures around concrete, recognizable practitioner tasks—such as invoice processing or human-approved operational changes—rather than generic model reasoning capabilities[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-28]. It establishes a layered composition linking reusable workflow patterns into complete reference architectures validated against real-world scenario evidence[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-28].

# Architecture / Specification

The architectural model operates as a three-tier hierarchy[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-28]:
1. **Reusable Patterns**: Atomic building blocks that resolve one recurring workflow challenge (such as [approval-checkpoint](../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md) or [durable-wait](../patterns/durable-wait.md)).
2. **Job-Oriented Reference Architectures**: Compositions combining patterns, capability roles, operational boundaries, guarantees, and exit criteria tailored for a defined practitioner role.
3. **Real-World Scenarios / Use Cases**: Empirical scenarios providing operational evidence to test whether a composed architecture fits the problem space.

The Workflows and Process Integration Working Group is evaluating two long-term north-star directions for this model: maintaining the reference architectures strictly as human-readable knowledgebase guidance (Option A), or standardizing a canonical, schema-valid, machine-readable Workflow Design Specification (WDS) serialized in YAML that renders multiple downstream architectural, diagrammatic, and review views (Option B)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-28].

# References

- Workflows and Process Integration Working Group [Issue #28](https://github.com/aaif/wg-workflows-and-process-integration/issues/28)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-28]

proposed_concept.title: Identity and Trust Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group defining vendor-neutral standards, reference architectures, and delegation frameworks for agentic identity, trust verification, and legal-role accountability.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Identity and Trust Working Group establishes vendor-neutral standards, reference architectures, and credential verification models for software agents operating across organisational boundaries[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-10]. The group addresses the legal and architectural distinctions between engineering primitives and formal regulatory definitions of agency, attestation, and data processing[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-10].

# Architecture / Specification

The working group focuses on reconciling technical delegation architectures with cross-jurisdictional legal requirements[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-10]:
- **Terminology and Legal Regimes**: Addressing collisions where engineering terms diverge from statutory definitions, including "operator" (EU AI Act Article 3(8)), "relying party" (eIDAS Regulation 2024/1183 Article 5b), "consent" (GDPR Articles 4(11), 7 vs PSD2 Article 64), "attestation" (eIDAS 2 electronic attribute attestations vs RATS evidence), and "mandate" (civil agency and EUDI representation vs technical objects)[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-10].
- **Multi-Hop Record Ownership**: Mapping delegation hops across user, workspace device, logical agent, and tool execution to determine statutory log holders and processors (e.g., GDPR Article 28 processor relationships, Article 30 records, and EU AI Act Articles 19 and 26(6) provider and deployer obligations)[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-10].

# References

- Identity and Trust Working Group [Issue #10](https://github.com/aaif/wg-identity-and-trust/issues/10)[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-10]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Accuracy and Reliability Working Group develops standardized failure taxonomies, evaluation benchmarks, and verification suites to quantify and improve the operational reliability of agentic systems[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-issue-12]. It defines structured deliverables spanning taxonomy, evaluation harnesses, and recovery mechanisms across varying deployment contexts[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-issue-12].

# Architecture / Specification

The group is defining key deliverables while addressing boundary and jurisdiction challenges:
- **Vocabulary Conformance (D6)**: Clarifying self-assessment tests, conformance validation artifacts, and consistency checks to avoid conflation with statutory "conformity assessment" procedures established under EU AI Act Article 43[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-issue-12].
- **Quality Thresholds (D4)**: Formulating operational thresholds for accuracy, robustness, and failure recovery while defining jurisdiction scope statements to distinguish technical benchmarks from regulatory presumption-of-conformity standards (such as EU AI Act Article 15 and CEN-CENELEC JTC 21 harmonised standards) and US voluntary guidance like the NIST AI RMF[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-issue-12].

proposed_concept.title: PostHog Reference Architecture
proposed_concept.description: Reference architecture detailing PostHog's Capture API ingestion, PII sanitization, and session analysis with jurisdiction-specific privacy classifications.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The PostHog reference architecture evaluates the ingestion pipeline, Capture API mechanics, and session telemetry methods used to track agent interactions and user journeys[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-55]. It provides guidance on client-side sanitization, event batching, and privacy-preserving observability patterns[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-55].

# Architecture / Specification

The architecture incorporates privacy and jurisdictional telemetry controls:
- **Installation Identifiers and Pseudonymity**: Addresses the classification of UUID-based installation identifiers. While technical claims describe random UUIDs as anonymous-by-design tracking without PII, regulatory frameworks such as GDPR (Recitals 26 and 30) and UK GDPR classify persistent tracking identifiers as pseudonymous personal data[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-55].
- **Cross-Border Transfers**: Identifies data transfer constraints when telemetry payloads and pseudonymous identifiers are routed to US-based endpoints (such as `us.i.posthog.com`) under international transfer regulations[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-55].
- **Regime-Keyed Classification**: Outlines the requirement for reference architectures to categorize data types (personal data, personal information, PII, none) explicitly against relevant legal regimes rather than relying solely on client-side regex redacting[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-55].

proposed_concept.title: Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Alignment Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing baseline policy themes, cross-jurisdictional gap analyses, and regulatory alignment frameworks for agentic AI.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Alignment Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body dedicated to mapping evolving international AI regulations, risk management frameworks, and accountability baselines to open-source agentic systems[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-922f59c26329-d5a40319]. The working group is co-chaired by Ryan Hagemann (IBM) and Deborah Eng (JPMorgan Chase)[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-922f59c26329-d5a40319].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group structures its regulatory gap analyses across a standardized baseline of 16 core governance and policy themes[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-922f59c26329-d5a40319]:
- **Governance & accountability**: Ownership, approvals, RACI frameworks, and risk acceptance.
- **Use-case classification & risk tiering**: Permitted versus prohibited uses and tiered controls, coordinating with the [Agentic Use Case Classification](../resources/agentic-use-case-classification.md).
- **Architecture**: Reference patterns, trust boundaries, and control placement across workflows.
- **Agent identity & delegation**: Authentication, authorization, acting-on-behalf-of semantics, and registries, linking with [Identity and Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md).
- **Guardrails & policy constraints**: Business rules, policy-as-code, and hard execution constraints.
- **Data protection & privacy**: PII handling, data minimization, retention schedules, and data residency.
- **Security & access controls**: Principle of least privilege, secrets management, process segmentation, and tool call authorization.
- **Model/agent risk management**: Model validation, drift detection, robustness, and runtime change control.
- **Human oversight**: Human-in-the-loop (HITL), human-on-the-loop (HOTL), escalation pathways, automated oversight, and [Kill Switches](../patterns/kill-switch.md).
- **Action management**: Pre-execution validation checks, dual control, and action reversibility.
- **Monitoring & logging**: Comprehensive audit trails, prompt/tool logs, and decision logs, coordinating with [Observability and Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md).
- **Testing & red teaming**: Adversarial prompt injection, tool abuse, and autonomous failure mode evaluation.
- **Third-party & supply chain**: Vendor due diligence and model/tool provenance verification.
- **Incident response**: Autonomous threat detection, containment protocols, and mandatory reporting.
- **Transparency & user disclosure**: Interaction notices, explainability, and user expectations.
- **Recordkeeping & auditability**: Retention schedules, replayability, and evidentiary reproducibility.

To ensure consistent extraction across divergent national legal regimes (including the EU AI Act, US state privacy acts, Korea's PIPA, Singapore's PDPA, and Japan's APPI), the group utilizes standardized "golden source" analysis prompts that structure requirements by legal jurisdiction and institutional role[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-922f59c26329-d5a40319][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-54].

# Lifecycle History
In August 2026, the working group ratified its 16 baseline themes and developed its golden source extraction prompt to execute Phase 2 comparative gap analyses, targeting an interim report for the Technical Committee[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-922f59c26329-d5a40319].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Use Case Inventory
proposed_concept.description: Production workflow catalog categorizing real-world agent deployments across verified multi-tiered execution dimensions and governance constraints.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Use Case Inventory is a curated catalog maintained by the Workflows and Process Integration Working Group that documents real-world, production deployments of autonomous and semi-autonomous AI agents across enterprise environments and software development lifecycles[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51]. Each entry records operational dimensions including trigger mechanisms, human oversight patterns, coordination topologies, and workflow classifications according to the [Agentic Use Case Classification](../resources/agentic-use-case-classification.md) matrix[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51].

# Architecture / Specification
Workflows cataloged in the inventory are categorized across six primary structural dimensions[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51]:
- **Trigger**: Execution activation vector (e.g., scheduled cron, event-driven webhook, interactive user dispatch).
- **HITL Pattern**: Enforced human oversight level, ranging from strict interactive approval gates to autonomous non-blocking runs (`None`).
- **Agent Count**: Structural agent topology (e.g., `Single-agent sufficient`, multi-agent swarms).
- **Coordination**: Execution coordination topology (e.g., `Single-agent, orchestrated`).
- **Workflow Pattern**: Execution sequence classification (e.g., sequential pipeline, fan-out/join, convergence loop).
- **Duration & Timeout**: Operational bounding windows and timeout limits.

### Verified Production Implementations
- **Upstream SDK Release Impact Analysis**: Sourced from the Model Context Protocol (MCP) Inspector `sdk-watch.yml` workflow[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51]. Operates as a scheduled sequential pipeline where an agent inspects upstream SDK release updates using read-only repository search tools (`Read`, `Grep`, `Glob`) under a non-privileged token[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51]. Write permissions are separated from analysis via CI/CD job isolation—an upstream script files the tracking issue, and a credential scanning job inspects the analysis output before a separate write-scoped job uploads the result—demonstrating a [Proposal-Execution Split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md) enforced strictly through system permissions rather than an interactive approval gate[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51].

# Lifecycle History
Maintained by the Workflows and Process Integration Working Group as a living reference catalog for grounding AAIF reference architectures in empirical production implementations[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51].

proposed_concept.title: nono Agent Runtime Sandbox
proposed_concept.description: Open-source agent runtime security tool providing kernel-enforced sandboxing, credential isolation, and deterministic cross-boundary audit logs.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
`nono` is an open-source agent runtime security framework that executes untrusted AI agent workloads inside kernel-enforced sandboxes with strict credential isolation[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-52]. Evaluated under the Primitives and Protocol Observability focus group of the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), `nono` serves as a reference architecture satisfying the SAF-M-74 runtime class by providing hardware- and kernel-level process boundaries, credential protection, and cryptographic execution logs[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-52].

# Architecture / Specification
`nono` establishes boundary observability and runtime protection across agent-to-gateway and agent-to-tool boundaries[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-52]:
- **Kernel-Enforced Execution Boundary**: Enforces process isolation below Layer 7 to prevent compromised agents or hijacked tools from accessing unauthorized host filesystems or network interfaces[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-52].
- **Cryptographic Audit Hashing**: Emits deterministic execution logs validated against golden test vectors and alpha hashing schemes to prove runtime integrity[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-52].
- **Trace Context Propagation Limitations**: Current runtime realizations do not propagate standard W3C distributed tracing context (`traceparent`, `tracestate`, `baggage`) into sandboxed execution environments by default, requiring explicit environment variable allow-lists and trace identifier mappings on audit records for full OpenTelemetry correlation[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-52].
- **Human-in-the-Loop Integration**: Surfaces runtime evidence records for Agent-to-Human (HITL) checkpoints and authorization delegations[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-52].

# Lifecycle History
Reviewed in the Observability and Traceability Working Group under reference architecture `AAIF-REF-ARCH-NONO`, establishing baseline telemetry rows and identifying downstream OTLP export requirements[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-52].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical committee body chartered to establish open threat models, secure operational architectures, privacy-preserving techniques, and runtime hardening baselines across open-source agentic systems[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076]. The working group collaborates across vertical initiatives to evaluate agent sandboxing, identity delegation, and cross-cutting security checklists[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group drives several active technical workstreams and standards deliverables[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076]:
- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide**: Comprehensive baseline detailing threat mitigation controls, least-privilege tool execution, and workload identity architectures[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076].
- **Agentic AI Threat Modeling**: Comparative framework and gap analysis evaluating prompt injection, tool abuse, autonomous failure modes, and supply chain boundaries[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076].
- **Cross-Working Group Review Checklist**: Assessment rubric executed by security delegates to review proposals from [Identity and Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md), [Observability and Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), and [Agentic Commerce](../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076].
- **Runtime Sandboxing & Isolation**: Architectural evaluation of kernel-enforced sandboxes like [nono](../resources/nono.md) and microVM-based isolation runtimes such as Eclipse Enclave that prevent process network bypasses[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076].
- **Standards Harmonization**: Collaborative liaison with external bodies such as ETSI TC SAI regarding cybersecurity requirements for AI agents and systems[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076].

# Lifecycle History
In September 2026, the working group adopted standing review windows in `CONTRIBUTING.md`, advanced the Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide through final comment resolution, implemented automated LLM provenance and edit tracking for taxonomy drafting, and began coordinating cross-working group review coverage for delegated commerce protocols[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Observability Prior Work Landscape
proposed_concept.description: Comparative landscape survey evaluating specifications, platforms, and hosted protocols across agent observability, runtime tracing, and security telemetry.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agent Observability Prior Work Landscape is an authoritative working group survey maintained by the Observability and Traceability Working Group that catalogs existing specifications, instrumentation libraries, and observability backends across the agentic ecosystem [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853]. It establishes a neutral baseline for evaluating runtime telemetry maturity, identifying cross-vendor instrumentation gaps, and framing the AAIF's standardization priorities across LLM execution, protocol boundaries, and distributed agent swarms.

The survey evaluates efforts according to scope, specification maturity, license, and architectural focus rather than competitive rankings [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853]. It spans telemetry generation across model APIs, tool execution boundaries, agent-to-agent delegation, and environment-level signals.

# Architecture / Specification

### Landscape Structure

The landscape categorizes agent observability efforts into primary operational sectors [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853]:

1. **Vendor-Neutral Telemetry Specifications**: Foundational standards defining data models and semantic conventions, notably OpenTelemetry GenAI Semantic Conventions (now housed in `open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai`) detailing spans for `create-agent`, `invoke-agent`, `invoke-workflow`, `execute-tool`, and `plan` operations [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853].
2. **Security and Integrity Schemas**: Governance and audit data models including the OWASP Agent Observability Standard (AOS)—decoupling Instrument, Trace, and Inspect specifications—and the Open Cybersecurity Schema Framework (OCSF) v1.9, which introduces AI Operation, AI Agent, Delegation, and Record Integrity classes [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853].
3. **Cross-Agent Protocols & Frameworks**: Protocol-level telemetry and propagation substrates including AGNTCY Observe SDK, A2A traceability extensions, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) telemetry mediation [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853].
4. **Application & Library Auto-Instrumentation**: Frameworks capturing LLM and agent execution runs, including Monocle (LF AI & Data), OpenInference, OpenLLMetry, and OpenLIT [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853].
5. **Evaluation, Tracing, and MLOps Backends**: Specialized analytical backends spanning Langfuse, Arize Phoenix, MLflow Tracing, W&B Weave, LangSmith, and Helicone [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853].
6. **Environment-Derived Signals**: Non-invasive runtime and kernel observability, notably eBPF-based instrumentation via OpenTelemetry BPF Instrumentation (OBI) to provide non-repudiable network and system telemetry [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853].

### Cross-Working Group Integration

The survey informs the WG's development of the `../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md` and provides grounding for cross-boundary telemetry mapping analyzed in `../resources/cross-boundary-observability-model.md` [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-03-15**: Initial landscape survey drafted in the Observability and Traceability Working Group [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853].
- **2026-08-13**: Mid-2026 refresh merged, incorporating OTel GenAI's dedicated repository migration, OCSF 1.9 agent security schemas, AOS specification modularization, AGNTCY Observe SDK `sdk-v1.0.43`, and A2A's donation into AAIF [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Telemetry context, turn correlation, and causality framework tracking agent execution across model calls, tools, and subagents.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agent Behavior Trace Model is a standardized telemetry and causality representation specifying how agentic reasoning steps, model invocations, tool operations, approval gates, and multi-agent delegations correlate across distributed execution boundaries [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45]. It provides an interoperable abstraction over raw OpenTelemetry spans and protocol events, ensuring that agent decision traces can be independently audited and replayed across heterogeneous runtimes.

The standard explicitly decouples telemetry ingestion from producer-specific state engines, requiring that serialized trace artifacts remain interpretable by third-party evaluation tools without access to private runtime fixtures [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45].

# Architecture / Specification

### Causality and Turn Correlation

The trace model defines graph schemas connecting parent goals, intermediate planning branches, tool payloads, and resulting environmental effects [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45]. It aligns with the cross-boundary taxonomy outlined in `../resources/cross-boundary-observability-model.md` and provides verifiable linkages to `../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md` records.

### Interoperability and Independent Interpretation Verification

To prevent the specification from being coupled to a single vendor implementation, the trace model execution plan establishes Task 7: Independent Interpretation Verification [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45]:

- **Dual Implementation Rule**: Telemetry emitted by reference agents must be consumed and interpreted by at least two independently developed reader implementations or query paths [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45].
- **State Isolation**: Neither reader may rely on hidden fixture mappings, internal harness state, or shared reconstruction code [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45].
- **Permutation Invariance**: Readers must produce identical semantic classifications when presented with identical trace events arriving in differing orders [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45].
- **Evidence Reconciliation**: For example, when reading valid approval and execution records, both readers must identify approved actions (`P1`), observed execution events (`E1`), and external effects; if underlying receipts are removed, both readers must flag the downstream effect as unconfirmed [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-08**: WG discussions formulated the nine-task execution plan, including Task 7 (Issue #45) establishing strict independent interpretation acceptance criteria for trace telemetry readers [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45].

proposed_concept.title: Cross-Working Group Security Review Checklist
proposed_concept.description: Lightweight assessment checklist and review workflow applied by the Security and Privacy WG to evaluate cross-working group specifications and surface scope overlaps.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Cross-Working Group Security Review Checklist is an operational evaluation framework led by the `../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md` Working Group to assess proposals, standards, and architecture templates emerging across the foundation [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e1f76734d747-7511fba6]. The checklist provides a standardized lens for detecting boundary vulnerabilities, unmitigated tool authority risks, and scope overlaps among parallel AAIF working groups.

By engaging with cross-foundation initiatives early in their development lifecycle, the checklist prevents conflicting security guidance and ensures coherent threat mitigation across working group boundaries [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e1f76734d747-7511fba6].

# Architecture / Specification

### Review Focus Areas

The checklist interrogates incoming specifications against core risk vectors:

1. **Protocol and Gateway Mediation**: Reviewing how agent gateways, reverse proxies, and communication protocols (such as Model Context Protocol and Agent-to-Agent / A2A) enforce identity authentication, tool capability authorization, and egress boundaries [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e1f76734d747-7511fba6].
2. **Observability and Boundary Tracing**: Collaborating with the Observability and Traceability Working Group (chaired by Pavan Sudheendra) to ensure telemetry frameworks, such as the `../resources/cross-boundary-observability-model.md`, do not leak sensitive payloads or bypass runtime sandboxes [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e1f76734d747-7511fba6, ^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-24].
3. **Scope and Overlap Deconfliction**: Identifying shared mandates across `../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md`, `../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md`, and `../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md` to prevent duplicate protocol or policy workstreams [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e1f76734d747-7511fba6].

### Operational Prerequisites

Effective execution of cross-WG security reviews relies on public running notes and structured git deliverables across all technical working groups [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e1f76734d747-7511fba6]. Where working groups fail to maintain transparent running notes or deliverables, review workstream leads conduct direct outreach with working group chairs to clarify architectural scopes [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e1f76734d747-7511fba6].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-08-18**: Govindaraj Palanisamy reported progress on the cross-WG overlap checklist during the Security and Privacy WG meeting, highlighting gaps in running notes across sibling groups and routing Pavan Sudheendra's draft cross-boundary observability framework into the review workstream [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e1f76734d747-7511fba6, ^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-24].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Open telemetry and correlation specification capturing causal agent execution, multi-agent context propagation, and plan-to-outcome mapping across heterogeneous runtimes.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open telemetry and execution correlation framework established by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) to preserve causal relationships and execution context across heterogeneous agents, SDKs, gateways, and observability backends [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]. Rather than replacing baseline telemetry specifications such as OpenTelemetry GenAI, the model defines portable telemetry context layers that link planning, decision-making, and side effects across distributed runtime boundaries.

# Architecture / Specification
The specification standardizes context preservation across execution boundaries without requiring the exfiltration or capture of raw chain-of-thought tokens [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]. Key structural capabilities include:

- **Portable Telemetry Context**: Standardized baggage and header semantics propagating trace identity, task context, and causal lineage across agents, gateways (such as [Agent Gateway](../resources/agentgateway.md)), and multi-agent delegation handoffs.
- **Decision and Plan Attribution**: Correlating high-level agent plans, intermediate tool or reasoning decisions, and final downstream actions without mandating internal cognitive trace disclosure.
- **Long-Running Task and Lifecycle Correlation**: Maintaining durable turn and session identifiers across asynchronous wait states, multi-turn human approvals, and distributed subagent fan-outs.
- **Verifiable Audit Hooks**: Integrating execution telemetry with cryptographic evidence collection to support tamper-evident audit trails and dispute resolution.

# Lifecycle History
In August 2026, the working group reached consensus on the initial model scope, establishing that portable context serves as a capability layer augmenting rather than displacing OpenTelemetry GenAI [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]. A reference implementation library, synthetic test suite, and conformance test plan were scheduled for September 2026 development to identify upstream contribution candidates for OpenTelemetry [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-38].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body developing vendor-neutral telemetry specifications, cross-boundary trace correlation standards, and reference architectures for agent observability [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]. The group bridges runtime execution telemetry, distributed tracing, and compliance auditing across model calls, MCP protocol boundaries, subagent delegations, and tool interactions.

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its technical deliverables into coordinated research and standardization tracks [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]:

- **[Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md)**: A portable context framework and reference library mapping execution intent, decisions, and outcomes across heterogeneous agent runtimes.
- **Cross-Boundary Observability**: Gap models and metadata mappings governing protocol transitions, including agent-to-skill, skill-to-tool, agent-to-agent, and agent-to-MCP interactions.
- **ARD Trust-Pipeline Observability**: Telemetry architecture and proof of concept tracing the Agent Resource Discovery lifecycle from client discovery through identity verification to skill execution via [Agent Gateway](../resources/agentgateway.md) span attributes.
- **Taxonomy Alignment**: Definition and cross-WG harmonization of core observability terms (Reasoning, Agent Trajectory, Context Propagation, Memory Access, Context Assembly, Retrieval, and Traceability) within the shared AAIF terminology corpus.

# Lifecycle History
As of August 2026, the working group confirmed the initial scope for the Agent Behavior Trace Model, merged contributor working methods and tracing landscape surveys, and advanced metadata mapping across protocol interfaces [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-38]. To consolidate participation, the Multi-Agentic Observability - Orchestration & Coordination track was integrated into the full working group assembly [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b].

proposed_concept.title: Accuracy and Reliability Working Group Survey
proposed_concept.description: Platform-neutral 16-question survey instrument evaluating real-world AI system deployments, failure modes, accuracy benchmarks, and future industry priorities.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Accuracy and Reliability Working Group Survey is a platform-neutral, 16-question evaluation instrument developed by the [Accuracy and Reliability Working Group](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md) to gather structured empirical data on production AI deployments, failure modes, and verification challenges [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-9]. The instrument is engineered to benchmark real-world reliability gaps across heterogeneous architectures without biasing respondents toward specific vendors or tooling ecosystems.

# Architecture / Specification
The survey is structured across five sequential functional sections with precise branching and validation mechanics [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-9]:

- **Eligibility (Q1)**: Initial qualification screening containing dedicated early-exit termination paths for ineligible respondents.
- **About the System (Q2–Q5)**: Descriptive characterization of target agent systems and deployment architectures, including structured write-ins for customized platforms (Q5 optional; Q2–Q4 required).
- **Benefits and Challenges (Q6–Q8)**: Assessment of operational gains and deployment obstacles using standardized five-choice response matrices.
- **Accuracy and Reliability (Q9–Q13)**: Targeted technical evaluation of observed failure rates, nondeterminism, hallucination frequencies, and mitigation mechanisms.
- **Future Priorities (Q14–Q16)**: Strategic industry benchmarking identifying critical needs for standardization and evaluation benchmarks (Q16 optional).

# Lifecycle History
In PR #9, the Accuracy and Reliability Working Group formalized and merged the platform-neutral survey design, establishing full question mechanics, screen-out paths, and prototype validation workflows prior to public distribution [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-9].

# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group is an AAIF technical body focused on defining open threat models, evaluating security frameworks, authoring implementation best practices, and cataloging security and privacy design patterns for agentic AI systems[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group is co-chaired by Alexander Frazer (Runlayer) and Junjie Bu (Google)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f]. It organizes community work across five active workstreams:
- **Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis**: Evaluates coverage across OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, CSA MAESTRO, and the NIST AI RMF, with ongoing alignment against STRIDE, PASTA, Model Context Protocol (MCP) vectors, and Human-User Agent (HUA) considerations[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f].
- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide**: Develops implementation guidance and threat mitigations, coordinating identity and authorization controls with the Identity and Trust working group[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f].
- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Establishes a catalog and contribution template for reusable architectural security patterns[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f].
- **Cross-Working Group Review Checklist**: Provides an assessment checklist and review workflow applied across AAIF working groups to evaluate cross-cutting security boundaries[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f].
- **Taxonomy and Landscape Integration**: Harmonizes security and privacy terminology across working groups, providing agent-specific terms and disambiguators[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-18].

# Lifecycle History
In August 2026, the working group established public meeting recordings by default and requested clarification from the Technical Committee regarding the scope of protocol-related security work following the Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol donation[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-22].

# Overview
The Workflows and Process Integration Working Group is an AAIF technical body establishing shared workflow execution models, reference architectures, execution profiles, and reusable pattern catalogs for agentic automation[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group is co-chaired by Yaron Schneider (Diagrid) and Adam Seligman (Workato)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26]. It executes its charter across three core workstreams:
- **Reference Architectures**: Defines seven execution profiles spanning from Profile 1 (fully deterministic) to Profile 7 (fully agentic), advocates a proposed "least agentic default" recommendation principle, and develops six charter-derived archetypes (including bounded automation and gated operations)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26]. The workstream demonstrates an automated specification-driven design flow compiling machine-readable YAML definitions into visual diagrams and technical documentation across standard and agentic variants[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26].
- **Critical Use Cases**: Maintains a catalog of 89 categorized production workflows classified by execution primitives (trigger, human-in-the-loop pattern, agent count, coordination model, workflow pattern) and maps them to a reusable pattern catalog that includes patterns such as the autonomous convergence loop[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26].
- **Taxonomy Alignment**: Coordinates cross-working group term harmonization, testing use case primitive classifications against universal taxonomy definitions to prevent terminology fragmentation[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26].

# Overview
The Agent Observability Use Cases catalog is a comprehensive register maintained by the Observability and Traceability Working Group, defining functional monitoring, debugging, security, and attestation scenarios across multi-boundary agent systems[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-56].

# Architecture / Specification
The catalog organizes agent observability requirements across functional categories and cross-cutting telemetry specifications:
- **Evidence-Grade Qualification Ladder**: Evaluates attestation and verification capabilities across distinct evidence grades (disambiguated from use case identifiers E1 through E4), establishing progressive tiers of artifact integrity and cryptographic assurance[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-56].
- **Cross-Cutting Jurisdiction and Legal Weight Requirements**: Separates technical record integrity mechanisms from their legal effect, requiring that obligations keyed to statutory mandates state the jurisdiction and legal role of the record holder rather than embedding legal status in technical enumerations[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-56].
- **Timestamp Technical Attestation**: In use case E4, specifies RFC 3161 trusted timestamping as a technical proof of prior existence and integrity, with legal admissibility and evidentiary weight explicitly deferred to the relying party's legal regime[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-56].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group advances the mission of the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) by establishing security and privacy as a shared discipline across the agentic AI ecosystem[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-511b4a56]. The group develops open threat models, taxonomies, and design patterns that providers, consumers, and peer working groups can adopt to share responsibility for trustworthy agentic AI[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-511b4a56].

The working group is chaired by Alex Frazer (Runlayer) and co-chaired by Junjie Bu (Google), serving appointed terms from March 1, 2026 through January 31, 2027[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-511b4a56]. Primary meetings convene biweekly on Tuesdays at 10:00 AM PT, with an alternate-week APAC time slot trialed at 10:00 PM ET to bridge contributors in Asia and the Americas[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-511b4a56][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group coordinates technical outputs across five main workstreams and collaboration tracks:
- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide**: Practical baseline implementation guide covering runtime sandboxing, capability brokering, and workload credential isolation[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821].
- **Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis**: Comparative framework analyzing agentic attack surfaces against OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, and CSA MAESTRO standards[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821].
- **Design Patterns Catalog**: Architecture and runtime control patterns, including out-of-band kill-switches and boundary filters[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821].
- **Cross-WG Security and Privacy Review Checklist**: Lightweight assessment rubric developed in collaboration with the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) and the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821].
- **Taxonomy and Landscape Integration**: Shared definitions alignment coordinated with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-02-17 to 2026-05-26**: Formation, orientation, and charter adoption[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-5484c59b].
- **2026-06-23**: Public repository launch on GitHub and adoption of monthly Technical Committee reporting rhythms[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-5484c59b].
- **2026-09-29**: Release approval for version 1 of the Best Practices Guide via PR #9, adoption of the deliverable separation rule barring authors from self-merging deliverables, and initiation of dedicated threat modeling sessions[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The *Agentic AI Security Best Practices* guide is a core technical deliverable developed by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) to define operational safeguards, threat mitigations, and workload isolation architectures for AI agents[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821]. It standardizes defensive practices across sandboxing boundaries, credential handling, and tool execution.

Following thorough community review, version 1 of the guide was approved to merge via PR #9, transitioning the deliverable into an actively maintained living foundation document[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821].

# Architecture / Specification
The guide addresses runtime security and isolation across key operational domains:
- **Kernel-Enforced Sandboxing**: Enforcing strict containment over tools and generated scripts to prevent container and host escapes[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821].
- **Workload Identity and Credential Isolation**: Shielding environment secrets from agent prompt context and ephemeral execution runtimes[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821].
- **Governance and Maintenance Rules**: Under the working group's deliverable governance rules, subsequent revisions require approval from designated mandatory reviewers (Fernando Lucktemberg and Matthew), with authors prohibited from merging their own pull requests into foundation deliverable directories[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-07-07 to 2026-08-04**: Skeleton draft authored and circulated for community feedback[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-5484c59b].
- **2026-09-01**: Text frozen for final reviews, with out-of-scope identity themes delegated to the Identity and Trust WG[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-5484c59b].
- **2026-09-29**: Final review completed; working group approved PR #9 for release while converting residual discussions into tracked issues[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821].

# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group is an AAIF technical body tasked with formulating vendor-neutral agent telemetry specifications, causal trace models, and distributed context propagation standards across agent architectures.

The group actively interfaces with peer working groups, including the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), to support cross-domain telemetry correlation and security review checklists[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821].

# Architecture / Specification
The group focuses on standardizing observability across multiple runtime boundaries:
- **Cross-Boundary Observability**: Frameworks correlating spans between client applications, orchestrators, Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, and foundational inference models[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821].
- **Telemetry Standards**: Harmonizing semantic conventions for agent execution traces, tool invocations, and error states.
- **Automated Metric Reporting**: Automated CI/CD reporting pipelines using GitHub Actions (`monthly-metrics.yml`) and `issue-metrics` to aggregate monthly PR and issue velocity, cycle times, and closure metrics for Technical Committee oversight[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-9373ed8bd5e2-54fdeb4c][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-59].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-10-01**: Merged PR #59 establishing scheduled GitHub Actions metrics collection to automate monthly Technical Committee reporting[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-9373ed8bd5e2-54fdeb4c][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-59].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices
proposed_concept.description: Implementation guidelines, failure patterns, and architectural controls across secrets management, secure tool invocation, guardrails, evaluation frameworks, and post-incident forensics.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide (Deliverable 4 of the Security and Privacy Working Group) provides practical architectural and operational controls for builders deploying agentic AI systems[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf]. Co-led by Fernando Lucktemberg (SAP) and Matthew Khouzam (Ericsson), the guide systematically addresses failure patterns observed in production deployments across five core areas: secrets management, secure tool invocation, guardrails, evaluation frameworks, and post-incident forensics[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-d0ff1066].

The specification explicitly delegates agent identity and delegated authorization architecture—such as SPIFFE/SVID workload attestation, RFC 8693 token exchange delegation chains, and UCAN capability tokens—to the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md), surfacing those cross-cutting requirements via the [Cross-WG Security Review Checklist](cross-wg-security-review-checklist.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf].

# Architecture / Specification
The best practices guide organizes controls across five primary operational domains and supplements them with an implementation feature matrix[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf]:

## Secrets Management
Static, long-lived credentials present a critical vulnerability in agentic runtimes, as state serialization or prompt injection attacks (exemplified by CVE-2025-68664) can expose environment variables and persistent secrets[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf]. The guide mandates an architectural migration to ephemeral credentials generated on demand and bounded by narrow time-to-live (TTL) windows[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc]:
- **Workload Identity:** Native platform attestation (AWS IRSA, GCP Workload Identity, Azure Managed Identity) exchanging cluster OIDC tokens for short-lived credentials with a typical one-hour maximum exposure window[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf].
- **Dynamic Secrets:** On-demand credential generation engines (e.g., HashiCorp Vault) scoped to individual requests or resources with 15–60 minute lifetimes[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf].
- **Network-Layer Injection:** Sidecars and egress proxies injecting credentials outside agent process visibility for legacy systems[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf].
- **Confidential Computing:** Hardware-isolated enclaves (Intel SGX/TDX, AMD SEV-SNP) providing enclave-attested key release for high-sensitivity multi-tenant or regulated environments[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf].

## Secure Tool Invocation
Tool invocation focuses heavily on Model Context Protocol (MCP) transport security, skill supply-chain hygiene, and runtime boundary protections[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf]:
- **Pre-Deployment Server Evaluation:** Mandatory verification of source repositories (active within 90 days), cross-referencing against vulnerability trackers (Vulnerable MCP Project, CVE/NVD), and static scanning (Cisco MCP Scanner) and runtime analysis (Snyk Agent Scan, Invariant mcp-scan)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf].
- **Transport Security:** Requiring OAuth 2.1 with PKCE and RFC 8707 resource audience binding for HTTP MCP connections, and treating local stdio transport servers as untrusted binaries requiring sandbox containment[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf].
- **Mediation Gateways:** Routing multi-server agent traffic through centralized policy proxies like [agentgateway](../resources/agentgateway.md) or Cloudflare MCP Portals to enforce per-tool permissions and capture payloads[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc].
- **Tool Invariant Enforcement:** Defenses against tool poisoning and rug pulls via tool description hash checks at session startup, server allowlists, and out-of-scope data category blocking[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf].
- **Supply Chain and Skill Verification:** Tiered verification scanning skills for undeclared domain requests, eval(), Base64 payloads, and validating allowed-tools manifests against stated operational intent[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc].

# Lifecycle History
The guide was established as Deliverable 4 of the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf]. Initial release Draft v0.1 was authored by leads Fernando Lucktemberg and Matthew Khouzam and merged into the working group repository[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-d0ff1066]. A working group governance decision on September 29, 2026 designated the guide as a living document with Lucktemberg and Khouzam acting as mandatory pull request reviewers[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-d0ff1066].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis
proposed_concept.description: Comparative gap analysis evaluating OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, CSA MAESTRO, and NIST AI RMF across eight agentic threat domains to establish AAIF framework baselines.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The *Agentic AI Threat Modeling: Gap Analysis and Framework Design* (Deliverable 2 of the Security and Privacy Working Group) evaluates existing artificial intelligence threat modeling frameworks to determine whether they adequately address threats unique to autonomous and multi-agent systems[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308]. Led by Fernando Lucktemberg (SAP) and co-led by Alon Mazor (Ocean Security), the analysis serves as the architectural foundation for downstream working group deliverables, including the Design Patterns Catalog (D3) and the [Security Best Practices Guide](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md) (D4)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-ece26d85][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308].

The study evaluated major baseline frameworks—principally OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications (ASI01–ASI10), MITRE ATLAS v4.6.0–v5.4.0, CSA MAESTRO, and NIST AI RMF—across eight threat domains: memory and context poisoning, multi-agent persuasion, agent sabotage/derailment/rogue agents, tool invocation risk, excessive agency and blast radius containment, delegated authorization boundaries, supply chain integrity, and commerce and payment-agent risk[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308].

# Architecture / Specification

## Evaluation Methodology
The gap analysis establishes that no single existing security framework comprehensively addresses all three requirements of an agentic security program[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308]:
1. **Developer Controls (OWASP):** Categorizing failure modes and developer-actionable controls via the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications and OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications 2026 (ASI01–ASI10)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308].
2. **SOC and Adversary Techniques (MITRE ATLAS):** Modeling concrete adversary actions across a structured attack lifecycle via `AML.T####` techniques, while lacking vocabulary for non-adversarial systemic failures[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308].
3. **Architectural Hardening Layers (CSA MAESTRO):** Allocating defense budgets across an L1–L7 stack where L6 (Security and Compliance) spans horizontally across foundation models, data, memory, tool, and ecosystem layers[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308].
4. **Governance Scaffolding:** Provided by NIST AI RMF 1.0 (Govern-Map-Measure-Manage), ISO/IEC 42001, and the CSA AI Controls Matrix v1.0[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308].

## Core Findings and Recommendations
The report concludes that existing industry frameworks jointly provide adequate vulnerability classification and adversary technique coding, advising the AAIF against building a competing threat taxonomy[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308]. However, the report identifies distinct voids requiring specific treatment[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308]:
- **Working Group Workstreams:** Five technical and methodological gaps require new AAIF guidance, specifically around multi-agent persuasion dynamics, tool invocation runtime invariants, supply chain verification, memory poisoning defenses, and blast radius containment[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-ece26d85][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308].
- **Cross-WG Delegations:** Architectural gaps in delegated authorization boundaries are handed off to the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md), while commerce and payment-agent risks are coordinated with the [Agentic Commerce Working Group](../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308].
- **Jurisdictional Boundaries:** Agent derailment and non-adversarial failure modes surface an unresolved boundary between adversarial security and operational robustness under the [Accuracy and Reliability Working Group](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308].

# Lifecycle History
The deliverable was chartered as Deliverable 2 of the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308]. Draft v0.1 was submitted for working group review under the leadership of Fernando Lucktemberg and Alon Mazor, establishing the baseline framework for the Design Patterns Catalog and Best Practices Guide[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-ece26d85][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308].
