proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing open threat models, security best practices, design patterns, and cross-WG security review checklists for agentic AI.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group is a technical body of the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) chartered to establish open security frameworks, threat models, design patterns, and operational best practices for agentic AI systems[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308]. The group focuses on vulnerabilities and architectural risks arising from agent autonomy, runtime tool execution, multi-agent collaboration, and memory systems[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-ece26d85][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308].

Rather than creating redundant taxonomies, the working group adopts industry baselines (OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, CSA MAESTRO, NIST AI RMF) and focuses on agentic-specific voids, delegating identity infrastructure to the [Identity and Trust Working Group](identity-and-trust.md) and commerce-specific payment controls to the [Agentic Commerce Working Group](agentic-commerce.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group's output is organized around a sequential set of five formal deliverables[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308]:
1. **D1: Taxonomy of Terms:** Shared terminology for agentic-AI security and threats. Initially incubated in the working group, maintenance was transferred to the cross-cutting [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](taxonomy-and-landscape.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a9e41c531556-11747157][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308].
2. **D2: Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design:** Evaluation of existing frameworks (OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, CSA MAESTRO, NIST AI RMF) determining agentic-specific coverage gaps across eight threat domains, led by Fernando Lucktemberg (SAP) and Alon Mazor (Ocean Security)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-ece26d85][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308]. See [Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis](../resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md).
3. **D3: Design Patterns Catalog:** Architectural implementation patterns addressing gaps flagged for original development in the threat modeling gap analysis[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308].
4. **D4: Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide:** Operational and architectural guidance covering secrets management, Model Context Protocol (MCP) security, skill supply-chain verification, guardrails, evaluation frameworks, and forensics, co-led by Fernando Lucktemberg and Matthew Khouzam (Ericsson)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-d0ff1066]. See [Agentic AI Security Best Practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md).
5. **D5: Cross-WG Security and Privacy Review Checklist:** Operational review framework and handoff checklist evaluating adjacent AAIF working group proposals[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308]. See [Cross-WG Security Review Checklist](../guidelines/cross-wg-security-review-checklist.md).

# Lifecycle History
The working group established active workstreams in early 2026. On June 22, 2026, the working group's Taxonomy deliverable (D1) was transitioned to the foundation-wide Taxonomy and Landscape workstream[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a9e41c531556-11747157]. On September 29–30, 2026, initial Draft v0.1 versions of both Deliverable 2 (Threat Modeling Gap Analysis) and Deliverable 4 (Security Best Practices Guide) were merged into the repository, establishing Fernando Lucktemberg and Matthew Khouzam as mandatory reviewers for ongoing best practices revisions[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a9e41c531556-11747157][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-d0ff1066].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Plugin Portability and Authorization Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Packaging, capability abstraction, directory resolution, and human authorization boundary standards ensuring agent skills execute portably across diverse client runtimes.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Plugin Portability and Authorization Guidelines establish runtime-agnostic packaging conventions, capability abstractions, and authorization boundaries for multi-client agent plugins [^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69]. By separating portable manifest declarations from client-specific user interfaces, agent skills achieve consistent execution across environments such as Codex, Cursor, and Claude Code without duplicating operational logic [^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69].

# Architecture / Specification

## Packaging and Manifest Hierarchy
Plugins maintain a canonical `plugin.json` manifest at the repository root defining shared identity, version metadata, and skill declarations compliant with [standards/agent-plugins](../standards/agent-plugins.md) [^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69]. Client-specific metadata overlays, such as Claude Code marketplace catalogs (`.claude-plugin/plugin.json`), map to the canonical root without requiring parallel overlays for clients lacking unique component configurations [^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69].

Skill files reference bundled scripts, assets, and workflows using relative paths resolved against the directory hosting `SKILL.md`, formally abstracted in documentation as `<skill-root>` [^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69]. Run-time engines resolve `<skill-root>` dynamically from the loaded skill path rather than environment variables or hardcoded filesystem paths [^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69].

## Abstract Capabilities
Skill instructions describe standard runtime capabilities rather than proprietary client tool names, mapping execution requirements across disparate host runtimes [^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69]:
- **Read bundled files**: Loads local workflow references or data assets; fails gracefully if resources are missing.
- **Run Python and subprocesses**: Executes deterministic local automation scripts and CLI binaries without ad-hoc reimplementation.
- **Read web pages**: Retrieves public event details or external documentation.
- **Show local files**: Presents generated artifacts (HTML reports, images, slide decks) for local user inspection.
- **Request user approval**: Halts execution across mutation boundaries pending explicit human confirmation.

## Authorization Boundaries
Loading or activating a portable skill does not convey permission to perform mutations on external systems [^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69]. Implementations enforce strict boundary controls aligning with [patterns/human-approval-gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md) and [patterns/proposal-execution-split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md) [^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69]:
- Workflows and reporting engines execute in read-only mode by default; mutating arguments such as `--write`, `--apply`, or `--create` require prior user review of generated proposals [^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69].
- Verification flags such as `--i-have-approval` indicate recorded human authorization and must never be injected autonomously by an agent [^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69].
- External identity updates, invitations, credential changes, and event publication require explicit gate clearance [^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69].
- Runtime secrets must resolve via environment variables, gitignored configuration files, or operating system keychains, prohibiting secret exposure in prompt context or public command logs [^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69].

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Create Chapter Skill
proposed_concept.description: Automated chapter provisioning and presentation estate engine managing OOXML paragraph rebranding, Gall Stereographic map projection calibration, and Drive template replication.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The AAIF Create Chapter skill automates the provisioning of new geographic community chapters by replicating presentation templates, rebranding slide decks, and positioning geographic markers [^evt-community-events-file-0dc3d95afe1f-91fcca49]. Powered by `create_chapter.py`, the skill executes paragraph-level OOXML transformations to avoid run-splitting corruption and applies a calibrated Gall Stereographic projection to position chapter markers on world maps [^evt-community-events-file-0dc3d95afe1f-91fcca49].

# Architecture / Specification

## Rebranding Engine
The rebranding engine operates on presentation files at the paragraph level by concatenating individual text runs, applying city and slug substitutions, and writing the transformed text back into the leading run [^evt-community-events-file-0dc3d95afe1f-91fcca49]. This architecture ensures resilience against OOXML run-splitting artifacts introduced by manual presentation edits [^evt-community-events-file-0dc3d95afe1f-91fcca49]. Abbreviation casing (such as preserving or adapting "SF") is determined contextually from adjacent tokens [^evt-community-events-file-0dc3d95afe1f-91fcca49]. Google Drive provisioning integrates via Google Workspace CLI (`gws`) commands covering file copy, creation, retrieval, and metadata updates [^evt-community-events-file-0dc3d95afe1f-91fcca49].

## Map Projection Calibration
Geographic dot placement on slide 5 utilizes a Gall Stereographic projection mapping latitude and longitude coordinates to pixel offsets [^evt-community-events-file-0dc3d95afe1f-91fcca49]:
- **Longitude mapping (`lon2x`)**: Linear in longitude relative to the calibrated central meridian [^evt-community-events-file-0dc3d95afe1f-91fcca49].
- **Latitude mapping (`lat2y`)**: Linear in `(1 + √2 / 2) · tan(lat / 2)` [^evt-community-events-file-0dc3d95afe1f-91fcca49].

The projection was fitted against Natural Earth 110m coastlines composited over the template base image, achieving a mean residual of 0.64 pixels [^evt-community-events-file-0dc3d95afe1f-91fcca49]. If template map assets change, the calibration is refitted using Nelder-Mead optimization across candidate projection parameters to minimize vertex-to-pixel distances [^evt-community-events-file-0dc3d95afe1f-91fcca49].

## Offline Execution and Validation
To support isolated validation without network geocoding services, local execution via `--rebrand-local` enforces mandatory `--lat` and `--lon` arguments [^evt-community-events-file-0dc3d95afe1f-91fcca49]. Automated test harnesses in `test_create_chapter.py` enforce calibration locks against San Francisco, check canvas bounds and monotonicity, and maintain a two-shape guard [^evt-community-events-file-0dc3d95afe1f-91fcca49].

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Audit Slack Skill
proposed_concept.description: Read-only Slack inspection skill auditing chapter channel mappings, organizer permissions, membership gaps, and public coordination room exposures.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The AAIF Audit Slack skill performs read-only inspections of community Slack workspaces to verify chapter channel topology, organizer permissions, and membership integrity [^evt-community-events-file-2ca2907cf349-5ea9efbb]. Its organizer engine reconciles intake records against live Slack channels and flags operational anomalies, including public exposure of private organizer coordination channels [^evt-community-events-file-2ca2907cf349-5ea9efbb].

# Architecture / Specification

## Data Sources and Ingestion
The organizer inspection engine (`audit_organizers.py`) aggregates and correlates data across three primary layers [^evt-community-events-file-2ca2907cf349-5ea9efbb]:
1. **Chapters List (`Chapters & Teams`)**: Authoritative roster defining city names, public channels, organizer channels, and country channels [^evt-community-events-file-2ca2907cf349-5ea9efbb].
2. **Intake Operations (`Organizers`)**: Personnel intake tracking acceptance status, organizer names, assigned cities, and email addresses [^evt-community-events-file-2ca2907cf349-5ea9efbb].
3. **Slack API**: Live workspace channel metadata and user directory lookups via `conversations.list`, `conversations.members`, and `users.lookupByEmail` [^evt-community-events-file-2ca2907cf349-5ea9efbb].

Intake filtering mandates exact string matches (`Accepted` and `Existing (from MLOps)`), dropping duplicate rows for identical individuals and applying deterministic city precedence where explicit chapter assignment overrides proposed intake strings [^evt-community-events-file-2ca2907cf349-5ea9efbb].

## Reconciliation and Finding Severities
- **Identity Correlation**: Organizers are matched to Slack accounts solely through email addresses [^evt-community-events-file-2ca2907cf349-5ea9efbb]. Missing accounts represent upper bounds on membership gaps, requiring secondary name verification before offboarding or remediation [^evt-community-events-file-2ca2907cf349-5ea9efbb].
- **Public Organizer Channels**: Designating an internal `-organizers` channel as public is classified as the highest-severity security finding (`public!`), as sensitive operational coordination (venue costs, budgets, speaker issues) becomes readable across the general workspace [^evt-community-events-file-2ca2907cf349-5ea9efbb].
- **Unvetted Rosters**: Chapters containing an active organizers channel with zero accepted intake organizers are flagged for immediate governance review [^evt-community-events-file-2ca2907cf349-5ea9efbb].
- **Pre-Provisioning Lifecycle**: Execution with `--planned-ok` permits non-existent or held-private channel names during pre-provisioning stages without aborting reconciliation runs, reporting them as planned until formal channel creation [^evt-community-events-file-2ca2907cf349-5ea9efbb].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Open telemetry and correlation specification capturing causal agent execution, multi-agent context propagation, and behavioral event semantics across runtime frameworks.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open telemetry and behavioral correlation standard developed by the [working-groups/observability-and-traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) to capture causal execution flows, subagent spawning, and tool interactions across heterogeneous agent runtimes [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-60]. Rather than assuming universal telemetry semantics, the standard follows an evidence-first roadmap that evaluates what production agents emit and standardizes telemetry across OpenTelemetry conventions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-60].

# Architecture / Specification

## Execution Phases
The trace model execution framework structures development across four sequential phases centered around an empirical gap register [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-60]:
1. **Agree**: Establish initial scope, dimensions, and baseline telemetry definitions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-60].
2. **Evidence**: Capture empirical telemetry emissions from real-world agent frameworks and coding assistants, documenting disparities in OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic convention adoption [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-60].
3. **Interpret**: Analyze captured traces against the central gap register to identify missing correlation attributes, lifecycle events, and causal links [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-60].
4. **Contribute**: Upstream structured semantic convention proposals into OpenTelemetry and publish normative AAIF behavioral trace specifications [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-60].

## Reference Implementation and Scope
The initial reference implementation for trace model baseline validation is [resources/goose](../resources/goose.md), leveraging its existing OpenTelemetry integration to capture live agent execution evidence [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-60]. Milestone 1 bounds specification coverage by explicitly defining what behavioral dimensions are modeled, enabled, or deferred, reserving full multi-agent behavioral coverage for subsequent milestone iterations [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-60].

proposed_concept.title: Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing baseline policy themes, regulatory requirement schemas, cross-jurisdictional gap analyses, and compliance boundary models for agentic AI.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Working Group (GRR WG) is an AAIF technical body chartered to establish open regulatory requirement models, cross-jurisdictional gap analyses, and technical compliance boundaries for autonomous AI systems [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-11]. The working group establishes neutral frameworks that translate legal and statutory obligations into verifiable architectural requirements without providing formal legal advice or commercial compliance solutions [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-11].

# Architecture / Specification

## Regulatory Theme Cards and Schema Separation
To address rapidly shifting global artificial intelligence statutes without embedding static or stale legal registers into repository code, the working group models regulatory tracking through a decoupled format-and-data architecture [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-11]:
- **Standardized Row Format**: A standardized schema capturing mandatory compliance attributes: `Jurisdiction`, `Instrument and article`, `Binds` (specifying role: provider, deployer, user, controller, or processor), `Duty`, `Scope`, `Status`, `Shape defined`, `Nothing binding found`, and instrument revision metadata [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-11].
- **Runtime Deployment Integration**: Following Linux Foundation precedents such as OpenSSF OSV schemas and CNCF Open Policy Agent, software frameworks consume regulatory requirements dynamically from maintained external sources selected by system deployers rather than treating repository artifacts as an exhaustive legal register [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-11].

This architectural boundary ensures open-source tools can ingest binding legal duties across dynamic jurisdictions while preserving the working group's charter restriction against offering definitive legal counsel [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-11].

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Chapter Provisioning and Estate Management
proposed_concept.description: Automated chapter provisioning and presentation estate engine managing OOXML paragraph rebranding, Google Drive hierarchies, asset backfills, and four-surface chapter renames.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The `aaif-create-chapter` skill automates the end-to-end provisioning, lifecycle maintenance, and presentation rebranding of local AAIF chapters across Google Drive and Office Open XML (OOXML) documents [^evt-community-events-file-799e4722911d-3d7dbf62]. It clones template structures, performs XML surgery on slide decks and spreadsheets, and maintains consistency across the global chapter estate [^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-08c3cbb3].

# Architecture / Specification
The skill operates across several automated sub-engines and maintenance utilities:

- **Template Cloning and Rebranding**: Converts base templates into chapter assets by performing exact OOXML XML node transformations across presentation paragraphs, shape descriptions, and sheet labels [^evt-community-events-file-799e4722911d-3d7dbf62].
- **Estate Backfill Engine**: Manages wide-scale updates to pre-existing slide decks without manual editing:
  - **Map Markers (`backfill_map_dots.py`)**: Places chapter dots and labels on global maps according to Gall Stereographic projections joined directly against the Google Sheets `Chapters & Teams` coordinates (`Generated Geolocation` mapped via folder URL) [^evt-community-events-file-799e4722911d-3d7dbf62]. A strict tolerance gate (default 1 px) skips already-aligned decks, and executions plan changes prior to non-destructive apply passes [^evt-community-events-file-799e4722911d-3d7dbf62].
  - **Host Footers and Project Rosters**: Sweeps templates and chapter decks (`backfill_host_footer.py`, `backfill_projects.py`) to align footer notices and active foundation project rosters [^evt-community-events-file-799e4722911d-3d7dbf62].
- **Four-Surface Chapter Renaming (`rename_chapter.py`)**: Implements strict atomic multi-surface renames when a chapter's designated city or identifier changes [^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-08c3cbb3]:
  1. Google Drive chapter folder hierarchy [^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-08c3cbb3].
  2. File and subfolder paths such as local CRM workbooks and icons [^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-08c3cbb3].
  3. OOXML document text streams in `.docx`, `.pptx`, and `.xlsx` archives [^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-08c3cbb3].
  4. Core document metadata (`docProps`) labels [^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-08c3cbb3].

To safeguard against dangling links or broken integrations, relationship parts (`.rels`) only receive slug transformations rather than naive city substitutions, preserving internal packaging integrity [^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-08c3cbb3]. Additionally, public Luma URLs are preserved unless explicitly instructed, preventing 404 deadlinks during administrative transitions [^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-08c3cbb3].

proposed_concept.description: Automated testing harness, pre-commit validation pipeline, and credential-isolated GitHub Actions workflow verifying AAIF community skills and plugins.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Community Events Evaluation Suite is an automated validation pipeline and behavioral testing harness verifying skill definitions, portability manifests, OOXML transformations, and security boundaries across the `aaif/community-events` repository [^evt-community-events-file-a5c0f08bc43f-b99183b6]. It enforces strict operational separation between untrusted pull request checks and privileged credentialed workflows [^evt-community-events-file-a5c0f08bc43f-b99183b6].

# Architecture / Specification
The evaluation infrastructure is organized across multi-tier verification gates:

- **Credential Isolation & Workflow Gate**: The primary pull request pipeline (`validate.yml`) runs in a strictly read-only execution context with zero access to Google Workspace, Slack, or Luma credentials [^evt-community-events-file-a5c0f08bc43f-b99183b6]. A structural check script (`scripts/check_workflows.py`) scans workflow configurations to ensure no secret tokens can be leaked via fork pull requests, restricting credentialed jobs exclusively to gated manual triggers [^evt-community-events-file-a5c0f08bc43f-b99183b6].
- **Pre-Commit Hygiene**: Pre-commit hooks enforce formatting, syntax integrity, and security policies across files [^evt-community-events-file-63a9c44a44ac-37822210]:
  - **Static Linting**: Employs Ruff for syntax and defect detection without disruptive auto-formatting [^evt-community-events-file-63a9c44a44ac-37822210].
  - **Secret Detection**: Leverages Gitleaks to inspect staged commits for exposed secrets [^evt-community-events-file-63a9c44a44ac-37822210].
  - **Targeted Exclusions**: Skips byte-level churn on vendored self-extracting payloads such as `design/aaif-design-system.html` [^evt-community-events-file-63a9c44a44ac-37822210].
  - **Operational Safeguards**: Enforces that secrets are never passed via process arguments (`argv`), that redactor mechanisms remain centralized to prevent unmasked personal data in public logs, and that tooling rule banners do not drift between copies across skills [^evt-community-events-file-63a9c44a44ac-37822210].
- **Manifest and Portability Conformance**: Automated checkers (`check_manifests.py`, `check_skill_portability.py`, and `check_frontmatter.py`) validate root Agent Plugins v1 specifications and skill frontmatter compliance, while the Claude Code CLI validates marketplace manifests [^evt-community-events-file-a5c0f08bc43f-b99183b6] [^evt-community-events-pr-54].
- **Deterministic Python Test Suite**: Executes unit tests across the standard-library event toolkit (`lib/aaif_events`), design token extractors, and skill scripts, requiring full git history checkout to evaluate deep archive transforms such as OOXML font-embed strip tests [^evt-community-events-file-a5c0f08bc43f-b99183b6].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Plugin and Skill Portability Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Packaging, capability abstraction, directory resolution, and manifest conventions ensuring interoperability between Agent Plugins v1 and agent runtimes.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Plugin Portability guidelines define structural conventions, execution path abstractions, and manifest standards that allow AI agent plugins and skills to operate interchangeably across diverse client runtimes [^evt-community-events-pr-54]. These conventions eliminate proprietary path dependencies, standardize client argument hints, and maintain portable declarative contracts [^evt-community-events-pr-54].

# Architecture / Specification
Portable plugin packages adhere to five architectural principles:

- **Dual-Manifest Packaging**: Plugins ship a root Agent Plugins v1 manifest (`plugin.json`) alongside runtime-specific catalogs (such as Anthropic Claude marketplace manifests) [^evt-community-events-pr-54].
- **Standardized Directory and Path Placeholders**: Runtime-specific environment variables (such as `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}`) are replaced with client-neutral `<skill-root>` placeholders within documentation, scripts, and invocation examples [^evt-community-events-file-799e4722911d-3d7dbf62] [^evt-community-events-pr-54].
- **Namespaced Metadata for UI Hints**: Runtime-specific features such as command line argument hints are decoupled from base frontmatter and isolated under namespaced `metadata` blocks, ensuring runtime validation does not fail on unrecognized root properties [^evt-community-events-pr-54].
- **Contract and Workflow Separation**: Operational procedures are decoupled into two distinct documents: a clean `SKILL.md` declaring interface metadata, tools, and constraints, and an auxiliary `WORKFLOW.md` specifying step-by-step execution procedures [^evt-community-events-pr-54].
- **Automated Portability Linting**: Manifest compliance, skill frontmatter compatibility declarations, and the absence of vendor-locked execution syntax are verified programmatically via dedicated CI and pre-commit linting tools (`check_manifests.py`, `check_skill_portability.py`) [^evt-community-events-file-63a9c44a44ac-37822210] [^evt-community-events-pr-54].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Use Case Inventory
proposed_concept.description: Verified production workflow catalog categorizing real-world agent deployments across horizontal business functions and vertical industries under strict evidentiary standards.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Use Case Inventory is a community-maintained catalog of verified real-world agentic workflows developed by the Workflows & Process Integration Working Group's Critical Use Cases Workstream [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c10bbaa87c3e-880211ae]. Classified against the multi-dimensional schema defined in `../resources/agentic-use-case-classification.md`, the inventory documents working deployments across horizontal business functions and vertical industries to identify recurring workflow shapes, coordination mechanisms, and failure patterns [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c10bbaa87c3e-880211ae].

The catalog emphasizes pattern diversity over exhaustive coverage, serving as an empirical reference for working group deliverables rather than a ranked list or normative endorsement [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c10bbaa87c3e-880211ae].

# Architecture / Specification

## Catalog Structure and Coverage
Workflows are cataloged across structured dimensions including trigger types, human-in-the-loop (HITL) patterns, agent counts, coordination mechanisms, workflow patterns, failure modes, and operational preconditions [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c10bbaa87c3e-880211ae]. Coverage spans:
- **Cross-Industry / Horizontal**: Sales, marketing, customer support, finance & operations, HR & recruiting, and research & intelligence [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c10bbaa87c3e-880211ae].
- **Technology & Engineering**: Software engineering, IT / network operations, software development lifecycle (SDLC), and platform engineering [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c10bbaa87c3e-880211ae].
- **Industry-Specific**: Healthcare, supply chain, legal, education, and real estate [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c10bbaa87c3e-880211ae].

## Sourcing and Evidentiary Standards
The inventory enforces strict evidentiary tiers for entries to eliminate speculative or unverified claims [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-41]:
- **Preferred Evidence**: Vendor product documentation or primary announcements citing a named customer production deployment [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-41].
- **Acceptable Evidence**: Primary vendor product documentation demonstrating strong feature evidence of production deployment at scale when customer names are proprietary [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-41].
- **Unacceptable Sources**: Secondary blog posts, analyst commentary, academic preprints, market projection statistics, or unsubstantiated individual implementer write-ups [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-41].

Each entry targets three primary citations, explicitly recording the source date and handling vendor renames or acquisitions to guard against link rot and reference decay [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-41]. Entries classified as multi-agent require explicit architectural rationale detailing why the problem is inherently or preferentially suited for multi-agent coordination [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-41].

# Lifecycle History
- **Initial Inventory**: Established by the Critical Use Cases Workstream to ground workflow pattern specifications [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c10bbaa87c3e-880211ae].

proposed_concept.description: Implementation guidelines, failure patterns, and architectural feature controls across people, process, and technology dimensions for securing agentic systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Security Best Practices guideline provides implementation controls, failure patterns, and operational guardrails for securing autonomous agent workflows [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-20]. Maintained by the Security and Privacy Working Group (`../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md`), the guideline structures defensive requirements across technological enforcement, operational governance, and personnel readiness [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-20].

# Architecture / Specification

## Control Dimensions
Security best practices within agent environments are analyzed through a three-dimensional feature matrix spanning operational and technical boundaries [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-20]:
- **People**: Capabilities requiring specialized skills, personnel training, security awareness, and human oversight to recognize agent compromise or policy deviation [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-20].
- **Process**: Requirements necessitating formalized security strategies, documented operational procedures, incident response playbooks, and governance policies [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-20].
- **Technology**: Technical enforcement mechanisms comprising digital or physical tools, hardware controls, software sandboxing, and automated policy verification engines [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-20].

Each best practice maps directly to the specific technical, procedural, or human features necessary to guarantee runtime containment, credential isolation, and auditability [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-20].

# Lifecycle History
- **Security Guidance Formulation**: Authored by the Security and Privacy WG to establish baseline threat modeling and mitigation patterns.
- **Feature Matrix Integration**: PR #20 introduced a systematic feature mapping classifying security control dependencies into people, process, and technology facets [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-20].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The `aaif-sync` skill is a procedural automation pipeline coordinating reconciliation across the Agentic AI Foundation's community estate [^evt-community-events-pr-55]. It audits organizer assignments, synchronizes chapter records, verifies directory metadata, and reconciles event operations while enforcing non-destructive record retention [^evt-community-events-pr-55].

# Architecture / Specification

## Chapter Sync Lifecycle and Non-Destructive Invariants
To prevent accidental data loss and maintain historical continuity across chapter directories, chapter synchronization enforces strict retention invariants [^evt-community-events-pr-55]:
- **No Row Deletions**: The sync engine never deletes or clears chapter rows from the central registry [^evt-community-events-pr-55]. Clearing rows previously risked wiping human-authored metadata, including city descriptions, imagery assets, and operational notes [^evt-community-events-pr-55].
- **Retirement Candidates**: When a chapter has no qualifying organizers, the engine flags it as a retirement candidate rather than executing an automated purge [^evt-community-events-pr-55]. Rows are preserved in place if organizer city associations are malformed or ambiguous [^evt-community-events-pr-55].
- **Human Lifecycle Transitions**: Formal decommissioning requires explicit human intervention, transitioning chapter status to `Deprecated` or setting `Status=Merged` alongside a destination target (`Merged Into`) [^evt-community-events-pr-55].
- **Drift Reporting**: Retirement candidates surface on operational drift dashboards as pending operator decisions without failing execution exit codes or creating spurious drift errors [^evt-community-events-pr-55].

# Lifecycle History
- **Automated Sync Implementation**: Standardized chapter and organizer data synchronization across Google Sheets and community tools.
- **Non-Destructive Deletion Fix**: PR #55 eliminated automated row clearing, introducing `retirement_candidates()` and requiring explicit human status transitions to protect chapter summaries and ops notes [^evt-community-events-pr-55].

proposed_concept.title: Single-Agent Process with Human Approval
proposed_concept.description: Reference architecture establishing an enforceable human approval gate and structural separation between agent proposal construction and workflow-controlled execution.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Single-Agent Process with Human Approval reference architecture establishes an enterprise workflow pattern where an AI agent plans and drafts a proposed action, a designated human approves or rejects the submission, and an independent workflow-controlled executor carries out the protected effect.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a4fea1b2d544-d6bb99fb] It applies when an agent's output can alter real-world environments—such as executing financial refunds, modifying production configurations, or publishing external communications—and the organization mandates enforceable authorization at the point of impact due to high reversal costs, auditability constraints, or explicit human decision ownership.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a4fea1b2d544-d6bb99fb]

Under this architecture, a high-level business task is differentiated from the discrete workflow activities executed to satisfy it.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a4fea1b2d544-d6bb99fb] [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-50]

# Architecture / Specification

The architecture composes three foundational design patterns:
- [Proposal/execution split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md): Enforces a structural separation ensuring the reasoning agent lacks permissions to invoke the capability causing the protected effect directly.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a4fea1b2d544-d6bb99fb]
- [Human approval gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md): Mandates that a designated human reviewer validate the exact payload before any state change occurs.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a4fea1b2d544-d6bb99fb]
- [Durable wait](../patterns/durable-wait.md): Converts long-running human review waits into persisted state records, allowing workflows to survive crashes, restarts, or deploys without losing pending tasks.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a4fea1b2d544-d6bb99fb]

### Invariants and Guarantees
1. **Protected effect authorization**: No protected effect occurs without an explicit human approval record, and the executed payload is guaranteed to match the approved proposal rather than a modified revision.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a4fea1b2d544-d6bb99fb]
2. **Durable suspension**: Runs can pause across hours or days while awaiting sign-off; platform restarts do not drop pending reviews or duplicate executed steps.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a4fea1b2d544-d6bb99fb]
3. **Deterministic exit states**: Every execution terminates in a defined end state, maintaining an immutable chain of intent, decision, and effect (proposer, approver, executor) in the audit system of record.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a4fea1b2d544-d6bb99fb]

### Structural Capabilities
Operating this workflow requires seven capability roles: an execution engine, an agent reasoning runtime, a tool access layer, a state/context store, a human interaction surface, a workflow-controlled executor, and an audit log.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a4fea1b2d544-d6bb99fb] Working group review has highlighted open inquiries into whether the executor requires a separate host process or can execute within an isolated harness step, as well as refining selection criteria for multi-agent escalation.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-45]

proposed_concept.title: Bounded Autonomous Remediation
proposed_concept.description: Reference architecture governing iterative, autonomous problem resolution within predefined task boundaries, budget constraints, and deterministic acceptance gates.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Bounded Autonomous Remediation reference architecture defines an operational model for autonomous incident remediation and bug resolution operating within explicit step and cost budgets.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-43] The architecture allows agents to iteratively hypothesize, patch, and test candidate solutions, terminating when objective criteria are satisfied or when boundary constraints force escalation.

# Architecture / Specification

The architecture relies on [Deterministic acceptance gate](../patterns/deterministic-acceptance-gate.md) checks to validate proposed fixes before applying them to target systems.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-43]

### Minimum Evidence Requirements
Gate evaluation strength scales with two primary properties of the permitted remediation effect:[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-43]
- **Blast radius**: The scope of systems, users, or data impacted if the proposed remediation introduces regressions.
- **Reversal cost**: The complexity, downtime, or operational cost necessary to roll back or undo the applied modification.

### Acceptance Invariants
Regardless of gate strength, three baseline properties hold for every generated acceptance record:[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-43]
1. **Determinism of the verdict**: The pass/fail outcome is produced through reproducible, deterministic validation checks rather than subjective or non-deterministic model self-evaluations.
2. **Binding of verdict to candidate**: The verdict record explicitly binds to the exact patch or candidate artifact evaluated.
3. **Preservation as execution evidence**: The evaluation record and associated diagnostic outputs are preserved within the execution trace for post-incident auditability.

# Overview

The `aaif-clean-data` skill provides procedural hygiene and data normalization for AAIF community operations spreadsheets, standardizing intake responses from organizers, hosts, and speakers.[^evt-community-events-pr-56] It preserves historical data through [Proposal/execution split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md) patterns, performing preview validations prior to executing in-place modifications.

The skill provides automated CLI utilities including the `chapter-flags` subcommand implemented in `clean.py`.[^evt-community-events-pr-56]

### Chapter Flagging Behavior
- **Conditional formatting**: Applies a red highlight to the `City` column on `Form Responses` and `City (Existing)` on role tabs (`Organizers`, `Hosts`, and `Speakers`) whenever the submitted city string begins with `Other` (case-insensitive).[^evt-community-events-pr-56]
- **Review separation**: Operates independently of row status or automated `Resolved City` extraction, signaling that an `Other` submission requires human organizer determination rather than programmatic resolution.[^evt-community-events-pr-56]
- **Idempotence and range safety**: Defaults to a read-only preview indicating planned updates. When executed with write flags, it replaces only its owned rules and validates stored ranges to prevent newly appended form rows from being omitted.[^evt-community-events-pr-56]

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide
proposed_concept.description: Security implementation guide detailing threat models, credential safeguards, in-loop tool controls, approval fatigue mitigations, and cross-framework vulnerability mappings.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide establishes defense-in-depth principles, operational controls, and failure pattern mitigations across agentic AI workflows. Developed by the Security and Privacy Working Group (../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), the guide addresses risk surfaces spanning tool invocation boundaries, credential life cycles, context window pollution, and human oversight failures.

# Architecture / Specification

## Credential Security and Host Boundaries
Section 2 addresses secret management and credential containment across agent execution environments [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-33]:
- **Client Configurations and Skills**: Secret audits must include Model Context Protocol (MCP) client configuration files (such as `.mcp.json`, `.cursor/mcp.json`, and `claude_desktop_config.json`) and agent skill bundles (../standards/agent-skills.md), which frequently store plaintext API tokens in repository trees [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-33].
- **Context and Memory Redaction**: Secrets retrieved by tools or read from environment files must be scrubbed before passing into session context, traces, persistent memory, or log streams to prevent memory-based privilege retention [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-33].
- **Host Credential Isolation**: Autonomous coding agents running on developer machines require hook-level path deny rules for SSH keys (`~/.ssh`), cloud credentials (`~/.aws`), and browser sessions, paired with short-lived tokens to mitigate host sandbox escapes [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-33].
- **Confidential Computing Threat Scopes**: Hardware-isolated execution environments protect guest memory against host access, but do not shorten token lifetimes; bearer tokens exposed by compromised guest software remain valid for their full issuance window, requiring tight credential scoping alongside enclave isolation [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-37].

## Gateway Checkpoints vs. In-Loop Execution Hooks
Section 3.1 establishes the functional boundary between network intermediaries and execution hooks [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-30]:
- **Network Gateway Functions**: Centralized gateways such as ../resources/agentgateway.md serve as network checkpoints for remote MCP and Agent-to-Agent (A2A) communications, managing external transport authentication and capturing wire request/response payloads [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-30].
- **In-Loop Hook Enforcement**: Because network gateways cannot inspect local `stdio` subprocesses, shell commands, or direct library bindings, and lack access to prompting context, authoritative policy enforcement must execute within an in-loop hook inside the agent runtime loop [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-30].

## Human Oversight and Approval Fatigue Dynamics
Section 4 analyzes human-in-the-loop controls (../patterns/human-approval-gate.md), evaluating empirical failure modes in interactive authorization [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-35]:
- **Reviewer Degradation**: Repetitive permission prompts produce rubber-stamping, with empirical testing showing that while 97% of permission requests are approved, humans catch only 13.6% of dangerous commands, falling to approximately 5% after 50 prior prompts [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-35].
- **Automated Pre-Gating**: Automated deterministic acceptance checks (../patterns/deterministic-acceptance-gate.md) that intercept high percentages of hazardous commands must serve as the primary defensive barrier, reserving human intervention for escalated, non-routine actions [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-35].

## Threat Taxonomy Cross-Mappings
Appendix A maps guide recommendations to MITRE ATLAS v5.6.0 and the OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications 2026 (ASI) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-32]:
- **Credential Theft**: Mapped to `AML.T0055`, `AML.T0083`, `AML.T0106`, and `ASI03` [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-32].
- **Tool and Description Poisoning**: Mapped to `AML.T0110`, `AML.T0051.001`, `AML.T0104`, and `ASI02`/`ASI04` [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-32].
- **Supply Chain and Package Tampering**: Mapped to `AML.T0010.005`, `AML.T0011.002`, `AML.T0010.001`, and `ASI04`/`ASI05` [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-32].
- **Context and Memory Injection**: Mapped to `AML.T0080.000`, `AML.T0080.001`, and `ASI06` [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-32].
- **Excessive Agency and Exfiltration**: Mapped to `AML.T0086`, `AML.T0101`, and `ASI01`/`ASI08`/`ASI10` [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-32].

# Lifecycle History
Following initial merging in PR #9, multiple technical issues were opened in the Security and Privacy Working Group to refine the guide: ISSUE#30 on gateway versus in-loop hooks [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-30], ISSUE#32 on ATLAS and ASI taxonomy mappings [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-32], ISSUE#33 on configuration secrets and context leakage [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-33], ISSUE#35 on empirical approval fatigue metrics [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-35], and ISSUE#37 on confidential computing threat boundaries [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-37].

mutations.rationale: Incorporate empirical human oversight metrics demonstrating high rubber-stamping rates and the necessity of automated pre-screening gates.

proposed_concept.title: Human Approval Gate
proposed_concept.description: Workflow governance pattern requiring authorized human review before executing sensitive agent actions, reinforced by automated pre-gates against approval fatigue.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Human Approval Gate pattern introduces a synchronous authorization checkpoint into an agent workflow, preventing the execution of sensitive or high-impact actions until an authorized operator inspects and approves the request. While standard across single-agent and multi-agent governance architectures (../architectures/single-agent-human-approval.md), unconditioned prompts are vulnerable to severe operator fatigue and habituated rubber-stamping [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-35].

# Architecture / Specification

## Approval Fatigue and Failure Dynamics
Empirical research highlights the degradation of human oversight under frequent interactive prompts [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-35]:
- **Passive Approval Rates**: In large-scale user studies, approximately 97% of interactive agent permission prompts are accepted by operators without substantive inspection [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-35].
- **Detection Decay**: Human testers caught only 13.6% of dangerous commands slipped into agent sessions, with detection efficacy falling to approximately 5% after 50 prior prompts in a single session [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-35].
- **Habituation**: Frequent binary confirmations train operators to clear modals automatically, negating the gate's efficacy against indirect prompt injections and subverted tool calls [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-35].

## Hardened Implementation Guidelines
To maintain security integrity, human approval checkpoints must be paired with automated evaluation and contextual throttling:
- **Automated Pre-Gating**: Workflows should evaluate candidate actions against deterministic policy engines (../patterns/deterministic-acceptance-gate.md) before presenting them to humans, which can catch up to 89% of hazardous actions automatically [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-35].
- **Velocity and Fatigue Tracking**: Runtimes must track prompt frequency and operator review latency, enforcing cooling-off intervals, batching routine executions, or triggering out-of-band sign-offs (../patterns/hardware-bound-human-authorization.md) when velocity indicates rubber-stamping [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-35].
- **Payload Verification**: Actions submitted for review must bind to unalterable execution artifacts via cryptographic checkpoints (../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md), ensuring the approved intent matches the executed payload [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-35].

# Lifecycle History
Originally formulated as a foundational human-in-the-loop pattern, this pattern was updated to reflect empirical human review studies submitted during Security and Privacy Working Group reviews [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-35].

proposed_concept.title: AgentGateway
proposed_concept.description: Open-source traffic mediation and policy enforcement proxy managing MCP and A2A communications as a network checkpoint feeding runtime execution hooks.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

AgentGateway is an open-source traffic mediation proxy and perimeter enforcement engine governing Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Agent-to-Agent (A2A) network communications. Accepted into the Agentic AI Foundation in June 2026, the project acts as a network-level policy checkpoint that mediates transport boundaries, standardizes protocol auth, and records full-fidelity request and response audit logs [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-30].

# Architecture / Specification

## Network Boundary Role
AgentGateway operates at the network ingress and egress points for distributed agent systems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-30]:
- **Protocol Translation**: Terminates remote MCP and A2A sessions over HTTP, SSE, and WebSocket transports, normalizing authentication headers and mapping OAuth credentials [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-30].
- **Centralized Telemetry**: Intercepts request and response payloads across remote MCP servers, streaming structured audit records to security monitoring and observability backends [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-30].
- **Perimeter Access Control**: Applies coarse-grained permission checks, network allowlists, and traffic rate limits across multi-tenant agent deployments [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-30].

## Coordination with In-Loop Hooks
Within the broader security architecture (../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md), AgentGateway acts as a perimeter control rather than an isolated policy engine [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-30]:
- **Transport Coverage**: Network gateways cannot inspect local `stdio` MCP processes, shell commands, or SDK-native function calls [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-30].
- **Prompt Context Gap**: Gateways evaluate invocations at the wire level without visibility into the conversational trajectory or prompting context that produced them [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-30].
- **Complementary Architecture**: AgentGateway captures remote network payloads and validates perimeter credentials, while runtime hooks embedded directly inside the agent loop enforce context-aware policies and least-privilege constraints across all transport types [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-30].

# Lifecycle History
Onboarded as an AAIF project in June 2026, AgentGateway's position within defense-in-depth frameworks was refined in Security and Privacy Working Group discussions to define its boundary alongside in-loop agent hooks [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-30].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Open telemetry and correlation framework capturing causal agent execution while driving OpenTelemetry semantic alignment through an upstream conformance suite.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an observability initiative within the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) designed to capture causal agent execution, tool invocations, and multi-agent context propagation. Rather than establishing a standalone telemetry schema, current work focuses on resolving semantic inconsistencies across agent SDK implementations of OpenTelemetry by developing an upstream conformance framework[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fc392a405330-7a0995cd].

# Architecture / Specification
The model addresses telemetry fragmentation where heterogeneous agent runtimes implement [OpenTelemetry](../resources/opentelemetry.md) using diverging span hierarchies and attribute conventions[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fc392a405330-7a0995cd].

Key components of the reframed model include:
- **OpenTelemetry Semantic Convergence:** Identifying high-impact semantic gaps in agent execution spans, model prompts, and tool calls across major cloud and runtime vendors[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fc392a405330-7a0995cd].
- **Conformance Framework:** An automated test harness hosted in the foundation repository to validate that agent SDK telemetry conformantly reflects causal execution graphs[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fc392a405330-7a0995cd].
- **Upstream Contributions:** Feeding standardized semantic conventions directly into OpenTelemetry working groups rather than maintaining an isolated competing specification[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fc392a405330-7a0995cd].

# Lifecycle History
In the September 30, 2026 meeting of the Observability and Traceability Working Group, technical leads reframed the behavior trace model from a standalone telemetry protocol to an upstream OpenTelemetry gap analysis and conformance testing effort[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fc392a405330-7a0995cd].

proposed_concept.title: Identity and Trust Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group defining vendor-neutral standards, reference architectures, and delegation frameworks for agent identity and confidential attestation.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Identity and Trust Working Group is an AAIF technical body establishing open specifications, reference architectures, and delegation frameworks for AI agent identity, authentication, attestation, and authorization. It addresses how agent instances establish cryptographic identity, bind to trusted execution environments, and delegate authority across trust boundaries.

# Architecture / Specification
The working group maintains the Identity and Trust Reference Architecture. Under ongoing review, the attestation module is being decomposed from a monolithic component into three distinct architectural layers to accommodate diverse platform trust models[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-12]:

1. **Platform Evidence:** Signed hardware or firmware reports and endorsement chains asserting the physical execution environment and launch measurements[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-12].
2. **Identity Binding:** A signed cryptographic statement tying an agent identifier or key to the hardware report (e.g., via AMD SEV-SNP `REPORT_DATA`, Azure Confidential VM paravisor `Runtime Claims`, or TPM quote `qualifyingData`)[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-12].
3. **Appraisal:** The relying party evaluation engine producing a policy verdict against defined trust thresholds[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-12].

This decomposition accounts for platform-specific hardware differences, such as single-link AMD SEV-SNP guest reports, multi-stage Azure paravisor runtime claims, and detached NVIDIA H100 GPU attestation reports[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-12]. It interfaces closely with the [Attested Isolated Runtime pattern](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md).

# Lifecycle History
In October 2026, working group members proposed formalizing the three-part attestation decomposition within the Reference Architecture to resolve verification mismatches across hyperscaler confidential virtual machines and GPU environments[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-12].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices
proposed_concept.description: Security implementation guide detailing threat models, credential safeguards, in-loop tool controls, and runtime sandbox limitations for autonomous agents.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Security Best Practices guide establishes implementation patterns, operational safeguards, and threat modeling baselines for securing agentic workflows. Authored by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), the deliverable covers credential isolation, tool execution controls, and execution environment containment.

# Architecture / Specification
The guideline defines defensive controls across the agent lifecycle, with specific attention to runtime execution boundaries:

- **Credential and Secret Safeguards:** Restricting model access to long-lived credentials, using scoped ephemeral tokens, and redacting sensitive outputs.
- **In-Loop Tool Controls:** Intercepting high-impact tool invocations and enforcing policy-as-code before execution.
- **Sandbox Blast-Radius Boundaries:** Defining the containment perimeter for unverified artifact generation and command execution. Ongoing community review emphasizes that filesystem sandboxing (such as directory scoping) does not eliminate external egress risks or prevent indirect escapes via trust handoffs to unsandboxed host tools[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-34].
- **Egress and Network Isolation:** Enforcing protocol-level network boundaries to prevent agents from circumventing shell command restrictions (e.g., using runtime HTTP libraries like Python `urllib` when CLI tools like `curl` are blocked)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-34].

# Lifecycle History
Drafted under pull request reviews in late 2026, Section 3.2's claim of "contained" blast radius for sandbox modes was challenged in issue discussions to explicitly account for host tool handoffs and egress circumvention observed in production coding agent environments[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-34].

proposed_concept.title: Agent-In-The-Loop Transaction
proposed_concept.description: Agentic Commerce taxonomy term defining a commercial transaction where an AI agent mediates or executes workflow steps under human oversight.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
An **agent-in-the-loop transaction** is an [Agentic Commerce](../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md) taxonomy classification defining a commercial transaction where an AI agent participates, assists, or mediates operational checkout steps while maintaining active human review or explicit authorization in the loop.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-71]

The definition was submitted by the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) to formalize commerce terminology and rename the earlier concept of an "agent-mediated transaction" based on working group feedback.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-71]

# Architecture / Specification
In contrast to fully autonomous purchasing, an agent-in-the-loop transaction enforces operational boundaries and decision checkpoints where human approval is required prior to binding financial commitments (see [agentic-checkout](./agentic-checkout.md) and [delegated-payment](./delegated-payment.md)).[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-71]

# Lifecycle History
- Proposed in `aaif/ws-taxonomy-landscape` PR #71 as part of the Agentic Commerce taxonomy harmonization.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-71]

proposed_concept.title: Agent-Initiated Transaction
proposed_concept.description: Agentic Commerce taxonomy term defining a commercial transaction triggered and executed autonomously by an AI agent under delegated authority.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
An **agent-initiated transaction** is an [Agentic Commerce](../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md) taxonomy classification defining a transaction triggered, negotiated, and completed autonomously by an AI agent without synchronous human intervention at execution time.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-72]

# Architecture / Specification
Agent-initiated transactions operate within pre-established spending limits, policy constraints, and cryptographic delegation structures. They rely on standardized commerce primitives such as [agentic-checkout](./agentic-checkout.md) and [delegated-payment](./delegated-payment.md) to safely process commercial commitments across protocol boundaries.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-72]

# Lifecycle History
- Proposed in `aaif/ws-taxonomy-landscape` PR #72 within the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md).[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-72]

# Overview
`aaif-clean-data` is an operational agent skill governing intake data hygiene, schema validation, and geographical normalization for AAIF community operations.[^evt-community-events-pr-57]

# Architecture / Specification
The skill enforces standardization rules across community data pipelines:
- **Proposal-Execution Separation**: Validates and stages prospective data adjustments prior to executing downstream mutations in operational sheets and Google Drive assets.
- **Country Chapter Folding**: Normalizes legacy and regional intake values to canonical country chapters via `COUNTRY_CHAPTER_FOLDS` (mirrored in `lib/aaif_events/cities.py`).[^evt-community-events-pr-57] Specifically, applicants selecting Tokyo are folded into `AAIF Japan`, while applicants selecting Wellington or Auckland are folded into `AAIF New Zealand`.[^evt-community-events-pr-57]
- **Precedence Guarantees**: Folding rules supersede historical rows in the Chapters List to prevent retired municipal records from reasserting city-level allocations over national chapters.[^evt-community-events-pr-57]

# Lifecycle History
- Updated in `aaif/community-events` PR #57 to establish national chapter folds for Japan and New Zealand across all intake reading engines.[^evt-community-events-pr-57]

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing vendor-neutral agent telemetry standards, cross-boundary trace correlation, and layered tracing reference architectures.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The **Observability and Traceability Working Group** is an AAIF technical body focused on defining vendor-neutral telemetry specifications, cross-boundary trace correlation protocols, and runtime monitoring architectures for autonomous AI systems.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-69d00b3de313-cc8ae721]

# Architecture / Specification
The working group evaluates tracing infrastructure through a structured, five-tier bottom-up narrative framework:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-69d00b3de313-cc8ae721]

1. **Foundations (Tier 01)**: Low-level binary encodings and comparative evaluation frameworks, including the [Common Trace Format](../resources/common-trace-format.md), [Linux tracing comparisons](../resources/linux-tracing-comparison.md), and [Trace Compass](../resources/trace-compass.md).
2. **Kernel Tracing (Tier 02)**: Operating system observability, performance counters, driver tracing, hypervisor pre-emption, and container scheduling throttling, spanning [FTrace](../resources/ftrace.md), [Linux perf](../resources/linux-perf.md), [LTTng-kernel](../resources/lttng-kernel.md), [LTTng-UST](../resources/lttng-ust.md), [Linux driver tracing](../resources/linux-driver-tracing.md), [virtualization tracing](../resources/virtualization-tracing.md), [container orchestration tracing](../resources/container-orchestration-tracing.md), [Tracy](../resources/tracy.md), [sysdig](../resources/sysdig.md), and [Falco](../resources/falco.md).
3. **Hardware Accelerators (Tier 03)**: GPU kernel dispatch profiling, tensor core utilization, and framework-to-hardware correlation.
4. **Network (Tier 04)**: Wire protocol analysis and packet capture.
5. **AI Agent Observability (Tier 05)**: Runtime agent instrumentation, LLM tracing platforms, and user product analytics.

# Lifecycle History
- Authored the structured Reference Architecture Assessments catalog documenting tracing tools and kernel instrumentation from binary foundations to agent telemetry.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-69d00b3de313-cc8ae721]

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream
proposed_concept.description: Cross-cutting AAIF workstream harmonizing agentic AI terminology across vertical working groups and maintaining horizontal data schemas.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream is a cross-cutting body within the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) tasked with maintaining a shared, horizontal vocabulary across all seven active Technical Working Groups and developing the foundation's ecosystem landscape [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eca12c0a30e2-92c6cc77]. While the workstream's charter encompasses both taxonomy and ecosystem market mapping, contributions are currently restricted strictly to taxonomy terms; landscape contribution workflows remain deferred on the future roadmap [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eca12c0a30e2-92c6cc77].

Operational workflows coordinate with vertical groups such as [Security and Privacy](security-and-privacy.md) and [Workflows and Process Integration](workflows-and-process-integration.md) using automated schema validation and contributor skills like [Taxonomy Contributions](../skills/taxonomy-contributions.md).

# Architecture / Specification

## Roles and Governance

The workstream structures participation across three functional tiers to maintain data integrity and distribute editorial responsibilities [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eca12c0a30e2-92c6cc77]:

- **Contributors**: Open to any community participant or external partner to propose terms or raise issues.
- **Domain Editors**: Nominated technical delegates representing each of the seven active Technical Working Groups. Domain Editors author domain-specific terms, guide definitions, and hold review and veto authority.
- **Maintainers**: Workstream co-chairs Junjie Bu and Gala Malbasic, who retain repository write access and execute final merges [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eca12c0a30e2-92c6cc77].

## Term Lifecycle and Review Workflow

Terms undergo a structured intake and consensus lifecycle prior to repository admission [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eca12c0a30e2-92c6cc77], [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-83]:

1. **Intake**: A working group delegate stages a candidate term in the central intake spreadsheet and signals the request in the community communications channel.
2. **Triage Vote**: Outstanding terms are reviewed during weekly meetings for practical real-world usage, novelty, and working-group ownership. The workstream assigns one of three formal dispositions:
   - `KEEP`: The term is accepted and authorized for pull request submission.
   - `CULL`: The term is rejected.
   - `DEBATE`: The term requires further cross-group deliberation.
3. **Pull Request Submission**: The owning delegate opens a pull request providing a single-sentence definition and an optional `scopeNote` for context. Pull requests for terms without a prior `KEEP` vote are closed automatically.
4. **Cross-Group Approval**: Pull requests require approvals from at least two Domain Editors representing distinct Technical Working Groups. Any delegate may exercise veto power.
5. **Finalization**: Maintainers merge approved pull requests using GitHub's rebase-and-merge strategy, updating the spreadsheet entry to `FINALIZED` [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eca12c0a30e2-92c6cc77].

## Build and Verification Tooling

Taxonomy entries are stored in structured JavaScript dictionaries (`taxonomy-data.js`) adhering to a SKOS-Lite schema [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eca12c0a30e2-92c6cc77]. Build verification includes automated schema validation (`tools/validate-taxonomy.mjs`) alongside automated generation and continuous integration verification of human-readable Markdown documentation (`tools/generate-taxonomy-markdown.mjs`) enforced via pre-commit hooks [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-89].

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy Contributions
proposed_concept.description: Operational skill and contributor workflow enforcing SKOS-Lite schemas, horizontal indexing rules, and cross-working-group consensus for AAIF glossary terms.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Taxonomy Contributions skill standardizes the authoring, triage, and submission workflow for new terms added to the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md). It ensures all additions adhere to SKOS-Lite metadata requirements, follow strict formatting invariants, and satisfy foundation governance thresholds [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eca12c0a30e2-92c6cc77].

Contributions are predominantly stewarded by appointed Domain Editors from the technical working groups, ensuring cross-domain consistency across groups like [Security and Privacy](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) and [Workflows and Process Integration](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md).

# Architecture / Specification

## Contributor Workflow

1. **Propose Term**: Non-delegate contributors coordinate with their respective working group delegate, or attend the weekly taxonomy meeting to advocate for candidate terms [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eca12c0a30e2-92c6cc77].
2. **Triage Gate**: The candidate term must be logged in the central tracking spreadsheet and receive a formal `KEEP` vote during the weekly workstream meeting before code changes are accepted [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eca12c0a30e2-92c6cc77].
3. **Authoring Rules**:
   - **Single-Sentence Definition**: The primary definition field must be exactly one concise sentence [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eca12c0a30e2-92c6cc77].
   - **Scope Notes**: Extended clarifications, nuances, and concrete usage examples must be placed in the `scopeNote` metadata field [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eca12c0a30e2-92c6cc77].
   - **Granularity**: Pull requests should ideally encompass exactly one term to facilitate isolated review.
4. **Review and Veto**:
   - Requires approval from at least two Domain Editors representing different technical working groups [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eca12c0a30e2-92c6cc77].
   - Any delegate retains absolute veto power over a proposed term definition [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eca12c0a30e2-92c6cc77].
5. **Merge**: Merges are executed by workstream maintainers via Git rebase-and-merge, transitioning the tracking record to `FINALIZED` [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eca12c0a30e2-92c6cc77].

## Scope Constraints

The skill strictly rejects pull requests attempting modifications to the ecosystem Landscape, as landscape contributions remain frozen pending formal contribution process adoption [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eca12c0a30e2-92c6cc77].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The AAIF Brand Guidelines govern visual identity standards, digital asset generation, color palettes, and typographic scales across foundation materials, chapter assets, and community event presentations. These rules ensure high visual consistency across autonomous agent pipelines such as [AAIF Brand Guidelines Skill](../skills/aaif-brand-guidelines.md) and chapter operations managed under [Community Event Operations](../skills/community-event-operations.md).

# Architecture / Specification

## Vector Asset Source of Truth

Official visual assets reside in the canonical repository `assets/` directory and must be directly consumed by all automated and manual design workflows [^evt-community-events-pr-41]:

- `aaif-mark.svg`: Represents the full brand lockup (combining the icon mark and wordmark typography), despite its concise filename [^evt-community-events-pr-41].
- Additional standalone vector SVGs provide the isolated icon mark and secondary lockup variants.

## Invariant Rules

- **Never Redraw the Mark**: Under no circumstances should autonomous agents, designers, or community organizers redraw, trace, or re-render the AAIF mark from screenshots or raster bitmaps [^evt-community-events-pr-41]. Implementations must directly import the canonical SVGs from the asset inventory.
- **Contrast & Surface Fidelity**: Asset compositions must strictly respect light and dark surface background tokens to ensure accessible visual hierarchy.
- **Typography**: Text styling must follow standardized font tokens and typographic scales defined in the foundation design specifications.

proposed_concept.title: Project Proposal Process
proposed_concept.description: Operating procedure establishing the intake, review, voting, trademark transfer, and onboarding workflow for open-source projects joining the AAIF.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Project Proposal Process defines the formal intake, community evaluation, and onboarding procedures for open-source initiatives seeking inclusion in the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF). Supervised by the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) in accordance with the [Project Lifecycle Policy](project-lifecycle-policy.md), this policy governs how prospective projects transition from submission to official foundation hosting.

# Architecture / Specification

## Proposal Submission and Legal Commitments

Project maintainers submit intake proposals via the foundation issue tracker. As part of submission submission validation, applicants must formally agree to legal and governance requirements governing project intellectual property and administrative control [^evt-foundation-issue-8]:

- **Trademark and Account Donations**: Under Section 8 of the AAIF Foundation Charter, applicants must acknowledge and agree that upon proposal acceptance, all project trademarks (including project names and logos) and administrative accounts (such as code repositories, package registries, and domain names) will be assigned and donated directly to the AAIF [^evt-foundation-issue-8].

## Review and Onboarding Stages

1. **Intake Triage**: Automated verification checks the proposal structure and ensures all legal acknowledgments are satisfied.
2. **Technical Committee Review**: The Technical Committee assesses architectural relevance, community health, and alignment with foundational agentic AI standards.
3. **Voting and Stage Admission**: Following formal TC approval, projects are admitted to Sandbox or Growth tiers, initiating legal asset transfer and repository namespace migration.
