proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Governance, Risk & Regulatory Alignment Working Group (GRRA WG) serves as a bridge between global AI policy developments and technical advancements across agentic AI systems.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-13ea07bf] Established to address the absence of cohesive regulatory guidance and policy regimes for autonomous agents, the working group identifies standards gaps, examines organizational protocol governance, and promotes transparent policy insights that accelerate the adoption of open-source AI projects.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-13ea07bf]

# Architecture / Specification

## Leadership and Administration
- **Short Name / Acronym:** GRRA WG[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-13ea07bf]
- **Approval Date:** 2026-06-01 (revised 2026-10-09)[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-13ea07bf]
- **Primary Contact (Chair/Lead):** Deborah Eng (JPMorgan Chase)[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-13ea07bf]
- **Secondary Contact (Co-chair):** Sriram Natarajan (Google)[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-13ea07bf]

## Technical and Policy Scope

### In-Scope Workstreams
The working group focuses on organizational governance, policy tracking, and technical governance specifications:[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-13ea07bf]
- **Global Regulatory Tracking:** Monitoring international regulations, standards, and policy frameworks impacting the legal and compliance status of agentic AI systems.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-13ea07bf]
- **Protocol Governance Implementation:** Examining organizational deployment models for agent protocols such as the Model Context Protocol (MCP) in enterprise governance workflows.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-13ea07bf]
- **Action Reversibility & Undo Infrastructure:** Defining formal methods, protocols, and standard formats for action reversibility characterization to safely expand autonomous execution envelopes.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-13ea07bf]
- **AI Agent Bill of Materials (AIBOM):** Establishing standards for tracking foundation models, scaffolding frameworks, tool interfaces, APIs, and dependencies with cryptographic provenance and versioning.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-13ea07bf]
- **Risk Assessment & Autonomy Patterns:** Formulating risk classification schemas, incident reporting workflows, discovery policies, and human-in-the-loop oversight patterns.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-13ea07bf]
- **Industry Vertical Frameworks:** Evaluating end-user vertical standards, including financial governance models like the FINOS AI Governance Framework.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-13ea07bf]

### Out-of-Scope Activities
The working group explicitly does not provide formal legal advice or commercial compliance solutions.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-13ea07bf]

# References

- Charter: `aaif/wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory/charter.md`[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-13ea07bf]
- Related concepts: `../taxonomy/ai-agent-bill-of-materials.md`, `../patterns/human-approval-gate.md`

proposed_concept.description: Technical working group defining vendor-neutral standards, reference architectures, delegation frameworks, and trust evaluation for AI agents.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Identity & Trust Working Group (I&T WG) identifies and promotes vendor-neutral, interoperable standards and architectural viewpoints for AI agent identity, attestation, authentication, delegation, and authorization.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-e2016059] It enables agents to prove their identity, identify their principals, assert their operating constraints, and verify human approval chains across multi-tenant systems and organizational boundaries.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-e2016059]

# Architecture / Specification

## Leadership and Administration
- **Short Name / Acronym:** I&T WG[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-e2016059]
- **Approval Date:** 2026-05-12 (revised 2026-10-09)[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-e2016059]
- **Primary Contact (Chair/Lead):** Grant Miller[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-e2016059]

## Scope and Core Themes

### In-Scope Focus Areas
The working group addresses six core functional areas across enterprise and consumer agent topologies:[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-e2016059]
- **Agent Identity, Authentication, and Provenance:** Defining mechanisms for identifying agents, authenticating agent communications, and conveying provenance including operating entities and underlying software or system context.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-e2016059]
- **Delegation and Authority Chains:** Specifying models for agents acting on behalf of humans, organizations, teams, or services, including verifiable delegation bounds and lifespan of delegated authority.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-e2016059]
- **Authorization and Consent Models:** Establishing fine-grained, short-lived authorization schemes, policy constraints, and human consent or approval controls.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-e2016059]
- **Trust Evaluation & Cross-Organizational Trust:** Standardizing frameworks for evaluating cross-domain agent trust and validating execution authority across boundary crossings.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-e2016059]
- **Agent Discovery & Metadata:** Standardizing discovery formats and trust-relevant metadata that facilitate interoperability, traceability, and observability.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-e2016059]
- **Enterprise and Consumer Contexts:** Harmonizing deployment models across both enterprise administrative domains and consumer application environments.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-e2016059]

### Out-of-Scope Activities
The working group's charter explicitly excludes:[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-e2016059]
- Serving as a formal standards development organization (SDO) or ratifying formal external standards directly.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-e2016059]
- Defining end-to-end agent runtime security controls or sandbox execution architectures, which are deferred to the Security and Privacy Working Group.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-e2016059]
- Defining normative ethical frameworks or public policy positions except where required for identity, consent, or accountability representations.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-e2016059]
- Operating production identity infrastructure or commercial certification authorities.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-e2016059]

# References

- Charter: `aaif/wg-identity-and-trust/charter.md`[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-e2016059]
- Sibling WGs: `../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md`, `../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md`, `../working-groups/attestation-and-evidence.md`

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The `aaif-clean-data` skill is an automated operational pipeline and data hygiene utility used across AAIF community intake trackers and event estates.[^evt-community-events-pr-58] It normalizes contributor and applicant submissions, enforces proposal-execution splits across operational spreadsheets, verifies contact identifiers, and manages hygiene flags across multi-role applicant records.[^evt-community-events-pr-58]

# Architecture / Specification

## Multi-Tab Verdict Filtering
Applicant records frequently span multiple role tabs (such as organizer and speaker) with distinct evaluation verdicts.[^evt-community-events-pr-58] To prevent unactionable issue alerts on rejected applicants, the data scanning engine implements unanimous negative verdict suppression:[^evt-community-events-pr-58]
- **Decided-No Suppression:** The `scan` command skips flagging a submission if and only if every role tab containing the applicant evaluates to a terminal negative status (`Denied`, `Inactive`, or `Duplicate`).[^evt-community-events-pr-58]
- **Mixed-Verdict Retention:** If an applicant is rejected on one role tab (e.g., organizer Denied) but remains active or prospective on another (e.g., speaker Prospect), issues continue to be flagged for review.[^evt-community-events-pr-58]
- **Missing Metadata Fallback:** If a role tab lacks standard `Status`, `Timestamp`, or `Email` columns, verdict suppression is disabled for that tab to prevent silent suppression.[^evt-community-events-pr-58]
- **Live Spreadsheet Formula Synchronization:** The `issues_formula()` helper generated via `install_flags` renders decided-no rows as blank rather than error-flagged, maintaining clean operational views for community organizers.[^evt-community-events-pr-58]

# References

- Repository: `aaif/community-events` (PR #58)[^evt-community-events-pr-58]
- Related skills: `../skills/aaif-audit-slack.md`, `../skills/community-event-operations.md`

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Commerce Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing vendor-neutral capability maps, protocol gap analyses, and reference architectures for agentic transactions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic Commerce Working Group establishes vendor-neutral capability maps, protocol gap analyses, and reference architectures governing AI agent interactions in commercial transactions and autonomous payment flows.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5] Its charter encompasses pre-purchase negotiation, payment execution, and post-purchase lifecycle management, including cross-boundary evidence preservation, dispute resolution, and auditability across agent, merchant, payment provider, and risk system boundaries.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5]

# Architecture / Specification

## Capability Map and Gap Analysis
The working group produces a comprehensive Capability Map and Protocol Gap Analysis evaluating specifications such as Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP), Agent Commerce Protocol (ACP), Mastercard Verifiable Intent (VI), Visa Trusted Agent Protocol (TAP), x402, and Agentic Payment Protocol (AP2).[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5]

### Cross-Boundary Evidence and Audit
A core dimension of the Capability Map addresses cross-boundary accountability across the post-purchase lifecycle:[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5]
- **Evidence Binding:** Binding claimed actions to delegation records, transaction identifiers, and agent/shopper identities in verifiable receipts or audit records, ensuring disputes can be resolved without re-negotiation.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5]
- **Signal Provenance:** Tracking capability and risk signals across agents, platforms, merchants, and payment networks, categorizing signals by assurance levels and distinguishing self-reported from independently observed markers.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5]
- **Authorization Strength for State Changes:** Distinguishing read-only order observations from authoritative state-changing requests (cancellations, returns, refunds, chargebacks), mandating explicit authorization scopes and renewed buyer consent.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5]
- **Auditability After the Fact:** Standardizing verifiable receipts, retained proof bundles, and audit trails required for dispute and claims resolution.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5]

### Machine-Readable Verdict Envelope Contract
To standardize evidence evaluation without imposing monolithic verification engines, the evidence framework defines a machine-readable verdict envelope containing:[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5]
1. `verdict`: Three-state classification (`supported`, `contradicted`, or `unresolvable`).[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5]
2. `verifier`: Cryptographic identity of the evaluating entity (distinct from the claim producer).[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5]
3. `verifier_signature`: Digital signature over the verdict and evidence fingerprints.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5]
4. `evidence_refs`: Bound references to delegation, transaction, and consent records.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5]
5. `evidence_fingerprints`: Canonical RFC 8785 hashes for deterministic verification replay.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5]
6. `verification_basis`: Enumeration of evaluated rules and validation checks.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5]
7. `witness_scope`: Explicit boundaries of what the verdict attests and excludes.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5]
8. `timestamp`: Freshness and issuance time.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5]

## Cross-Working-Group Interfaces
The Agentic Commerce WG coordinates with sibling foundations:[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5]
- `../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md`: Agent identity representation and delegated authority chains.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5]
- `../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md`: Telemetry formats, audit log custody, and dispute evidence pipelines.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5]

# References

- Issue: `aaif/wg-agentic-commerce#5`[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5]
- Related concepts: `../taxonomy/agent-in-the-loop-transaction.md`, `../taxonomy/agent-initiated-transaction.md`, `../taxonomy/delegated-payment.md`, `../taxonomy/three-state-reconciliation.md`

proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing open threat models, security best practices, design patterns, and cross-working-group review checklists.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group is an AAIF technical body tasked with establishing vendor-neutral threat models, security best practices, design patterns, and cross-working-group review checklists for agentic systems.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-c575359e] The group coordinates with the [Governance, Risk and Regulatory Alignment Working Group](../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md), [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md), and [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) to define consistent security baselines across foundation architectures.

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its deliverables across dedicated workstreams:
- **Best Practices**: Authors the [Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md) and maintains the Security Best Practices Feature Matrix.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-c575359e]
- **Threat Modeling**: Maintains the [Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis](../resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md), aligning frameworks such as OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, and NIST AI RMF.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-c575359e]
- **Design Patterns**: Catalogs architectural security patterns including [attested isolated runtimes](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md), [inherited security floors](../patterns/inherited-security-floor.md), and [kill switches](../patterns/kill-switch.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-c575359e]
- **Cross-WG Review**: Maintains the [Cross-WG Security Review Checklist](../guidelines/cross-wg-security-review-checklist.md) to audit technical specifications across peer working groups.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-c575359e]

# Lifecycle History
The working group was established in June 2026, forming five initial workstreams and transferring terminology harmonization to the cross-WG taxonomy effort.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-c575359e] In July and August 2026, the group opened meeting archives, advanced deliverable drafts, and instituted cross-WG checklist reviews.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-c575359e] In September 2026, the working group registered its initial formal deliverables with the Technical Committee—including the Best Practices Guide, Threat Modeling Gap Analysis, and first four design pattern drafts—while formalizing merge governance for the deliverables directory and piloting alternate-week APAC meetings.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-c575359e]

mutations.rationale: Add candidate supply-chain taxonomy term covering tools and manifests that are deliberately malicious upon creation.

proposed_concept.title: Tool Poisoning
proposed_concept.description: Supply-chain attack where an agent tool or tool definition is deliberately crafted or modified to execute malicious actions or alter agent behavior.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Tool poisoning is an agent tool supply-chain attack pattern where a tool or tool definition (such as a Model Context Protocol server manifest) is inherently malicious from its point of creation or publication.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-88] In agentic deployments, poisoned tool definitions manipulate how foundation models select, parameterize, or execute functions, potentially triggering unauthorized tool calls, indirect prompt injection, or sensitive data exfiltration.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-88]

Within the AAIF taxonomy, tool poisoning is distinguished from a [rug pull](rug-pull.md) by timing: tool poisoning characterizes tools that are malicious from the outset, whereas a rug pull involves a previously trusted and verified tool turning malicious after initial approval.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-88]

# Architecture / Specification
The concept aligns with MITRE ATLAS technique AML.T0110 (AI Agent Tool Poisoning) and OWASP MCP Top 10 vulnerabilities.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-88] Adversaries exploit the natural language descriptions consumed by model orchestrators to misrepresent tool capabilities or embed covert instructions. Mitigation strategies require mandatory [tool definition verification](tool-definition-verification.md), strict policy-as-code proxies, and architectural isolation such as [proposal-execution splits](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md).[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-88]

# Lifecycle History
Introduced in PR #88 of the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) as part of a cross-working-group vocabulary proposal aligned with the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) and [Governance, Risk and Regulatory Alignment Working Group](../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md).[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-88]

mutations.rationale: Add candidate supply-chain taxonomy term covering tools or manifests that turn malicious after runtime admission or approval.

proposed_concept.title: Rug Pull
proposed_concept.description: Agent tool supply-chain attack where a previously verified or trusted tool definition or endpoint is modified after approval to introduce malicious behavior.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
A rug pull in agentic systems is a supply-chain vulnerability and attack pattern where a tool definition, manifest, or endpoint that was previously vetted, approved, and admitted into an agent environment is altered to introduce malicious behavior after admission.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-88] The attack exploits the ongoing trust, operational permissions, and integration access granted during the initial approval checkpoint.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-88]

The term contrasts with [tool poisoning](tool-poisoning.md) on the basis of temporal state: while tool poisoning concerns tools that are malicious from the moment of introduction, a rug pull exploits post-admission mutability, remote endpoint updates, or upstream package compromises.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-88]

# Architecture / Specification
Rug pulls correspond to MITRE ATLAS technique AML.T0109 (AI Supply Chain Rug Pull) and OWASP MCP Top 10 risks.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-88] In protocols like the Model Context Protocol (MCP), dynamic schemas or remote tool hosting can allow server operators or compromised repositories to alter descriptions, parameter scopes, or backend endpoints silently without re-triggering user admission gates unless continuous [tool definition verification](tool-definition-verification.md) and cryptographic content-addressable pinning are enforced.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-88]

# Lifecycle History
Drafted in PR #88 of the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) in coordination with the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) and [Governance, Risk and Regulatory Alignment Working Group](../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md).[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-88]

mutations.rationale: Add candidate supply-chain taxonomy term covering procedures that verify tool manifests and schemas prior to admission.

proposed_concept.title: Tool Definition Verification
proposed_concept.description: Process of validating the authenticity, schema integrity, and behavioral claims of an agent tool definition or manifest prior to runtime admission.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Tool definition verification (also referred to as tools manifest verification) is the evaluation process of checking an agent tool's schema, metadata, description, and source integrity before admitting it into an agent runtime or context window.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-88] It establishes that tool capabilities conform to expected schemas, declare explicit parameter boundaries, and originate from verified publishers.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-88]

In the AAIF taxonomy, tool definition verification contrasts with attestation: attestation refers to the generation of signed assertions regarding an artifact's provenance or state, whereas verification is the operational evaluation performed by an agent runtime or operator against policy constraints before use.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-88]

# Architecture / Specification
Tool definition verification guards against [tool poisoning](tool-poisoning.md) and [rug pulls](rug-pull.md) through several checks:
- Verifying cryptographic signatures on tool manifests and upstream packages.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-88]
- Semantic and static analysis of natural language descriptions to detect prompt injection or deceptive documentation.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-88]
- Schema validation ensuring that declared input parameters and return types adhere to assigned boundary policies.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-88]
- Binding immutable content hashes to prevent unauthenticated runtime endpoint drift.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-88]

# Lifecycle History
Proposed in PR #88 of the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) as a cross-WG taxonomy term shared between the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) and [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md).[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-88]

mutations.rationale: Add candidate supply-chain taxonomy term defining session and memory isolation failures across clients on shared tool servers.

proposed_concept.title: Cross-Client Data Leakage
proposed_concept.description: Security vulnerability where confidential session state, prompt data, or tool responses cross isolation boundaries on a shared agent tool server.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Cross-client data leakage is an isolation vulnerability occurring on shared tool servers (such as multi-tenant Model Context Protocol servers) where session state, credentials, prompts, or execution outputs belonging to one client are inadvertently exposed to another client session.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-88] The flaw occurs when tool server implementations maintain unsegmented global variables, shared cache buffers, or connection multiplexing without strict per-session boundaries.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-88]

# Architecture / Specification
When multiple agent clients interact with a shared tool server, context contamination can propagate through:
- In-memory conversation state or tool execution history retained across distinct client invocations.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-88]
- Shared credential caches exposing elevated access tokens across multi-user environments.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-88]
- Error logs and telemetry payloads returning raw context from previous sessions.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-88]

Countermeasures include enforcing [branch isolation](../patterns/branch-isolation.md), requiring ephemeral sandboxing for tool execution, and strictly partitioning session state in tool runtime protocols.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-88]

# Lifecycle History
Proposed in PR #88 of the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) in coordination with the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) and [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md).[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-88]

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Commerce Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing vendor-neutral capability maps, protocol gap analyses, and reference flows for autonomous and mediated transactions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic Commerce Working Group establishes vendor-neutral capability maps, protocol gap analyses, and reference architectures governing autonomous and agent-assisted commercial transactions. It evaluates commerce-enabling protocols across discovery, identity, cart management, checkout negotiation, and payment settlement to ensure operational safety and regulatory alignment.

# Architecture / Specification

The working group assesses emerging and legacy transaction protocols—including UCP, ACP, AP2, and x402—against standardized operational requirements. Key dimensions under development include:
- **Buyer Capacity and Verification**: Addressing legal capacity, minor principal delegations, and jurisdiction-specific age validation mandates where an agent transacts without a human present at checkout [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-8].
- **Multi-Layer Record Retention**: Specifying data retention obligations across AI safety mandates (such as EU AI Act provider and deployer log retention), personal data protection limits, and financial anti-money laundering (AML) regulatory periods [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-8].
- **Delegated Authority and Settlement**: Analyzing boundaries between autonomous decision-making and human authorization checkpoints across payment execution.

# Lifecycle History

Active discussions within the working group identified structural gaps in protocol scoring frameworks, specifically highlighting that capability maps must capture principal capacity verification and multi-tier evidentiary retention across commercial jurisdictions [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-8].

# References

- [Agentic Checkout](../taxonomy/agentic-checkout.md)
- [Agent-Initiated Transaction](../taxonomy/agent-initiated-transaction.md)
- [Delegated Payment](../taxonomy/delegated-payment.md)

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices
proposed_concept.description: Security implementation guide detailing threat models, credential safeguards, in-loop tool controls, and pre-execution policy hooks.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Security Best Practices guideline provides design-time recommendations and runtime controls for securing autonomous AI agents. It addresses identity validation, sandbox isolation, credential boundaries, and policy enforcement across tool invocations.

# Architecture / Specification

Security enforcement in agent runtime environments balances automated programmatic controls with human oversight:
- **Pre-Execution Control Hooks**: Intercepting every tool call prior to execution using deterministic code rules, returning discrete decisions (allow, deny, modify, or escalate) rather than relying exclusively on post-hoc review [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-31].
- **Contextual Action Keying**: Evaluating tool execution permissions dynamically based on tool name, verified input arguments, and execution context rather than static operation classifications [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-31].
- **Tiered Approval Routing**: Using automated controls as primary operational gates, reserving human-in-the-loop workflows for explicit escalation paths to mitigate approval fatigue and bypassed security prompts [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-31].

# Lifecycle History

Working group reviews identified limitations in purely human-in-the-loop permission prompts, proposing integration with standardized hook specifications to execute deterministic boundary checks prior to human escalation [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-31].

# References

- [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md)
- [Human Approval Gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md)
- [Approval Checkpoint](../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md)

proposed_concept.title: Parallel Research and Merge Reference Architecture
proposed_concept.description: Multi-agent reference architecture coordinating concurrent, isolated subagent research across disparate domains before merging findings into a unified output.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Parallel Research and Merge reference architecture governs multi-agent workflows where independent subagents concurrently execute targeted information gathering, synthesis, or analysis tasks without direct inter-agent communication, returning artifacts to a centralized coordinator for consolidation [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-55].

# Architecture / Specification

The architecture defines distinct execution phases:
1. **Task Partitioning**: A primary coordinating agent or runtime decomposes an analytical objective into distinct research tasks.
2. **Isolated Concurrency**: Subagents operate in parallel execution envelopes with isolated context windows and independent tool access, maintaining separation without direct agent-to-agent signaling [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-55].
3. **Result Reconciliation**: Completed research outputs are aggregated and merged through deterministic acceptance criteria or synthesizer models, detecting contradictions across concurrent branches.

# Lifecycle History

Initiated by the Workflows and Process Integration Working Group following consensus in architectural sync meetings to establish baseline reference architectures for non-communicating parallel subagents prior to complex multi-agent dialog patterns [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-55].

# References

- [Parallel Fan-Out and Join](../patterns/parallel-fan-out-and-join.md)
- [Branch Isolation](../patterns/branch-isolation.md)
- [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md)

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Backup Skill
proposed_concept.description: Operational backup skill generating immutable, timestamped local snapshots of Google Drive and local files prior to mutating edits.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The `aaif-backup` skill is an operational utility within the AAIF community events toolkit that generates immutable, timestamped local snapshots of critical operations data—such as the Community Intake Ops sheet or arbitrary Google Drive and local files—prior to executing destructive or risky mutations.[^evt-community-events-file-91fd6707275c-36b98c09]

# Architecture / Specification

## Execution and Engine
The skill is powered by the `scripts/backup.py` engine and accepts an optional Google Drive file ID or local file path as an argument.[^evt-community-events-file-91fd6707275c-36b98c09] By default, it exports the AAIF Community Intake Ops sheet into `.xlsx` format.[^evt-community-events-file-91fd6707275c-36b98c09]

## Storage Conventions
Every invocation creates a new immutable file without overwriting prior snapshots, establishing a verifiable version history for differential auditing or manual rollback.[^evt-community-events-file-91fd6707275c-36b98c09] Snapshots land using the structured layout:

```
<dest>/<slug>/<UTC-timestamp>.<ext>
```

The destination defaults to the `backups/` directory within the toolkit's data path, configurable via `--dest`.[^evt-community-events-file-91fd6707275c-36b98c09]

## Tooling Rules and Prohibitions
All interactions with Google Drive files are strictly governed by the Google Workspace (`gws`) CLI driven by Python.[^evt-community-events-file-91fd6707275c-36b98c09] Native Google formats (`application/vnd.google-apps.*`) must be modified directly through Google APIs rather than round-tripping through converted Office documents.[^evt-community-events-file-91fd6707275c-36b98c09] Headless desktop office converters like LibreOffice (`soffice`) and `unoconv` are strictly prohibited due to font substitutions and lossy OOXML rendering.[^evt-community-events-file-91fd6707275c-36b98c09]

Prerequisite authentication for `gws` is validated using [aaif-check-setup](aaif-check-setup.md).[^evt-community-events-file-91fd6707275c-36b98c09]

mutations.rationale: Update aaif-audit-slack with operational specifications for multi-engine Slack auditing, git-leak prevention, cache reconciliation, untrusted input boundaries, and the single-HTML reporting pipeline.

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Slack Audit Skill
proposed_concept.description: Read-only inspection skill auditing community Slack workspace coverage, organizer membership, topic channel vitality, and member demographics into a unified HTML report.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The `aaif-audit-slack` skill is a read-only governance and operational audit utility that inspects the AAIF community Slack workspace to evaluate chapter channel provisioning, organizer placement, subject-matter channel activity, and overall member composition into a consolidated HTML report.[^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-84165b73]

It functions as Phase 8 of the estate reconciliation pipeline orchestrated by [aaif-sync](aaif-sync.md), serving as an independent verification layer isolated from the engines performing data writes.[^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-84165b73]

# Architecture / Specification

## Multi-Engine Architecture
The audit orchestrates three distinct inspection engines and a shared activity measurement layer:[^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-84165b73]

- **Organizers Audit (`audit_organizers.py`)**: Validates whether each chapter possesses designated public and organizer channels, and verifies that accepted organizers are active members.[^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-84165b73]
- **Topics Audit (`audit_topics.py`)**: Evaluates thematic community channels for quietness, functional overlap, and discoverability.[^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-84165b73]
- **Members Audit (`audit_members.py`)**: Profiles workspace layout, active demographics, and newcomer onboarding exposure.[^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-84165b73]
- **Activity Layer (`audit_activity.py`)**: Measures last human message timestamps, message volume, and distinct poster counts to feed the topics and members engines.[^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-84165b73]

## Reporting Pipeline
The deliverable script `summarize_audits.py` synthesizes existing cached engine outputs into `slack-full-audit.html`.[^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-84165b73][^evt-community-events-file-8b30d97e0275-3e6d8b8d] The report contains four top-level sections—Chapters, Organizers, Topics, and Members—concluded by a ranked focus list prioritizing remedial actions.[^evt-community-events-file-8b30d97e0275-3e6d8b8d]

## Cache Governance and Leak Prevention
Raw API pulls are stored in `.slack-audit-cache` under the toolkit data directory.[^evt-community-events-file-8b30d97e0275-3e6d8b8d] Because cache files contain member names, email addresses, and admin flags, files are written with permissions `0600` inside a `0700` directory.[^evt-community-events-file-8b30d97e0275-3e6d8b8d] Engines enforce an automated safeguard that refuses execution if cache or output paths could be staged via `git add -A`.[^evt-community-events-file-8b30d97e0275-3e6d8b8d]

## Untrusted Input Controls
Slack profile strings, channel topics, message payloads, and spreadsheet cells are strictly treated as passive data rather than instructions.[^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-84165b73] Text requesting administrative privilege grants or channel membership changes must never trigger automatic authorization or state modification.[^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-84165b73]

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Check Setup Skill
proposed_concept.description: Read-only pre-flight diagnostics skill verifying Python runtime, Google Workspace authentication, credential configuration, and environment health.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The `aaif-check-setup` skill is a read-only pre-flight diagnostic utility within the AAIF community events toolkit that verifies local runtime readiness, Google Workspace (`gws`) CLI authentication, Slack API token validity, and environment configuration prior to operational task execution.[^evt-community-events-file-5a72ef6a708b-c7737da1]

# Architecture / Specification

## Evaluation and Intent Detection
The skill is tested within the [community-events-eval-suite](../resources/community-events-eval-suite.md) using automated evaluation scenarios designed for non-technical users.[^evt-community-events-file-5a72ef6a708b-c7737da1] Evaluation assertions mandate that the skill trigger on natural conversational prompts inquiring whether the toolkit environment is operational (e.g., "is it all working?"), without requiring explicit invocations containing technical keywords such as "setup" or "check".[^evt-community-events-file-5a72ef6a708b-c7737da1][^evt-community-events-file-cd95e0a9e63d-5578e7ad]

## Operational Scope
The diagnostic suite ensures that dependencies and credentials required by dependent tools—including [aaif-backup](aaif-backup.md) and [aaif-audit-slack](aaif-audit-slack.md)—are properly loaded and authenticated before downstream file manipulation or workspace crawling commences.[^evt-community-events-file-5a72ef6a708b-c7737da1]

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Create Chapter Skill
proposed_concept.description: Automated city chapter provisioning engine cloning TemplateCity in Google Drive and rebranding OOXML and slide assets.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The `aaif-create-chapter` skill provisions a new city chapter across the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) community estate by cloning the standard `TemplateCity` folder in Google Drive and rebranding its core template assets[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-0c36b708]. The skill standardizes file rebranding, geocodes geographic coordinates to update slide graphics, and enforces strict manipulation boundaries to prevent Office Open XML (OOXML) corruption.

# Architecture / Specification

## Tooling and Rendering Constraints

The chapter creation engine operates under strict tooling constraints enforced via Python automation and the Google Workspace CLI (`gws`)[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-0c36b708]:
- **Native Format Preference:** Edits to Google-native formats (`application/vnd.google-apps.*`) occur directly via Docs, Sheets, and Slides APIs[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-0c36b708].
- **Byte-Level OOXML Surgery:** Binary Office files (`.docx`, `.pptx`, `.xlsx`) are unpacked and edited at the ZIP part level to preserve embedded font streams and non-target XML parts[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-0c36b708].
- **Prohibition of Desktop Suites:** Headless office tools such as LibreOffice (`soffice`), `unoconv`, or local desktop suites are forbidden for edits and preview rendering, as font substitution corrupts brand typography and discards unhandled OOXML elements[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-0c36b708]. Visual inspection requires exporting temporary files through Google APIs or dedicated rendering scripts[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-0c36b708].

## Rebranding and Token Substitution

During provisioning, the engine rebrands specific identifier tokens while leaving per-event placeholders (dates, agendas, speaker rosters, and neighborhood markers) untouched for chapter organizers[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-0c36b708]:
- `San Francisco` / `SAN FRANCISCO` transforms to the new city name matching case[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-0c36b708].
- `SF` abbreviations transform into the full city name in Title Case or uppercase as context dictates[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-0c36b708].
- Luma community slugs and hyperlink targets transform from `aaif-sanfrancisco` to `aaif-<slug>`[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-0c36b708].
- File and directory names carrying these tokens (such as `Attendee CRM.xlsx`) are identically renamed[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-0c36b708].

## Geographic Coordinate Mapping

In addition to text transformations, the skill relocates the graphical "you-are-here" dot and `<CITY> · TONIGHT` callout on slide 5 ("THE NETWORK") of `Event Template/Slides.pptx`[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-0c36b708]. The engine maps coordinates derived from manual `--lat`/`--lon` parameters or automated Nominatim geocoding onto the world map projection, falling back to San Francisco with an operator warning if coordinates fail to resolve[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-0c36b708].

# Lifecycle History

- Merged into `aaif/community-events` repository under `skills/aaif-create-chapter/SKILL.md` replacing legacy manual prompt documents with automated agent skills[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-0c36b708].

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Check Setup Skill
proposed_concept.description: Read-only pre-flight diagnostic skill auditing Google Workspace authentication, credential resolution order, and runtime dependencies.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The `aaif-check-setup` skill provides a plain-language diagnostic readiness check for operators running the AAIF Community Events Toolkit across client environments such as [Goose](../resources/goose.md), Claude Desktop, Claude Code, and standalone checkouts[^evt-community-events-pr-60]. It inspects runtime dependencies, validates binary accessibility, tests Google Workspace authentication, and verifies credential availability across multiple storage backends[^evt-community-events-pr-60][^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-aa074a1c].

# Architecture / Specification

## Diagnostic Verification Engine

When invoked by the operator ("check my setup"), the skill audits each component required for operational workflows and outputs actionable remediation instructions rather than silent failures[^evt-community-events-pr-60]:
- **CLI Visibility:** Verifies that the Google Workspace CLI (`gws`) binary is installed and executable in the assistant application's shell context[^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-aa074a1c].
- **OAuth Scopes and Sign-in:** Validates `gws` OAuth authorization; if expired or unauthenticated, it generates the exact scoped login command rather than permitting an unconstrained `gws auth login`[^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-aa074a1c].
- **Credential Chain Verification:** Verifies read and write permissions for external services using the standardized credential resolution hierarchy[^evt-community-events-pr-60].

## Secret Lookup Resolution

The skill and underlying toolkit engines inspect secrets using a strict priority order cached per execution run[^evt-community-events-pr-60]:
1. Process environment variables[^evt-community-events-pr-60].
2. Repository-root `.env` file (when operating inside a git checkout)[^evt-community-events-pr-60].
3. Local operating system secure store (macOS Keychain entries `aaif-slack-write-token`, `aaif-slack-read-token`, and `luma-api-key` under account `aaif`)[^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-aa074a1c].

This multi-tier discovery enables non-technical users to retain secrets across automated agent plugin updates where shell environments are not propagated by the client host[^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-aa074a1c].

# Lifecycle History

- Introduced in PR #60 to support non-technical operators and standalone plugin installations in desktop agent clients[^evt-community-events-pr-60].

proposed_concept.title: Community Event Operations Toolkit
proposed_concept.description: Procedural operations pipeline and runtime infrastructure managing chapter provisioning, credentials resolution, and data directory isolation.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Community Event Operations Toolkit provides runtime infrastructure, data hygiene, and procedural automation for managing AAIF community chapters, event scheduling, and organizer directories[^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-aa074a1c]. Packaged as a portable [Agent Plugin](../standards/agent-plugins.md) leveraging [Agent Skills](../standards/agent-skills.md), the toolkit operates consistently across [Goose](../resources/goose.md), Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor[^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-aa074a1c].

# Architecture / Specification

## Multi-Client Packaging

The toolkit exposes two integration manifests to maximize client portability[^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-aa074a1c]:
- A root `plugin.json` adhering to cross-client Agent Plugin standards[^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-aa074a1c].
- A `.claude-plugin/` directory providing backwards compatibility with Anthropic Claude marketplaces[^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-aa074a1c].

Individual operations are structured as modular skills under `skills/aaif-*`, each loaded through progressive disclosure rules and relative `<skill-root>` path execution to prevent path breakage in isolated cache environments[^evt-community-events-pr-60].

## Data Directory Isolation

To decouple state and audit artifacts from the active working directory or ephemeral plugin cache clones, the engine routes file outputs through `aaif_events.datadir`[^evt-community-events-pr-60]:
- **Repository Checkout Mode:** Writes reports (`sync-reports/`), backups, and JSON outputs directly to the repository root[^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-aa074a1c].
- **Installed Plugin Mode:** Diverts state files and backups to `~/Library/Application Support/AAIF` on macOS (or XDG data homes on Linux), ensuring that automatic plugin version updates do not orphan local backup snapshots or overwrite user files[^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-aa074a1c].
- **Override Control:** Accepts an absolute path via `AAIF_DATA_DIR` while rejecting relative values to safeguard execution integrity[^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-aa074a1c][^evt-community-events-pr-60].

## Operational Pipelines

The operational suite pairs diagnostics ([`aaif-check-setup`](../skills/aaif-check-setup.md)) with chapter estate management ([`aaif-create-chapter`](../skills/aaif-create-chapter.md)), backup snapshots, and CRM synchronization, enforcing strict data normalization and proposal-execution boundaries across all administrative actions[^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-aa074a1c].

# Lifecycle History

- Expanded via PR #60 to support non-technical operator execution inside desktop agent environments without local git checkouts or pre-configured shell environments[^evt-community-events-pr-60].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Landscape Catalog and Validation Architecture
proposed_concept.description: Interactive ecosystem market map and catalog backed by landscape.yml, governed by strict schema validation, failsafe YAML parsing, and CI security bounds.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Landscape is an open ecosystem market map and architectural catalog maintained by the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md). It catalogs agentic AI tools, frameworks, and protocols structured as categories, subcategories, and projects defined in a declarative `landscape/landscape.yml` registry and rendered via an interactive web interface [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-28].

# Architecture / Specification

## Schema and Data Model
The landscape data file `landscape/landscape.yml` organizes entries into a category and subcategory hierarchy [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-28]. Each catalog item mandates:
- Unicode-normalized unique item names without duplication [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-28].
- Valid project enum classifications [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-28].
- Valid HTTPS URLs containing no whitespace or embedded credentials [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-28].
- Strict rejection of unknown top-level or item-level fields [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-28].

## Parsing Parity and Resource Bounds
To prevent parser mismatch vulnerabilities between the continuous integration pipeline and the browser runtime, both the Node.js CI validator (`scripts/validate-landscape.mjs`) and the client application (`app.js`) parse YAML with `FAILSAFE_SCHEMA` and explicit recursion depth limits [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-28]. This guarantees that numeric scalars remain strings rather than type-coerced integers that would fail browser search operations [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-28].

Resource bounds enforced during validation include [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-28]:
- **File Size Cap**: Strict 512 KB file size threshold checked via `statSync` prior to parsing [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-28].
- **Catalog Budgets**: Maximum limit of 500 items, 5,000 objects or arrays, and 20,000 references across the object graph [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-28].
- **YAML Feature Restrictions**: Explicit rejection of YAML merge keys, node aliases/cycles on objects or arrays, and control or format characters [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-28].
- **Search Highlighting Bounds**: Browser search highlights use bounded regular expression walks with shared match budgets, case-folding, and Unicode normalization [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-28].

## CI Pipeline and Artifact Integrity
The repository execution pipeline enforces verification steps across pull requests [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-28]:
- Execution in Node 22 with pinned dependencies and disabled credential persistence (`persist-credentials: false`) [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-28].
- Automated validation via `node:test` covering schema limits and failure modes [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-28].
- Symlink containment verification (`scripts/check-no-symlinks.sh`), preventing `upload-pages-artifact` from dereferencing local runner files via committed symbolic links [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-28].

# References
- [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices
proposed_concept.description: Actionable security implementation guide detailing threat models, kernel-enforced sandboxing, in-hook policy decision points, and MITRE ATLAS / OWASP ASI controls.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Security Best Practices guide establishes vendor-neutral implementation controls, threat mitigations, and architectural safeguards for agentic systems across execution runtimes, tool boundaries, and authorization workflows.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-39] Developed by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), the guide maps concrete operational countermeasures against taxonomy attack vectors such as [tool poisoning](../taxonomy/tool-poisoning.md) and [rug pulls](../taxonomy/rug-pull.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-40]

The guide articulates explicit execution boundaries, clarifying that sandbox modes narrow the scope of exposure rather than providing absolute containment unless reinforced by kernel-level primitives.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-41] Furthermore, runtime authorizations are governed through a multi-stage policy decision point at the hook, preventing compromised or prompt-injected agents from labeling their own exfiltration operations as routine.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-39]

# Architecture / Specification

## Policy Decision Point at the Hook
Section 4 defines an authorization control architecture placing a Policy Decision Point (PDP) directly at the agent execution hook.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-39] The PDP intercepts the complete invocation payload—including the target tool, call arguments, and run context—and returns one of four decisions: `allow`, `deny`, `modify`, or `ask`.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-39] Keying decisions on full argument payloads ensures that destructive actions using common tools (e.g., shell executions or file deletions) are isolated from benign invocations.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-39]

Evaluation proceeds across three decoupled stages where the originating agent has no execution or modification path into any evaluation tier:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-39]
1. **Deterministic Rules Engine**: First-stage deterministic rules evaluate immutable constraints (such as immediate blocking of Tier 4 destructive destinations) prior to any hand-off.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-39]
2. **Automated Secondary Classifier**: Calls handed off by deterministic rules undergo evaluation by an independent classifier, model, or deterministic verification agent.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-39]
3. **Escalated Ask Path**: A human-in-the-loop approval gate is invoked solely when an `ask` verdict is rendered.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-39] This design counters approval fatigue, grounded by empirical findings where 97% of unsegmented prompts are reflexively approved by operators and only 13.6% of human reviewers detect planted hazardous commands without automated pre-filtering.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-39]

## Sandbox Confinement and Egress Boundaries
Section 3.2 specifies that sandbox execution modes narrow an unverified artifact's accessibility from the broader user account to an isolated working directory.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-41] However, logical sandboxes do not guarantee isolation against network egress or external host execution unless supported by kernel-enforced mechanisms:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-41]
- **Kernel Enforcement**: Full isolation requires kernel-enforced filesystem confinement, Linux namespaces, and syscall filtering (such as seccomp or [nono](../resources/nono.md)).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-41]
- **Egress Gaps**: Application-level proxies that restrict standard utilities (e.g., `curl`) can be bypassed if the agent leverages secondary runtimes or HTTP client libraries; egress filtering must be strictly enforced at the network proxy layer with allowlisting.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-41]
- **Host Component Escapes**: Sandboxes do not protect against attacks where the agent writes payloads to the filesystem that are subsequently executed by unconfined, trusted host processes outside the boundary.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-41]

## Framework Mappings: MITRE ATLAS and OWASP ASI
Clauses across tool implementation, input/output validation, and execution controls are tagged against industry threat frameworks:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-40]
- **MITRE ATLAS v5.6.0**: Key behaviors are aligned with ATLAS technique identifiers, including technique AML.T0109 (*AI Supply Chain Rug Pull*) applied to tool definition drift, hash verification, and silent package updates, alongside AML.T0110 and AML.T0051.001.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-40]
- **OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications 2026**: Clauses map directly to Agentic Security Issues (ASI codes such as ASI02 and ASI04), enforcing controls such as the Rule of Two and mitigations for the lethal trifecta (autonomous write access, untrusted inputs, and unauthenticated tools).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-40]

# Lifecycle History
The guide was initially drafted by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md). In October 2026, PR #39 restructured the Section 4 authorization framework behind an in-hook Policy Decision Point,[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-39] PR #40 introduced inline tagging against MITRE ATLAS v5.6.0 and OWASP ASI 2026,[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-40] and PR #41 refined Section 3.2 to detail the operational limits and kernel requirements of sandbox containment.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-41]

proposed_concept.title: Rug Pull
proposed_concept.description: Agent tool supply-chain attack where a previously verified tool definition, package, or endpoint is silently replaced with malicious behavior.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
A rug pull is an agentic supply-chain attack in which a previously verified, benign, or trusted tool definition, Model Context Protocol (MCP) package, or external API endpoint is silently modified or replaced with malicious logic post-admission.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-40] This threat exploits static or one-time [tool definition verification](../taxonomy/tool-definition-verification.md) by altering runtime behavior while retaining established trust tokens or namespace identifiers.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-40]

The attack is formally recognized in the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) best practices guide and mapped to the MITRE ATLAS matrix under technique AML.T0109 (*AI Supply Chain Rug Pull*).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-40]

# Architecture / Specification

## Attack Vectors and Mechanics
Rug pull attacks across agent ecosystems typically manifest across three primary surfaces:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-40]
- **Tool Definition Hash Drift**: The registered schema or manifest of a tool changes on the remote host without incrementing version identifiers or triggering re-attestation.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-40]
- **Silent Package Updates**: Dependencies, plugins, or MCP server packages introduce unauthorized capabilities or altered tool behaviors during downstream updates.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-40]
- **Dynamic Endpoint Redirection**: An agent tool's underlying routing configuration is redirected to an attacker-controlled endpoint that mimics the schema but captures sensitive execution context or delivers manipulated responses.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-40]

## Mitigations and Mapping
Mitigating rug pulls requires continuous verification of execution invariants rather than relying on one-time registration approvals:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-40]
- **Cryptographic Hash Invariants**: Binding tool definitions to immutable cryptographic digests and rejecting runtime executions where hash drift is observed.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-40]
- **In-Hook Policy Enforcement**: Intercepting invocations via policy decision points to verify runtime signatures and destination allowlists prior to execution.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-40]
- **Framework Alignment**: Categorized under MITRE ATLAS v5.6.0 as technique AML.T0109 (*AI Supply Chain Rug Pull*), and classified under OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications (ASI) supply-chain risk categories.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-40]

# Lifecycle History
Defined within the AAIF threat modeling and taxonomy landscape initiatives, the term was formally linked to MITRE ATLAS technique AML.T0109 during the 2026 update to the [Agentic AI Security Best Practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md) guide.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-40]

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Project Proposal Process
proposed_concept.description: Six-step operating procedure and review gate governing project proposal intake, engagement thresholds, voting, and onboarding into the Agentic AI Foundation.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The AAIF Project Proposal Process defines the operating procedure for submitting, reviewing, voting on, and onboarding open technical projects into the Agentic AI Foundation [^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-9c234333]. Governed by the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) in coordination with the Governing Board, the process operationalizes the admission criteria defined in the [Project Lifecycle Policy](project-lifecycle-policy.md) [^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-9c234333].

Submissions are managed publicly via issue forms in the `aaif/project-proposals` repository, which acts as the official application and tracking ledger [^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-3d9290b7]. Foundation membership is explicitly decoupled from project admission; non-member organizations may submit projects, and project acceptance confers neither commercial membership tiers nor Governing Board seats [^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-3d9290b7].

# Architecture / Specification

## Sequential Operating Steps

The evaluation lifecycle prioritizes asynchronous, offline review across six sequential stages plus parallel legal drafting [^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-9c234333]:

1. **Initial Intake (Step 1)**: The AAIF CTO, supported by an automated intake agent executing technical smoke tests, screens new submissions for scope, OSI-compliant permissive licensing, and completeness before alerting the Technical Committee chairs [^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-9c234333].
2. **TC Q&A Window (Step 2)**: An offline review window conducted via comments on the GitHub issue. To advance, proposals must satisfy an *engagement bar* requiring substantive interaction from multiple TC members rather than relying on a single project sponsor [^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-9c234333]. If the bar is unmet, TC chairs may appoint an on-demand TC supporter to champion the proposal; lack of engagement results in decline [^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-9c234333]. An optional live presentation may be scheduled upon request [^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-9c234333].
3. **Parallel Contributor Paperwork**: Linux Foundation PMO and Legal coordinate technical charters, contribution agreements, and trademark assignments in parallel with technical evaluations [^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-9c234333].
4. **TC Vote (Step 3)**: The Technical Committee evaluates admission and recommends an initial lifecycle stage (Sandbox, Growth, or Impact) via LFX Vote [^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-9c234333][^evt-project-proposals-file-6c7de919a622-15a00e3a].
5. **Governing Board Vote (Step 4)**: The Governing Board votes via LFX Vote to confirm organizational readiness, resource allocation, and stage entry [^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-9c234333].
6. **LF Legal Formation (Step 5)**: Final execution of contribution agreements, trademark transfers, and technical charters via DocuSign [^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-9c234333].
7. **Technical Onboarding (Step 6)**: LF IT and PMO transfer repository ownership, configure CI/CD credentials, and establish project infrastructure [^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-9c234333].

## Repository Tracking Labels

Issue tracking in `aaif/project-proposals` reflects candidate status via five canonical labels: `New`, `Approved`, `Declined`, `Waiting on Comment`, and `Too Early` [^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-3d9290b7]. Projects must satisfy all legal and governance criteria before publicly representing themselves as accepted or foundation-hosted [^evt-project-proposals-file-6c7de919a622-15a00e3a].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-08-28**: Operating procedure version v0.3 enacted, formalizing the offline engagement bar and automated intake mechanics [^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-9c234333].

proposed_concept.description: Governing technical body of the Agentic AI Foundation overseeing project lifecycles, working group charters, and architectural alignment across hosted technologies.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Technical Committee (TC) is the primary technical governing body of the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF), established as a directed fund of The Linux Foundation [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-b0f27f04]. The TC assists the Governing Board by reviewing new project proposals, recommending projects aligned with foundation scope, establishing and archiving working groups, and implementing the [Project Lifecycle Policy](../policies/project-lifecycle-policy.md) [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-b0f27f04].

TC operations focus on asynchronous consensus, distributed review, and cross-project collaboration, operating under a formal Charter adopted on March 3, 2026 [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-b0f27f04].

# Architecture / Specification

## Composition and Officers

- **Representation**: Each Platinum Member of the AAIF is entitled to appoint one representative to the Technical Committee [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-b0f27f04].
- **Leadership**: The TC elects a Chair and optional Co-Chair annually to preside over meetings and administrative workflows [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-b0f27f04].

## Governance Responsibilities

The TC executes core operational mandates across foundation activities [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-b0f27f04]:

1. Establishing, managing, and archiving technical [Working Groups](../policies/working-group-lifecycle-policy.md).
2. Coordinating cross-project technical priorities, interoperability standards, and technical vision.
3. Evaluating candidate submissions via the [Project Proposal Process](../policies/project-proposal-process.md) and recommending admissions to the Governing Board.
4. Administering stage progression (Sandbox, Growth, Impact, Emeritus) and conducting annual project reviews.
5. Recommending foundation resource allocations to the Governing Board.

## Voting and Consensus Mechanics

- **Consensus Principle**: The TC operates on a consensus-first basis, utilizing *lazy consensus* (a 7-day silence-as-agreement model) where proposals pass automatically if no voting member records a formal objection [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-b0f27f04].
- **Formal Voting**: When consensus cannot be reached, decisions require a one-vote-per-representative electronic ballot requiring a majority of all voting members [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-b0f27f04].
- **Quorum**: Live decision-making meetings require at least 50% voting member attendance to establish quorum [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-b0f27f04].
- **Escalation**: Unresolved deadlocks may be referred to the Governing Board for final resolution [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-b0f27f04].
- **Charter Amendments**: Require approval by a two-thirds majority of the TC and subsequent Governing Board ratification [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-b0f27f04].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-03-03**: Formal Charter adopted establishing TC purpose, voting rules, and working group oversight [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-b0f27f04].

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Project Lifecycle Policy
proposed_concept.description: Governance policy defining admission criteria, stage progressions across Sandbox, Growth, and Impact, and annual review procedures for AAIF technical projects.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The AAIF Project Lifecycle Policy provides the formal framework through which open technical projects join, advance within, and retire from the Agentic AI Foundation [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-04c1d0b2]. Enforced by the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md), the policy establishes objective expectations, resource support, and governance alignment across distinct maturity stages [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-04c1d0b2].

Intake into the lifecycle is governed by the [Project Proposal Process](project-proposal-process.md), requiring public documentation of OSI permissive licensing, code repositories, release practices, automated validation, and leadership governance [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-04c1d0b2][^evt-project-proposals-file-6c7de919a622-15a00e3a].

# Architecture / Specification

## Lifecycle Stages

The policy organizes projects into four distinct tiers [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-04c1d0b2]:

- **Sandbox Stage**: Entry-level stage intended for nascent, experimental, or emerging projects. Focuses on fostering initial adoption, contributor growth, and alignment with AAIF architectural standards [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-04c1d0b2].
- **Growth Stage**: Intermediate tier for projects demonstrating sustained development velocity, broadening multi-organization contributor bases, and verified production deployments [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-04c1d0b2].
- **Impact Stage**: Climax maturity stage for mission-critical, industry-standard technologies demonstrating widespread multi-vendor adoption, rigorous open governance, and deep cross-project integration [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-04c1d0b2].
- **Emeritus Stage**: End-of-life classification for projects that have completed their active utility, transitioned to alternative homes, or ceased maintenance, preserving historical artifacts under Linux Foundation stewardship [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-04c1d0b2].

## Annual Review

All admitted projects undergo a mandatory Annual Review conducted by the TC to evaluate ongoing community health, governance compliance, milestone completion, and eligibility for stage graduation or retirement [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-04c1d0b2].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-03-18**: Policy established under initial foundation charter [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-04c1d0b2].
- **2026-10-15**: Policy updated to align with automated intake procedures and revised proposal criteria [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-04c1d0b2].

proposed_concept.description: Progressively disclosed agent skill converting LFX meeting recordings, transcripts, and AI summaries into standardized, evidence-cited working group minutes.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The AAIF Working Group Meeting Notes Generator is an operational agent skill designed to ingest raw LFX meeting recordings, transcripts, and AI summaries to produce standardized working group minutes [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-63]. The generator enforces consistent recording of decisions, action item ownership, and factual verification grounded in meeting evidence [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-63].

Minutes generation follows the reporting standards defined in the [Taxonomy and Landscape Meeting Notes Guidelines](../guidelines/taxonomy-landscape-meeting-notes.md) while maintaining human editorial approval prior to pull request submission [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-63].

# Architecture / Specification

## Toolkit and Integration Layer

The skill leverages a modular Python CLI and tool suite providing [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-63]:

- **LFX MCP Integration**: Connectors interfacing with the Linux Foundation LFX Model Context Protocol endpoints to extract committee metadata, schedules, and raw audio transcripts [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-63].
- **Transcript and Summary Synthesis**: Date-driven processing pipeline that cross-correlates automated LFX summaries against raw speech-to-text transcripts to verify claim accuracy [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-63].
- **Evidence Grounding**: Heuristics ensuring action items and recorded consensus decisions cite corresponding timestamped evidence from meeting dialog [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-63].
- **Credential Isolation and Portability**: Managed under `uv` virtual environments, designed to transition generic components to the shared `working-groups-chair` repository while preserving WG-specific meeting configurations locally [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-63].

## Governance Invariants

Generated output is strictly advisory; human chair review is required before publishing minutes to GitHub repositories, ensuring automated summaries cannot misrepresent working group consensus [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-63].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-03**: Initial implementation proposed in [Observability and Traceability WG](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) PR #63 as a reusable cross-WG date-driven minutes tool [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-63].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Technical Committee (TC) is the governing technical body of the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF), responsible for steering technical vision, ratifying standards, and overseeing project and working group lifecycles across the Foundation[^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-8f2953e0]. Operating under the Technical Charter, the TC provides architectural oversight, manages project stage progressions, and approves working group charters[^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-8f2953e0].

# Architecture / Specification

## Governance Authority and Policies
The Technical Committee maintains and enforces the authoritative technical governance documents of the AAIF[^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-8f2953e0]:
- **Technical Charter**: Defines TC composition, voting mechanics, quorum requirements, and delegated technical powers.
- **[Project Lifecycle Policy](../policies/project-lifecycle-policy.md)**: Governs project admission, review cadences, and stage transitions across Sandbox, Growth, and Impact.
- **[Project Proposal Process](../policies/project-proposal-process.md)**: Standardizes intake workflows, legal paperwork, technical evaluation, and onboarding for prospective Foundation projects.
- **[Working Group Lifecycle Policy](../policies/working-group-lifecycle-policy.md)**: Defines working group intake, Sandbox charter drafting, annual review, and retirement.
- **[Working Group Reporting Template](../guidelines/working-group-reporting-template.md)**: Standardizes monthly progress tracking and KPI disclosures submitted to the TC.

## Composition and Term
All founding TC members were appointed by the AAIF Governing Board for an initial term running from March 1, 2026 through December 31, 2026[^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-8f2953e0]:
- **David Soria Parra** (Chair) — Anthropic
- **Caitie McCaffrey** (Co-Chair) — Microsoft
- **Alan Blount** — Google
- **Bradley Axen** — Block
- **James Ward** — Amazon Web Services
- **Nick Cooper** — OpenAI
- **Sambhav Kothari** — Bloomberg
- **Steve Faulkner** — Cloudflare

## Hosted Projects
The TC evaluates and oversees Foundation projects through graduated lifecycle tiers. As of the 2026 term, the Foundation hosts flagship efforts at the Impact Stage[^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-8f2953e0]:
- **Model Context Protocol (MCP)**: Open protocol enabling integration between language model applications and external data sources or tools.
- **goose**: Open-source, extensible agent runtime executing, editing, and testing code with heterogeneous model providers (see [goose reference architecture](../resources/goose.md)).

proposed_concept.title: Working Group Submission Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Operational guidelines governing working group proposal intake, membership tier eligibility restrictions, issue tracking labels, and Sandbox progression.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Working Group Submission Guidelines provide practical instructions for proposing a new Working Group (WG) or reviving a Concluded WG under the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF)[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-a2eb51a2]. The guide complements the authoritative [Working Group Lifecycle Policy](../policies/working-group-lifecycle-policy.md) and [Working Group Reporting Template](../guidelines/working-group-reporting-template.md), defining intake workflows through GitHub issue forms and project tracking boards[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-6c29ea3b].

# Architecture / Specification

## Eligibility Requirements
Proposals and leadership roles adhere to distinct membership prerequisites[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-a2eb51a2]:
- **Proposal Submission**: Proposers must belong to an AAIF member organization in good standing (Platinum, Gold, Silver, or Associate). Non-member contributors may partner with an AAIF member organization to sponsor and submit the proposal[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-a2eb51a2].
- **Chair Eligibility**: Working group chairs must represent Platinum, Gold, or Silver member organizations. The submitter is not required to serve as chair[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-a2eb51a2].
- **Participation**: Working group meetings and technical contributions are open to all community members regardless of Foundation membership[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-a2eb51a2].

## Proposal Submission and Review Process
1. **Scope Assessment**: Proposers must verify that the proposed domain represents an enduring, multi-year challenge rather than a time-boxed deliverable suited for an existing WG workstream[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-a2eb51a2].
2. **Issue Application**: The submitter opens a Working Group Proposal issue via the standardized template in `aaif/working-group-proposals`[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-87b3376703c5-313cc435].
3. **Staff Triage and Asynchronous Review**: AAIF staff verify completeness before the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) conducts an asynchronous review on the issue thread[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-6c29ea3b].
4. **Approval Gate**: Approval requires consensus from both the Technical Committee and the Governing Board. Once approved, the WG enters the Sandbox stage[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-6c29ea3b].
5. **Sandbox Chartering**: Approval of a proposal places the WG into Sandbox to start meetings, institute monthly reporting, and draft a formal charter; Active status is granted only after TC ratification of that completed charter[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-6c29ea3b].

## Tracking Status Labels
Proposal progress is tracked on the Working Group Proposals Board using explicit labels[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-6c29ea3b]:
- `New`: The proposal is placed in the review backlog.
- `Approved`: Received required TC and Governing Board approvals; enters Sandbox.
- `Declined`: Proposal rejected with documented feedback in issue comments.
- `Waiting on Comment`: Clarification or supplemental data requested from submitters.
- `Too Early`: Premature proposal requiring further maturation prior to reapplication.

## Revival of Concluded Working Groups
Proposals seeking to revive a Concluded working group must reference the historical repository and prior charter while explicitly describing changes in ecosystem landscape, leadership commitments, and renewed problem relevance[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-a2eb51a2].
