proposed_concept.title: Accuracy and Reliability Survey
proposed_concept.description: Platform-neutral 16-question survey instrument evaluating real-world AI system deployments, failure modes, error recovery, and accuracy constraints.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Accuracy and Reliability Survey is an empirical, platform-neutral instrument developed by the [Accuracy and Reliability Working Group](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md) to gather cross-industry data on operational AI failures, testing methodologies, and reliability blockers[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-14]. The survey captures quantitative and qualitative metrics across real-world agent deployments without harvesting proprietary or identifying information[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-14].

# Architecture / Specification

## Instrument Structure and Question Ordering
The 16-question survey assesses production AI systems across distinct evaluation domains[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-14]:
- **Demographics and Architecture (Q1–Q4)**: System maturity, organizational footprint, and foundational architecture.
- **Operational Oversight and Benefits (Q5–Q8)**: Human checking touchpoints, organizational scale, realized benefits, and core operational constraints[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-14].
- **Failure Taxonomy and Reliability Factors (Q9–Q16)**: Specific failure rates, quality degradations, error recovery limitations, and cross-industry remediation priorities[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-14].

## Accuracy and Reliability Factors (Q10)
Question 10 evaluates observed deployment degradation factors, incorporating failure dimensions addressing system evolution and operational resilience[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-14]:
- **Post-Change Quality Decline**: Degradation triggered by modifications to underlying models, prompts, tool definitions, or harness software versions[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-14].
- **Unsafe Error Recovery**: Failures where the agent fails to recover cleanly after runtime errors, leaving behind partial tool mutations, corrupted state, or uncommitted execution fragments[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-14].

## Consent and Data Governance Protocol
The intake protocol enforces strict data hygiene[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-14]:
- **Anonymity**: No personal names or contact details are collected.
- **Reporting**: Responses are synthesized and published solely in aggregated benchmarking reports.
- **Administration**: Stored and governed by AAIF with administrative oversight coordinated via Foundation support channels[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-14].

proposed_concept.title: Continuous Assurance
proposed_concept.description: Ongoing automated or semi-automated verification evaluating an agent system against an approved specification throughout its operational lifecycle.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Continuous assurance is an ongoing evaluation process that verifies an AI agent or multi-agent system against an approved specification across its runtime lifecycle[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-92]. Unlike point-in-time conformance testing, continuous assurance monitors operational drift, boundary adherence, and behavioral compliance as models, tools, and execution environments evolve[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-92].

# Architecture / Specification

## Scope and Core Principles
Continuous assurance establishes persistent operational oversight using neutral verification standards[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-92]:
- **Approved Specification Alignment**: Conformance is assessed against explicit, ratified specifications rather than proprietary blueprints or ad-hoc behavioral heuristics[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-92].
- **Lifecycle Integration**: Spans pre-deployment validation, runtime telemetry auditing, and post-execution attestation reconciliation (see [attested isolated runtime](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md) and [three-state reconciliation](../taxonomy/three-state-reconciliation.md)).
- **Drift Detection**: Identifies performance degradation, prompt or tool definition drift, and unauthorized capability expansion before catastrophic failures occur[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-92].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Registry
proposed_concept.description: Centralized or federated directory storing validated identities, metadata, capabilities, and governance policies for discoverable AI agents.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
An agent registry is an indexed catalog and discovery service that stores validated agent identities, capability definitions, endpoint metadata, and operational governance constraints[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-92]. Registries enable runtime discovery, access control, and policy enforcement across heterogeneous agent-to-agent and client-to-agent architectures[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-92].

# Architecture / Specification

## Core Capabilities
Agent registries maintain machine-readable records facilitating secure inter-agent coordination[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-92]:
- **Identity and Metadata Management**: Catalogs verifiable credentials, public keys, and cryptographic attestations for registered agents (see [Identity and Trust WG](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md)).
- **Capability Discovery**: Exposes discoverable skills, supported protocol bindings, and tool definitions for autonomous or human-mediated delegation (see [Agentic Resource Discovery](../standards/agentic-resource-discovery.md)).
- **Policy Enforcement**: Integrates with runtime boundary gateways and mediation proxies to verify admission criteria and regulatory constraints prior to session establishment (see [AgentGateway](../resources/agentgateway.md) and [Context Forge](../resources/context-forge.md)).

proposed_concept.title: Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group bridging global AI policy developments and technical agentic systems, tracking regulatory gap analyses, legal context schemas, and operational governance.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Working Group (WG Government, Risk & Regulatory Alignment) aligns technical agentic AI architectures with evolving international legal frameworks, regional AI governance instruments, and corporate risk policies [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-60f28464dd94-576a1dc7]. The group translates regulatory requirements into actionable engineering guidance, policy schemas, and technical compliance baselines for autonomous agent deployments.

The working group is co-chaired by Deborah Eng (JPMorgan Chase) and Sriram Natarajan (Google) [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-60f28464dd94-576a1dc7].

# Workstreams and Deliverables

- **Regional Regulatory Gap Analysis (Phase 2):** Evaluates regional and international agentic AI regulatory instruments against a standardized 16-theme governance baseline [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-60f28464dd94-576a1dc7]. Standardized prompt-driven evaluation methods ensure uniform comparative rigor across contributor jurisdictions.
- **Operationalizing Agent Governance:** A cross-cutting framework defining concrete engineering patterns for runtime agent oversight, alignment verification, and lifecycle supervision, submitted to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) for consortium-wide alignment [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-60f28464dd94-576a1dc7].
- **Legal Context Schema:** A structured schema standardizing machine-readable legal constraints, contractual boundaries, and regulatory parameters ingested by agent execution engines [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-60f28464dd94-576a1dc7].
- **Agentic Evidence Collection Best Practice Guide:** Standardized guidelines for capturing audit-grade telemetry, authorization records, and forensic execution traces in compliance with regulatory oversight standards [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-60f28464dd94-576a1dc7].

# Lifecycle History

Following a leadership transition in autumn 2026, Deborah Eng assumed the role of Chair, and Sriram Natarajan was selected as Vice-Chair/Co-Chair to expand operational bandwidth across delivery milestones [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-60f28464dd94-576a1dc7].

proposed_concept.title: Identity and Trust Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group defining vendor-neutral standards, reference architectures, delegation frameworks, and verification test suites for agentic identity and credentials.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Identity and Trust Working Group establishes vendor-neutral standards, verifiable credential profiles, and cryptographic trust frameworks for autonomous agent systems. Its remit covers agent identity establishment, fine-grained delegation trees, authorization proofs, and interoperable revocation mechanisms across heterogeneous runtime boundaries.

# Workstreams and Deliverables

- **Delegation Lifecycle and Evidence Vectors:** Development of standardized test suites and test vectors verifying delegation trees, revocation enforcement, and cryptographic evidence validity [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-18][^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-20].
- **Disputed Revocation across Delegation Trees:** Test profiles evaluating edge cases where parent delegation keys are revoked while descendant subagent delegations remain actively presented [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-18].
- **Identifier Re-registration and Artifact Binding:** Validation cases linking prior agent execution records and public keys to newly issued identifiers without breaking provenance chains [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-18].
- **Recovery after Compromised Keys:** Standardized recovery record rules signed jointly by registries and responsible entities, matched against software attestations to ensure revocation history persists across key transitions while barring retroactive authority or unauthorized regrants [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-20].

# Cross-Group Alignment

The group collaborates with the [Attestation and Evidence Working Group](../working-groups/attestation-and-evidence.md) and [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) on hardware-attested trust anchors and execution token binding.

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing vendor-neutral agent telemetry standards, cross-boundary trace models, and evaluation publication criteria for agent execution harnesses.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability and Traceability Working Group standardizes vendor-neutral telemetry specifications, distributed context propagation mechanisms, and causal trace representations for agentic AI workloads. The group addresses the observability gap between LLM inference invocations, agent harness loops, tool protocols, and operating system events.

# Workstreams and Deliverables

- **Agent Behavior Trace Model:** Open telemetry and correlation specification capturing causal agent execution, tool invocations, and memory updates while driving upstream OpenTelemetry semantic conventions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-66].
- **Approval Evidence and Bounded Work:** Integration of durable authorization records and bounded execution constraints into runtime trace representations [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-66].
- **Auditable Harness Evaluation Standards:** Scoping criteria for what evidence harnesses must publish to make evaluation claims verifiable and falsifiable by independent third parties [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-66]. The proposed properties include commitment before observation, coverage identity, pinned trust roots, separation of observation and judgment, typed outcomes treating model refusals as first-class, measurement of benign cost, adversarial maintenance, and explicit temporal bounds on approval and withdrawal [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-66].

# Cross-Group Alignment

The working group aligns with the [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) on workflow checkpoint telemetry and the [Attestation and Evidence Working Group](../working-groups/attestation-and-evidence.md) on cryptographic evidence verification.

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing vendor-neutral agent telemetry standards, cross-boundary trace models, and execution provenance specifications.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability and Traceability Working Group (WG O&T) defines vendor-neutral standards, semantic conventions, and integration architectures for capturing telemetry across agent execution boundaries.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-60f28464dd94-2a91d869] Co-chaired by Pavan Sudheendra (Cisco) and Matthew Lee (Datadog), the group establishes instrumentation specifications covering client-to-agent interactions, tool execution, model inference, and cross-boundary protocol handoffs.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-60f28464dd94-2a91d869]

The working group addresses gaps in traditional distributed tracing by standardizing causal relationship capture, human-in-the-loop decisions, and non-deterministic agent workflows across heterogeneous runtimes.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-60f28464dd94-2a91d869]

# Architecture / Specification

The working group organizes its technical output into several active focus tracks and deliverables:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-60f28464dd94-2a91d869]

- **Agent Behavior Trace Model:** An evidence-driven specification targeting OpenTelemetry semantic conventions, using [Goose](../resources/goose.md) as the primary reference implementation to capture trace continuity, retries, approval checkpoints, and operational effects.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-60f28464dd94-2a91d869]
- **Cross-Boundary Observability:** Systematic matrix analyses mapping span propagation, W3C Trace Context, Baggage, security scopes, and timing across critical agent seams, including the [Agent-to-Tool CLI Boundary](../resources/agent-tool-cli-boundary.md) and Agent-to-MCP links.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-60f28464dd94-2a91d869]
- **LLM Primitives & Protocols:** Focus area covering upstream protocol alignment, including lifecycle observability proposals for [Agentic Resource Discovery](../standards/agentic-resource-discovery.md) (ARD) and low-level execution provenance.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-60f28464dd94-2a91d869]
- **State, Context & Reasoning:** Focus group examining agent state-space representation, task topology observability, and harness-independent state inference layers.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-60f28464dd94-2a91d869]
- **Taxonomy Alignment:** Contributing foundational observability definitions—including Reasoning, Agent Trajectory, Context Propagation, Context Assembly, Memory Access, Retrieval, and Traceability—into the shared [Taxonomy and Landscape](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) catalog.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-60f28464dd94-2a91d869]

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-07:** Published initial Working Methods & Process, Prior Work Survey, and Use Case Inventory as living documents.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-60f28464dd94-2a91d869]
- **2026-09:** Merged seven core O&T terms into the shared taxonomy; published the Agent-to-Tool CLI boundary analysis; merged the [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md) execution plan; adopted Goose as the reference capture implementation; submitted an upstream ARD lifecycle-observability proposal; established a monthly APAC/APJ synchronization meeting.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-60f28464dd94-2a91d869]

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Open telemetry and correlation framework capturing causal agent execution, tool invocations, and approval decisions, driving upstream OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agent Behavior Trace Model is a standardized telemetry framework developed by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) to capture causal relationships, decision state transitions, tool invocations, and human-in-the-loop approvals across autonomous agent execution cycles.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-60f28464dd94-2a91d869]

The standard addresses wide disparities in existing [OpenTelemetry](../resources/opentelemetry.md) GenAI instrumentation by shifting from speculative schema drafting to an evidence-first approach derived from real-world agent runtimes.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-60f28464dd94-2a91d869]

# Architecture / Specification

The specification structures telemetry around four core execution questions:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-60f28464dd94-2a91d869]

1. **Continuity:** Unifying hierarchical session spans, conversational threads, and asynchronous subagent spawning under deterministic causal context.
2. **Calls and Retries:** Capturing model queries, tool delegations, network failures, retry loops, and parameter backoffs with standardized semantic attributes.
3. **Approvals:** Formally recording human and policy gating actions, approval checkpoints, rejections, and authority escalation tokens directly in span attributes.
4. **Effects:** Tracing persistent state modifications, file system mutations, external API side effects, and rollback states back to the originating prompt and planning step.

To bridge the gap between specification and ecosystem adoption, [Goose](../resources/goose.md) serves as the primary reference implementation.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-60f28464dd94-2a91d869] The trace model analyzes spans emitted by Goose's native OpenTelemetry integration, catalogs deficiencies against the core execution questions, and feeds proposed extensions upstream into OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-60f28464dd94-2a91d869]

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-09:** The working group merged the execution plan for the trace model and opened eight tracking workstreams covering shared contracts, baselines, reference implementations, and upstream PRs.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-60f28464dd94-2a91d869] The WG pivoted to an evidence-first roadmap anchored on Goose capture data after identifying widespread inconsistencies in commercial coding agent OpenTelemetry emissions.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-60f28464dd94-2a91d869]

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing open threat models, security best practices, design patterns, and attestation standards for agentic AI systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group establishes security and privacy as a shared discipline across the Agentic AI Foundation ecosystem.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-2c5c574e] It produces open threat models, security best-practice guidelines, taxonomy terms, and architectural design patterns that providers and consumers can adopt to build trustworthy agentic systems.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-2c5c574e]

The working group is chaired by Alex Frazer (Runlayer) and co-chaired by Junjie Bu (Google), with an elected term running from March 1, 2026 through January 31, 2027.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-2c5c574e] The group holds alternating biweekly primary meetings (Tuesdays at 10:00 AM PT) and Asia-Pacific working sessions (Mondays at 9:00 PM ET).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-2c5c574e][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a5dc3314]

# Architecture / Specification

The working group coordinates several core deliverable streams:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a5dc3314]

- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices:** An implementation guide addressing threat modeling, execution sandboxing, tool verification, and credential protection, developed under lead Fernando and open to external contributions.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a5dc3314]
- **Threat Modeling & Gap Analysis:** Comprehensive assessments evaluating existing security frameworks (such as OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, and NIST AI RMF) against agentic vectors like tool poisoning and memory manipulation.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a5dc3314]
- **Design Patterns Catalog:** Formal architectural patterns governing runtime security, including [Approval Checkpoint](../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md), [Attested Isolated Runtime](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md), and [Kill Switch](../patterns/kill-switch.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a5dc3314]
- **Attestation & Hardware-Rooted Trust:** Initiatives exploring Merkle tree action attestation (such as Agent Action Capsules and CIGAR) and standardized agent identity kill-switch protocols aligned with OpenID CAEP and Shared Signals.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a5dc3314]
- **Security & Privacy Taxonomy:** Drafting and contributing standardized definitions for agent security primitives into the shared cross-WG taxonomy.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a5dc3314]

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-03:** Working group convened under elected Chair Alex Frazer; adopted mission statement and charter priorities.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a5dc3314]
- **2026-05:** Charter formally approved; Junjie Bu confirmed as co-chair; established cross-WG collaboration on taxonomy.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a5dc3314]
- **2026-09:** Best Practices Guide merged via PR #9; APAC biweekly meeting established.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a5dc3314]
- **2026-10:** Multiple security design patterns merged to catalog; initial batch of security taxonomy terms merged; proposed 90-day attestation pilot to AAIF leadership.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a5dc3314]

proposed_concept.title: ToolSurface
proposed_concept.description: Normative schema, static safety predicates, and rule-based conformance suite standardizing safe, unpoisoned Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool descriptions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

ToolSurface is an open specification that governs the safety of the `description` field in Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool registrations.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-64] While the Model Context Protocol specifies tool invocation transport and JSON Schema validation for tool inputs, it does not constrain the free-text description block where prompt-injection, secondary coercion, and tool-poisoning payloads typically reside.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-64]

ToolSurface defines a canonical schema and static validation rules that prevent tool authors or compromised MCP endpoints from embedding imperative system instructions into tool descriptions without altering the underlying MCP wire protocol.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-64]

# Architecture / Specification

ToolSurface introduces three primary components to enforce description safety:[^evt-project-proposals-issue-64]

- **Normative Description Schema:** Replaces unconstrained prose with a structured JSON object containing five defined fields: a required `purpose`, alongside optional `params`, `returns`, `side_effects`, and `examples` fields. Any free-text directives outside these keys violate conformance.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-64]
- **Static Safety Predicates:** A deterministic, dependency-free validation rule set that rejects descriptions containing cross-tool imperatives (e.g., ordering an agent to call another tool), embedded credentials, system paths, or security-justification coercion phrases.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-64]
- **Rule-Scored Conformance Suite:** A third-party test framework that verifies implementations against frozen corpora (derived from ToolSieve and the 367-instance MCPTox benchmark subset). Conformance is established without an LLM judge by computing attack success rates (ASR) and utility-completion scores under Wilson 95% confidence intervals.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-64]

ToolSurface provides a Python reference implementation containing `canonicalise(description)` and `validate(description)` routines for integration into tool registries, gateways, and agent runtimes.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-64]

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-10:** Developed as an open specification originating from the ToolSieve research project and MCPTox benchmark.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-64]
- **2026-10:** Submitted as an AAIF Sandbox project proposal licensed under the Community Specification License 1.0.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-64]

proposed_concept.title: kdeps
proposed_concept.description: Open-source AI appliance builder packaging declarative YAML agent workflows into containers, Kubernetes deployments, or standalone binaries with built-in MCP client support.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

kdeps is an open-source AI appliance builder written in Go that compiles declarative YAML agent and workflow definitions into deployable artifacts such as Docker container images, Kubernetes manifests, or standalone binaries.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-65] Maintained under an Apache-2.0 license, the project enables reproducible agent packaging and execution across local runtimes (such as Ollama and llamafile) and remote cloud foundation models via langchaingo.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-65]

In March 2025, kdeps was submitted to the Agentic AI Foundation as a proposed [Sandbox](../policies/project-lifecycle-policy.md) project under the foundation's [project proposal process](../policies/project-proposal-process.md).[^evt-project-proposals-issue-65]

# Architecture and Capabilities

kdeps structures agent systems around a declarative `workflow.yaml` schema, generating portable deployment units tailored for both cloud and air-gapped enterprise environments:[^evt-project-proposals-issue-65]

- **Appliance Packaging**: Produces immutable execution units packaged as container images, Kubernetes deployments, or Go binaries with integrated local model runners.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-65]
- **Protocol Integration**: Ships an integrated Model Context Protocol (MCP) client (`pkg/tools/mcp`) for external tool invocation, with planned extensions for server mode.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-65]
- **Instruction Ingestion**: Collects context and agent configuration from repository root instruction files including `AGENTS.md`, `KDEPS.md`, and platform-specific manifests.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-65]
- **Air-Gapped Operation**: Designed to execute in restricted network environments without mandatory cloud dependencies, supporting private infrastructure deployments.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-65]

mutations.rationale: Introduces the universal taxonomy term Identity aligned with ISO/IEC 24760-1 as proposed in the Taxonomy and Landscape workstream.

proposed_concept.title: Identity
proposed_concept.description: Universal taxonomy term defining a set of attributes related to an entity across agentic authentication, delegation, and discovery.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Identity is a universal taxonomy term defined within the [Taxonomy and Landscape](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) and [Identity and Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) workstreams as a set of attributes related to an entity.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-97] The definition reproduces normative phrasing from ISO/IEC 24760-1 across its 2011, 2019, and 2025 editions to align foundation terminology with international identity management standards.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-97]

# Scope and Disambiguation

- **Non-Uniqueness**: An entity may possess multiple distinct identities depending on operational context, role, or administrative domain.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-97]
- **Identity versus Identifier**: An identity represents the attribute set describing an entity, whereas an identifier is a specific attribute or token used to uniquely reference or address that entity within a particular scope.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-97]

mutations.rationale: Defines the universal taxonomy term Principal designating the entity on whose authority an agent executes actions.

proposed_concept.title: Principal
proposed_concept.description: Universal taxonomy term designating an entity on whose behalf an agent acts or executes actions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Principal is a universal taxonomy term defined by the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) designating the legal, organizational, or human entity on whose authority and behalf an artificial agent executes actions.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-94]

# Scope and Conventions

Under the AAIF taxonomy, every agentic action is associated with at least one principal and may bind to multiple principals across delegated workflows.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-94] The working group explicitly discourages ambiguous or contradictory terminology such as "principal agent" in favor of distinct designations for the authorizing entity (the principal) and the executing software entity (the agent).[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-94]

mutations.rationale: Defines the universal taxonomy term Capability covering declared agent abilities and registry discovery matching.

proposed_concept.title: Capability
proposed_concept.description: Universal taxonomy term defining a declared ability or function of an agent asserted in an identity record and matched during discovery.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Capability is a universal taxonomy term established by the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) designating an explicit ability, operation, or functional skill declared by an agent.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-93]

# Scope and Usage

In agentic architectures, capabilities are asserted within an agent's [identity](../taxonomy/identity.md) or descriptor record and evaluated by orchestrators and registries during [resource discovery](../standards/agentic-resource-discovery.md) to match delegated tasks to appropriate agent runtimes.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-93]

mutations.rationale: Defines the universal taxonomy term Agent self-disclosure covering explicit automated identification in external interactions.

proposed_concept.title: Agent Self-Disclosure
proposed_concept.description: Universal taxonomy term defining an agent's explicit identification of its artificial nature during interaction with external systems or users.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Agent self-disclosure is a universal taxonomy term defined by the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) specifying the mechanism or act whereby an artificial agent explicitly identifies its automated, non-human nature to external counterparties.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-95]

# Scope and Application

Self-disclosure applies whenever an agent engages in external interactions, such as completing an online form or negotiating with third-party web services, establishing transparency regarding artificial agency and operational origin.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-95]

mutations.rationale: Defines the universal taxonomy term User and disambiguates interface interaction from agent principal direction.

proposed_concept.title: User
proposed_concept.description: Universal taxonomy term distinguishing human or client counterparties interacting with interfaces from the operators directing agent execution.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

User is a universal taxonomy term defined by the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) designating an individual or client entity interacting with a system or interface.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-96]

# Scope and Disambiguation

The taxonomy clarifies the boundary between different user contexts in agentic systems, distinguishing between the user interacting with an online surface (such as a web form or service) and the user acting as an agent's [principal](../taxonomy/principal.md) directing or configuring agent behavior.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-96]

mutations.rationale: Draft profile v0.3 submitted to the Security and Privacy WG specifies administrative control surfaces, external authorization checkpoints, and delegation mechanics for agentic harnesses.

proposed_concept.title: Control Surfaces for Agentic Harnesses Profile
proposed_concept.description: Standardized profile defining harness lifecycle events, external authorization checkpoints, and delegation controls using OpenID AuthZEN and OCSF.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Control Surfaces for Agentic Harnesses profile defines an interoperable administrative contract that AI agent harnesses expose to enterprise administrators, standardizing lifecycle event telemetry and external authorization checkpoints.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-44] Authored under the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), the profile bridges operational guidelines in the [Agentic AI Security Best Practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md) with implementation-independent design patterns into a concrete protocol implemented by clients and policy services.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-44]

# Architecture / Specification

The profile composes several existing open standards into an integrated control plane architecture:

- **Policy Enforcement and Checkpoints:** Utilizes OpenID AuthZEN for external policy decision point (PDP) discovery and evaluation at designated execution checkpoints, implementing concrete decision binding and record tracking for the [Approval Checkpoint](../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md) pattern.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-44]
- **Event Hooks and Audit Trail:** Adopts portable hook nomenclature from [Agent Plugins](../standards/agent-plugins.md) and formats lifecycle audit telemetry using Open Cybersecurity Schema Framework (OCSF) event classes.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-44]
- **Delegation and Scope Narrowing:** Employs OAuth token exchange to enforce an asserted invocation chain with server-issued root authority, monotonic privilege narrowing across subagents, and capability-scoped tool invocation tokens.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-44]
- **Memory and Data Provenance:** Mandates session-wide integrity and provenance labels (such as `untrusted` and `sensitive`), enabling policy decision points to enforce session-level boundary rules (such as egress restrictions across untrusted contexts).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-44]

# Cross-Working Group Dependencies

The specification spans multiple working group charters and ongoing standardization efforts:

- **Delegation Architecture:** Invocation chains and principal assertions align with delegation frameworks led by the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-44]
- **Activity Schemas:** Lifecycle event logging coordinates with the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) and upstream OCSF AI Agent Activity classifications.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-44]
- **Pattern Reconciliation:** The profile introduces design reconciliations with catalog patterns, specifically regarding clock skew assumptions in approval checkpoints, stateless PDP handling versus shared action identifiers in the [Attested Isolated Runtime](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md), and separating session-binding revocation from downstream credential identity providers in the [Kill Switch](../patterns/kill-switch.md) pattern.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-44]

mutations.rationale: Incorporate reconciliation requirements from the Control Surfaces for Agentic Harnesses profile addressing clock skew tolerance, argument minimization digest comparison, and failure mode mapping.

proposed_concept.title: Approval Checkpoint
proposed_concept.description: Runtime governance pattern binding approval records to exact execution payloads and tracking decision validity across enforcement boundaries.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Approval Checkpoint pattern binds authorization decisions to exact action payloads, cryptographic hashes, and execution contexts before an agent is permitted to invoke tools or execute state-changing operations.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-44] It operates as a runtime verification gate ensuring that signed approval records correspond precisely to the runtime invocation payload dispatched by the agent harness.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-44]

# Architecture / Specification

The pattern establishes an enforcement protocol separating the policy decision point (PDP) from the policy enforcement point (PEP) embedded within the execution harness.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-44] Implementation profiles such as the [Control Surfaces for Agentic Harnesses](../standards/control-surfaces-for-agentic-harnesses.md) define concrete reconciliation criteria for this checkpoint:

- **Digest Evaluation and Argument Minimization:** While basic checkpoint models require the enforcement point to recompute action payload digests directly from runtime arguments, privacy-preserving argument minimization protocols require PDPs to evaluate client-supplied digests against registered decision digests without full argument disclosure.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-44]
- **Clock Skew and Validity Windows:** Verification mandates explicit clock skew tolerances between distributed policy decision points and enforcement points, preventing premature expiration or replay windows.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-44]
- **Failure Classification:** Checkpoint implementations fold integrity mismatches, policy unavailability, and verification timeouts into deterministic fail-closed denials (`fail_closed_deny`), classifying the source of failure explicitly for audit trails.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-44]

mutations.rationale: Incorporate session authority revocation mechanics and delegation lineage separation identified in the Control Surfaces profile.

proposed_concept.title: Kill Switch
proposed_concept.description: Architectural control plane pattern establishing an independent out-of-band mechanism to immediately terminate agent execution and revoke session authorities.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Kill Switch pattern defines an out-of-band control mechanism capable of terminating agent execution sessions immediately, revoking active credentials, and halting downstream action delegation cascades upon detecting anomalous or unconstrained behavior.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-44]

# Architecture / Specification

Kill switch architectures operate across multiple structural tiers to guarantee immediate containment:

- **Session Binding Revocation:** Rather than relying exclusively on centralized identity provider credential invalidation, containment mechanisms invalidate session authorization bindings issued by the policy decision point (PDP), cutting off runtime authorization without altering underlying long-term identities.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-44]
- **Delegation Lineage Cascades:** Containment relies on explicit invocation lineage tracking (e.g., `parent_uid` hierarchies), ensuring that terminating a root agent session cascades instantly to revoke authorization across all child subagents and delegated task tokens.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-44]
- **Integration with Control Surfaces:** Standardized harness interfaces, such as the [Control Surfaces for Agentic Harnesses](../standards/control-surfaces-for-agentic-harnesses.md) profile, expose normative revocation endpoints and fail-closed session termination behaviors.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-44]

mutations.rationale: Document five proposed integration seams connecting OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions to signed action and evidence records.

proposed_concept.title: OpenTelemetry for Agentic AI
proposed_concept.description: Reference architecture for vendor-neutral agent telemetry collection, OTLP pipelines, and gen_ai semantic conventions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

OpenTelemetry (OTel) provides the vendor-neutral foundation for distributed tracing, metrics, and structured event logging across agentic AI systems through its GenAI semantic conventions (`semantic-conventions-genai`).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-67] Within the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), work focuses on mapping standard OTel telemetry pipelines to cryptographic audit trails and verifiable execution layers.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-67]

# Architecture / Specification

Recent technical proposals delineate five architectural seams required to connect standard OTel GenAI telemetry spans with signed evidence and [Action Record](../taxonomy/action-record.md) layers:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-67]

1. **Span-to-Record Join:** Bi-directional linkage between transient distributed tracing span identifiers and immutable, signed action or evidence record hashes.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-67]
2. **Decision and Approval Seam:** Recording human and policy gating outcomes, approval checkpoint identifiers, and authorization validity metadata directly alongside invocation spans.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-67]
3. **Effect Target and Status:** Distinguishing intended execution effects from actual environmental state mutations and post-condition verification statuses across external tools.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-67]
4. **Evidence Origin:** Propagating witness metadata, cryptographic provenance, and verification vantage points into span attributes as specified in the [Evidence Record Specification](../standards/evidence-record-spec.md).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-67]
5. **Integrity Without Disclosure:** Providing cryptographic digest verification over span payloads and tool arguments to maintain tamper-evidence without exposing sensitive data in telemetry collectors.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-67]

mutations.rationale: Record the addition of Ouroboros to the Agentic Runtime layer of the AAIF landscape catalog.

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Landscape
proposed_concept.description: Interactive ecosystem market map and catalog backed by landscape.yml tracking open-source agentic projects and runtime categories.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Landscape is an interactive market map and categorical ecosystem registry maintained by the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md).[^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-23] It provides a comprehensive view of open-source frameworks, runtime engines, protocol implementations, and observability platforms across the agentic artificial intelligence ecosystem.[^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-23]

# Architecture / Specification

The landscape is structured around categorized entries validated against strict automated schema rules and project health criteria (such as minimum GitHub star thresholds, open-source licensing, and vector branding assets).[^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-23]

- **Agentic Runtime Category:** Captures execution runtimes and multi-agent coordination engines. Recent entries include Ouroboros, an MIT-licensed autonomous agent runtime capable of coordinating specialist subagents, managing external project repositories, and self-evolving its implementation via structured review processes.[^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-23]
- **Governance:** Ecosystem additions follow community submission pull requests evaluated by automated pre-commit and schema validation pipelines prior to hosted preview publication.[^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-23]

proposed_concept.title: Technical Committee
proposed_concept.description: Governing technical body of the Agentic AI Foundation overseeing technical vision, standards, project lifecycles, and working groups.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The AAIF Technical Committee (TC) is the technical governing body of the Agentic AI Foundation, responsible for overseeing technical standards, best practices, and the technical vision of the Foundation.[^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-fc8fa852] The TC operates under the AAIF Technical Charter and manages project admissions, lifecycle stage progressions, and working group reviews across the foundation's ecosystem.[^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-fc8fa852]

# Architecture / Specification

## Composition and Terms

Founding TC members were appointed by the AAIF Governing Board for the term running from March 1, 2026, through December 31, 2026:[^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-fc8fa852]

- **David Soria Parra (Chair)** — Anthropic
- **Caitie McCaffrey (Co-Chair)** — Microsoft
- **Alan Blount** — Google
- **Bradley Axen** — Block
- **James Ward** — Amazon Web Services
- **Nick Cooper** — OpenAI
- **Sambhav Kothari** — Bloomberg
- **Steve Faulkner** — Cloudflare

## Governance Authority and Processes

The Technical Committee maintains and enforces authoritative governance documents across the AAIF repository estate:[^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-fc8fa852]

- **Technical Charter**: Defines TC composition, meeting structure, voting quorums, and formal responsibilities.
- **Project Lifecycle Policy**: Dictates admission gates and criteria across Sandbox, Growth, and Impact stages (see [Project Lifecycle Policy](../policies/project-lifecycle-policy.md)).[^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-fc8fa852]
- **Project Proposal Process**: Establishes project intake, legal review, and onboarding workflows (see [Project Proposal Process](../policies/project-proposal-process.md)).[^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-fc8fa852]
- **Working Group Lifecycle Policy**: Governs proposal, charter approval, annual renewal, and sunsetting of working groups (see [Working Group Lifecycle Policy](../policies/working-group-lifecycle-policy.md)).[^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-fc8fa852]
- **Working Group Monthly Reporting**: Defines cadence and review workflows for working group operational reporting (see [Working Group Reporting Template](../guidelines/working-group-reporting-template.md)).[^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-fc8fa852]

## Project Oversight

The TC tracks projects across stages, including [Agent Skills](../standards/agent-skills.md) (Impact Stage), Agent Router (Growth Stage), and Agent2Agent / A2A (Growth Stage).[^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-fc8fa852]

mutations.rationale: Update the control surfaces profile to incorporate v0.3 specifications, protocol composition choices (AuthZEN, OCSF, OAuth), and reconciliation requirements with existing security patterns.

proposed_concept.title: Control Surfaces for Agentic Harnesses
proposed_concept.description: Standardized profile defining administrative harness lifecycle events, external authorization checkpoints, and delegated execution boundaries.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Control Surfaces for Agentic Harnesses profile (v0.3) defines the administrative control plane an agentic harness exposes to system operators: the lifecycle events it records and the checkpoints where an external authorization decision gates agent execution.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-45] Rather than defining an abstract security model, the specification functions as an interoperable contract realized by client harnesses and policy services, bridging the implementation-independent patterns catalog and operational guides maintained by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-45]

# Architecture / Specification

## Protocol Composition

The profile composes four external standards to govern runtime interactions:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-45]

- **OpenID AuthZEN**: Implements runtime authorization checkpoint decisions and decision record binding.
- **Agent Plugins Portable Hooks**: Provides canonical lifecycle event naming across tool execution, step transitions, and subagent spawning (see [Agent Plugins](../standards/agent-plugins.md)).
- **Open Cybersecurity Schema Framework (OCSF)**: Structures structured audit trail records and telemetry payloads.
- **OAuth Token Exchange**: Enforces monotonic scope narrowing, principal assertion, and delegation lineage across subagent chains.

## Concrete Pattern Realization

The specification provides normative implementations for core catalog design patterns:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-45]

- **Approval Checkpoint (Section 8.3 & 8.4)**: Realizes decision binding and decision records (see [Approval Checkpoint](../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md)).
- **Runtime Policy Enforcement (Section 8)**: Standardizes external Policy Decision Point (PDP) checkpoint queries and timeout/failure semantics (`fail_closed_deny`).
- **Delegation Constraint & Permission Downgrade (Section 6.2)**: Mandates monotonic narrowing and per-sub-agent scope issuance.
- **Capability-Based Tool Invocation (Sections 5.3 & 6.2)**: Associates canonical tool identifiers with scope tokens.
- **Memory Provenance (Section 7)**: Establishes context sources and integrity labels (`untrusted`, `sensitive`), implementing the Rule of Two per session defined in [Agentic AI Security Best Practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md).
- **Audit Trail (Section 5)**: Defines normative lifecycle event capture.

## Pattern Reconciliation Points

The draft highlights specific reconciliation requirements against existing patterns:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-45]

- **Approval Checkpoint Alignment**: Reconciles clock skew tolerance, recomputed digests under argument minimization, and error outcome classifications.
- **Attested Isolated Runtime Alignment**: Evaluates single-use action identifier consumption across persistent restart state versus stateless PDP verification (see [Attested Isolated Runtime](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md)).
- **Kill Switch Alignment**: Clarifies session binding revocation and cascade lineage mechanics, distinguishing the session authority PDP from downstream identity providers (see [Kill Switch](../patterns/kill-switch.md)).

## Cross-Working-Group Dependencies

Delegation chain architecture and principal assertion link directly to the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md), while lifecycle telemetry coordinates with the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-45]

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing vendor-neutral agent telemetry standards, cross-boundary trace correlation, and OpenTelemetry semantic conventions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability and Traceability Working Group establishes vendor-neutral telemetry specifications, distributed tracing models, and cross-boundary correlation standards for single-agent and multi-agent systems.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e1eff34e54a6-f9dca54f] The working group collaborates closely with upstream standards bodies—including the OpenTelemetry GenAI Special Interest Group (SIG)—to formalize semantic conventions for agent execution lifecycles, token accounting, and provenance tracking.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e1eff34e54a6-f9dca54f]

# Architecture / Specification

## Semantic Conventions and Turn Definition

A primary initiative within the working group is standardizing agent conversational and execution units:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e1eff34e54a6-f9dca54f]

- **Turn vs. Step**: Formal proposal submitted to the OpenTelemetry GenAI SIG defining a "turn" as a single user or trigger input that produces a sequence of intermediate "steps" (e.g., model reasoning iterations and tool calls).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e1eff34e54a6-f9dca54f]
- **Taxonomy Alignment**: Coordinating with the Taxonomy and Landscape workstream to define foundational execution terms (turn, step, and session bounds).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e1eff34e54a6-f9dca54f]
- **Token Attribution**: Ensuring consistent token consumption attribution across complex iterative and multi-agent loops.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e1eff34e54a6-f9dca54f]

## Cross-Domain Tracing and SDK Strategy

- **Provenance and Domain Traversal**: Drafting extensions to baseline [OpenTelemetry](../resources/opentelemetry.md) specifications to support cross-domain distributed tracing, privacy preservation, and causality across multi-agent environments.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e1eff34e54a6-f9dca54f]
- **Multi-Language Implementation**: Developing SDK integrations supporting Golang for cloud-native infrastructure, alongside Rust, TypeScript, JavaScript, and Python bindings.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e1eff34e54a6-f9dca54f]

## Inter-Working-Group Coordination

- **Accuracy and Reliability**: Collaborating with the [Accuracy and Reliability Working Group](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md) to define standard instrumentation points for capturing agent evaluation outcomes and benchmark failure modes.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e1eff34e54a6-f9dca54f]
- **Attestation Liaison**: Coordinating with the interim attestation initiative regarding cross-cutting runtime evidence capture.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e1eff34e54a6-f9dca54f]
- **Context and Memory**: Tracking proposals with the proposed [Agent Context and Memory Working Group](../working-groups/agent-context-and-memory.md) regarding memory inspection and state observability.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e1eff34e54a6-f9dca54f]

proposed_concept.title: Attestation and Evidence Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Cross-cutting AAIF working group operating an interim trial to define verification standards, witness taxonomies, and portable attestation bundles.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Attestation and Evidence Working Group is a cross-cutting AAIF initiative focused on standardizing verification, cryptographic attestation, and evidentiary claims for autonomous agent behaviors.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e1eff34e54a6-f9dca54f] Formed to address critical industry gaps in proof of control and verifiable execution, the group coordinates verification mechanisms across runtime environments, policy engines, and external witness frameworks.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e1eff34e54a6-f9dca54f]

# Architecture / Specification

## Organizational Trial Status

The initiative operates under a 90-day trial approved to evaluate industry need and determine its permanent institutional structure within the foundation.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e1eff34e54a6-f9dca54f] Following the trial period, leadership will submit formal recommendations to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) on whether the effort should transition into a permanent workstream, a full Technical Working Group, or a cross-working-group committee.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e1eff34e54a6-f9dca54f]

## Cross-Working-Group Liaisons

The attestation effort bridges overlapping verification needs across foundational AAIF domains:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e1eff34e54a6-f9dca54f]

- **Security and Privacy**: Aligning with the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) on hardware-attested execution and policy enforcement records.
- **Observability and Traceability**: Coordinating with the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) on causal trace records, execution event attestation, and provenance metadata.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e1eff34e54a6-f9dca54f]

mutations.rationale: Document the proposed Agent Face Protocol (AFP) sandbox standard submitted to the AAIF for agent emotional, operational, and conversational state representation.

proposed_concept.title: Agent Face Protocol
proposed_concept.description: Transport-agnostic JSON specification enabling AI agents to communicate operational state, facial expressions, reactions, and speech visemes to human users.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agent Face Protocol (AFP) is a lightweight, transport-agnostic JSON specification designed to give autonomous AI agents an interpretable visual and conversational face.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-66] Proposed to the AAIF as a Sandbox stage project alongside the open-source `bbot` reference renderer, AFP provides a neutral vocabulary for agents to display operational lifecycle states (`thinking`, `working`, `waiting`, `error`), nuanced expressions, reactive gestures, and speech with lip-sync.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-66]

# Architecture / Specification

## Protocol Components

The protocol decouples emotional and operational state semantics from graphical rendering engines, exposing four foundational signaling primitives:[^evt-project-proposals-issue-66]

- **Operational States**: Standardized high-level statuses indicating background agent execution (such as tool execution, waiting for human approval, or encountering exceptions).
- **Expressions**: A catalog of thirty distinct emotional expressions paired with plain-language glosses to support accessibility captions and screen readers.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-66]
- **Reactions**: Discrete one-shot non-verbal reactions (such as `nod` or `shake`).
- **Speech and Visemes**: Timed phonetic viseme sequences enabling real-time lip synchronization with speech synthesis backends.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-66]

## Integration Surfaces

- **Model Context Protocol (MCP)**: AFP defines standard MCP tool bindings (`face_state`, `face_express`, `face_react`, `face_look`, `face_speak`), allowing any MCP-compliant agent host to manipulate avatar rendering via direct tool calls.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-66]
- **Agent Host Integrations**: Sits at the human-facing edge of execution hosts like [Goose](../resources/goose.md) to visualize multi-minute background tasks such as code generation and tool negotiation.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-66]
- **Skills Discovery**: Ships with structured discovery manifests compatible with [Agent Skills](../standards/agent-skills.md) conventions (`SKILL.md` and `llms.txt`) enabling coding agents to provision visual interfaces autonomously.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-66]

proposed_concept.description: Architectural control plane pattern establishing an independent out-of-band mechanism to immediately halt agent execution and revoke credentials.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Kill Switch pattern defines an independent, out-of-band control mechanism capable of terminating autonomous agent execution, isolating network boundaries, and revoking downstream credentials immediately upon trigger activation.

# Architecture / Specification
The pattern decouples runtime control planes from agent execution loops to guarantee uninterceptable containment:
- **Out-of-Band Control Plane**: Operating paths isolated from model context and tool invocation channels prevent agents from intercepting or suppressing termination signals.
- **Credential Revocation Containment**: A protocol mapping that instantly invalidates delegated tokens, API session keys, and active authorization grants across relying parties to halt in-flight transactions.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-43]
- **Blast Radius Mitigation**: Enforces immediate transition into an unprivileged quarantine state, preventing recursive subagent spawning or unapproved state persistence.

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-10**: The [working-groups/security-and-privacy](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) design patterns workstream mapped credential revocation containment protocols into the pattern specification.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-43]

# Overview
The Agentic Use Case Classification Framework structures real-world agent deployments across standardized architectural dimensions to evaluate workflow orchestration, human oversight, and operational complexity.

# Architecture / Specification
The classification framework categorizes production workflows defined in the inventory ([resources/agentic-use-case-inventory](../resources/agentic-use-case-inventory.md)):
- **Core Dimensions**: Analyzes trigger mechanism, human intervention gates, agent cardinality (single-agent vs. multi-agent), execution determinism (fixed/scripted vs. adaptive), and orchestration topology (sequential pipeline, fan-out/join, or iterative loop).
- **Boundary Scope (Proposed)**: Evaluates the output destination perimeter across three discrete values: `Same team`, `Across teams`, and `Across companies`.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-60]
- **Architectural Implications**: Workflows crossing team or enterprise boundaries mandate differentiated approval routing, audit logging, and payload validation even when sharing identical triggering and topology primitives.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-60]

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-10**: Issue #60 proposed extending the schema with the `Boundary` dimension to disambiguate routing and handoff requirements across inventory use cases.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-60]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Identity and Trust Working Group (WG Identity & Trust) develops open standards, reference architectures, and cryptographic conformance criteria for autonomous agent identity, delegated authority, and decentralized trust verification.

# Architecture / Specification
The working group's foundational output includes the Identity and Trust Reference Architecture v1 (October 2026), defining normative invariants for agent delegation and governance:
- **Time-of-Use Verification (§3.5.1)**: Mandates runtime validation of five delegation elements, ensuring grants remain in force without relying on an agent's self-reported status.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-22]
- **Chain Separation (§3.5.2)**: Separates functional delegation pathways from legal and operational accountability chains.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-22]
- **Hop Attenuation (§3.5.3)**: Prohibits authority widening across multi-hop delegation chains; child grants must strictly narrow or match parent constraints.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-22]
- **Root Issuance and Cascading Revocation (§3.5.4, §3.6)**: Enforces bounded-time cascading invalidation across all derived subordinate authority upon principal revocation.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-22]
- **Zero-Knowledge Principal Accountability (§5)**: Enables relying parties to verify that an accountable principal exists at a declared assurance level without disclosing intermediate surveillance graphs or principal identities.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-22]
- **Delegated Authority Conformance Cases**: An eight-case evaluation suite (including stale revocation, authority amplification, unavailable escalation, and disputed revocation) requiring designs to declare their explicit residual trade-offs.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-22]

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-10**: Reference Architecture v1 established core delegation and revocation invariants; issue #22 introduced an eight-case conformance test matrix mandating documented residual trade-offs for candidate implementations.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-22]

proposed_concept.title: Kill Switch
proposed_concept.description: Architectural control plane pattern establishing out-of-band credential revocation and containment mechanisms to immediately halt autonomous agent execution.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Kill Switch pattern defines an authoritative, out-of-band operational mechanism to instantly revoke credentials, terminate runtime access, or halt execution loops across autonomous agent systems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-faf61688d774-51e9e85a]. As autonomous agents interact across heterogeneous environments, relying solely on cooperative in-band halting is insufficient; a robust kill switch enforces containment at identity, network, and harness boundaries [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-faf61688d774-51e9e85a].

The pattern addresses containment across both enterprise boundaries—where standards like SPIFFE, RFC 7009, and OpenID Continuous Access Evaluation Profile (CAEP) apply—and open internet environments where identity attestation, decentralized verification, and third-party credential revocation are required [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-faf61688d774-51e9e85a].

# Architecture / Specification

The pattern encompasses three primary revocation pathways and enforcement surfaces [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-faf61688d774-51e9e85a]:

1. **Direct Agent or User Revocation:** An agent runtime can self-revoke, or an authenticated principal holding a hardware- or credential-backed token can trigger termination directly through an out-of-band control interface [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-faf61688d774-51e9e85a].
2. **Cascade Revocation:** Revoking a root principal credential automatically invalidates all derived subagent keys, active sessions, and delegated authorization proofs across downstream services [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-faf61688d774-51e9e85a].
3. **Issuer Emergency Revocation:** The authoritative issuer or validator publishes an emergency status root update, forcing verifiers to refuse incoming requests signed by the compromised agent or harness [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-faf61688d774-51e9e85a].

### Open Internet and Ledger Distribution

While enterprise systems rely on reachable central identity providers and Continuous Access Evaluation Profile (CAEP) endpoints, open internet deployments face availability risks such as DNS failures or hyperscaler outages [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-faf61688d774-51e9e85a]. In decentralized architectures, such as the open-source MintID protocol and ZadQ validator ecosystem, agents present short-lived zero-knowledge proofs (e.g., valid for 10 seconds) bound to requests, verified against public ledger status [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-faf61688d774-51e9e85a].

In evaluated benchmarks, ledger-recorded kill switches achieved strict propagation bounds where verifiers systematically refused revoked agents within 245 seconds, with empirical network tests recording revocation refusal between 27.5 and 33.8 seconds [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-faf61688d774-51e9e85a]. Additionally, kill switch events can integrate directly into Model Context Protocol (MCP) server transports and task loops, barring flagged agents at tool authentication time [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-faf61688d774-51e9e85a].

# Lifecycle History

Evaluated within the Security and Privacy Working Group design patterns catalog, with clarification ongoing regarding central identity provider assumptions versus decentralized ledger mechanisms for open internet scenarios [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-faf61688d774-51e9e85a] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-46].

# Overview

The Identity and Trust Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body responsible for defining open standards, architectures, and taxonomies for agent identity, delegation, consent receipts, and verifiable action records [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-922f59c26329-928a222f]. Co-chaired by Grant Miller (IBM) and Alper Dedeoğlu (SAP SE), the working group focuses on establishing verifiable boundaries between principals, agent runtimes, and downstream services [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-922f59c26329-928a222f].

# Architecture / Specification

The working group organizes its technical agenda into three specialized sub-working groups [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-922f59c26329-928a222f]:

- **Taxonomy Sub-WG:** Coordinates with the cross-cutting `../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md` workstream to standardize formal definitions for trust, attestation, delegation, and identifiers [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-922f59c26329-928a222f].
- **Reference Architecture Sub-WG:** Employs a primitive-first methodology, developing modular core primitives (beginning with the identity primitive draft) that aggregate into concrete use cases and full reference architectures [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-922f59c26329-928a222f].
- **Critical Use Cases Sub-WG:** Formulates end-to-end lifecycle models across Internal, B2B, and B2C operational scopes, spanning agent naming, deployment, delegation, per-request authorization, audit/compliance, and principal-attested revocation [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-922f59c26329-928a222f].

### Functional Requirements & External Inputs

The group evaluates external industry implementations to refine its technical deliverables, including NVIDIA's Secure Agent Workspace reference design and Uber's agentic identity architecture [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-922f59c26329-928a222f]. Key technical requirements under active specification include verifiable delegation hierarchies, dynamic per-request authorization gates, selective disclosure for content-private action records, and tamper-evident revocation mechanics [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-922f59c26329-928a222f].

# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body tasked with formulating actionable security guidance, reference threat models, cross-working group review checklists, and containment patterns for agentic AI deployments [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-faf61688d774-51e9e85a]. The group collaborates across AAIF workstreams and external initiatives to maintain unified security baselines for the agent ecosystem [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-faf61688d774-51e9e85a].

# Architecture / Specification

The working group's active deliverables and initiatives include [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-faf61688d774-51e9e85a]:

- **Design Patterns Catalog:** Standardizing architectural mitigation patterns, notably the `../patterns/kill-switch.md` pattern and its containment models across enterprise CAEP and decentralized zero-knowledge identity fabrics [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-faf61688d774-51e9e85a].
- **Cross-WG Security & Privacy Review Checklist:** Integrating cross-functional review processes with `../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md` and `../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md` to establish consistent security evaluation gates [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-faf61688d774-51e9e85a].
- **Attestation & Verification:** Engaging in cross-cutting initiatives, including a 90-day pilot attestation workstream and evaluating runtime execution verification tools such as CIGAR (Context Intelligence Graph Agentic Runtime), Agent Action Capsules, and immutable Merkle root anchoring protocols [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-faf61688d774-51e9e85a].
- **Cross-Ecosystem Alignment:** Coordinating alignment on definitions and identity models with bodies such as the x402 Identity Working Group and the Open Secure AI Alliance to provide unified industry recommendations [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-faf61688d774-51e9e85a].

### Operational Evolution

The group is pursuing structural alignment between working group deliverables and core foundation projects, exploring bi-directional feedback loops via automated GitHub issue tracking to alert project builders of recommended architectural requirements and capture breaking changes early [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-faf61688d774-51e9e85a].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The `aaif-audit-slack` skill is a read-only audit engine and independent verification check operating as phase 8 of the AAIF community estate sync pipeline (`../skills/aaif-sync.md`) [^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-92673e4e]. It verifies whether chapters have designated public and organizer channels, confirms that approved organizers occupy appropriate channels, assesses channel clutter and newcomer experience, and generates an integrated HTML diagnostic report [^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-92673e4e].

In accordance with operational hygiene rules, the skill executes from an isolated code path separate from the write engines, adhering to the principle that generation filters cannot validate their own output [^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-92673e4e]. Findings must be remediated at the source (e.g., via `../skills/aaif-clean-data.md`) and verified by re-running the sync pipeline [^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-92673e4e].

# Architecture / Specification

The skill structures workspace auditing across three core reports, a shared measurement layer, an on-demand spam scanner, and a single consolidated HTML deliverable [^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-92673e4e]:

| Report / Component | Script | Function | Execution Model |
|---|---|---|---|
| Organizers Report | `audit_organizers.py` | Verifies channel presence for every chapter and validates accepted organizer memberships | Phase 8 sync pipeline |
| Topics Report | `audit_topics.py` | Evaluates activity, discoverability, and overlap across subject-matter channels | Phase 8 sync pipeline |
| Members Report | `audit_members.py` | Analyzes workspace accessibility, roster composition, and headline counts | Phase 8 sync pipeline |
| Activity Layer | `audit_activity.py` | Measures human message volumes, latest human message timestamps, and distinct posters | Feeds Topics & Members reports |
| Spam Inspection | `audit_spam.py` | Detects solicitations, account rentals, and multi-channel message blasts across public threads and token-visible scopes; exits with code 2 on partial lead lists (`INCOMPLETE:`) | On-demand script (manual triage) |
| Deliverable Engine | `summarize_audits.py` | Compiles an interactive HTML report containing indexed audit sections and a prioritized remediation TL;DR | Pipeline completion output |

### Tooling Invariants

The audit skill strictly enforces Google Workspace environment rules: all Google Drive interactions must pass through the `gws` CLI driven via Python [^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-92673e4e]. Native Docs, Sheets, and Slides APIs are mandatory for editing Google Apps documents, and byte-level OOXML surgery is reserved strictly for non-native files [^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-92673e4e]. Desktop office suites such as LibreOffice, `soffice`, or `unoconv` are strictly prohibited to prevent font substitution, tab stripping, and OOXML schema corruption [^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-92673e4e].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Open telemetry and correlation framework capturing causal agent execution, tool invocations, approval gates, and multi-turn conversational intervals across distributed systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open telemetry and tracing specification developed by the [Observability and Traceability WG](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) to define standard instrumentation, span hierarchies, and semantic conventions for agent execution.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-71] It extends core OpenTelemetry distributed tracing standards to capture autonomous loops, external tool calls, human checkpoints, and execution turns across heterogeneous agent runtimes.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-72]

# Architecture / Specification

### OpenTelemetry Integration Gaps

The model establishes solutions for seven documented operational gaps observed across coding agents, agent SDKs, and AI gateways using OpenTelemetry semantic conventions:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-71]

1. Missing standard conventions for autonomous multi-step loops.
2. Inconsistent interpretation of agent-to-agent boundaries and parent-child span linking.
3. Non-adoption of standard attributes across proprietary model gateway proxies.
4. Instrumentation defects leading to broken causal graphs during asynchronous delegate dispatch.
5. Incomplete contextual attribution for tool execution results and transient sandbox side-effects.
6. Fragmented representation of human-in-the-loop pause and resumption events.
7. Uncorrelated cost, token usage, and latency attribution across federated subagent swarms.

### Turn and Step Modeling

To align agent execution traces with conversational and operational lifecycles, the model specifies standardized hierarchical intervals for upstream inclusion in the OpenTelemetry GenAI Special Interest Group (SIG):[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-72]

- **Turn**: A high-level interaction interval bounded by an incoming trigger or user intent and the delivery of a terminal response or handoff.
- **Agent Step** (aliased as **Step**): A discrete operational iteration within a turn comprising reasoning, action proposal, and execution dispatch.
- **Turn Segment**: An OpenTelemetry-specific span unit demarcating streaming chunks or sub-phases within a turn.

Formal inclusion of Turn and Agent Step within shared AAIF vocabularies coordinates through term sheets in the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-72]

# Lifecycle History

- **October 2026**: Added working document gap analysis detailing seven telemetry deficiencies across coding agents and SDKs.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-71]
- **October 2026**: Formulated turn and agent step proposal (`AGENT-BEHAVIOR-TRACE-MODEL-TURN.md`) scheduled for upstream review with the OpenTelemetry GenAI SIG.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-72]

# References

- [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md)
- [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)
- [OpenTelemetry Reference Architecture](../resources/opentelemetry.md)
