proposed_concept.title: Agent Observability Use Cases Catalog
proposed_concept.description: Catalog defining multi-category agent observability use cases, cross-cutting telemetry requirements, and legal compliance retention boundaries.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agent Observability Use Cases Catalog is a structured reference inventory maintained by the [Observability and Traceability WG](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) outlining operational, security, diagnostic, and compliance requirements for instrumented agent systems.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-68] It documents concrete evaluation profiles and storage invariants needed across enterprise and multi-agent deployments.

# Architecture / Specification

### Enterprise Audit and Evidence Retention (E4)

Use case E4 governs authorization tracing, approval chain provenance, and legal evidence retention for high-consequence agent actions.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-68] To reconcile verifiable audit trails with statutory privacy obligations, the specification deprecates unconditional write-once-read-many (WORM) storage semantics in favor of tamper-evident stores with declared retention bases:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-68]

- **Regulatory Conflict Resolution**: Absolute WORM semantics preclude lawful operation under GDPR Article 17(1) (Right to Erasure) and Article 5(1)(e) (Storage Limitation) when approval records contain identifiable natural persons, given that linkable hashes constitute personal data under Recital 26.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-68]
- **Tamper-Evident Storage with Declared Retention**: Record integrity must remain verifiable through cryptographic hash-chaining and external timestamps without requiring personal identifiers to be held indefinitely beyond their lawful basis.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-68]
- **Typed Tombstones**: When personal identifiers or sensitive parameters are removed under policy or data-subject requests, the record must preserve a typed tombstone. This allows downstream verifiers to differentiate between an expired record subjected to policy redaction and an invalid record that omitted mandatory fields at emission.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-68]
- **EU AI Act Alignment**: Reflects retention floors under EU AI Act Article 19(1) for providers and Article 26(6) for deployers, enforcing bounded retention rather than permanent identifier storage.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-68]

# Lifecycle History

- **October 2026**: Replaced unconditional write-once storage clause in use case E4 with tamper-evident retention with typed tombstones to ensure GDPR and EU AI Act compliance.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-68]

- [Evidence Record Specification](../standards/evidence-record-spec.md)
- [Approval Checkpoint Pattern](../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md)

proposed_concept.title: URACE (Unified Runtime for Autonomous Collaborative Evolution)
proposed_concept.description: Open-source P2P lifecycle control plane and governed runtime for autonomous software evolution, qualification gates, and post-quantum audited code distribution.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

URACE (Unified Runtime for Autonomous Collaborative Evolution) is an open-source, peer-to-peer lifecycle control plane designed to govern autonomous, AI-driven software development and distribution across decentralized networks without central authorities.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-67] It bridges the gap between raw AI code generation and production repositories by enforcing qualification gates, post-quantum cryptographic identity, and tamper-evident audit ledgers.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-67]

# Architecture / Specification

### Governed Improvement Loop

URACE coordinates autonomous executors (LLMs or automated agents) through an immutable execution cycle:[^evt-project-proposals-issue-67]

1. **Objective Ingestion**: Practitioners define declarative targets (e.g., latency reduction, test coverage).
2. **Executor Planning**: AI executors draft structured execution plans and code modifications.
3. **Qualification Gate**: An automated evaluation harness executes trial tests, safety predicates, and schema constraints. Executors are strictly prohibited from altering governance rules, authority configurations, or evaluation criteria.
4. **Accepted Operations**: Changes meeting acceptance thresholds are committed to the codebase.
5. **Immutable Audit Trail**: All decisions, trial evidence, and operations are recorded in an HMAC-chained, cryptographically verifiable ledger.

### P2P Feature Marketplace and Token Economy

Verified improvements can be tokenized, exchanged, or borrowed between peers across a decentralized network using a physics-calibrated token model.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-67] Peer reputation is calculated via Wilson lower-bound scoring based on verified delivery history rather than subjective assertions, providing defense against Sybil attacks and cartel manipulation.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-67]

### Cryptographic Architecture

URACE implements hybrid post-quantum cryptography combining ML-KEM-768 with classical TLS transport, alongside self-signed cryptographic identity certificates and machine-readable `AGENTS.md` interface manifests for zero-configuration executor onboarding.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-67]

# Lifecycle History

- **October 2026**: Submitted to the Agentic AI Foundation as a Growth stage project proposal under the Apache 2.0 license.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-67]

- [Project Lifecycle Policy](../policies/project-lifecycle-policy.md)

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability and Traceability Working Group is an AAIF technical body tasked with establishing vendor-neutral telemetry specifications, distributed tracing conventions, and evaluation frameworks for AI agent architectures.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-73] The group harmonizes telemetry across client SDKs, gateway proxies, tool sandboxes, and execution runtimes while liaising directly with upstream standards bodies such as OpenTelemetry.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-72][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-73]

# Architecture / Specification

### Active Deliverables and Workstreams

- **[Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md)**: Standardizing span graphs, causal linking, and execution models. Recent work includes a gap analysis identifying seven major OpenTelemetry instrumentation shortfalls in agent SDKs and coding tools,[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-71] and a formal proposal standardizing Turn, Agent Step, and Turn Segment semantics.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-72]
- **[Agent Observability Use Cases](../resources/agent-observability-use-cases.md)**: Cataloging diagnostic, operational, and audit profiles, including GDPR- and AI Act-compliant evidence retention with typed tombstones.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-71]
- **Cross-Boundary Telemetry Models**: Defining correlation headers across MCP server, subprocess CLI, and agent-to-agent boundaries.

### Upstream Liaisons

The working group maintains a structured liaison roster (`LIAISONS.md`) tracking outbound follow-ups and inbound requests across peer foundations and standards initiatives.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-73] Primary upstream collaboration focuses on the OpenTelemetry GenAI SIG to contribute native agent semantic conventions.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-72][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-73]

# Lifecycle History

- **October 2026**: Established the working group liaison roster tracking formal touchpoints with OpenTelemetry and partner foundations.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-73]
- **October 2026**: Published Gap Analysis for the Agent Behavior Trace Model and scheduled upstream turn modeling proposals for the OpenTelemetry GenAI SIG.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-71][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-72]

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Brand Guidelines and Design System
proposed_concept.description: Visual identity rules, typography tokens, dual surface palettes, component styling, and agent motif usage policies for AAIF assets.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The AAIF Design System defines the visual standards, typographic hierarchy, token extraction architecture, and rendering constraints across human-facing interfaces, generated reports, slide decks, and community assets [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-bbae69b7]. The design system strictly enforces a flat, monochrome-led identity with two distinct surfaces (white editorial and black plate) and explicitly disallows automated dark-mode inversions [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-bbae69b7].

# Architecture / Specification

## Source of Truth and Token Architecture
- **Canonical Bundle**: `design/aaif-design-system.html` serves as the authoritative, self-extracting single source of truth containing design tokens, component specifications, agent motif assets, and reference one-pager layouts [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-bbae69b7].
- **Generated Token File**: `design/aaif-tokens.css` contains the extracted `:root` token declarations consumed verbatim by report-styling scripts (`report_style.py`). It is regenerated using `scripts/extract_design_tokens.py`, and CI enforces freshness using `--check` [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-bbae69b7].
- **Official Assets**: Official vector marks (`assets/aaif-mark.svg`, `assets/aaif-mark-square.svg`, and `assets/aaif-logo-white.svg`) must be used verbatim without redrawing [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-bbae69b7].

## Typographic and Color Rules
- **Typeface**: Instrument Sans (OFL) is the exclusive typeface (weights 400, 500, 600, 700) for both display and interface copy; system monospace is reserved strictly for metadata and eyebrows, never body copy [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-bbae69b7].
- **Heading Metrics**: Headings are set at weight 500 with tracking `-0.02em` and line height between 1.05 and 1.15; bold weights are avoided except for h5/h6 set at weight 600 [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-bbae69b7].
- **Color Roles**: Black (`--accent: var(--ink)`) is the primary action accent; spectrum hues (`--spec-1` through `--spec-10`, e.g., coral as `--spec-8`) serve exclusively as subordinate accents within an individual surface [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-bbae69b7].
- **Flat Surface Depth**: Drop shadows are eliminated entirely. Depth is achieved through 1px hairlines, inset strokes, and paper tinting (`--paper` page ground, `--paper-2` section banding, `--paper-3` tinted panels) [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-bbae69b7]. Cards, statistics, tables, and chips maintain square corners (`border-radius: 0`), reserving rounded pills strictly for standalone badges and buttons [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-bbae69b7].
- **No Dark Mode**: Automated `prefers-color-scheme` overrides are prohibited; components exist exclusively on white editorial or black plate surfaces as explicitly selected by designers [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-bbae69b7].

## Motif Usage Boundaries
- **Agent Motif Restriction**: The agent bot motif derived from mark primitives is designated solely for empty states, loaders, event graphics, and dividers [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-bbae69b7]. It is strictly prohibited from governance, board, press, or audit documentation [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-bbae69b7].

# Lifecycle History
Codified in repository design documentation and synchronized via automated token extraction tooling to ensure consistent styling across Python reporting pipelines and OOXML asset generators [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-bbae69b7].

proposed_concept.description: Procedural pipeline orchestrator coordinating AAIF community estate reconciliation, organizer verification, report site navigation, and directory synchronization.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The `aaif-sync` skill orchestrates automated synchronization across AAIF community touchpoints, Google Drive chapter folders, CRM trackers, and Slack workspaces [^evt-community-events-pr-62][^evt-community-events-pr-63]. It cross-checks public intake records against active chapter rosters, enforces human authorization before altering public organizer listings, and produces connected multi-page HTML audit reports following the AAIF design system [^evt-community-events-pr-62][^evt-community-events-pr-63].

# Architecture / Specification

## Cross-Report Navigation Bar
- **Page Manifest Generation**: `sync.py` computes the list of active report pages (`run_pages`), recording the sequence in `run.json` and exposing it to rendering engines via `AAIF_REPORT_NAV` [^evt-community-events-pr-63].
- **Sticky Header Component**: `report_style.page()` renders a persistent top navigation bar across sibling HTML reports, resolving relative links and marking the active view while automatically suppressing the bar during print operations [^evt-community-events-pr-63].
- **Broken Link Prevention**: `render_report.py` filters links against actually written outputs so that failed sub-steps do not introduce dead links [^evt-community-events-pr-63].

## Organizer Qualification and Removal Gating
- **Accepted Organizer Requirement**: In `sync_crm`, folderless cities are only surfaced for chapter creation via `aaif-create-chapter` if they have an accepted organizer; general pipeline applicants, speakers, and operations staff are aggregated into counts without naming [^evt-community-events-pr-62].
- **Human-in-the-Loop Roster Pruning**: Implementing the [proposal-execution split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md), `sync_chapters` flags non-qualifying organizers for removal but restricts execution to an explicit manual flag (`--apply-removals`) to protect public rosters against malicious or mistaken intake submissions [^evt-community-events-pr-62].
- **Roster Invariants**: Untracked hand entries and historical organizers are preserved, and any removal proposal that would completely empty a chapter's organizer cell is halted as an operational retirement question that halts execution with exit code 2 [^evt-community-events-pr-62].

# Lifecycle History
- Extended in PR#62 to enforce organizer acceptance requirements for chapter provisioning and human-gated roster pruning [^evt-community-events-pr-62].
- Enhanced in PR#63 with unified multi-page top navigation across sync report suites [^evt-community-events-pr-63].
